faqs.question: ¿Qué es used to?
faqs.answer: Hábito o estado del pasado que ya no es verdad: I used to play football when I was young. Forma: used to + infinitivo. Negativa: didn't use to.

faqs.question: ¿Qué es be used to?
faqs.answer: Estar acostumbrado ahora: I am used to the noise. Forma: be used to + nombre o -ing (not infinitivo).

faqs.question: ¿Qué es get used to?
faqs.answer: El proceso de acostumbrarse: It took me months to get used to living here. También: I am getting used to… / I will get used to…

faqs.question: ¿Used to vs be used to — error típico?
faqs.answer: *I am used to play* es incorrecto. Si es hábito pasado: I used to play. Si estás acostumbrado: I am used to playing.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 9?
faqs.answer: En la [Unidad 9 del curso B1](/curso-b1/unit-9): gramática, habits, reading, listening y writing.

content:
Tras [Modals of deduction (U8)](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-8-modals-deduction), la **Unidad 9 del curso B1** (*Used to, be used to, get used to*) te enseña a hablar de **hábitos pasados** y de **acostumbrarte** a una vida nueva.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 9 — Used to / be used to / get used to](/curso-b1/unit-9)  
> **Antes:** [U8 — Modals of deduction](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-8-modals-deduction) · [Repaso A2→B1 (used to)](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-1-repaso-a2-b1)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 9 (B1)

- **used to + verbo** (hábito pasado).
- **be used to + nombre/-ing** (acostumbrado ahora).
- **get used to + nombre/-ing** (proceso de adaptación).
- Negativa y pregunta con *used to* (*didn't use to*, *Did you use to…?*).
- Vocabulario de **habits & lifestyle**.

![Trío used to](/blog/curso-b1/unit-9/used-to-trio.png)

---

## 1. Mapa rápido

| Estructura | Significado | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **used to + verb** | solía (ya no) | I **used to** live in a village. |
| **be used to + -ing/noun** | estar acostumbrado | I **am used to** the noise. |
| **get used to + -ing/noun** | acostumbrarse | I **got used to** living here. |

---

## 2. *used to* — hábitos del pasado

> I **used to** play football when I was young.  
> I **used to** live in a small village.  
> We **used to** have a dog when we were children.  
> He **used to** drink alcohol but now he has stopped.  
> I **didn't use to** like coffee but now I love it.  
> **Did** you **use to** live in London?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-9/used-to-play.mp3" title="🔊 I used to play football when I was young."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-9/used-to-live.mp3" title="🔊 I used to live in a small village."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-9/didnt-use-to.mp3" title="🔊 I didn't use to like coffee but now I love it."></audio>

Ojo: en negativa/pregunta, **use** (sin *-d*): *didn't **use** to*, *Did you **use** to…?*

---

## 3. *be used to* — acostumbrado ahora

> She **is used to** living in a big city.  
> We **are used to** getting up early.  
> She **is used to** driving in the city.  
> I **am used to** the noise and the busy lifestyle.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-9/is-used-to-living.mp3" title="🔊 She is used to living in a big city."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-9/are-used-to-getting-up.mp3" title="🔊 We are used to getting up early."></audio>

Después de *be used to* → **nombre** o **-ing**, nunca infinitivo (*to play* ✗ → *playing* ✓).

---

## 4. *get used to* — el proceso

> It took me a few months to **get used to** living here.  
> I am **getting used to** working from home now.  
> They **got used to** the cold weather after a few months.  
> I will **get used to** living alone soon.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-9/get-used-to-living.mp3" title="🔊 It took me a few months to get used to living here."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-9/getting-used-to.mp3" title="🔊 I am getting used to working from home now."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-9/got-used-to-cold.mp3" title="🔊 They got used to the cold weather after a few months."></audio>

## 5. Vocabulario: Habits & lifestyle

![Vocabulario de hábitos](/blog/curso-b1/unit-9/habits-vocab.png)

| Palabra / frase | Idea |
| :--- | :--- |
| habit | hábito |
| routine | rutina |
| lifestyle | estilo de vida |
| tradition | tradición |
| adapt | adaptarse |
| maintain | mantener |
| give up | dejar (un hábito) |
| take up | empezar (una actividad) |
| keep up | mantener / continuar |
| wake-up time | hora de despertar |
| adjustment period | periodo de ajuste |
| no longer | ya no |

---

## 6. Reading: village → city

![Del pueblo a la ciudad](/blog/curso-b1/unit-9/village-city.png)

> I used to live in a small village when I was young. I used to walk to school every day and play in the fields after class. Now I live in a big city and I am used to the noise and the busy lifestyle. It took me a few months to get used to living here. I used to hate traffic but now I don't mind it. My parents used to visit me every weekend but they live far now.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-9/reading-village.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: village to city"></audio>

Marca: *used to live / walk / play / hate / visit* · *am used to the noise* · *get used to living*.

---

## 7. Mini-diálogo

> Did you use to live in a village?  
> Yes — I used to walk to school every day.  
> Are you used to the city now?  
> Yes. It took a few months to get used to the noise.  
> Do you still hate traffic?  
> No — I used to hate it, but now I don't mind it.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-9/dialogue-habits.mp3" title="🔊 Dialogue: habits"></audio>

---

## 8. Practica en voz alta

> I used to play football. She is used to living in a big city. It took me months to get used to living here. I didn't use to like coffee.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-9/practice-four.mp3" title="🔊 Practice four sentences"></audio>

---

## 9. Ejercicios

### Ejercicio 1 — Elige la estructura

1. I \_\_\_\_ play football when I was young. (*used to*)  
2. She \_\_\_\_ living in a big city. (*is used to*)  
3. It took months to \_\_\_\_ living here. (*get used to*)  
4. We \_\_\_\_ getting up early. (*are used to*)  
5. They \_\_\_\_ the cold after a few months. (*got used to*)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **used to** · 2. **is used to** · 3. **get used to** · 4. **are used to** · 5. **got used to**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Forma correcta

1. I didn't \_\_\_\_ to like coffee. (*use*)  
2. Did you \_\_\_\_ to live in London? (*use*)  
3. I am used to \_\_\_\_. (*drive* → -ing)  
4. I used to \_\_\_\_ football. (*play*)  
5. He is getting used to \_\_\_\_ from home. (*work*)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **use** · 2. **use** · 3. **driving** · 4. **play** · 5. **working**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Vocabulario

1. Something you do regularly = \_\_\_\_  
2. Start a new activity = \_\_\_\_ up  
3. Stop a habit = \_\_\_\_ up  
4. Way you live = \_\_\_\_  
5. Become familiar with something new = get \_\_\_\_ to

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **habit** · 2. **take** · 3. **give** · 4. **lifestyle** · 5. **used**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Reading

1. He used to live in a small \_\_\_\_.  
2. Now he lives in a big \_\_\_\_.  
3. He is used to the \_\_\_\_.  
4. It took a few \_\_\_\_ to get used to living there.  
5. He used to hate \_\_\_\_.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **village** · 2. **city** · 3. **noise** · 4. **months** · 5. **traffic**
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Corrección

1. *I am used to play tennis* → \_\_\_\_  
2. *I used to living in Paris* → \_\_\_\_  
3. *I didn't used to smoke* → \_\_\_\_

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I am used to **playing** tennis. / I **used to play** tennis.  
2. I **used to live** in Paris.  
3. I didn't **use** to smoke.
</details>

---

## 10. Errores frecuentes

1. *be used to + infinitive* → **-ing** / noun.  
2. *didn't used to* → **didn't use to**.  
3. Mezclar *used to* (pasado) con *be used to* (ahora).  
4. Olvidar que *get used to* es un **proceso** (tiempo, *took me…*).

---

## Tip del profesor

Pregúntate: ¿**ya no** lo hago? → *used to*. ¿**Ya no me cuesta**? → *be used to*. ¿**Todavía me estoy adaptando**? → *get used to* / *getting used to*.

Este artículo reúne **los ejercicios de la Unidad 1 del curso B2** (*Repaso B1 → B2: Wish, Participle Clauses & Mixed Conditionals*) con **soluciones comentadas**.

> **Guía teórica:** [Repaso B1 → B2 B2](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-1-repaso-b1-b2)

Haz cada bloque **sin mirar** la solución. Luego comprueba y lee la explicación.

![Repaso B1 → B2](/blog/curso-b2/unit-1/wish-regret.png)

**Contenido de la unidad:**
1. [Lección 1 — Gramática](#leccion-1--gramatica)
2. [Lección 2 — Vocabulario](#leccion-2--vocabulario)
3. [Lección 3 — Reading: Nina's growth plan](#leccion-3--reading)
4. [Lección 4 — Listening: Nina on personal development](#leccion-4--listening)
5. [Lección 5 — Writing](#leccion-5--writing)

## Lección 1 — Gramática

**Objetivo:** wish / if only + past perfect, participle clauses, mixed conditionals

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. I wish I ___ studied harder for the exam. → *have / had / has*
2. If only we ___ more time yesterday. → *have / had / has*
3. She regrets ___ so much junk food. → *eat / eating / to eat*
4. ___ by her coach, she signed up immediately. → *Motivating / Motivated / Having motivate*
5. If he had taken the medicine, he ___ better now. → *feels / would feel / will feel*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **had** · 2. **had** · 3. **eating** · 4. **Motivated** · 5. **would feel**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige / completa

1. I wish I ___ afford a personal trainer. → *can / could / will*
2. ___ finished the course, she updated her CV. → *Having / Have / Had*
3. If only you ___ me sooner! → *tell / told / had told*
4. Encouraged ___ the results, he set new goals. → *by / with / for*
5. I wish they ___ stop interrupting me. → *will / would / can*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **could** · 2. **Having** · 3. **had told** · 4. **by** · 5. **would**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Corrige

1. *I wish I have studied more.*
2. *If only he takes the job.* (past regret)
3. *Motivating by her mentor, she applied.*
4. *If she studied harder, she would pass now.* (mixed)
5. *Having finish the test, she left.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I wish I **had studied** more.
2. If only he **had taken** the job.
3. **Motivated** by her mentor, she applied.
4. If she **had studied** harder, she **would pass** now.
5. Having **finished** the test, she left.

</details>

---

## Lección 2 — Vocabulario

**Objetivo:** personal development

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Empareja / elige

1. self-discipline → *autodisciplina · aeropuerto · billete*
2. set goals → *fijar objetivos · posponer · cancelar*
3. personal growth → *crecimiento personal · clima · equipaje*
4. regret → *arrepentirse · reservar · despegar*
5. motivated by → *motivado por · cansado de · alejado de*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **autodisciplina** · 2. **fijar objetivos** · 3. **crecimiento personal** · 4. **arrepentirse** · 5. **motivado por**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Completa

1. take up ≈ ___ → *empezar (actividad) / dejar / posponer*
2. give up ≈ ___ → *dejar (hábito) / empezar / reservar*
3. achieve ≈ ___ → *lograr / olvidar / retrasar*
4. mindset ≈ ___ → *mentalidad / horario / pasaporte*
5. commit to ≈ ___ → *comprometerse con / cancelar / posponer*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **empezar (actividad)** · 2. **dejar (hábito)** · 3. **lograr** · 4. **mentalidad** · 5. **comprometerse con**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — En contexto

11. Usa 3 palabras nuevas en frases con el foco gramatical.
12. Di en voz alta el vocabulario de la unidad.
13. Empareja cada palabra con un ejemplo personal.
14. Revisa la tabla de vocabulario de la [guía teórica](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-1-repaso-b1-b2).
15. Continúa en la [Unidad 1 del curso](/curso-b2/unit-1).

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11–13. Open answers — check meaning in theory. · 14. Theory vocab section. · 15. **/curso-b2/unit-1**

</details>

## Lección 3 — Reading: Nina's growth plan

**Objetivo:** comprender un texto con el foco de la unidad.

### Texto y audio

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-1/reading-workbook.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Nina's growth plan"></audio>

> Last year Nina regretted starting so many online courses and never finishing them. I wish I had been more disciplined, she says. Motivated by a podcast on personal growth, she enrolled in a B2 programme. If she had studied mixed conditionals in B1, she would understand them better now. Having completed the diagnostic test, she set clear goals for the month. Encouraged by her progress, she plans to join a study group next week.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. Who regret not finishing courses? → *Nina / James / Sofia*
2. What does she wish about discipline? → *had been more disciplined / will study / can fly*
3. Motivated by what? → *a podcast / rain / a flight*
4. Mixed conditional in text? → *yes / no*
5. Participle: Having completed… → *diagnostic test / airport / hotel*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Nina** · 2. **had been more disciplined** · 3. **a podcast** · 4. **If she had studied… she would understand** · 5. **diagnostic test**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. Encouraged by what? → *progress / traffic / rain*
7. Plans to join what? → *study group / hiking club / embassy*
8. Structure for past regret? → *wish + past perfect / will / going to*
9. Structure for mixed? → *mixed / only first / only zero*
10. Went to study group already? → *False / True*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **her progress** · 7. **study group** · 8. **wish + past perfect** · 9. **if + past perfect, would + base** · 10. **False**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. Underline 2× wish / if only.
12. Write one mixed conditional.
13. Key vocab? → *yes / none*
14. Tone? → *motivated / angry / empty*
15. Course link → */curso-b2/unit-1*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **See text** · 12. **Model OK** · 13. **discipline, goals, progress** · 14. **motivated** · 15. **/curso-b2/unit-1**

</details>

---

## Lección 4 — Listening: Nina on personal development

**Objetivo:** escuchar el foco gramatical en contexto.

### Audio y guion

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-1/listening-workbook.mp3" title="🔊 Listening: Nina on personal development"></audio>

> Hi, I am Nina. I wish I had started this course earlier — I regret wasting so much time on social media last year. Motivated by my coach, I signed up for a leadership workshop. If I had taken better notes in B1, I would feel more confident now. Having finished the first module, I am planning my next goals.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. Who speaks? → *Nina / James / Maya*
2. Wishes she had started ___ → *earlier / later / never*
3. Regrets wasting time on ___ → *social media / work / travel*
4. Motivated by her ___ → *coach / pilot / chef*
5. Mixed: If I had taken notes in B1… → *yes / no*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Nina** · 2. **earlier** · 3. **social media** · 4. **coach** · 5. **would feel confident now**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. Having finished the first ___ → *module / flight / meal*
7. Participle: Motivated by… → *coach / rain / ticket*
8. Grammar focus? → *wish/participle/mixed / only will*
9. Already in study group? → *False / planning*
10. Write one I wish I had…

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **module** · 7. **coach** · 8. **wish, participle, mixed** · 9. **planning (not yet)** · 10. **Model OK**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. Write one mixed conditional.
12. Shadow full audio.
13. Key vocab? → *yes / none*
14. Tone? → *reflective / angry*
15. Open Ver solución after try. → *yes*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **Model OK** · 12. **done** · 13. **goals, coach, module** · 14. **reflective & motivated** · 15. **yes**

</details>

---

## Lección 5 — Writing

**Objetivo:** producir frases con el foco de la unidad.

1. Escribe 2 frases con *I wish I had…* (arrepentimiento).
2. Completa: I wish I ___ (study) harder last year.
3. Completa: If only she ___ (tell) me the truth.
4. Completa: ___ by her mentor, she applied for the course.
5. Escribe un mixed conditional sobre tu progreso en inglés.
6. Completa: Having ___ (finish) the test, she relaxed.
7. Usa *regret + gerund* en una frase.
8. Corrige: *I wish I have more time.*
9. Corrige: *Motivating by the coach, she signed up.*
10. Párrafo (4 frases): metas de desarrollo personal.
11. Traduce: Ojalá hubiera empezado antes.
12. Traduce: Si hubiera practicado más, entendería mejor ahora.
13. Escribe *I wish they would…* (queja educada).
14. Participle clause: *Encouraged by…, I…*
15. Autochequeo: 1× wish, 1× participle, 1× mixed.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. Model: I wish I had started earlier. I wish I had been more consistent.
2. **had studied**
3. **had told**
4. **Motivated**
5. Open — If I had…, I would… now.
6. Having **finished**
7. I regret wasting so much time.
8. I wish I **had** more time.
9. **Motivated** by the coach, she signed up.
10. Open paragraph with goals vocabulary.
11. I wish I **had started** earlier. / If only I **had started** earlier.
12. If I **had practised** more, I **would understand** better now.
13. I wish they **would** reply faster.
14. Encouraged by my progress, I set new goals.
15. Self-check vs theory.

</details>

title: Repaso B1 → B2: Wish, Participle Clauses & Mixed Conditionals
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 1 del curso B2: puente B1 → B2 con wish, participle clauses y mixed conditionals.

alt: Repaso B1 a B2 wish regret

faqs.question: ¿Wish + pasado perfecto?
faqs.answer: **I wish / If only + past perfect** para arrepentimientos pasados: I wish I **had studied**.

faqs.question: ¿Participle clause -ed o -ing?
faqs.answer: **-ed** = pasiva (Encouraged by…); **-ing** = activa (Motivating the team…). **Having + pp** = acción completada antes.

faqs.question: ¿Mixed conditional?
faqs.answer: Pasado irreal → presente: If he **had taken** medicine, he **would feel** better **now**.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico?
faqs.answer: En la [Unidad 1 del curso B2](/curso-b2/unit-1).

content:
Empiezas el [curso B2](/blog/metodos/ingles-b2) con la **Unidad 1** (*Repaso B1 → B2*): activas **wish/regret**, **participle clauses** y **mixed conditionals** con vocabulario de **personal development**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 1](/curso-b2/unit-1)  
> **Antes:** [Inglés B2 — guía del nivel](/blog/metodos/ingles-b2)

---

## Qué aprenderás

- **I wish / If only + past perfect / could**
- **Regret + gerund**
- **Participle clauses** (-ing / -ed / Having + pp)
- **Mixed conditionals**
- Vocabulario: personal development

![Repaso B1 a B2 wish regret](/blog/curso-b2/unit-1/wish-regret.png)

---

## 1. Wish / If only + regret

| Estructura | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| **wish / if only + past perfect** | I **wish I had joined** the gym. |
| **wish + could** (presente) | I **wish we could afford** a membership. |
| **regret + gerund** | They **regret eating** so much junk food. |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-1/wish-had.mp3" title="🔊 wish had"></audio>
<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-1/wish-could.mp3" title="🔊 wish could"></audio>
<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-1/if-only.mp3" title="🔊 if only"></audio>
<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-1/regret-gerund.mp3" title="🔊 regret gerund"></audio>

---

## 2. Participle clauses

![Participle clauses](/blog/curso-b2/unit-1/participle-clauses.png)

| Tipo | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| **-ed** (pasiva) | **Encouraged by** the crowd, the runner crossed the line. |
| **Having + pp** | **Having finished** the workout, he felt exhausted. |
| **-ing** (activa) | **Motivated by** the results, he increased his training. |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-1/participle-ed.mp3" title="🔊 participle -ed"></audio>
<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-1/having-finished.mp3" title="🔊 having finished"></audio>

---

## 3. Mixed conditionals

![Mixed conditionals](/blog/curso-b2/unit-1/mixed-conditionals.png)

> If he **had taken** the medicine, he **would feel** better **now**.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-1/mixed-cond.mp3" title="🔊 mixed conditional"></audio>

Pasado irreal → consecuencia **presente**: *had + pp* en la *if*-clause, *would + infinitive* en el resultado.

---

## 4. Vocabulario: Personal development

![Personal development](/blog/curso-b2/unit-1/personal-dev-vocab.png)

| Word | Idea |
| :--- | :--- |
| goal / motivation | objetivo / motivación |
| self-discipline / habit | autodisciplina / hábito |
| resilience / wellbeing | resiliencia / bienestar |

---

## 5. Reading

> I wish I had joined the gym when I had the chance. If only she had followed the doctor's advice. Encouraged by the crowd, the runner crossed the line. Having finished the workout, he felt exhausted. If he had taken the medicine, he would feel better now.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-1/reading-u1.mp3" title="🔊 Reading"></audio>

---

## 6. Diálogo

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-1/dialogue-u1.mp3" title="🔊 Dialogue"></audio>

> Do you regret skipping breakfast? — Yes, I regret eating so fast.  
> Wish you had warned me? — I wish I had told you about the allergy.

---

## 7. Practica

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-1/practice-u1.mp3" title="🔊 Practice"></audio>

---

## 8. Ejercicios

1. I wish I ___ (join) the gym earlier.  
2. If only she ___ (follow) the advice.  
3. ___ by the crowd, he crossed the line. (Encourage)  
4. ___ finished the workout, he rested. (Have)  
5. If he had rested, he ___ (feel) better now.

<details><summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **had joined** · 2. **had followed** · 3. **Encouraged** · 4. **Having** · 5. **would feel**
</details>

---

## Tip del profesor

*Wish + past perfect* no es pasado narrativo: expresa un deseo sobre algo que **ya no puedes cambiar**.

---

## Practica ahora

1. Repasa los ejemplos en voz alta.  
2. Practica en la [Unidad 1 del curso B2](/curso-b2/unit-1).

## Lección 1 — Gramática

**Objetivo:** wish, would rather, mixed conditionals, participle clauses

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. I wish I ___ booked the tickets earlier. → *have / had / has*
2. I would rather ___ by train than fly. → *travel / to travel / travelling*
3. If we had left earlier, we ___ at the museum now. → *are / would be / will be*
4. ___ read the guide, we chose the eco tour. → *Having / Have / Had*
5. It is time we ___ our carbon footprint. → *reduce / reduced / reducing*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **had** · 2. **travel** · 3. **would be** · 4. **Having** · 5. **reduced**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige / completa

1. I wish my brother ___ help more at home. → *will / would / can*
2. She would prefer ___ with family. → *celebrate / to celebrate / celebrating*
3. If only they ___ the early bus! → *take / took / had taken*
4. ___ by the campaign, they recycle more. → *Encourage / Encouraged / Encouraging*
5. I'd rather you ___ drive so fast. → *don't / didn't / not*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **would** · 2. **to celebrate** · 3. **had taken** · 4. **Encouraged** · 5. **didn't**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Corrige

1. *I wish I have booked earlier.*
2. *I would rather to travel by bus.*
3. *If we leave early, we would be there now.*
4. *Having read, we chose the tour.* (add pp)
5. *It is time we reduce emissions.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I wish I **had booked** earlier.
2. I would rather **travel** by bus.
3. If we **had left** early, we **would be** there now.
4. Having **read** the guide, we chose the tour.
5. It is time we **reduced** emissions.

</details>

---

## Lección 2 — Vocabulario

**Objetivo:** feelings, family, travel, environment (mix)

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Empareja / elige

1. eco-friendly → *ecológico · ruidoso · caro*
2. queue → *cola / fila · maleta · billete*
3. carbon footprint → *huella de carbono · ascenso · beca*
4. feelings → *sentimientos · equipaje · pasaporte*
5. module review → *repaso de módulo · vuelo · embarque*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **ecológico** · 2. **cola / fila** · 3. **huella de carbono** · 4. **sentimientos** · 5. **repaso de módulo**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Completa

1. wish + past perfect = ___ → *arrepentimiento pasado / plan futuro*
2. would rather + bare inf = ___ → *preferencia / obligación / imposibilidad*
3. mixed conditional = ___ → *mezcla de condicionales / solo zero*
4. participle clause = ___ → *frase reducida con participio / pregunta*
5. it's time + past = ___ → *debería haber pasado ya / futuro seguro*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **arrepentimiento pasado** · 2. **preferencia** · 3. **mezcla de condicionales** · 4. **frase reducida con participio** · 5. **debería haber pasado ya**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — En contexto

11. Usa 3 palabras nuevas en frases con el foco gramatical.
12. Di en voz alta el vocabulario de la unidad.
13. Empareja cada palabra con un ejemplo personal.
14. Revisa la tabla de vocabulario de la [guía teórica](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-10-repaso-6-9).
15. Continúa en la [Unidad 10 del curso](/curso-b2/unit-10).

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11–13. Open answers — check meaning in theory. · 14. Theory vocab section. · 15. **/curso-b2/unit-10**

</details>

## Lección 3 — Reading: Olivia's module review

**Objetivo:** comprender un texto con el foco de la unidad.

### Texto y audio

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-10/reading-workbook.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Olivia's module review"></audio>

> Olivia's family is reviewing everything they learned in units six to nine. She wishes she had listened to the travel podcast before the trip. She would rather take the train than fly short distances. If they had left home earlier, they would not be queuing at the station now. Having joined a local green group, they recycle more than ever. It is time they talked openly about their feelings and plans.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. Olivia wishes she had listened to ___ → *travel podcast / cooking show / nothing*
2. Would rather take ___ than fly short distances → *train / taxi / boat*
3. If they had left earlier, they wouldn't be ___ → *queuing / hiking / sleeping*
4. Having joined green group, they recycle ___ → *more / less / never*
5. It is time they talked about ___ → *feelings / flights only / nothing*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **travel podcast** · 2. **train** · 3. **queuing** · 4. **more** · 5. **feelings and plans**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. Review covers units ___ → *6–9 / 1–4 / 11–15*
7. Find wish.
8. Find would rather.
9. Find mixed conditional.
10. Find participle.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **6–9** · 7. **I wish I had listened…** · 8. **would rather take the train** · 9. **If they had left… wouldn't be queuing** · 10. **Having joined…**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. Find it's time.
12. Write 4 sentences: wish, rather, mixed, participle.
13. Main idea? → *review / only travel / only work*
14. Vocab themes? → *yes / none*
15. Course link → */curso-b2/unit-10*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **It is time they talked…** · 12. **Model OK** · 13. **module 1 review U6–9** · 14. **feelings, family, travel, environment** · 15. **/curso-b2/unit-10**

</details>

---

## Lección 4 — Listening: Olivia mixes U6–9

**Objetivo:** escuchar el foco gramatical en contexto.

### Audio y guion

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-10/listening-workbook.mp3" title="🔊 Listening: Olivia mixes U6–9"></audio>

> Hi, I am Olivia. I wish I had booked the tickets earlier — we missed the concert. I would rather travel by train than drive. If we had taken the early bus, we would be at the museum now. Having read the guide, we chose the eco-friendly tour. It is time we reduced our carbon footprint as a family.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. Who speaks? → *Olivia / Nina / Maya*
2. Wishes had booked ___ earlier → *tickets / hotel / flight*
3. Missed the ___ → *concert / exam / flight*
4. Would rather travel by ___ → *train / plane / boat*
5. If had taken early bus, would be at ___ → *museum / beach / office*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Olivia** · 2. **tickets** · 3. **concert** · 4. **train** · 5. **museum**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. Having read the guide, chose ___ tour → *eco-friendly / luxury / random*
7. It's time reduced ___ footprint → *carbon / luggage / noise*
8. Review grammar U6–9? → *yes / no*
9. At museum now? → *False / True*
10. Find wish / rather / mixed / participle / it's time.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **eco-friendly** · 7. **carbon** · 8. **yes** · 9. **False (missed concert/bus)** · 10. **See script**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. Write one sentence each structure.
12. Shadow audio.
13. Mixed vocab themes? → *yes / none*
14. Module 1 complete after U10? → *yes / no*
15. Open Ver solución. → *yes*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **Model OK** · 12. **done** · 13. **travel, environment, feelings** · 14. **yes** · 15. **yes**

</details>

---

## Lección 5 — Writing

**Objetivo:** producir frases con el foco de la unidad.

1. Una frase con cada: wish, would rather, mixed conditional, participle, it's time.
2. Completa: I wish I ___ (book) earlier.
3. Completa: I would rather ___ (travel) by train.
4. Completa: If we had left earlier, we ___ (be) at the museum now.
5. Completa: ___ read the guide, we chose the eco tour.
6. Completa: It is time we ___ (reduce) our footprint.
7. Mini-historia (6 frases) mezclando U6–9.
8. Corrige: *I wish I have booked.*
9. Corrige: *I would rather to stay.*
10. Matching: estructura → unidad (6–9).
11. Traduce: Ojalá hubiera reservado antes.
12. Traduce: Preferiría no conducir tan rápido.
13. Autochequeo con mapa U10.
14. Shadow reading + listening una vez más.
15. Siguiente paso: teoría U11 en el curso.
16. Enlace /curso-b2/unit-10.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. Open — one of each U6–9 structure.
2. **had booked**
3. **travel**
4. **would be**
5. Having **read**
6. **reduced**
7. Open mixed paragraph.
8. I wish I **had booked** earlier.
9. I would rather **stay** at home.
10. wish→U6; rather→U7; mixed→U8; participle→U9.
11. I wish I **had booked** earlier.
12. I would rather you **didn't** drive so fast.
13. Self-check vs review map.
14. Practice again without solutions.
15. Next: relative clauses (Unit 11 theory).
16. **/curso-b2/unit-10**

</details>

## Lección 1 — Gramática

**Objetivo:** defining / non-defining relative clauses; who / which / that / whose / where

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. The district ___ we visited has a mural. → *that / , which / who*
2. The festival, ___ is annual, attracts thousands. → *which / that / who*
3. My neighbour, ___ family runs the festival, is friendly. → *whose / who / which*
4. The landmark ___ we met is near the skyscraper. → *where / which / that*
5. Non-defining clauses need ___. → *commas / no commas / that*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **that** · 2. **which** · 3. **whose** · 4. **where** · 5. **commas**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige / completa

1. In non-defining clauses, avoid ___. → *that / which / who*
2. Defining clauses give ___ information. → *essential / extra / optional*
3. People ___ live here love the nightlife. → *who / which / where*
4. The mural ___ won the prize is huge. → *which/that / who / whose*
5. The community ___ heritage is rich organises walks. → *whose / who / which*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **that** · 2. **essential** · 3. **who** · 4. **which/that** · 5. **whose**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Corrige

1. *The festival that is annual, attracts thousands.*
2. *My neighbour who family runs it is kind.*
3. *The place which we met is famous.*
4. *The district, that we visited, has a mural.*
5. *People which live here are friendly.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. The festival, **which** is annual, attracts thousands.
2. My neighbour, **whose** family runs it, is kind.
3. The place **where** we met is famous.
4. The district **that** we visited has a mural.
5. People **who** live here are friendly.

</details>

## Lección 3 — Reading: Sara in the city

**Objetivo:** comprender un texto con el foco de la unidad.

### Texto y audio

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-11/reading-workbook.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Sara in the city"></audio>

> Last weekend Sara explored a new district in the city. The district that she visited has a famous mural by a local artist. The festival, which is annual, attracts thousands of visitors from abroad. Her neighbour, whose family runs the festival, gave her a free ticket. The landmark where they met is near a glass skyscraper. Heritage and tradition still matter in this modern community. Nightlife around the square is busy but friendly.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. Who explored a district? → *Sara / Omar / Lena*
2. Defining: The district ___ she visited → *that / , which*
3. The festival, which is ___, attracts thousands → *annual / cancelled / quiet*
4. Whose family runs the festival? → *neighbour / designer / donor*
5. Landmark is near a ___ → *skyscraper / runway / compost*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Sara** · 2. **that** · 3. **annual** · 4. **her neighbour's** · 5. **skyscraper**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. Heritage and ___ still matter → *tradition / invoice / merger*

faqs.question: ¿Defining o non-defining?
faqs.answer: **Defining** = información esencial, **sin comas**. **Non-defining** = extra, **con comas**; no uses *that*.

faqs.question: ¿Who, which o that?
faqs.answer: En defining: **who** (personas), **which/that** (cosas), **whose** (posesión), **where** (lugar). En non-defining: **who/which**, no *that*.

faqs.question: ¿Cuándo uso where?
faqs.answer: Con lugares cuando la cláusula funciona como complemento de lugar: the district **where** I grew up.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico?
faqs.answer: En la [Unidad 11 del curso B2](/curso-b2/unit-11).

faqs.question: ¿Qué es una reduced relative clause?
faqs.answer: Omite el pronombre relativo + verbo *be*: *People **who are** attending* → *People **attending***.

faqs.question: ¿-ing o -ed?
faqs.answer: **-ing** = activa (*People attending…*). **-ed** = pasiva (*The soundtrack recorded…*).

faqs.question: ¿Cuándo no reducir?
faqs.answer: Si el verbo no es *be* o la cláusula es non-defining con información extra compleja, mantén la forma completa.

faqs.answer: En la [Unidad 12 del curso B2](/curso-b2/unit-12).

## Lección 1 — Gramática

**Objetivo:** must / have to / need to / needn't / don't have to

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. You ___ save all receipts for the budget. → *must / can / might*
2. I ___ submit the report by Friday. (external rule) → *have to / must / needn't*
3. We ___ raise more donations. → *need to / needn't / can't*
4. You ___ pay interest if you repay early. → *needn't / must / have to*
5. Volunteers ___ work every weekend. → *don't have to / must / need to*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **must** · 2. **have to** · 3. **need to** · 4. **needn't** · 5. **don't have to**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige / completa

1. Must often = obligation from the ___. → *speaker / weather / ticket*
2. Have to often = ___ obligation. → *external / imaginary / past perfect*
3. Needn't ≈ ___. → *don't have to / must / can't*
4. Past obligation: yesterday I ___ finish early. → *had to / must / needn't*
5. You must wear your ___ at the shelter. → *badge / runway / seedling*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **speaker** · 2. **external** · 3. **don't have to** · 4. **had to** · 5. **badge**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Corrige

1. *You must to save the receipts.*
2. *I have submit the budget.*
3. *We need raise donations.*
4. *You mustn't pay — it's optional.* (no obligation)
5. *Volunteers must not to work weekends.* (optional)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. You must **save** the receipts.
2. I **have to** submit the budget.
3. We **need to** raise donations.
4. You **needn't** / **don't have to** pay.
5. Volunteers **don't have to** work weekends.

</details>

Donors needn't pay interest if they repay the loan early. Volunteers don't have to work every weekend, yet many choose to help at the shelter.

## Lección 5 — Writing

**Objetivo:** producir frases con el foco de la unidad.

1. Escribe must, have to, need to, needn't y don't have to (1 cada uno).
2. Completa: You ___ (must) save the receipts.
3. Completa: I ___ (have to) submit the budget.
4. Completa: We ___ (need to) raise donations.
5. Completa: You ___ (needn't) pay interest early.
6. Explica must vs have to en 1 frase.
7. Corrige: *You must to wear a badge.*
8. Corrige: *Volunteers must work every weekend.* (si es opcional)
9. Párrafo money/volunteering con modales.
10. Traduce: No hace falta que pagues hoy.
11. Traduce: Tengo que entregar el informe el viernes.
12. Diálogo en un refugio / charity.
13. Matching: must/have to/needn't → uso.
14. Autochequeo.
15. Enlace teoría U13.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. Open — one of each modal.
2. **must**
3. **have to**
4. **need to**
5. **needn't**
6. Must ≈ speaker; have to ≈ external rule.
7. You must **wear** a badge.
8. Volunteers **don't have to** work every weekend.
9. Open paragraph.
10. You **needn't** / **don't have to** pay today.
11. I **have to** submit the report on Friday.
12. Open dialogue.
13. must→speaker; have to→external; needn't→no obligation.
14. Self-check.
15. [Guía U13](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-13-modals-money)

</details>

faqs.question: ¿Must o have to?
faqs.answer: Ambos expresan obligación. **Must** = hablante / regla interna. **Have to** = obligación externa / reglas.

faqs.question: ¿Needn't o don't have to?
faqs.answer: En afirmativo: **need to** = necesidad. En negativo: **needn't** y **don't have to** = no hay obligación (sinónimos en B2).

faqs.question: ¿Must en pasado?
faqs.answer: Para pasado usa **had to** (obligación) o **didn't have to / needn't have** según el matiz.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico?
faqs.answer: En la [Unidad 13 del curso B2](/curso-b2/unit-13).

## 1. Modals: obligation & necessity

| **need to** | necesidad | We **need to raise** donations. |
| **needn't / don't have to** | sin obligación | You **needn't pay** today. |

**Must** suena a regla o consejo del hablante; **have to** a norma externa. En negativo, **needn't** = *no es necesario* (libertad).

## Lección 1 — Gramática

**Objetivo:** must have / might have / can't have + past participle

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. She ___ missed the deadline. (almost sure) → *must have / might have / can't have*
2. They ___ changed the launch date. (possible) → *might have / must have / can't have*
3. He ___ sent the invoice yet. (almost impossible) → *can't have / must have / might have*
4. The designer ___ finished early. (almost sure) → *must have / can't have / will*
5. Structure: modal + ___ + past participle. → *have / had / has*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **must have** · 2. **might have** · 3. **can't have** · 4. **must have** · 5. **have**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige / completa

1. Must have = ___. → *strong certainty past / future plan*
2. Can't have = ___. → *strong impossibility past / permission*
3. Might have = ___. → *possibility past / obligation*
4. She must have ___ the pitch. → *rewritten / rewrite / rewriting*
5. They can't have ___ the merger yet. → *announced / announce / announcing*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **strong certainty past** · 2. **strong impossibility past** · 3. **possibility past** · 4. **rewritten** · 5. **announced**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Corrige

1. *She must missed the deadline.*
2. *They might changed the date.*
3. *He can't have send the invoice.*
4. *She must has finished early.*
5. *They must have change the brand.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. She must **have missed** the deadline.
2. They might **have changed** the date.
3. He can't have **sent** the invoice.
4. She must **have** finished early.
5. They must have **changed** the brand.

</details>

1. deadline → *fecha límite · seedling · mural*
2. launch → *lanzamiento · compost · barrio*
3. invoice → *factura · premiere · heritage*
4. merger → *fusión · greenhouse · shelter*
5. runway → *pasarela · donation · landmark*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **fecha límite** · 2. **lanzamiento** · 3. **factura** · 4. **fusión** · 5. **pasarela**

</details>

faqs.question: ¿Qué estructura uso?
faqs.answer: **must / might / can't + have + past participle** para deducir sobre el **pasado**.

faqs.question: ¿Must have vs can't have?
faqs.answer: **Must have** = casi seguro que sí pasó. **Can't have** = casi imposible que pasara.

faqs.question: ¿Might have?
faqs.answer: Posibilidad, no certeza: They **might have changed** the launch date.

| **might have + pp** | posible | They **might have changed** the launch date. |
| **can't have + pp** | casi imposible | He **can't have sent** the invoice yet. |

## Lección 1 — Gramática

**Objetivo:** relative clauses, reduced relatives, obligation modals, past deduction

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. The festival, ___ is annual, starts soon. → *which / that / who*
2. People ___ the premiere waited outside. → *attending / attended / attend*
3. You ___ save receipts for the audit. → *must / might have / can't*
4. She ___ missed the client call. (deduction) → *must have / must / have to*
5. The compost ___ in the garden is ready. → *produced / producing / produce*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **which** · 2. **attending** · 3. **must** · 4. **must have** · 5. **produced**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige / completa

1. Non-defining → use ___ , not that. → *which/who / that only*
2. Reduced -ing ≈ ___ meaning. → *active / passive*
3. Needn't ≈ ___. → *don't have to / must have*
4. Can't have + pp = ___. → *almost impossible past / obligation*
5. Whose marks ___. → *possession / place / time*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **which/who** · 2. **active** · 3. **don't have to** · 4. **almost impossible past** · 5. **possession**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Corrige

1. *The district, that we visited, is nice.*
2. *People who are attending → reduce*
3. *You must to wear a badge.*
4. *She must missed the deadline.*
5. *Volunteers helped at the show greeted us.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. The district **that** we visited is nice. (defining, no commas)
2. People **attending**…
3. You must **wear** a badge.
4. She must **have missed** the deadline.
5. Volunteers **helping** at the show greeted us.

</details>

## Lección 1 — Gramática

**Objetivo:** passive in all tenses: is/was/is being/has been/had been/will be + V3

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. Ancient monuments ___ every year. (present) → *are visited / visit / is visiting*
2. The castle ___ in the twelfth century. (past) → *was built / built / is built*
3. The site ___ right now. (present continuous) → *is being restored / is restored / restores*
4. The fresco ___ already. (present perfect) → *has been unveiled / unveiled / is unveiling*
5. The artefacts ___ when we arrived. (past perfect) → *had been moved / were moved / move*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **are visited** · 2. **was built** · 3. **is being restored** · 4. **has been unveiled** · 5. **had been moved**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige / completa

1. Future: The ruins ___ by 2030. → *will be excavated / excavate / are excavating*
2. Future perfect: It ___ by next month. → *will have been opened / will open / opened*
3. Past continuous: It ___ when the fire started. → *was being digitised / digitised / is digitised*
4. Passive = ___ + past participle. → *be / have / do*
5. Use *by* when the ___ matters. → *agent / adjective / adverb*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **will be excavated** · 2. **will have been opened** · 3. **was being digitised** · 4. **be** · 5. **agent**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Corrige

1. *The castle built in 1200.* (add be)
2. *The site is restore right now.*
3. *The fresco have been unveiled.*
4. *Monuments is visited every year.*
5. *The artefacts had moved already.* (passive)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. The castle **was built** in 1200.
2. The site **is being restored** right now.
3. The fresco **has been unveiled**.
4. Monuments **are visited** every year.
5. The artefacts **had been moved** already.

</details>

**Objetivo:** producir frases con el foco de la unidad.

title: Passive Voice B2: All Tenses + History & Heritage
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 16 del curso B2: passive en todos los tiempos y vocabulario de history & heritage.
description: Aprende la voz pasiva en todos los tiempos (present, past, perfect, future, continuous) en inglés B2 con vocabulario de history & heritage. Guía Unidad 16 con audios.
alt: Passive all tenses heritage B2

faqs.question: ¿Qué cambia entre los distintos tiempos de la pasiva?
faqs.answer: Solo cambia la forma de **be**: *is / was / is being / has been / had been / will be / will have been* + **past participle** (V3). El participio (*built, restored, unveiled*) permanece siempre igual; lo único que indica el tiempo verbal es el auxiliar **be**, exactamente igual que en la voz activa cambia solo el verbo auxiliar y no el significado central de la acción.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo se forma el present continuous passive y cuándo se usa?
faqs.answer: Con **is/are being + V3**: *The site **is being restored** right now.* Se usa para una acción pasiva que ocurre en este momento o alrededor de ahora, igual que el present continuous activo (*They are restoring the site*), pero con el foco en el objeto (*the site*) en lugar de en quién restaura.

faqs.question: ¿Cuándo debo usar (o no) el complemento con by?
faqs.answer: Usa **by + agente** solo cuando esa información es relevante o nueva para el oyente: *The castle was visited **by** thousands of tourists.* Si el agente es obvio, desconocido o poco importante, se omite: *The castle was built in 1200* (no decimos *by unknown builders*). Añadir *by* de forma automática es uno de los errores más comunes de los hispanohablantes.

faqs.question: ¿Qué es la "reporting passive" (is said to be, is believed to have been)?
faqs.answer: Es una estructura muy típica de textos de historia y patrimonio para transmitir información no confirmada al 100 %: **is said to be / is believed to have been + V3**. Ejemplo: *The manuscript **is believed to have been written** in the fourteenth century.* Equivale a "se cree que fue escrito" y suena mucho más natural que *people believe that it was written*.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 16 del curso B2?
faqs.answer: En la [Unidad 16 del curso B2 de Linguafly](/curso-b2/unit-16) tienes gramática, vocabulario, audios, reading y writing guiados, y en el [cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-16-passive-all-tenses-heritage-ejercicios-soluciones) puedes practicar 75 actividades comentadas sobre esta misma unidad.

content:
Hasta ahora usabas la voz pasiva sobre todo en presente y pasado simples (*The letter is sent* / *The letter was sent*). En la **Unidad 16 del curso B2** (*Passive Voice — All Tenses*) das el salto a un nivel más completo: vas a poder construir la pasiva en **los ocho tiempos verbales principales** —presente, presente continuo, pasado, pasado continuo, present perfect, past perfect, future y future perfect— y a usarla con naturalidad en textos de **historia y patrimonio cultural** (*history & heritage*), uno de los contextos donde la pasiva aparece con más frecuencia en inglés real: guías de museos, documentales, artículos de National Geographic o textos de turismo cultural.

Tras el [Repaso 11–14](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-15-repaso-11-14), esta unidad te da la base perfecta para la siguiente, donde combinarás la pasiva con modales (*must be tested*, *should have been done*). Domina primero **be + past participle** en todos los tiempos y el resto del bloque de pasivas te resultará mucho más sencillo.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 16 — Passive Voice (All Tenses)](/curso-b2/unit-16)  
> **Cuaderno de ejercicios:** [Unidad 16 con soluciones](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-16-passive-all-tenses-heritage-ejercicios-soluciones)  
> **Antes:** [U15 — Repaso 11–14](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-15-repaso-11-14)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 16 (B2)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Formar la voz pasiva en **los ocho tiempos** (present, present continuous, past, past continuous, present perfect, past perfect, future, future perfect).
- Elegir la forma correcta de **be** para cada tiempo, manteniendo el past participle invariable.
- Decidir **cuándo usar (o quitar) by + agente** según su relevancia.
- Reconocer y usar la **reporting passive** (*is said to be*, *is believed to have been*) en textos históricos.
- Hablar de **history & heritage**: ruinas, restauración, manuscritos, patrimonio y tradición.

![Passive all tenses heritage B2](/blog/curso-b2/unit-16/passive-all-tenses.png)

---

## 1. Por qué existe la voz pasiva (y cuándo usarla)

En español usamos mucho las oraciones impersonales o la pasiva refleja (*se construyó el castillo*, *se restauran los frescos*) sin pensarlo demasiado. En inglés, ese mismo matiz se consigue con la **passive voice**: *the castle **was built***, *the frescoes **are being restored***. La regla de fondo es siempre la misma: usamos la pasiva cuando **el objeto de la acción importa más que quien la realiza**, cuando el agente es desconocido, obvio, o cuando simplemente queremos sonar más formal u objetivo, como en un texto académico o en la placa informativa de un museo.

Compara estas dos versiones de la misma idea:

> **Activa:** Workers built the castle in the twelfth century.  
> **Pasiva:** The castle **was built** in the twelfth century.

En la versión activa, el sujeto gramatical es *workers* (que no nos interesa lo más mínimo). En la pasiva, el sujeto pasa a ser *the castle*, que es realmente el protagonista de la frase. Este cambio de foco es la razón número uno por la que los textos de historia, arqueología y patrimonio están llenos de pasivas: hablamos de monumentos, manuscritos y ruinas, no de quién concretamente los construyó, encontró o restauró.

### El truco para no perderte con los tiempos

Todo el bloque de pasivas se reduce a una única fórmula:

```
sujeto + BE (en el tiempo que necesites) + past participle (V3)
```

El **past participle nunca cambia** (*built, restored, unveiled, moved, excavated, opened*…). Lo único que tienes que decidir es **qué tiempo necesitas** y, después, conjugar solo el verbo **be** en ese tiempo. Si controlas bien los tiempos verbales en activa, ya sabes conjugar *be* en pasiva: es exactamente el mismo patrón que ya usas con *be* como verbo normal (*I am*, *I was*, *I have been*, *I will be*…), solo que aquí va seguido de un participio.

---

## 2. Mapa completo de los ocho tiempos

La tabla siguiente resume la fórmula y un ejemplo de cada tiempo. Estúdiala de arriba abajo una vez y, después, ve a los audios de las secciones 3 y 4 para fijar la pronunciación de cada estructura.

| Tiempo | Forma de *be* + V3 | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Present simple** | is / are + V3 | Ancient monuments **are visited** every year. |
| **Present continuous** | is / are being + V3 | The site **is being restored** right now. |
| **Past simple** | was / were + V3 | The castle **was built** in the twelfth century. |
| **Past continuous** | was / were being + V3 | It **was being digitised** when the fire started. |
| **Present perfect** | has / have been + V3 | The fresco **has been unveiled** before the ceremony. |
| **Past perfect** | had been + V3 | The artefacts **had already been moved** when we arrived. |
| **Future simple (will)** | will be + V3 | The ruins **will be excavated** next year. |
| **Future perfect** | will have been + V3 | The gallery **will have been opened** by next spring. |

Fíjate en un detalle importante: en los tiempos continuos (*is being*, *was being*) aparece la palabra **being**, que es el gerundio de *be*. Muchos estudiantes lo olvidan y dicen *the site is restored right now* en lugar de *the site is being restored right now*; la primera versión suena a estado permanente o repetido, no a una acción en curso ahora mismo.

---

## 3. Passive en presente y presente continuo

El **present simple passive** (*is/are + V3*) describe hechos generales, rutinas o verdades que no dependen de un momento concreto: es la pasiva que encontrarás en descripciones de monumentos o normas de un museo.

> Ancient monuments **are visited** by thousands of tourists every year.  
> This exhibition **is updated** twice a year.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-16/present-visited.mp3" title="🔊 Ancient monuments are visited every year"></audio>

El **present continuous passive** (*is/are being + V3*), en cambio, se usa para una acción pasiva **en desarrollo ahora mismo** o durante un periodo temporal cercano al presente. Es muy habitual en guías turísticas para explicar por qué un ala del museo está cerrada: *the historic site is being restored right now, so visitors cannot enter the west wing*.

> The historic site **is being restored** right now.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-16/cont-restored.mp3" title="🔊 The historic site is being restored right now"></audio>

La diferencia entre ambos tiempos es la misma que ya conoces en voz activa: *the museum restores buildings every year* (rutina) frente a *the museum is restoring this building right now* (acción en curso). En pasiva solo añadimos *be* delante del participio y quitamos el sujeto agente.

---

## 4. Passive en pasado y pasado continuo

El **past simple passive** (*was/were + V3*) es probablemente el tiempo pasivo más frecuente en textos de historia, porque narra hechos completados en un momento del pasado: fechas de construcción, descubrimientos, publicaciones.

> The castle **was built** in the twelfth century.  
> The manuscript **was discovered** in an old monastery.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-16/past-built.mp3" title="🔊 The castle was built in the twelfth century"></audio>

El **past continuous passive** (*was/were being + V3*) describe una acción pasiva que estaba en curso cuando ocurrió otra cosa, normalmente introducida con *when*. Es menos frecuente que el resto de tiempos, pero aparece en narraciones más elaboradas: *the collection was being digitised when the fire started* (la colección se estaba digitalizando cuando empezó el incendio). No existe un audio específico para esta estructura, pero sigue exactamente el mismo patrón que *cont-restored.mp3*, cambiando solo *is* por *was*.

> It **was being digitised** when the fire started in the archive.

---

## 5. Passive en present perfect y past perfect

El **present perfect passive** (*has/have been + V3*) conecta una acción pasada con el presente: algo ha ocurrido y sigue teniendo relevancia ahora, sin especificar cuándo exactamente. Es el tiempo perfecto para anuncios y noticias sobre patrimonio: *the fresco has been unveiled*, *the museum has been renovated*.

> The fresco **has been unveiled** ahead of the ceremony.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-16/pp-unveiled.mp3" title="🔊 The fresco has been unveiled ahead of the ceremony"></audio>

El **past perfect passive** (*had been + V3*) se usa para hablar de una acción pasiva anterior a otro momento del pasado, exactamente igual que el past perfect activo. Es habitual en narraciones históricas para marcar el orden de los sucesos: primero ocurrió A, y cuando ocurrió B, A **ya había pasado**.

> The artefacts **had already been moved** when the historians arrived at the site.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-16/past-perf-moved.mp3" title="🔊 The artefacts had already been moved when the historians arrived"></audio>

Observa cómo *already* se coloca entre *had* y *been*: es la posición habitual de los adverbios de frecuencia/tiempo en las formas compuestas de la pasiva (*had already been moved*, *has recently been restored*).

---

## 6. Passive en future y future perfect

El **future simple passive** (*will be + V3*) anuncia una acción pasiva que ocurrirá en el futuro: planes de restauración, excavaciones programadas, aperturas previstas.

> The ruins **will be excavated** next year, once the funding is approved.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-16/future-excavated.mp3" title="🔊 The ruins will be excavated next year"></audio>

El **future perfect passive** (*will have been + V3*) señala que, en un momento futuro concreto, una acción pasiva ya estará completada. Es un tiempo poco frecuente en el habla cotidiana, pero muy útil en planificación de proyectos culturales: *by 2030, the gallery will have been opened to the public for over a decade*.

> The gallery **will have been opened** to the public by next spring.

No existe un audio dedicado a esta última estructura porque es la menos frecuente de las ocho, pero su formación es idéntica a la del future perfect activo (*will have opened*), solo que añadimos *been* antes del participio.

---

## 7. El agente: usar y omitir *by*

Añadir *by + agente* es opcional y depende únicamente de si esa información aporta algo nuevo o importante:

> Ancient monuments **are visited by thousands of tourists** every year. *(el número de visitantes es relevante)*  
> The castle **was built** in the twelfth century. *(no decimos by workers: es irrelevante y obvio)*  
> The exhibition **was opened by the mayor**. *(el agente es una figura importante: sí se menciona)*

Un error típico de los hispanohablantes es traducir literalmente el "por" de la pasiva refleja española y colocar *by* en frases donde en inglés jamás aparecería (*the castle was built by people in 1200*). La regla práctica es: si al quitar el complemento con *by* la frase sigue siendo clara y completa, probablemente no lo necesitas.

---

## 8. La "reporting passive": is said to be / is believed to have been

En textos de historia y patrimonio es muy común hablar de datos que no están confirmados al cien por cien: leyendas, atribuciones, fechas aproximadas. Para eso el inglés usa una estructura muy elegante llamada **reporting passive**, con verbos como *say*, *believe*, *think*, *know* o *report*:

```
sujeto + is/are + said/believed/thought + to be/to have been + (V3)
```

> The sword **is believed to have belonged** to a Viking chief.  
> The manuscript **is said to be** over eight hundred years old.  
> The ruins **are thought to have been built** by an unknown civilisation.

Esta construcción evita la torpeza de *people believe that the sword belonged to a Viking chief* y suena mucho más cercana al inglés real de documentales y artículos de divulgación histórica. Fíjate en el matiz de tiempo: **to be** describe algo que sigue siendo cierto ahora (*is said to be old*), mientras que **to have been** se refiere a una acción o estado pasado (*is believed to have been built*).

---

## 9. Vocabulario: History & Heritage

![Heritage vocabulary](/blog/curso-b2/unit-16/heritage-vocab.png)

| Word | Idea | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **heritage** | patrimonio | Cultural **heritage** must be protected for future generations. |
| **tradition** | tradición | This festival **is** a **tradition** that goes back centuries. |
| **ruins** | ruinas | The **ruins** of the old fortress are open to visitors. |
| **landmark** | monumento / hito | The tower **is** a famous **landmark** in the city. |
| **restore** | restaurar | The mural **was restored** by a team of specialists. |
| **excavate** | excavar | The tomb **was excavated** in the 1920s. |
| **manuscript** | manuscrito | The **manuscript is believed to have been written** by monks. |
| **archive** | archivo | The letters **are kept** in the national **archive**. |
| **artefact** | artefacto | Several **artefacts had been moved** before the flood. |
| **fresco** | fresco (pintura) | The **fresco has been unveiled** after months of restoration. |
| **monument** | monumento | A new **monument will be built** to honour the explorers. |
| **ancient** | antiguo, ancestral | These are some of the most **ancient** ruins in Europe. |
| **preserve** | conservar | The building **is being preserved** as a historic site. |
| **inheritance** | herencia (cultural/legal) | The palace was part of the royal family's **inheritance**. |
| **ancestor** | antepasado | Her **ancestors are said to have founded** this village. |
| **dynasty** | dinastía | The temple **was commissioned** by an ancient **dynasty**. |

Practica combinando cada palabra con una pasiva distinta: *heritage sites are protected*, *the ruins were excavated*, *the manuscript is believed to have been written*…

---

## 10. Reading: Nora at the archive

![Heritage in context](/blog/curso-b2/unit-16/heritage-scene.png)

> Nora works as a historian and spends most of her time visiting archives across the country. Ancient monuments are visited by thousands of tourists every year, but few people know how much work happens behind the scenes. The castle she is studying was built in the twelfth century, and the historic site is being restored right now, so the main gate is temporarily closed to the public. Last month, a beautiful fresco has been unveiled ahead of a special ceremony attended by local officials. When the historians first arrived at the archive, they discovered that several artefacts had already been moved to a safer location because of rising damp. According to local legend, the oldest manuscript in the collection is believed to have been written by monks over eight hundred years ago, although this has never been fully confirmed. Nora hopes that, by next spring, the entire collection will have been catalogued and made available online for researchers around the world.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-16/reading-u16.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Nora at the archive"></audio>

---

## 11. Diálogo: A visit to the heritage site

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-16/dialogue-u16.mp3" title="🔊 Dialogue: a visit to the heritage site"></audio>

> **Tom:** Is this the old castle we talked about?  
> **Nora:** Yes, it is. The castle was built in the twelfth century, believe it or not.  
> **Tom:** Wow. Can we go inside?  
> **Nora:** Not today, unfortunately. The historic site is being restored right now.  
> **Tom:** That's a shame. Is there anything else to see?  
> **Nora:** Actually, yes. A fresco has been unveiled in the small chapel next door.  
> **Tom:** Really? When was it found?  
> **Nora:** It had been hidden under layers of paint for centuries before it was discovered.  
> **Tom:** Incredible. Is it true the manuscripts here are really old?  
> **Nora:** Yes, one of them is believed to have been written by monks.  
> **Tom:** And what happens next with the whole site?  
> **Nora:** The ruins will be excavated further next year, and the museum will have been fully renovated by 2030.

---

## 12. Errores típicos de hispanohablantes

| ❌ Incorrecto | ✅ Correcto | Explicación |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *The castle built in 1200.* | *The castle **was built** in 1200.* | Falta el verbo **be**: sin él no hay pasiva. |
| *The site is restore right now.* | *The site **is being restored** right now.* | Falta **being** en el continuous passive. |
| *The fresco have been unveiled.* | *The fresco **has been unveiled**.* | Tercera persona singular → **has**, no *have*. |
| *Monuments is visited every year.* | *Monuments **are visited** every year. | Sujeto plural → **are**, no *is*. |
| *The artefacts had moved already.* | *The artefacts **had been moved** already.* | Falta **been**: sin él, el verbo suena activo. |
| *The castle was built by people.* | *The castle **was built** in 1200.* | Con agente desconocido u obvio, se omite **by**. |
| *It is said that the sword belonged...* (traducción literal) | *The sword **is said to have belonged**...* | La reporting passive va con el sujeto real, no con *it*. |
| *The ruins will excavated next year.* | *The ruins **will be excavated** next year.* | Falta **be** tras el modal **will**. |
| *The gallery will have opened by 2030* (sin pasiva) | *The gallery **will have been opened** by 2030.* | Falta **been** en el future perfect passive. |

---

## 13. Pronunciación útil

| Forma | Consejo de pronunciación |
| :--- | :--- |
| **is being** | Se enlazan de forma fluida: */ɪz ˈbiːɪŋ/*, casi como una sola palabra. |
| **has been / had been** | La *h* de *has/had* suele debilitarse en habla rápida: *hazbin*, *hadbin*. |
| **will have been** | Tres palabras que se comprimen: */wɪl əv bɪn/*. |
| **-ed final** (*restored, excavated*) | *restored* = /d/ sonora; *excavated* = /ɪd/, sílaba extra. |
| **heritage / archive** | *heritage* = HER-i-tij; *archive* = ar-KAIV, acento en la segunda sílaba. |

Escucha los audios de esta guía y repite en voz alta, prestando especial atención a la conexión entre el auxiliar *be* y el participio: no son dos palabras sueltas, sino una unidad rítmica.

---

## 14. Practica en voz alta

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-16/practice-u16.mp3" title="🔊 Practice: passive all tenses"></audio>

> Ancient monuments are visited every year. The castle was built in the twelfth century. The historic site is being restored right now. The fresco has been unveiled ahead of the ceremony. The artefacts had already been moved when the historians arrived. The ruins will be excavated next year. The manuscript is believed to have been written by monks.

Repite cada frase dos veces: la primera fijándote en el significado, la segunda solo en la conexión entre *be* y el participio.

---

## 15. Plan de práctica (15 minutos)

1. **3 min** — Recita en voz alta los ocho tiempos de la tabla de la sección 2, sustituyendo *build* por otro verbo (*restore, excavate, discover*).  
2. **4 min** — Escucha los audios de las secciones 3 a 6 y repite cada frase.  
3. **4 min** — Escribe 4 frases sobre un monumento real de tu ciudad usando 4 tiempos distintos de la pasiva.  
4. **4 min** — Lee el texto de Nora en voz alta y subraya todas las formas pasivas que encuentres.

### Checklist

- [ ] Formo la pasiva en los ocho tiempos sin dudar sobre la forma de *be*.  
- [ ] Distingo *is restored* (estado/rutina) de *is being restored* (acción en curso).  
- [ ] Sé cuándo añadir y cuándo omitir *by + agente*.  
- [ ] Uso la reporting passive (*is said to be*, *is believed to have been*).  
- [ ] Conozco al menos 12 palabras de vocabulario de *history & heritage*.

---

## 16. Ejercicios prácticos (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — Completa con la forma pasiva correcta

1. Ancient monuments \_\_\_\_ (visit) every year.  
2. The castle \_\_\_\_ (build) in the twelfth century.  
3. The site \_\_\_\_ (restore) right now.  
4. The fresco \_\_\_\_ (unveil) already.  
5. The artefacts \_\_\_\_ (move) when we arrived.  
6. The ruins \_\_\_\_ (excavate) next year.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **are visited**  
2. **was built**  
3. **is being restored**  
4. **has been unveiled**  
5. **had been moved**  
6. **will be excavated**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Elige la opción correcta

1. The manuscript (is / are) believed to have been written by monks.  
2. The gallery will (be / been) opened next spring.  
3. The exhibition (has / have) been updated recently.  
4. The collection was (digitise / being digitised) when the fire started.  
5. By 2030, the museum (will have been / will be) fully renovated.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **is**  
2. **be**  
3. **has**  
4. **being digitised**  
5. **will have been**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Transforma de activa a pasiva

1. Workers built the castle in 1200.  
2. They are restoring the site right now.  
3. Historians had moved the artefacts before the flood.  
4. Monks are believed to have written the manuscript.  
5. The council will excavate the ruins next year.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **The castle was built in 1200.**  
2. **The site is being restored right now.**  
3. **The artefacts had been moved before the flood.**  
4. **The manuscript is believed to have been written by monks.**  
5. **The ruins will be excavated next year.**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Corrige el error

1. *The castle built in 1200.*  
2. *The site is restore right now.*  
3. *The fresco have been unveiled.*  
4. *Monuments is visited every year.*  
5. *The artefacts had moved already.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. The castle **was built** in 1200.  
2. The site **is being restored** right now.  
3. The fresco **has been unveiled**.  
4. Monuments **are visited** every year.  
5. The artefacts **had been moved** already.
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Vocabulario: traduce

1. patrimonio  
2. excavar  
3. artefacto  
4. manuscrito  
5. antepasado  
6. restaurar

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **heritage**  
2. **excavate**  
3. **artefact**  
4. **manuscript**  
5. **ancestor**  
6. **restore**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Comprensión del reading

1. What does Nora do for a living?  
2. When was the castle built?  
3. Why is the main gate closed?  
4. What had happened to the artefacts before the historians arrived?  
5. What is the manuscript believed to have been?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **She is a historian.**  
2. **In the twelfth century.**  
3. **Because the historic site is being restored.**  
4. **They had already been moved to a safer location.**  
5. **Written by monks over eight hundred years ago.**
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Traduce al inglés

1. El castillo fue construido en el siglo XII.  
2. El yacimiento se está restaurando ahora mismo.  
3. Los artefactos ya habían sido trasladados.  
4. Se cree que la espada perteneció a un jefe vikingo.  
5. El museo se habrá renovado por completo para 2030.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **The castle was built in the twelfth century.**  
2. **The site is being restored right now.**  
3. **The artefacts had already been moved.**  
4. **The sword is believed to have belonged to a Viking chief.**  
5. **The museum will have been fully renovated by 2030.**
</details>

### Ejercicio 8 — Escribe tu propio texto

Escribe 6–8 frases sobre un monumento o lugar histórico que conozcas, usando al menos cinco tiempos distintos de la pasiva y dos palabras del vocabulario de heritage.

**Modelo:**

> This cathedral was built over three hundred years ago. It is visited by millions of tourists every year. Part of it is being restored at the moment. A hidden fresco has recently been unveiled inside. According to legend, the bells are said to have been made from melted coins. By next year, the whole facade will have been cleaned.

---

## Tip del profesor

En la pasiva, fija primero **el tiempo** que necesitas y conjuga solo **be** en ese tiempo; el past participle no cambia nunca (*built, restored, unveiled, moved*). Si dudas entre añadir o no *by + agente*, pregúntate: "¿esta información es nueva o relevante?" Si la respuesta es no, quítala.

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tiempo | Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Present | is/are + V3 | are visited |
| Present cont. | is/are being + V3 | is being restored |
| Past | was/were + V3 | was built |
| Past cont. | was/were being + V3 | was being digitised |
| Present perfect | has/have been + V3 | has been unveiled |
| Past perfect | had been + V3 | had been moved |
| Future | will be + V3 | will be excavated |
| Future perfect | will have been + V3 | will have been opened |
| Reporting | is said/believed to (have) be(en) + V3 | is believed to have been written |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso B2

content:
Este artículo reúne **los ejercicios de la Unidad 17 del curso B2** (*Modal Passive & Have Something Done + Adventure*) con **soluciones comentadas**.

> **Guía teórica:** [Modal passive & Adventure B2](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-17-modal-passive-adventure)  
> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 17 — Modal passive & Adventure](/curso-b2/unit-17)

Haz cada bloque **sin mirar** la solución. Luego comprueba y lee la explicación.

![Modal passive & Adventure](/blog/curso-b2/unit-17/modal-passive-have-done.png)

**Contenido de la unidad:**
1. [Lección 1 — Gramática](#leccion-1--gramatica)
2. [Lección 2 — Vocabulario](#leccion-2--vocabulario)
3. [Lección 3 — Reading: Leo before the climb](#leccion-3--reading)
4. [Lección 4 — Listening: Leo on gear safety](#leccion-4--listening)
5. [Lección 5 — Writing](#leccion-5--writing)

---

## Lección 1 — Gramática

**Objetivo:** must/should be + V3; should have been + V3; have/get + object + V3

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. Gear ___ before the climb. (obligation) → *must be tested / must test / must testing*
2. The report ___ earlier. (past criticism) → *should have been published / should publish / should be publish*
3. I ___ my parachute ___ next week. → *am having / serviced · have / service · am having / service*
4. She ___ her wetsuit ___ yesterday. → *had / repaired · has / repair · had / repair*
5. Harnesses ___ before each climb. → *must be inspected / must inspect / must inspecting*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **must be tested** · 2. **should have been published** · 3. **am having / serviced** · 4. **had / repaired** · 5. **must be inspected**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige / completa

1. Modal passive = modal + ___ + V3. → *be / have / to*
2. Should have been + V3 = criticism about the ___. → *past / future / weather*
3. Have something done = someone does it ___ you. → *for / against / without*
4. He ___ his ropes checked every six months. → *has / have / having*
5. They ___ their kayak repaired at the moment. → *are having / have / had*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **be** · 2. **past** · 3. **for** · 4. **has** · 5. **are having**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Corrige

1. *Gear must tested before the climb.*
2. *The report should have published earlier.*
3. *I am having my parachute service.*
4. *She had repaired her wetsuit.* (causative)
5. *Harnesses must inspect before climbs.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. Gear **must be tested** before the climb.
2. The report **should have been published** earlier.
3. I am having my parachute **serviced**.
4. She **had** her wetsuit **repaired**.
5. Harnesses **must be inspected** before climbs.

</details>

---

## Lección 2 — Vocabulario

**Objetivo:** adventure & extreme sports

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Empareja / elige

1. harness → *arnés · fresco · paperback*
2. parachute → *paracaídas · mural · dough*
3. wetsuit → *traje de neopreno · archive · plot*
4. expedition → *expedición · recipe · edition*
5. rope → *cuerda · soufflé · critique*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **arnés** · 2. **paracaídas** · 3. **traje de neopreno** · 4. **expedición** · 5. **cuerda**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Completa

1. gear ≈ ___ → *equipo / harina / novela*
2. base camp ≈ ___ → *campamento base / archivo / reseña*

faqs.question: ¿Qué es exactamente el modal passive y cómo se forma?
faqs.answer: Es la combinación de un **modal verb** (*must, should, can, might, have to*) con la voz pasiva: **modal + be + past participle**. Ejemplo: *Gear **must be tested** before every climb.* Funciona igual que un modal normal (*must test*), solo que ahora el foco está en el objeto (*gear*) y no en quién realiza la acción.

faqs.question: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre must be + V3 y should have been + V3?
faqs.answer: **must be + V3** expresa una obligación u obligación lógica en el presente o futuro: *The rope must be checked before use.* **should have been + V3** es una crítica sobre algo que **no ocurrió en el pasado** y debería haber ocurrido: *The rope should have been checked, but nobody did it.* Es una de las estructuras más útiles del B2 para hablar de errores y responsabilidades pasadas.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo funciona have something done y en qué se diferencia de have done algo?
faqs.answer: **Have/get + objeto + past participle** indica que **otra persona** realiza la acción por ti, normalmente porque la pagas o la encargas: *I **had** my parachute **serviced**.* (alguien lo revisó por mí). Es distinto de *I have serviced my parachute*, donde tú mismo has hecho el trabajo. El orden es siempre have + objeto + participio, nunca have + participio + objeto.

faqs.question: ¿Puedo usar get en lugar de have en esta estructura?
faqs.answer: Sí, **get + objeto + V3** es una alternativa más informal y muy habitual en inglés hablado: *I got my harness checked yesterday.* Significa exactamente lo mismo que *I had my harness checked*, pero suena algo menos formal, ideal para conversación cotidiana entre amigos o compañeros de expedición.
