## Lección 3 — Reading: Eva's module review

**Objetivo:** comprender un texto con el foco de la unidad.

### Texto y audio

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-20/reading-workbook.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Eva's module review"></audio>

> Eva is reviewing Units 16 to 19. The historic site is being restored this month. Climbing gear must be tested and she is having her ropes checked. It was such a great cooking class that she signed up again. The more she reads, the better she writes. By far the best tip she heard was to practise every structure in short paragraphs. Module 2 is almost complete.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. Who is reviewing U16–19? → *Eva / Sam / Leo*
2. Site is being ___ → *restored / cooked*
3. Gear must be ___ → *tested / written*
4. Having ropes ___ → *checked / check*
5. Such a great ___ class → *cooking / climbing only*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Eva** · 2. **restored** · 3. **tested** · 4. **checked** · 5. **cooking**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. The more she reads, the better she ___ → *writes / climbs*
7. By far the best ___ → *tip / soup*
8. Module 2 almost ___ → *complete / started*
9. Mix of four grammar blocks? → *True / False*
10. Units sixteen to nineteen? → *True / False*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **writes** · 7. **tip** · 8. **complete** · 9. **True** · 10. **True**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. List 4 structures from text.
12. Write a 4-line mix.
13. Key idea? → *yes / none*
14. Feeling? → *ready / lost*
15. Course → */curso-b2/unit-20*

faqs.question: ¿Qué gramática repasa exactamente la Unidad 20?
faqs.answer: Cuatro bloques completos del módulo 2 de B2: la **voz pasiva en los ocho tiempos** (U16), el **modal passive** y **have something done** (U17), los contrastes **so / such / too / enough** (U18) y los **comparativos avanzados** con *the...the...*, *much/far/slightly* y *by far* (U19). Es un repaso integrador, no una unidad con gramática nueva.

faqs.question: ¿En qué orden debería estudiar este repaso?
faqs.answer: Lo más eficaz es repasar primero las tablas resumen de cada unidad original (enlazadas en esta guía), identificar en qué estructura fallas más, y después trabajar los ejemplos mezclados y los ejercicios de esta Unidad 20, donde las cuatro estructuras aparecen combinadas en el mismo texto, como ocurre en un examen real.

faqs.question: ¿Por qué es importante mezclar estas cuatro estructuras en los mismos ejercicios?
faqs.answer: Porque en un texto o conversación real nunca aparece una sola estructura aislada: un mismo párrafo puede combinar pasiva (*the site is being restored*), modal passive (*gear must be tested*), *so/such* (*such a great class*) y comparativos avanzados (*the more you read...*) en pocas frases. Practicar la identificación rápida de cada estructura es tan importante como saber formarla.

faqs.question: ¿Qué pasa si todavía fallo en alguna de las cuatro áreas?
faqs.answer: Vuelve a la guía teórica correspondiente (enlazada en la sección "Mapa del repaso") y repite sus ejercicios antes de continuar. No pasa nada por repetir una unidad: el objetivo del repaso es justo detectar huecos antes de avanzar al siguiente módulo, donde estas estructuras se dan por asumidas.

faqs.question: ¿Qué viene después de este repaso en el curso B2?
faqs.answer: Tras la Unidad 20, el curso continúa con un nuevo módulo centrado en **linkers avanzados y phrasal verbs** (Unidad 21), así que aprovecha este repaso para consolidar bien la pasiva, los modales y los comparativos antes de seguir avanzando.

content:
Has completado cuatro unidades muy densas: la **pasiva en todos los tiempos** ([U16](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-16-passive-all-tenses-heritage)), el **modal passive y have something done** ([U17](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-17-modal-passive-adventure)), **so / such / too / enough** ([U18](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-18-so-such-too-enough-food)) y los **comparativos avanzados** ([U19](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-19-advanced-comparatives-literature)). La **Unidad 20** no introduce gramática nueva: su función es **integrar** estas cuatro estructuras en los mismos textos y ejercicios, tal y como aparecerán mezcladas en cualquier conversación, lectura o examen de nivel B2.

Este tipo de repaso "mezclado" es mucho más exigente que estudiar cada estructura por separado, porque tu cerebro tiene que **identificar primero qué estructura necesita cada frase** antes de poder formarla correctamente. Es exactamente la habilidad que se evalúa en exámenes como el First Certificate (FCE) de Cambridge.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 20 — Repaso 16–19](/curso-b2/unit-20)  
> **Cuaderno de ejercicios:** [Unidad 20 con soluciones](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-20-repaso-16-19-ejercicios-soluciones)  
> **Antes:** [U19 — Advanced comparatives](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-19-advanced-comparatives-literature)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 20 (B2)

Al terminar este repaso serás capaz de:

- Reconocer y usar la **pasiva en los ocho tiempos** sin dudar sobre la forma de *be*.
- Combinar **modales con pasiva** (*must be tested*) y la causativa **have something done**.
- Elegir correctamente entre **so, such, too y enough** según el contexto.
- Usar con soltura **the...the...**, los intensificadores de comparativos y **by far**.
- Repasar el vocabulario de **heritage, adventure, cooking y literature** de forma integrada.

![Repaso B2 unidades 16 a 19](/blog/curso-b2/unit-20/review-map.png)

---

## 1. Mapa del repaso

![Review map](/blog/curso-b2/unit-20/review-map.png)

| Unidad | Gramática | Vocabulario | Guía teórica |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **16** | Passive voice (all tenses) | history & heritage | [Ver guía](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-16-passive-all-tenses-heritage) |
| **17** | Modal passive + have something done | adventure & extreme sports | [Ver guía](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-17-modal-passive-adventure) |
| **18** | So / such / too / enough | cooking & recipes | [Ver guía](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-18-so-such-too-enough-food) |
| **19** | Advanced comparatives | literature & books | [Ver guía](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-19-advanced-comparatives-literature) |

Antes de seguir, repasa mentalmente la fórmula de cada bloque: **be + V3** (pasiva), **modal + be + V3** / **have + objeto + V3** (U17), **so/such/too/enough** según el tipo de palabra que modifican (U18), y **the + comp., the + comp.** / **much, far, slightly** / **by far** (U19).

---

## 2. Repaso: Passive voice en todos los tiempos (U16)

Recuerda que la pasiva se forma siempre con **be (en el tiempo que necesites) + past participle**, y que el participio nunca cambia:

> The historic site **is being restored** this month.  
> The castle **was built** in the twelfth century.  
> The fresco **has been unveiled** ahead of the ceremony.  
> The ruins **will be excavated** next year.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-20/review-passive.mp3" title="🔊 Review: passive voice"></audio>

Si dudas entre dos tiempos, pregúntate primero **cuándo** ocurre la acción (ahora, en el pasado, en curso, ya terminada, en el futuro) y después elige solo la forma de *be* correspondiente.

---

## 3. Repaso: Modal passive y have something done (U17)

El modal passive combina un modal con *be + V3* para hablar de obligaciones y recomendaciones; *should have been + V3* critica algo que no ocurrió; y *have/get + objeto + V3* indica que otra persona hace la acción por ti:

> All climbing gear **must be tested** before the expedition.  
> The safety report **should have been published** earlier.  
> She **is having** her ropes **checked** this week.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-20/review-modal.mp3" title="🔊 Review: modal passive"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-20/review-have-done.mp3" title="🔊 Review: have something done"></audio>

Recuerda el orden fijo de la causativa: **have/get + objeto + participio**, nunca al revés (*have checked her ropes* significaría que ella misma las revisó).

---

## 4. Repaso: So / such / too / enough (U18)

La pregunta clave sigue siendo la misma: ¿la palabra siguiente es un **adjetivo/adverbio** (→ *so*, *too*, o *enough* después) o un **sustantivo** (→ *such*, o *enough* antes)?

> It was **such a** great cooking class that she signed up again.  
> The soup was **too** hot **to** eat immediately.  
> We don't have **enough** time to finish the recipe.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-20/review-so-such.mp3" title="🔊 Review: so, such, too, enough"></audio>

Recuerda también que *too* siempre implica un problema o exceso negativo, mientras que *enough* puede usarse tanto en frases afirmativas como negativas para hablar de cantidad suficiente.

---

## 5. Repaso: Advanced comparatives (U19)

La estructura **the...the...** conecta dos cambios paralelos; los intensificadores **much/far/a lot** (fuerte) y **slightly/a bit** (leve) matizan un comparativo; y **by far** refuerza un superlativo:

> **The more** she reads, **the better** she writes.  
> This edition is **much more** expensive than the paperback.  
> By far, the best tip she heard was to practise every structure in short paragraphs.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-20/review-comparative.mp3" title="🔊 Review: advanced comparatives"></audio>

Recuerda: ambos lados de *the...the...* llevan comparativo (nunca superlativo), y *by far* jamás acompaña a un comparativo suelto.

---

## 6. Vocabulario mezclado: heritage, adventure, cooking, literature

![Review examples](/blog/curso-b2/unit-20/review-examples.png)

| Categoría | Palabras clave | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Heritage** (U16) | heritage, ruins, restore, manuscript | The **manuscript** is believed to have been written by monks. |
| **Adventure** (U17) | harness, parachute, expedition, gear | All the **gear** must be tested before the expedition. |
| **Cooking** (U18) | recipe, ingredient, simmer, garnish | Let the sauce **simmer** for ten more minutes. |
| **Literature** (U19) | novel, sequel, paperback, review | The **sequel** is getting more and more popular. |

Combina cada categoría con el foco gramatical de su unidad: pasiva con heritage, modal passive con adventure, so/such con cooking, comparativos avanzados con literature. Este cruce es exactamente lo que vas a leer en el texto de la siguiente sección.

---

## 6b. Pronunciación: repaso rápido de las cuatro unidades

| Forma | Unidad | Consejo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **is being + V3** | U16 | Se enlaza fluido: */ɪz ˈbiːɪŋ/*. |
| **must be / should have been** | U17 | *should have been* suena */ˈʃʊdəv bɪn/* en habla rápida. |
| **such a / enough** | U18 | *enough* = */ɪˈnʌf/*, con la *gh* sonando como **f**. |
| **the more... the better** | U19 | Ritmo marcado: *the-MORE-you-READ, the-BET-ter-you-WRITE*. |

Practicar la pronunciación de las cuatro estructuras juntas, una detrás de otra, es un excelente ejercicio de fluidez antes de un examen oral: te obliga a cambiar de patrón rítmico constantemente, igual que en una conversación real.

---

## 7. Reading: Eva's module review

> Eva has spent the whole week reviewing Units 16 to 19 before her B2 exam. The historic site near her house is being restored this month, and she used that example to remember the present continuous passive. For Unit 17, she remembered that all climbing gear must be tested before an expedition, and that her cousin is having his ropes checked at the moment because he loves extreme sports. Cooking gave her the best examples for Unit 18: it was such a great cooking class last weekend that she signed up again, even though the soup was too hot to eat at first. Finally, for the comparatives in Unit 19, Eva kept repeating her favourite sentence: the more she reads, the better she writes. By far, the best tip she has learned this month was to practise every structure in short paragraphs instead of studying long grammar tables alone. As she closed her notebook, she realised that Module 2 was almost complete, and that mixing all four structures together had helped her remember them far better than studying them separately.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-20/reading-mix.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Eva's module review"></audio>

---

## 8. Diálogo: Comparing notes before the exam

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-20/dialogue-mix.mp3" title="🔊 Dialogue: comparing notes before the exam"></audio>

> **Eva:** Are you ready for the exam on Units 16 to 19?  
> **Leo:** Almost. The passive still confuses me sometimes.  
> **Eva:** Just remember: be in the right tense, plus the past participle. Look — the site is being restored right now.  
> **Leo:** Right, that helps. What about modal passive?  
> **Eva:** Easy — gear must be tested before every climb.  
> **Leo:** And have something done?  
> **Eva:** My cousin is having his ropes checked this week — someone else does it for him.  
> **Leo:** Got it. What about so and such?  
> **Eva:** It was such a great cooking class that I signed up again.  
> **Leo:** And the comparatives?  
> **Eva:** The more you practise, the better you get. By far the best tip is to mix everything together.  
> **Leo:** Thanks, Eva. I think I'm finally ready for this exam.

---

## 9. Errores típicos: repaso mezclado

| ❌ Incorrecto | ✅ Correcto | Unidad |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *The site is restored right now* (para acción en curso) | *The site **is being restored** right now.* | U16 |
| *Gear must tested before the climb.* | *Gear **must be tested** before the climb.* | U17 |
| *I have checked my ropes* (queriendo decir causativa) | *I **have** my ropes **checked**.* | U17 |
| *It was so a great class.* | *It was **such a** great class.* | U18 |
| *We have time enough.* | *We have **enough time**.* | U18 |
| *The more you read, the best you write.* | *The more you read, **the better** you write.* | U19 |
| *This edition is very more expensive.* | *This edition is **much** more expensive.* | U19 |
| *This is by far better novel.* | *This is **by far the best** novel.* | U19 |

---

## 10. Practica en voz alta

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-20/practice-mix.mp3" title="🔊 Practice: mixed review U16-19"></audio>

> The historic site is being restored. All climbing gear must be tested. I am having my parachute serviced. It was such a great cooking class that we signed up again. The more you read, the better you write. This is by far the best novel I've ever read.

### Mini-repaso relámpago

> Pasiva → be + V3.  
> Modal passive → modal + be + V3.  
> Have something done → have + objeto + V3.  
> So / such → adjetivo o sustantivo.  
> Too / enough → exceso o suficiencia.  
> The...the... → dos comparativos en paralelo.  
> By far → refuerza el superlativo.

### Frases extra para practicar en voz alta

> Ancient monuments are visited every year, but this one is being restored right now.  
> All the gear must be tested, and I am having my own equipment checked today.  
> It was such a delicious meal that we didn't have enough time to try dessert.  
> The more you practise these four structures, the more natural they become.  
> This is, by far, the most useful unit I've studied so far this year.

Léelas dos veces en voz alta: la primera fijándote en el significado completo, la segunda solo en identificar qué unidad (16, 17, 18 o 19) corresponde a cada parte de la frase.

---

## 11. Plan de práctica (15 minutos)

1. **4 min** — Repasa las cuatro tablas resumen (secciones 2 a 5) en voz alta, una tras otra.  
2. **4 min** — Lee el texto de Eva (sección 7) y subraya con cuatro colores distintos cada una de las cuatro estructuras.  
3. **4 min** — Escribe un mini-párrafo de 5 frases combinando al menos tres de las cuatro estructuras.  
4. **3 min** — Practica el diálogo de la sección 8 cambiando de rol con otra persona.

### Checklist final del módulo

- [ ] Formo la pasiva en los ocho tiempos sin dudar sobre la forma de *be*.  
- [ ] Combino modales con pasiva y uso *have something done* en el orden correcto.  
- [ ] Elijo bien entre *so, such, too* y *enough*.  
- [ ] Construyo *the...the...* y uso *by far* solo con superlativos.  
- [ ] Reconozco las cuatro estructuras mezcladas en un mismo texto.

---

### Ejercicio 6 — Vocabulario mezclado: traduce

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Comprensión del reading (Eva)

1. What is Eva reviewing this week?  
2. What example did she use for the present continuous passive?  
3. What is her cousin having done at the moment?  
4. What was Eva's favourite comparative sentence?  
5. What did Eva realise about mixing the four structures together?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Units 16 to 19, before her B2 exam.**  
2. **The historic site near her house is being restored.**  
3. **He is having his ropes checked.**  
4. **The more she reads, the better she writes.**

</details>

### Ejercicio 8 — Traduce al inglés (mezclado)

1. El yacimiento se está restaurando ahora mismo.  
2. El equipo debe ser probado antes de la expedición.  
3. Fue una clase de cocina tan buena que nos apuntamos otra vez.  
4. Cuanto más lees, mejor escribes.  
5. Esta es, con diferencia, la mejor novela.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **The site is being restored right now.**  
2. **The gear must be tested before the expedition.**  
3. **It was such a great cooking class that we signed up again.**  
4. **The more you read, the better you write.**  
5. **This is by far the best novel.**
</details>

### Ejercicio 9 — Escribe tu propio texto integrador

Escribe un párrafo de 8–10 frases combinando al menos una estructura de cada unidad (passive, modal passive/have something done, so/such/too/enough, advanced comparatives).

**Modelo:**

> The museum near my house is being renovated this year. All the old paintings must be checked by a specialist before they go back on display, and the curator is having several frescoes restored professionally. It was such an interesting exhibition that I visited it twice. The more I learn about art history, the more I appreciate these old buildings. This is, by far, the most impressive museum in my city.

---

## Tip del profesor

En un repaso mezclado, identifica primero **el bloque** al que pertenece cada frase (pasiva / modal / so-such / comparativo) antes de intentar formarla. Esa identificación rápida es la habilidad clave que separa un B2 sólido de uno que solo memoriza estructuras sueltas.

---

## Resumen rápido

| Unidad | Fórmula clave | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| U16 | be + V3 (8 tiempos) | is being restored |
| U17 | modal + be + V3 / have + obj. + V3 | must be tested / had it repaired |
| U18 | so/such + adj/noun · too...to · enough | such a great class |
| U19 | the + comp., the + comp. · by far + superl. | the more, the better · by far the best |

Este artículo reúne **los ejercicios de la Unidad 3 del curso B2** (*Gerund vs Infinitive (1) + Education*) con **soluciones comentadas**.

> **Guía teórica:** [Gerund vs Infinitive B2](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-3-gerund-infinitive-education)  
> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 3 — Gerund vs Infinitive](/curso-b2/unit-3)

Haz cada bloque **sin mirar** la solución. Luego comprueba y lee la explicación.

![Gerund vs Infinitive](/blog/curso-b2/unit-3/gerund-infinitive.png)

**Contenido de la unidad:**
1. [Lección 1 — Gramática](#leccion-1--gramatica)
2. [Lección 2 — Vocabulario](#leccion-2--vocabulario)
3. [Lección 3 — Reading: Sofia at university](#leccion-3--reading)
4. [Lección 4 — Listening: Sofia on study habits](#leccion-4--listening)
5. [Lección 5 — Writing](#leccion-5--writing)

---

## Lección 1 — Gramática

**Objetivo:** enjoy / mind / avoid + gerund; decide / agree + infinitive; stop + -ing / to

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. I enjoy ___ lectures on Fridays. → *attend / attending / to attend*
2. She decided ___ for the scholarship. → *apply / applying / to apply*
3. Would you mind ___ the door? → *open / opening / to open*
4. He avoids ___ classes when possible. → *skip / skipping / to skip*
5. They agreed ___ the research project. → *join / joining / to join*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **attending** · 2. **to apply** · 3. **opening** · 4. **skipping** · 5. **to join**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige / completa

1. She stopped ___ TV and started revising. → *watch / watching / to watch*
2. He stopped ___ a break after three hours. → *take / taking / to take*
3. I aim ___ my degree by 2027. → *finish / finishing / to finish*
4. Do you mind ___ me your notes? → *lend / lending / to lend*
5. He regrets not ___ harder. → *study / studying / to study*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **watching** · 2. **to take** · 3. **to finish** · 4. **lending** · 5. **studying**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Corrige

1. *I enjoy to read academic papers.*
2. *She decided applying for the grant.*
3. *Would you mind to wait?*
4. *He stopped to smoke.* (= dejó de fumar)
5. *They agreed joining the team.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I enjoy **reading** academic papers.
2. She decided **to apply** for the grant.
3. Would you mind **waiting**?
4. He stopped **smoking**.
5. They agreed **to join** the team.

</details>

---

## Lección 2 — Vocabulario

**Objetivo:** education

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Empareja / elige

1. lecture → *clase magistral · maleta · billete*
2. scholarship → *beca · ascenso · nómina*
3. deadline → *fecha límite · embarque · pasaporte*
4. major in → *especializarse en · cancelar · posponer*
5. procrastinate → *procrastinar · despegar · reservar*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **clase magistral** · 2. **beca** · 3. **fecha límite** · 4. **especializarse en** · 5. **procrastinar**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Completa

1. enrol ≈ ___ → *matricularse / graduarse / suspender*
2. seminar ≈ ___ → *seminario / aeropuerto / equipaje*
3. tuition ≈ ___ → *matrícula (universidad) / billete / maleta*
4. assignment ≈ ___ → *tarea / vuelo / pasaporte*
5. revise ≈ ___ → *repasar / posponer / cancelar*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **matricularse** · 2. **seminario** · 3. **matrícula (universidad)** · 4. **tarea** · 5. **repasar**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — En contexto

11. Usa 3 palabras nuevas en frases con el foco gramatical.
12. Di en voz alta el vocabulario de la unidad.
13. Empareja cada palabra con un ejemplo personal.

15. Continúa en la [Unidad 3 del curso](/curso-b2/unit-3).

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11–13. Open answers — check meaning in theory. · 14. Theory vocab section. · 15. **/curso-b2/unit-3**

</details>

## Lección 3 — Reading: Sofia at university

**Objetivo:** comprender un texto con el foco de la unidad.

### Texto y audio

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-3/reading-workbook.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Sofia at university"></audio>

> University life requires balance. Sofia enjoys attending seminars but avoids missing deadlines. She decided to major in biology and agreed to mentor first-year students. She stopped checking her phone during lectures and started taking detailed notes. Her tutor advised her to read more academic journals. Would you mind sharing your notes after class?

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. Sofia enjoys ___ → *attending / to attend / attend*
2. Avoids missing ___ → *deadlines / flights / relatives*
3. Decided to ___ → *major / majoring / majored*
4. Stopped checking phone and started ___ → *taking / take / to take*
5. Tutor advised her to ___ → *read / reading / reads*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **attending seminars** · 2. **deadlines** · 3. **major in biology** · 4. **taking notes** · 5. **read journals**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. Mind + ___ structure? → *gerund / infinitive / past*
7. Agreed to ___ → *mentor / mentoring / mentored*
8. Stop + -ing vs stop + to? → *both in text*
9. Already graduated? → *False / True*
10. Underline enjoy / avoid / decide.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **gerund** · 7. **mentor students** · 8. **stopped checking (dejar) / started taking** · 9. **False** · 10. **See text**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. Write enjoy + gerund sentence.
12. Education vocab? → *yes / none*
13. Main topic? → *study habits / travel / family*
14. Would you mind + ? → *gerund / infinitive / past*
15. Course link → */curso-b2/unit-3*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **Model OK** · 12. **seminars, deadlines, major** · 13. **study habits** · 14. **gerund** · 15. **/curso-b2/unit-3**

</details>

---

## Lección 4 — Listening: Sofia on study habits

**Objetivo:** escuchar el foco gramatical en contexto.

### Audio y guion

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-3/listening-workbook.mp3" title="🔊 Listening: Sofia on study habits"></audio>

> Hi, I am Sofia. I enjoy attending lectures, but I avoid skipping classes. I decided to apply for a scholarship and agreed to help with the research project. Would you mind opening the window? I stopped procrastinating and started revising every evening.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. Who speaks? → *Sofia / Clara / Olivia*
2. Enjoys ___ lectures → *attending / to attend*
3. Avoids ___ classes → *skipping / attending*
4. Decided to apply for ___ → *scholarship / visa / ticket*
5. Mind + ___ the window? → *opening / open / to open*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Sofia** · 2. **attending** · 3. **skipping** · 4. **scholarship** · 5. **opening**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. Stopped procrastinating and started ___ → *revising / flying / camping*
7. Agreed to help with ___ → *research / travel / cooking*
8. Gerund after enjoy? → *yes / no*
9. Already got scholarship? → *unknown / yes / no*
10. Write enjoy + gerund.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **revising** · 7. **research project** · 8. **yes** · 9. **Not stated** · 10. **Model OK**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. Write decide + to inf.
12. Shadow audio.
13. Education vocab? → *yes / none*
14. Stop + -ing example?
15. Open Ver solución. → *yes*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **Model OK** · 12. **done** · 13. **lectures, scholarship, revising** · 14. **stopped procrastinating** · 15. **yes**

</details>

---

## Lección 5 — Writing

**Objetivo:** producir frases con el foco de la unidad.

1. Escribe 3 frases: enjoy, decide, avoid + forma correcta.
2. Completa: I enjoy ___ (read) academic articles.
3. Completa: She decided ___ (apply) for the grant.
4. Completa: Would you mind ___ (wait) a moment?
5. Completa: He stopped ___ (procrastinate) and started revising.
6. Stop + to vs stop + -ing — explica con un ejemplo.
7. Completa: They agreed ___ (help) with the project.
8. Corrige: *I enjoy to attend lectures.*
9. Corrige: *She stopped to smoke.* (= dejó de fumar)
10. Párrafo sobre hábitos de estudio.
11. Traduce: Evito perder clases.
12. Traduce: ¿Te importaría abrir la ventana?
13. Escribe *regret + gerund*.
14. Escribe *aim to + inf*.
15. Autochequeo: gerund vs infinitive.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. Model using enjoy/decide/avoid correctly.
2. **reading**
3. **to apply**
4. **waiting**
5. stopped **procrastinating**
6. Stop **smoking** = dejar; stop **to rest** = parar con propósito.
7. **to help**
8. I enjoy **attending** lectures.
9. He stopped **smoking**.
10. Open study habits paragraph.
11. I avoid **missing** classes.
12. Would you mind **opening** the window?
13. I regret not **studying** harder.
14. I aim **to finish** my degree by 2027.
15. Self-check.

</details>

faqs.question: ¿Enjoy + gerund o infinitivo?
faqs.answer: **Enjoy + gerund**: I enjoy **attending** lectures.

faqs.question: ¿Stop + -ing vs stop + to?
faqs.answer: **Stop + -ing** = dejar de hacer. **Stop + to** = parar con un propósito.

faqs.question: ¿Mind + gerund?
faqs.answer: Sí: Would you **mind opening** the door?

content:
Tras la [Unidad 2](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-2-future-tenses-work), la **Unidad 3** trabaja **gerund vs infinitive (1)** con vocabulario de **education**.

> **Antes:** [U2 — Future tenses & work](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-2-future-tenses-work)

---

## Qué aprenderás

- Verbos + **gerund** (enjoy, mind, avoid, stop)
- Verbos + **infinitive** (decide, agree, aim)
- Contraste **stop + -ing / stop + to**
- Vocabulario: education

![Gerund vs infinitive B2 education](/blog/curso-b2/unit-3/gerund-infinitive.png)

---

## 1. Gerund vs infinitive

| Patrón | Verbos | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **+ gerund** | enjoy, mind, avoid, stop (cease) | I **enjoy attending** lectures. |
| **+ infinitive** | decide, agree, aim, intend | She **decided to apply**. |
| **stop + -ing** | cesar | They **stopped procrastinating**. |
| **stop + to** | propósito | He stopped **to rest**. |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-3/enjoy-gerund.mp3" title="🔊 enjoy gerund"></audio>

## 2. Más ejemplos

## 3. Vocabulario: Education

![Education](/blog/curso-b2/unit-3/education-vocab.png)

| Word | Idea |
| :--- | :--- |
| degree / scholarship | título / beca |
| assignment / deadline | tarea / fecha límite |
| lecture / seminar | conferencia / seminario |

---

## 4. Reading

![At university](/blog/curso-b2/unit-3/education-scene.png)

> I enjoy attending lectures. She decided to apply for a scholarship. They stopped procrastinating. Would you mind opening the seminar room?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-3/reading-u3.mp3" title="🔊 Reading"></audio>

---

## 5. Diálogo

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-3/dialogue-u3.mp3" title="🔊 Dialogue"></audio>

> Do you enjoy studying? — I enjoy attending lectures.

## 6. Practica

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-3/practice-u3.mp3" title="🔊 Practice"></audio>

## 7. Ejercicios

1. I enjoy ___ (attend) lectures.  
2. She decided ___ (apply) for a scholarship.  
3. They stopped ___ (procrastinate).  
4. Would you mind ___ (open) the door?

<details><summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **attending** · 2. **to apply** · 3. **procrastinating** · 4. **opening** · 5. **scholarship**
</details>

## Tip del profesor

Aprende los verbos en bloques: *enjoy/mind/avoid + **-ing*** vs *decide/agree/aim + **to***.

## Lección 1 — Gramática

**Objetivo:** convince / ask / tell / want + object + to + infinitive

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. She convinced me ___ join the club. → *to / for / -*
2. He asked her ___ wait outside. → *to / for / -*
3. They told us ___ be quiet. → *to / for / -*
4. I want my brother ___ take up cycling. → *to / for / -*
5. The coach advised him ___ rest. → *to / for / -*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **to** · 2. **to** · 3. **to** · 4. **to** · 5. **to**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige / completa

1. My parents allowed me ___ camp overnight. → *to / for / -*
2. She persuaded him ___ try rock climbing. → *to / for / -*
3. Would you like me ___ help you? → *to / for / -*
4. The guide told the group ___ follow the path. → *to / for / -*
5. He wants his friends ___ join the trip. → *to / for / -*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **to** · 2. **to** · 3. **to** · 4. **to** · 5. **to**

</details>

1. *She convinced me join the team.*
2. *He asked her for wait.*
3. *They told us to don't shout.*
4. *I want that my sister takes photos.*
5. *She allowed me camp there.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. She convinced me **to join** the team.
2. He asked her **to wait**.
3. They told us **not to shout**.
4. I want my sister **to take** photos.
5. She allowed me **to camp** there.

</details>

2. Asked him to ___ equipment → *book / booking / booked*

5. Parents allowed them to ___ → *travel alone / stay home / skip class*

1. **rock climbing** · 2. **book** · 3. **arrive** · 4. **photography** · 5. **travel alone**

</details>

9. Structure tell + obj + to? → *yes / no*
10. Already joined photography? → *False / True / not stated*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **to + infinitive** · 7. **join cycling club** · 8. **climbing, camping, cycling** · 9. **yes in text** · 10. **Not stated / implied wanting**

12. Write ask + obj + to.

## Lección 5 — Writing

**Objetivo:** producir frases con el foco de la unidad.

1. Escribe 4 frases: convince, ask, tell, want + obj + to.
2. Completa: She convinced me ___ (join) the club.
3. Completa: He asked her ___ (wait) outside.
4. Completa: They told us ___ (be) quiet.
5. Completa: I want my friend ___ (take up) photography.
6. Completa: My parents allowed me ___ (travel) alone.
7. Corrige: *She persuaded him join the team.*
8. Corrige: *He asked me for help her.*
9. Párrafo sobre un hobby de ocio.
10. Traduce: Me convenció para que me uniera.
11. Traduce: Quiero que mi hermana venga conmigo.
12. Diálogo: ask + tell + want.
13. Usa *would like + obj + to*.
14. Usa *advise + obj + to*.
15. Autochequeo: siempre *to* antes del infinitivo.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. Open — four correct object + infinitive sentences.
2. **to join**
3. **to wait**
4. **to be**
5. **to take up**
6. **to travel**
7. She persuaded him **to join** the team.
8. He asked me **to help** her.
9. Open leisure paragraph.
10. She convinced me **to join**.
11. I want my sister **to come** with me.
12. Open dialogue.
13. I would like you **to join** us.
14. My tutor advised me **to read** more.
15. Self-check.

</details>

## Lección 1 — Gramática

**Objetivo:** wish, future tenses, gerund vs infinitive, verb + object + inf

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. I wish I ___ started revising earlier. → *have / had / has*
2. By Friday she ___ have submitted both essays. → *will / is / would*
3. She enjoys ___ case studies. → *analyse / analysing / to analyse*
4. Her professor persuaded her ___ present. → *to / for / -*
5. If I had read the guide, I ___ understand now. → *will / would / am*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **had** · 2. **will** · 3. **analysing** · 4. **to** · 5. **would**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige / completa

1. ___ reviewed units 1–4, she feels ready. → *Having / Have / Had*
2. He avoids ___ tasks until the last day. → *leave / leaving / to leave*
3. I am going to ___ the draft tonight. → *finish / finishing / to finish*
4. I wish we ___ more time for leisure. → *have / had / would have*
5. She told him ___ check the data again. → *to / for / -*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Having** · 2. **leaving** · 3. **finish** · 4. **had** · 5. **to**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Corrige

1. *By Friday I will submit both essays.*
2. *I wish I have more discipline.*
3. *She enjoys to analyse data.*
4. *Having review the notes, she left.*
5. *If she studied B1, she would pass now.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. By Friday I **will have submitted** both essays.
2. I wish I **had** more discipline.
3. She enjoys **analysing** data.
4. Having **reviewed** the notes, she left.
5. If she **had studied** B1, she **would pass** now.

</details>

## Lección 5 — Writing

**Objetivo:** producir frases con el foco de la unidad.

1. Una frase de cada: wish, future perfect, gerund, obj + inf, participle.
2. Completa: I wish I ___ (start) revising earlier.
3. Completa: By Friday she ___ (submit) both essays.
4. Completa: She enjoys ___ (analyse) data.
5. Completa: Her professor persuaded her ___ (present).
6. Completa: ___ (review) units 1–4, she feels ready.
7. Mixed conditional sobre B2.
8. Corrige: *By Friday I will submit both.*
9. Corrige: *I wish I have more time.*
10. Mini-historia (5 frases) mezclando U1–4.
11. Traduce: Ojalá hubiera empezado antes.
12. Traduce: Para el viernes habrá entregado los ensayos.
13. Matching: estructura → unidad.
14. Autochequeo con el mapa U5.
15. Escribe Having + pp + main clause.
16. Enlace al curso U5.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. Open — one of each structure from U1–4.
2. **had started**
3. **will have submitted**
4. **analysing**
5. **to present**
6. Having **reviewed**
7. If I **had studied** mixed conditionals, I **would feel** confident now.
8. By Friday she **will have submitted** both essays.
9. I wish I **had** more time.
10. Open mixed paragraph.
11. I wish I **had started** earlier.
12. By Friday she **will have submitted** the essays.
13. wish→U1; future perfect→U2; gerund→U3; obj+inf→U4.
14. Self-check vs review map.
15. Having **finished** the exercises, I took a break.
16. **/curso-b2/unit-5**

</details>

Este artículo reúne **los ejercicios de la Unidad 6 del curso B2** (*Wish & If Only + Feelings*) con **soluciones comentadas**.

> **Guía teórica:** [Wish & If only B2](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-6-wish-if-only-feelings)  
> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 6 — Wish & If only](/curso-b2/unit-6)

Haz cada bloque **sin mirar** la solución. Luego comprueba y lee la explicación.

![Wish & If only](/blog/curso-b2/unit-6/wish-if-only.png)

**Contenido de la unidad:**
1. [Lección 1 — Gramática](#leccion-1--gramatica)
2. [Lección 2 — Vocabulario](#leccion-2--vocabulario)
3. [Lección 3 — Reading: Maya and feelings](#leccion-3--reading)
4. [Lección 4 — Listening: Maya on emotions](#leccion-4--listening)
5. [Lección 5 — Writing](#leccion-5--writing)

---

## Lección 1 — Gramática

**Objetivo:** wish + past simple / were / could / would; if only + past perfect

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. I wish I ___ calmer before exams. → *am / were / had been*
2. If only I ___ told her the truth! → *tell / told / had told*
3. I wish my neighbours ___ stop playing loud music. → *will / would / can*
4. I wish I ___ express my feelings better. → *can / could / will*
5. She wishes she ___ more sleep last night. → *gets / got / had got*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **were** · 2. **had told** · 3. **would** · 4. **could** · 5. **had got**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige / completa

1. If only you ___ here now! → *are / were / had been*
2. I wish he ___ so shy. → *isn't / weren't / hadn't been*
3. She regrets ___ silent for so long. → *stay / staying / to stay*
4. I wish they ___ me about the problem. → *tell / told / had told*
5. If only it ___ stop raining! → *will / would / can*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **were** · 2. **weren't** · 3. **staying** · 4. **had told** · 5. **would**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Corrige

1. *I wish I am taller.*
2. *If only you tell me earlier.*
3. *I wish they will be quiet.*
4. *She wishes she can dance.*
5. *I wish I have slept more.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I wish I **were** taller.
2. If only you **had told** me earlier.
3. I wish they **would** be quiet.
4. She wishes she **could** dance.
5. I wish I **had slept** more.

</details>

---

## Lección 2 — Vocabulario

**Objetivo:** feelings & emotions

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Empareja / elige

1. anxious → *ansioso · aliviado · orgulloso*
2. calm → *tranquilo · furioso · celoso*
3. express feelings → *expresar sentimientos · reservar · posponer*
4. apologise → *disculparse · cancelar · despegar*
5. flatmate → *compañero/a de piso · pasajero · guía*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **ansioso** · 2. **tranquilo** · 3. **expresar sentimientos** · 4. **disculparse** · 5. **compañero/a de piso**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Completa

1. relieved ≈ ___ → *aliviado / avergonzado / furioso*
2. frustrated ≈ ___ → *frustrado / agradecido / emocionado*
3. embarrassed ≈ ___ → *avergonzado / seguro / calmado*
4. if only ≈ ___ → *ojalá (más enfático) / porque / aunque*
5. wish + would = ___ → *queja / deseo pasado / certeza*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **aliviado** · 2. **frustrado** · 3. **avergonzado** · 4. **ojalá (más enfático)** · 5. **queja**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — En contexto

11. Usa 3 palabras nuevas en frases con el foco gramatical.
12. Di en voz alta el vocabulario de la unidad.
13. Empareja cada palabra con un ejemplo personal.
14. Revisa la tabla de vocabulario de la [guía teórica](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-6-wish-if-only-feelings).
15. Continúa en la [Unidad 6 del curso](/curso-b2/unit-6).

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11–13. Open answers — check meaning in theory. · 14. Theory vocab section. · 15. **/curso-b2/unit-6**

</details>

## Lección 3 — Reading: Maya and feelings

**Objetivo:** comprender un texto con el foco de la unidad.

### Texto y audio

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-6/reading-workbook.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Maya and feelings"></audio>

> Feelings are not always easy to share. Maya wishes she were braver when speaking in public. If only she had apologised sooner, her friendship would be stronger today. She wishes her flatmate would turn down the music after ten. She wishes she could sleep better before important meetings. Regretting her silence, she wrote a long message to her friend.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. Maya wishes she were ___ → *braver / taller / richer*
2. If only she had ___ sooner → *apologised / travelled / cooked*
3. Wishes flatmate would ___ → *turn down music / travel / cook*
4. Wishes she could ___ better → *sleep / fly / negotiate*
5. Regretting silence, she ___ → *wrote a message / flew / camped*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **braver** · 2. **apologised** · 3. **turn down music** · 4. **sleep** · 5. **wrote a message**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. Wish + were = present ___ → *unreal / real / past fact*
7. If only + past perfect = ___ → *past regret / future plan / zero*
8. Wish + would = ___ → *complaint / past regret*
9. Already apologised in person? → *False / True*
10. Underline wish / if only.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **unreal** · 7. **past regret** · 8. **complaint / change** · 9. **False** · 10. **See text**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. Write wish + could.
12. Feelings vocab? → *yes / none*
13. Friendship would be stronger if ___
14. Main idea? → *feelings / work / travel*
15. Course link → */curso-b2/unit-6*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **Model OK** · 12. **anxious, braver, silence** · 13. **she had apologised** · 14. **expressing feelings** · 15. **/curso-b2/unit-6**

</details>

---

## Lección 4 — Listening: Maya on emotions

**Objetivo:** escuchar el foco gramatical en contexto.

### Audio y guion

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-6/listening-workbook.mp3" title="🔊 Listening: Maya on emotions"></audio>

> Hi, I am Maya. I wish I were calmer before exams — I always feel anxious. If only I had told my friend how I felt, we would not have argued. I wish my neighbours would stop playing loud music at night. I wish I could express my feelings more easily.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. Who speaks? → *Maya / Sofia / Clara*
2. Wishes she were ___ before exams → *calmer / taller / richer*
3. If only had told friend about ___ → *feelings / flights / food*
4. Would not have ___ → *argued / travelled / cooked*
5. Wishes neighbours would stop ___ → *loud music / raining / working*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Maya** · 2. **calmer** · 3. **feelings** · 4. **argued** · 5. **loud music**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. Wishes could express ___ → *feelings / luggage / reports*
7. Wish + were = present unreal? → *yes / no*
8. If only + past perfect? → *yes / no*
9. Already told friend? → *False / True*
10. Write wish + would.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **feelings** · 7. **yes** · 8. **yes** · 9. **False (regret)** · 10. **Model OK**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. Write if only + past perfect.
12. Shadow audio.
13. Feelings vocab? → *yes / none*
14. Wish + could example?
15. Open Ver solución. → *yes*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **Model OK** · 12. **done** · 13. **anxious, argued, feelings** · 14. **wish I could express** · 15. **yes**

</details>

---

## Lección 5 — Writing

**Objetivo:** producir frases con el foco de la unidad.

1. Escribe 2× wish (presente irreal) y 1× if only (pasado).
2. Completa: I wish I ___ (be) calmer.
3. Completa: If only I ___ (tell) her sooner!
4. Completa: I wish they ___ (stop) making noise.
5. Completa: I wish I ___ (can) sleep better.
6. Wish + would — queja sobre un vecino.
7. Regret + gerund en una frase.
8. Corrige: *I wish I am taller.*
9. Corrige: *If only you tell me.*
10. Párrafo sobre expresar emociones.
11. Traduce: Ojalá pudiera expresarme mejor.
12. Traduce: Ojalá me lo hubieras dicho antes.
13. Diálogo con wish / if only.
14. Diferencia wish vs if only (1 frase).
15. Autochequeo: past simple vs past perfect after wish.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. Model using wish/if only correctly.
2. **were**
3. **had told**
4. **would stop**
5. **could**
6. I wish my neighbours **would** turn down the music.
7. I regret **staying** silent.
8. I wish I **were** taller.
9. If only you **had told** me.
10. Open feelings paragraph.
11. I wish I **could** express myself better.
12. If only you **had told** me earlier.
13. Open dialogue.
14. If only is often more emphatic than wish.
15. Self-check.

</details>

faqs.question: ¿Wish + past simple o past perfect?
faqs.answer: **Past simple / were / could** = presente irreal. **Past perfect** = arrepentimiento pasado.

faqs.question: ¿If only es igual que wish?
faqs.answer: Sí en significado; **If only** suele sonar más enfático.

faqs.question: ¿Wish + would?
faqs.answer: Para queja o deseo de **cambio de comportamiento**: I wish they **would** stop…

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico?
faqs.answer: En la [Unidad 6 del curso B2](/curso-b2/unit-6).

content:
Tras el [Repaso 1–4](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-5-repaso-1-4), la **Unidad 6** profundiza **wish / if only** (presente y pasado) con vocabulario de **feelings**.

## Qué aprenderás

- **wish + past simple / were** (presente irreal)
- **wish / if only + past perfect** (pasado)
- **wish + could** (habilidad)
- **wish + would** (cambio/queja)
- Vocabulario: feelings & emotions

![Wish if only feelings B2](/blog/curso-b2/unit-6/wish-if-only.png)

---

## 1. Wish / If only: presente vs pasado

| Estructura | Uso | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **wish + past simple / were** | presente irreal | I **wish I had** a bigger studio. |
| **wish + could** | habilidad presente | I **wish I could** play well. |
| **wish / if only + past perfect** | arrepentimiento pasado | If only you **had told** me sooner. |
| **wish + would** | cambio / queja | I **wish they would** stop playing loudly. |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-6/wish-had-studio.mp3" title="🔊 wish present"></audio>
<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-6/wish-had-checked.mp3" title="🔊 wish past"></audio>

2. If only you ___ (tell) me sooner.  
3. He wishes he ___ (be) at the concert now.

## Tip del profesor

Si el deseo es sobre **ahora**, usa pasado simple / *were* / *could*. Si es sobre **antes**, usa **past perfect**.

## Lección 1 — Gramática

**Objetivo:** would rather + inf; would rather + subject + past; would prefer; It's time + past

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. I would rather ___ at home this year. → *stay / to stay / staying*
2. She would prefer ___ by train. → *travel / to travel / travelling*
3. It is high time we ___ our cousins. → *visit / visited / visiting*
4. I would rather my sister ___ early. → *comes / came / come*
5. He would rather not ___ abroad alone. → *travel / to travel / travelling*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **stay** · 2. **to travel** · 3. **visited** · 4. **came** · 5. **travel**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige / completa

1. Would you rather ___ or fly? → *drive / to drive / driving*
2. I would prefer tea ___ coffee. → *to / than / over*
3. It is about time he ___ a job. → *find / found / finding*
4. She would rather her parents ___ with them. → *stay / stayed / staying*
5. I'd rather you ___ tell anyone yet. → *don't / didn't / not*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **drive** · 2. **to** · 3. **found** · 4. **stayed** · 5. **didn't**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Corrige

1. *I would rather to stay home.*
2. *She would prefer travel by bus.*
3. *It is time we leave.*
4. *I would rather my brother comes early.*
5. *Would you rather to cook?*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I would rather **stay** home.
2. She would prefer **to travel** by bus.
3. It is time we **left**.
4. I would rather my brother **came** early.
5. Would you rather **cook**?

</details>

---

## Lección 2 — Vocabulario

## Lección 1 — Gramática

**Objetivo:** if + past perfect → would + base (now); if + past simple → would have + pp

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. If we had left earlier, we ___ stuck now. → *aren't / wouldn't be / won't be*
2. If I had checked the forecast, I ___ a raincoat. → *pack / would pack / would have packed*
3. If she ___ more organised, she would have caught the flight. → *is / were / had been*
4. We ___ at the beach now if the ferry hadn't been cancelled. → *are / would be / will be*
5. If he had booked online, he ___ waiting in the queue. → *isn't / wouldn't be / won't be*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **wouldn't be** · 2. **would have packed** · 3. **were** · 4. **would be** · 5. **wouldn't be**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige / completa

1. If I ___ taller, I would have joined the team. → *am / were / had been*
2. If they had taken a taxi, they ___ here by now. → *are / would be / will be*
3. If she ___ the alarm, she wouldn't be late now. → *sets / set / had set*
4. Mixed: past → present uses ___ in the if-clause. → *past perfect / past simple / will*
5. If he were braver, he ___ asked for help yesterday. → *will / would / would have*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **were** · 2. **would be** · 3. **had set** · 4. **past perfect** · 5. **would have**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Corrige

1. *If we left earlier, we wouldn't be stuck.* (mixed)
2. *If I checked the forecast, I would pack a coat.*
3. *If she was organised, she would have caught it.*
4. *If he had booked, he isn't waiting.*
5. *If I am taller, I would have joined.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. If we **had left** earlier, we wouldn't be stuck.
2. If I **had checked** the forecast, I **would have packed** a coat.
3. If she **were** organised, she **would have caught** it.
4. If he **had booked**, he **wouldn't be** waiting.
5. If I **were** taller, I **would have joined**.

</details>

title: Mixed Conditionals B2: Pasado → Presente/Futuro + Travel
author: linguafly-team

faqs.question: ¿Qué es un mixed conditional?
faqs.answer: Combina tiempos de distintos condicionales: p. ej. **pasado irreal** → **resultado presente**.

faqs.question: ¿Fórmula más frecuente?
faqs.answer: **If + past perfect**, **would + infinitive** (ahora / futuro): If he **had caught** the bus, he **would be** here now.

faqs.question: ¿También presente → pasado?
faqs.answer: Sí: If I **were** taller, I **would have joined** the team.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico?
faqs.answer: En la [Unidad 8 del curso B2](/curso-b2/unit-8).

content:
Tras [Would rather & Family](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-7-would-rather-family), la **Unidad 8** consolida **mixed conditionals** con vocabulario de **travel**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 8](/curso-b2/unit-8)  
> **Antes:** [U7 — Would rather & Family](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-7-would-rather-family)

---

## Qué aprenderás

- Mixed: **pasado → presente**
- Mixed: **pasado → futuro**
- Contraste con 2.º / 3.er condicional
- Vocabulario: travel

![Mixed conditionals travel B2](/blog/curso-b2/unit-8/mixed-conditionals.png)

---

## 1. Mixed conditionals

| Tipo | If-clause | Resultado | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Pasado → presente | past perfect | would + inf | If he **had caught** the bus, he **would be** here now. |
| Pasado → futuro | past perfect | would + inf | If he **had passed**, he **would start** next week. |
| Presente → pasado | past simple | would have + pp | If I **were** taller, I **would have joined**… |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-8/mixed-bus.mp3" title="🔊 bus"></audio>
<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-8/mixed-booked.mp3" title="🔊 booked"></audio>

## 2. Más ejemplos

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-8/mixed-spanish.mp3" title="🔊 Spanish"></audio>
<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-8/mixed-tickets.mp3" title="🔊 tickets"></audio>
<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-8/mixed-warning.mp3" title="🔊 warning"></audio>

| Word | Idea |
| :--- | :--- |
| itinerary / layover | itinerario / escala |

| delay / destination | retraso / destino |

## 4. Reading

![Travel scene](/blog/curso-b2/unit-8/travel-scene.png)

> If he had caught the bus, he would be here now. If we had booked the hotel, we would have a room. If he had passed the interview, he would start next week. If I had learned Spanish, I would speak fluently now.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-8/reading-u8.mp3" title="🔊 Reading"></audio>

---

## 5. Diálogo

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-8/dialogue-u8.mp3" title="🔊 Dialogue"></audio>

> Missed the bus? — If he had caught it, he would be here.  
> Booked yet? — If we had booked last week, we would have a room.

## 6. Practica

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-8/practice-u8.mp3" title="🔊 Practice"></audio>

---

## 7. Ejercicios

1. If he ___ (catch) the bus, he would be here now.  
2. If we ___ (book) the hotel, we would have a room.  
3. If he had passed, he ___ (start) next week.  
4. If I had learned Spanish, I ___ (speak) fluently now.  
5. Vocab: escala en un vuelo = ___

<details><summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **had caught** · 2. **had booked** · 3. **would start** · 4. **would speak** · 5. **layover**
</details>

## Tip del profesor

Pregúntate: ¿la causa es **pasada** y el resultado es **ahora**? → mixed (*had + pp* / *would + inf*).

## Lección 1 — Gramática

**Objetivo:** -ing / -ed participle clauses; Having + past participle

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. ___ by the noise, residents protested. → *Disturbing / Disturbed / Having disturb*
2. ___ planted trees, the council cut pollution. → *Having / Have / Had*
3. ___ through the park, I saw less litter. → *Walk / Walking / Walked*
4. ___ by the results, schools joined the programme. → *Encourage / Encouraged / Encouraging*
5. ___ finished the audit, experts made recommendations. → *Having / Have / Had*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Disturbed** · 2. **Having** · 3. **Walking** · 4. **Encouraged** · 5. **Having**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige / completa

1. -ing clause = usually ___ meaning. → *active / passive / past*
2. -ed clause = usually ___ meaning. → *passive / active / future*
3. Having + pp = action ___ the main verb. → *before / after / during*
4. Same ___ in both clauses. → *subject / object / tense*
5. Disturbed by… = cláusula ___ → *-ed / -ing / infinitive*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **active** · 2. **passive** · 3. **before** · 4. **subject** · 5. **-ed**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Corrige

1. *Disturbing by noise, they protested.*
2. *Having plant trees, air improved.*
3. *Walked through the park, I noticed birds.*
4. *Encouraging by reports, the mayor acted.*
5. *Having finish the audit, they left.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Disturbed** by noise, they protested.
2. Having **planted** trees, air improved.
3. **Walking** through the park, I noticed birds.
4. **Encouraged** by reports, the mayor acted.
5. Having **finished** the audit, they left.

</details>

---

## Lección 2 — Vocabulario

**Objetivo:** environment

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Empareja / elige

1. pollution → *contaminación · ascenso · nómina*
2. recycling → *reciclaje · billete · maleta*
3. solar panels → *paneles solares · pasaporte · embarque*
4. litter → *basura tirada · equipaje / vuelo*
5. carbon footprint → *huella de carbono · beca · tesis*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **contaminación** · 2. **reciclaje** · 3. **paneles solares** · 4. **basura tirada** · 5. **huella de carbono**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Completa

1. sustainable ≈ ___ → *sostenible / barato / ruidoso*
2. renewable ≈ ___ → *renovable / cancelado / retrasado*
3. single-use ≈ ___ → *de un solo uso / reutilizable / permanente*
4. audit ≈ ___ → *auditoría / fiesta / vacaciones*
5. volunteer ≈ ___ → *voluntario / pasajero / guía turístico*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **sostenible** · 2. **renovable** · 3. **de un solo uso** · 4. **auditoría** · 5. **voluntario**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — En contexto

11. Usa 3 palabras nuevas en frases con el foco gramatical.
12. Di en voz alta el vocabulario de la unidad.
13. Empareja cada palabra con un ejemplo personal.
14. Revisa la tabla de vocabulario de la [guía teórica](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-9-participle-clauses-environment).
15. Continúa en la [Unidad 9 del curso](/curso-b2/unit-9).

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11–13. Open answers — check meaning in theory. · 14. Theory vocab section. · 15. **/curso-b2/unit-9**

</details>

---

## Lección 3 — Reading: Green city action

**Objetivo:** comprender un texto con el foco de la unidad.

### Texto y audio

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-9/reading-workbook.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Green city action"></audio>

> Environmental action starts locally. Disturbed by rising pollution levels, citizens demanded cleaner transport. Having installed solar panels, the school cut its energy bills by forty percent. Walking along the river, volunteers collected bags of litter. Encouraged by international reports, the mayor promised to ban single-use plastics. Having finished the audit, experts recommended stricter recycling rules.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. Disturbed by ___, citizens demanded transport → *pollution / music / homework*
2. Having installed ___, school cut bills → *solar panels / tickets / essays*
3. Walking along river, volunteers collected ___ → *litter / luggage / reports*
4. Encouraged by ___, mayor promised ban → *reports / rain / flights*
5. Having finished ___, experts recommended rules → *audit / flight / party*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **pollution** · 2. **solar panels** · 3. **litter** · 4. **international reports** · 5. **audit**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. -ed clause example? → *Disturbed by… / Walking… / Having…*
7. -ing clause example? → *Walking… / Disturbed…*
8. Having + pp = action ___ main verb → *before / after / never*
9. Already banned plastics? → *False / promised*
10. Underline participle clauses.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **Disturbed by…** · 7. **Walking along…** · 8. **before** · 9. **promised (not done yet)** · 10. **See text**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. Write Having + pp sentence.
12. Environment vocab? → *yes / none*
13. Main idea? → *environment / work / family*
14. Same subject in clauses? → *yes / no*
15. Course link → */curso-b2/unit-9*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **Model OK** · 12. **pollution, recycling, litter** · 13. **local green action** · 14. **yes** · 15. **/curso-b2/unit-9**

</details>

---

## Lección 4 — Listening: Ben on the environment

**Objetivo:** escuchar el foco gramatical en contexto.

### Audio y guion

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-9/listening-workbook.mp3" title="🔊 Listening: Ben on the environment"></audio>

> Hi, I am Ben. Disturbed by the noise from the factory, local residents protested last week. Having planted hundreds of trees, the council improved air quality in the area. Walking through the park, I noticed fewer plastic bottles on the ground. Encouraged by the results, more schools joined the recycling programme.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. Who speaks? → *Ben / James / Tom*
2. Disturbed by noise from ___ → *factory / school / airport*
3. Residents ___ last week → *protested / travelled / slept*
4. Having planted trees, council improved ___ → *air quality / luggage / grades*
5. Walking through park, noticed fewer ___ bottles → *plastic / glass / metal*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Ben** · 2. **factory** · 3. **protested** · 4. **air quality** · 5. **plastic**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. Encouraged by results, ___ joined programme → *schools / flights / bosses*
7. -ed participle clause? → *yes / no*
8. Having + pp? → *yes / no*
9. Protest because of pollution? → *True / False*
10. Write -ing clause.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **schools** · 7. **Disturbed by…** · 8. **Having planted…** · 9. **True** · 10. **Model OK**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. Write Having + pp clause.
12. Shadow audio.
13. Environment vocab? → *yes / none*
14. Same subject in clauses? → *yes / no*
15. Open Ver solución. → *yes*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **Model OK** · 12. **done** · 13. **pollution, recycling, plastic** · 14. **yes** · 15. **yes**

</details>

---

## Lección 5 — Writing

**Objetivo:** producir frases con el foco de la unidad.

1. Escribe una cláusula -ing, -ed y Having + pp.
2. Completa: ___ by the noise, residents protested.
3. Completa: ___ planted trees, air quality improved.
4. Completa: ___ through the park, I saw less litter.
5. Completa: ___ finished the audit, experts spoke.
6. Explica mismo sujeto en 1 frase.
7. Corrige: *Disturbing by noise, they left.*
8. Corrige: *Having plant trees, we left.*
9. Párrafo sobre medio ambiente local.
10. Traduce: Al terminar la auditoría, publicaron el informe.
11. Traduce: Caminando por el río, recogieron basura.
12. Encouraged by… + main clause.
13. Disturbed by… + main clause.
14. Autochequeo: -ing activo / -ed pasivo.
15. Enlace teoría U9.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. Open — three participle clause types.
2. **Disturbed**
3. Having **planted**
4. **Walking**
5. Having **finished**
6. The participle clause and main clause share the same subject.
7. **Disturbed** by the noise, they left.
8. Having **planted** trees, we left.
9. Open environment paragraph.
10. Having **finished** the audit, they published the report.
11. **Walking** along the river, they collected litter.
12. Encouraged by the results, the mayor acted.
13. Disturbed by pollution, citizens protested.
14. Self-check.
15. [Guía U9](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-9-participle-clauses-environment)

</details>

faqs.question: ¿-ing o -ed?
faqs.answer: **-ing** = activa / simultánea (*Walking…*). **-ed** = pasiva / estado (*Disturbed by…*).

faqs.question: ¿Having + pp?
faqs.answer: Acción **completada antes** de la principal: **Having finished**, we left.

faqs.question: ¿Mismo sujeto?
faqs.answer: Sí: la cláusula de participio y la principal comparten sujeto.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico?
faqs.answer: En la [Unidad 9 del curso B2](/curso-b2/unit-9).

Tras [Mixed conditionals & Travel](/blog/curso-b2/unidad-8-mixed-conditionals-travel), la **Unidad 9** trabaja **participle clauses** con vocabulario de **environment**.

## Qué aprenderás

- Cláusulas **-ing** (activas)

---

## 1. Participle clauses

| Forma | Significado | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **-ing** | activa / simultánea | **Walking** along the beach, he found a shell. |
| **-ed** | pasiva / causa | **Disturbed** by the news, she couldn't sleep. |
| **Having + pp** | completada antes | **Having finished** the tasks, we went home. |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-9/walking-beach.mp3" title="🔊 -ing"></audio>

## 2. Más ejemplos

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-9/having-completed.mp3" title="🔊 Having completed"></audio>
<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-9/built-bridge.mp3" title="🔊 built"></audio>

## 3. Vocabulario: Environment

![Environment vocabulary](/blog/curso-b2/unit-9/environment-vocab.png)

| Word | Idea |
| :--- | :--- |
| pollution / recycle | contaminación / reciclar |
| sustainable / renewable | sostenible / renovable |
| biodiversity / habitat | biodiversidad / hábitat |

---

## 4. Reading

![Environment scene](/blog/curso-b2/unit-9/environment-scene.png)

> Having completed the report, she sent it. Walking along the beach, he found a shell. Disturbed by the news, she couldn't sleep. Having finished the tasks, we went home.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-9/reading-u9.mp3" title="🔊 Reading"></audio>

---

## 5. Diálogo

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-9/dialogue-u9.mp3" title="🔊 Dialogue"></audio>

> Finished already? — Having finished the tasks, we went home.  
> Sleep well? — Disturbed by the news, she couldn't sleep.

---

## 6. Practica

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b2/unit-9/practice-u9.mp3" title="🔊 Practice"></audio>

---

## 7. Ejercicios

1. ___ along the beach, he found a shell. (Walk)  
2. ___ by the news, she couldn't sleep. (Disturb)  
3. ___ finished the tasks, we went home. (Have)  
4. The bridge ___ in 1950 is still in use. (build)  
5. Vocab: reciclar = ___

<details><summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Walking** · 2. **Disturbed** · 3. **Having** · 4. **built** · 5. **recycle**
</details>

---

## Tip del profesor

Si la acción ya terminó **antes** de la principal, usa **Having + participio** (*Having finished…*).

5. [Lección 5 — Writing: My shopping](#leccion-5--writing-my-shopping)

---

## Lección 1 — Gramática: plurales

**Objetivo:** plurales regulares (*apples, tomatoes, potatoes*) e irregulares básicos (*children, people*); *fish*.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. I need two ____ for the salad. → *tomatoes / tomatos / tomato*  
2. We have three ____ in the fridge. → *potatoes / potatos / potato*  
3. There are many ____ in the fruit section. → *apples / apple / appls*  
4. I want two ____ of fish. → *pieces / piece / fishs*  
5. How many ____ do you need? → *eggs / egg / egges*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **tomatoes** — *tomato → tomatoes* (*-es*).  
2. **potatoes** — *potato → potatoes*.  
3. **apples** — plural regular *-s*.  
4. **pieces** — *two pieces of fish*.  
5. **eggs**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Elige

6. Plural of *child* = ____. → a) children · b) childs · c) childes  
7. Correct plural of *person*: ____. → a) people · b) persons (usual A1) · c) persones  
8. We add *-es* for plural when ____. → a) the word ends in *-s, -ch, -sh, -x* (or *-o* like tomato) · b) the word is short · c) always  
9. *Fish* as food (plural) = ____. → a) fish (same) · b) fishs · c) fishes only  
10. *Vegetable* plural = ____. → a) vegetables · b) vegetable · c) vegetabls

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) children**  
7. **a) people**  
8. **a) the word ends in *-s, -ch, -sh, -x* (or *-o* like tomato)**  
9. **a) fish (same)**  
10. **a) vegetables**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–13 — Ordena

11. The / apples / are / in / aisle / five.  
12. I need / some / meat / and / fish.  
13. Where are / the / vegetables?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. The apples are in aisle five.  
12. I need some meat and fish.  
13. Where are the vegetables?

</details>

### Ejercicios 14–15 — Verdadero o falso

14. *Tomato* and *potato* add *-es* for the plural. → True / False  
15. We say *two fish* for two pieces of fish. → True / False

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

14. **True**  
15. **True**

</details>

## Lección 2 — Vocabulario: supermercado

**Objetivo:** *fruit, vegetables, meat, fish, aisle, trolley, checkout, basket, shelf*.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Elige el significado

1. *Fruit* = ____. → a) apples, bananas, oranges · b) meat · c) bread  
2. *Vegetables* = ____. → a) carrots, tomatoes, potatoes · b) fish · c) milk  
3. *Meat* = ____. → a) chicken, beef, pork · b) fish · c) eggs  
4. *Fish* = ____. → a) salmon, tuna, cod · b) chicken · c) bread  
5. *Aisle* = ____. → a) space between shelves in a supermarket · b) checkout · c) basket

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) apples, bananas, oranges**  
2. **a) carrots, tomatoes, potatoes**  
3. **a) chicken, beef, pork**  
4. **a) salmon, tuna, cod**  
5. **a) space between shelves in a supermarket**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–7 — Empareja

6. Empareja: apple / carrot / chicken / salmon / aisle → fruit · vegetable · meat · fish · between shelves  
7. Empareja: banana / tomato / beef / tuna / checkout → fruit · vegetable · meat · fish · pay here

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **apple → fruit** · **carrot → vegetable** · **chicken → meat** · **salmon → fish** · **aisle → between shelves**  
7. **banana → fruit** · **tomato → vegetable** · **beef → meat** · **tuna → fish** · **checkout → pay here**

</details>

### Ejercicios 8–13 — Completa / elige

8. The ____ are in aisle three. → *vegetables / meat / fish*  
9. I need some ____ and chicken. → *beef / apples / bread*  
10. Where is the ____ section? → *fruit / meat / fish*  
11. *Basket* = ____. → a) a container to carry shopping · b) an aisle · c) checkout  
12. *Trolley* = ____. → a) a cart for many items · b) a basket · c) a shelf  
13. *Shelf* = ____. → a) a flat surface for products · b) an aisle · c) a basket

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

8. **vegetables**  
9. **beef**  
10. **fruit**  
11. **a) a container to carry shopping**  
12. **a) a cart for many items**  
13. **a) a flat surface for products**

</details>

### Ejercicios 14–15 — Verdadero o falso

14. An aisle is where you find products on shelves. → True / False  
15. Meat and fish are usually in different sections. → True / False

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

14. **True**  
15. **True**

</details>

## Lección 3 — Reading: Every Saturday

**Objetivo:** leer sobre una compra en el supermercado.

### Texto

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-51/reading-supermarket.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Every Saturday"></audio>

> I go to the supermarket every Saturday. First I get a trolley. The fruit and vegetables are in aisle one. I buy apples, bananas and tomatoes. The meat and fish are at the back. I need some chicken and two pieces of fish. Then I pay at the checkout.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Elige la respuesta correcta

1. When does the writer go to the supermarket? → a) Every Saturday · b) Every Sunday · c) Every day  
2. What does he/she get first? → a) A trolley · b) A basket · c) Fruit  
3. Where are fruit and vegetables? → a) In aisle one · b) At the back · c) At checkout  
4. Which fruit/veg does he/she buy? → a) Apples, bananas, tomatoes · b) Only apples · c) Oranges  
5. Where are meat and fish? → a) At the back · b) In aisle one · c) At the entrance

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) Every Saturday**  
2. **a) A trolley**  
3. **a) In aisle one**  
4. **a) Apples, bananas, tomatoes**  
5. **a) At the back**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Comprensión

6. What meat does he/she need? → a) Chicken · b) Beef · c) Pork  
7. How many pieces of fish? → a) Two · b) One · c) Three  
8. Where does he/she pay? → a) At the checkout · b) In aisle one · c) At the back  
9. Which word means *pasillo*? → a) Aisle · b) Checkout · c) Trolley  
10. *Trolley* means ____. → a) shopping cart · b) basket · c) shelf

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) Chicken**  
7. **a) Two**  
8. **a) At the checkout**  
9. **a) Aisle**  
10. **a) shopping cart**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Detalles

11. The text is about ____. → a) shopping at the supermarket · b) cooking · c) a restaurant  
12. *Checkout* means ____. → a) where you pay · b) aisle · c) fruit section  
13. *At the back* means ____. → a) at the end of the shop · b) at the entrance · c) in aisle one  
14. *Vegetables* means ____. → a) carrots, tomatoes, etc. · b) meat · c) fish  
15. The main topic is ____. → a) a supermarket shopping trip · b) cooking at home · c) eating at a restaurant

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) shopping at the supermarket**  
12. **a) where you pay**  
13. **a) at the end of the shop**  
14. **a) carrots, tomatoes, etc.**  
15. **a) a supermarket shopping trip**

</details>

## Lección 4 — Listening: Where are the vegetables?

**Objetivo:** escuchar un diálogo para encontrar productos.

### Audio y guion

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-51/listening-supermarket.mp3" title="🔊 Listening: Where are the vegetables?"></audio>

> **A:** Where are the vegetables?  
> **B:** In aisle two.  
> **A:** And the fruit?  
> **B:** Aisle one, next to the entrance.  
> **A:** I need some chicken and fish.  
> **B:** Meat and fish are at the back.  
> **A:** Thank you. Where is the checkout?  
> **B:** Over there. Get a trolley if you have many things.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Comprensión

1. What does A ask first? → a) Where are the vegetables? · b) Where is the fruit? · c) Where is the checkout?  
2. Which aisle for vegetables? → a) Aisle two · b) Aisle one · c) Aisle three  
3. Where is the fruit? → a) Aisle one, next to the entrance · b) At the back · c) Aisle two  
4. What does A need? → a) Chicken and fish · b) Vegetables only · c) Fruit only  
5. Where are meat and fish? → a) At the back · b) Aisle one · c) At checkout

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a) Where are the vegetables?**  
2. **a) Aisle two**  
3. **a) Aisle one, next to the entrance**  
4. **a) Chicken and fish**  
5. **a) At the back**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–10 — Detalles

6. What does A say to B? → a) Thank you · b) Goodbye · c) Sorry  
7. Where is the checkout? → a) Over there · b) Aisle one · c) At the back  
8. What does B suggest if A has many things? → a) Get a trolley · b) Get a basket · c) Go to aisle one  
9. The dialogue is at ____. → a) the supermarket · b) a restaurant · c) home  
10. *Aisle* means ____. → a) space between shelves · b) checkout · c) entrance

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. **a) Thank you**  
7. **a) Over there**  
8. **a) Get a trolley**  
9. **a) the supermarket**  
10. **a) space between shelves**

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Forma

11. *Trolley* means ____. → a) shopping cart · b) basket · c) shelf  
12. *At the back* means ____. → a) at the end of the shop · b) at the entrance · c) at checkout  
13. *Checkout* means ____. → a) where you pay · b) aisle · c) fruit section  
14. *Next to the entrance* means ____. → a) near the door · b) at the back · c) at checkout  
15. The dialogue is about ____. → a) finding things in the supermarket · b) cooking · c) eating out

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **a) shopping cart**  
12. **a) at the end of the shop**  
13. **a) where you pay**  
14. **a) near the door**  
15. **a) finding things in the supermarket**

</details>

## Lección 5 — Writing: My shopping

**Objetivo:** escribir sobre una compra con plurales y vocabulario de tienda.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. The ____ are in aisle one. → *vegetables / vegetable / vegetabls*  
2. I need two ____ of fish. → *pieces / piece / fishs*  
3. We have three ____ and four tomatoes. → *potatoes / potatos / potato*  
4. Where are the ____? → *apples / apple / fish*  
5. Meat and fish are ____ the back. → *at / in / on*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **vegetables**  
2. **pieces**  
3. **potatoes**  
4. **apples**  
5. **at**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–8 — Ordena

6. The / vegetables / are / in / aisle / two.  
7. I need / some / chicken / and / fish.  
8. Where is / the / checkout?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. The vegetables are in aisle two.  
7. I need some chicken and fish.  
8. Where is the checkout?

</details>

### Ejercicios 9–15 — Escribe (modelos)

9. Dónde está la fruta (*aisle one*).  
10. Qué necesitas comprar (*chicken, fish* o *vegetables*).  
11. Dos frases: qué compras y dónde pagas.  
12. Pregunta *Where are the vegetables?* y respuesta *In aisle two.*  
13. Párrafo corto (3–4 frases): trolley, pasillos, fruta/verdura, caja.  
14. 2–3 frases: qué hay en cada pasillo.  
15. Lista de la compra (3–4 cosas) y dónde las encuentras.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución (ejemplos)</summary>

9. The fruit is in aisle one.  
10. I need some chicken and two pieces of fish.  
11. I buy apples and tomatoes. I pay at the checkout.  
12. Where are the vegetables? In aisle two.  
13. I go to the supermarket and get a trolley. The fruit and vegetables are in aisle one. I pay at the checkout.  
14. The fruit is in aisle one. Vegetables are in aisle two. Meat and fish are at the back.  
15. I need apples, tomatoes, chicken and fish. Fruit is in aisle one. Meat is at the back.

</details>

---

## Resumen rápido

| Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| **-s** | apple**s**, banana**s**, egg**s** |
| **-es** | tomato**es**, potato**es** |
| **irregular** | children · people |
| **fish** | two fish / two pieces of fish |
| **tienda** | aisle · trolley · checkout |
