## Lección 4 — Listening: Tom the teacher

**Objetivo:** Escuchar una entrevista corta sobre profesiones.

### Audio y guion

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-9/listening-tom.mp3" title="🔊 Listening: Tom"></audio>

> **Interviewer:** What do you do?  
> **Tom:** I am a teacher. I work in a primary school.  
> **Interviewer:** Where is the school?

1. What is Tom's job? → a) Doctor · b) Teacher · c) Engineer  
2. Where does Tom work? → a) In a hospital · b) In a primary school · c) In an office  
3. Where is the school? → a) In the centre of town · b) In a village · c) Near the hospital  
4. Does Tom like his job? → a) Yes · b) No · c) He doesn't say  
5. What is Tom's sister's job? → a) Teacher · b) Nurse · c) Doctor  
6. Where does Tom's sister work? → a) In a school · b) In a hospital · c) In an office

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **b) Teacher**  
2. **b) In a primary school**  
3. **a) In the centre of town**  
4. **a) Yes**  
5. **b) Nurse**  
6. **b) In a hospital**

</details>

### Ejercicios 7–10 — Verdadero o falso

7. Tom is a secondary school teacher. → ?  
8. Tom and his sister like their jobs. → ?  
9. The interviewer asks "What do you do?". → ?  
10. Tom's sister works in a school. → ?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

7. **Falso** (primary school)  
8. **Verdadero**  
9. **Verdadero**  
10. **Falso** (hospital)

</details>

### Ejercicios 11–15 — Comprensión global

11. Main topic:  
    a) Food · b) A person talks about his job and his sister's job · c) Sports  
12. What is Tom's job?  
    a) Teacher · b) Nurse · c) Doctor  
13. Which questions does the interviewer ask?  
    a) Only Where do you work? · b) What do you do?, Where is the school?, Do you like your job? · c) How old are you?  
14. What type of school does Tom work in?  
    a) Secondary · b) Primary · c) University  
15. Does Tom mention his sister?  
    a) No · b) Yes, she is a nurse · c) Yes, she is a teacher

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

11. **b) A person talks about his job and his sister's job**  
12. **a) Teacher**  
13. **b) What do you do?, Where is the school?, Do you like your job?**  
14. **b) Primary**  
15. **b) Yes, she is a nurse**

## Lección 5 — Writing: Jobs

**Objetivo:** Escribir frases y párrafos sobre profesiones y lugares de trabajo.

### Modelo

> I am a teacher. I work in a school.  
> He is an engineer. She is a doctor.  
> Where do you work? I work in a hospital.  
> My mother is a nurse. She likes her job.

### Ejercicios 1–5 — Completa

1. I ____ a teacher. (*am / is / are*)  
2. He is ____ engineer. (*a / an*)  
3. She is ____ doctor. (*a / an*)  
4. Where ____ you work? (*do / does*)  
5. I work ____ a hospital. (*in / at / on*)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **am**  
2. **an**  
3. **a**  
4. **do**  
5. **in**

</details>

### Ejercicios 6–8 — Ordena las palabras

6. I / am / a / teacher.  
7. Where / do / you / work?  
8. She / works / in / a / hospital.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

6. I am a teacher.  
7. Where do you work?  
8. She works in a hospital.

</details>

### Ejercicios 9–12 — Escribe frases guiadas (ejemplos)

9. Say a job (*I am a/an …* or *My … is a/an …*).  
10. Say a workplace (*I work in a/an …*).  
11. Job + workplace (two sentences).  
12. Question + answer (*What do you do?* / *Where do you work?*).

<details>
<summary>Ver solución (ejemplos)</summary>

9. I am a teacher. / My sister is a nurse.  
10. I work in a school. / She works in a hospital.  
11. I am a teacher. I work in a school.  
12. What do you do? I am a doctor. / Where do you work? I work in a hospital.

</details>

### Ejercicios 13–15 — Párrafos cortos (ejemplos)

13. Your job or a family member's job (4–6 sentences).  
14. Jobs of 2–3 people you know.  
15. Short presentation: name, job, workplace, like.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución (ejemplos)</summary>

**13.**  
My mother is a nurse. She works in a hospital. She likes her job. My father is an engineer. He works in an office. I am a student.

**14.**  
My brother is a driver. He works on a bus. My friend is a chef. She works in a restaurant. My uncle is a doctor. He works in a hospital.

**15.**  
My name is Ana. I am a teacher. I work in a school. I like my job. My sister is a nurse. She works in a hospital.

</details>

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Recuerda |
|------|----------|
| Profesión | *I am a teacher.* · *He is an engineer.* |
| *a / an* | *a* + consonante · *an* + vocal |
| Lugar | *I work in a school / hospital / office.* |
| Preguntas | *What do you do?* · *Where do you work?* |

title: Future B1: will, going to y present continuous (travel)
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 6 del curso B1: will, going to y present continuous para el futuro, con vocabulario de travel y el viaje a Tokio.
description: Contrasta will, going to y present continuous para el futuro en inglés B1: predicciones, planes e intenciones, arreglos fijos. Guía Unidad 6 con vocabulario de travel y audios.
alt: Contraste will, going to y present continuous para el futuro B1

faqs.answer: Predicciones de opinión (I think it will rain), promesas (I will call you), decisiones espontáneas (Wait, I will help you) y planes inciertos (I will probably stay at home).
faqs.question: ¿Cuándo uso will?

faqs.answer: Planes o intenciones ya decididos (I am going to visit my parents) y predicciones con evidencia (Look at the clouds! It is going to rain).
faqs.question: ¿Cuándo uso going to?

faqs.answer: Arreglos fijos con hora/lugar (She is meeting her boss at 3 PM; We are flying to Rome on Friday). Suele haber billete, cita o acuerdo.
faqs.question: ¿Cuándo uso present continuous para el futuro?

faqs.answer: Horarios oficiales: The flight departs at 10 AM. El avión “sale” según el horario, no es tu plan personal.
faqs.question: ¿Y el Present Simple para el futuro?

faqs.answer: En el [cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-6-future-will-going-to-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la Unidad 6 del curso B1 de Linguafly: will / going to / continuous, travel & transport, reading, listening, speaking y writing.
faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 6 del curso B1?

content:
Tras el [Repaso 1–4](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-5-repaso-1-4), la **Unidad 6 del curso B1** (*Future: will, going to, present continuous*) te enseña a **elegir la forma futura** correcta: predicción, plan o arreglo fijo — con vocabulario de **travel & transport**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 6 — Future forms](/curso-b1/unit-6)  
> **Antes:** [U5 — Repaso 1–4](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-5-repaso-1-4) · [will vs going to](/blog/gramatica/will-going-to-diferencia)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 6 (B1)

- Usar **will** (predicción, promesa, decisión espontánea).
- Usar **going to** (plan / intención / evidencia).
- Usar **present continuous** (arreglo fijo con hora/lugar).
- Reconocer **Present Simple** en horarios (*The flight departs…*).
- Aplicarlo al vocabulario de **viajes y transporte**.

![Tres formas de futuro](/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/future-forms.png)

---

## 1. Mapa rápido

| Forma | Uso principal | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **will** | opinión, promesa, espontáneo | I think it **will** rain. · Wait, I **will** help you. |
| **going to** | plan / intención / evidencia | I **am going to** visit my parents. · It **is going to** rain. |
| **am/is/are + -ing** | arreglo fijo | We **are flying** to Rome on Friday. |
| **Present Simple** | horario | The flight **departs** at 10 AM. |

---

## 2. *going to* — planes e intenciones

> I **am going to** visit my parents next weekend.  
> He **is going to** take the train tomorrow.  
> I **am going to** book the tickets next week.  
> What **are you going to** do this weekend?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/am-going-to-visit.mp3" title="🔊 I am going to visit my parents next weekend."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/is-going-to-take.mp3" title="🔊 He is going to take the train tomorrow."></audio>

**Evidencia ahora:**

> Look at the clouds! It **is going to** rain.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/going-to-rain.mp3" title="🔊 Look at the clouds! It is going to rain."></audio>

---

## 3. *will* — predicciones, promesas, espontáneo

> I think it **will** rain tomorrow.  
> Wait, I **will** help you.  
> I promise I **will** call you when I arrive.  
> I **will** probably stay at home tonight.  
> Perhaps we **will** see you there.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/will-rain.mp3" title="🔊 I think it will rain tomorrow."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/will-help.mp3" title="🔊 Wait, I will help you."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/will-call.mp3" title="🔊 I promise I will call you when I arrive."></audio>

Truco: *I think / probably / perhaps* → suele ir **will**.

---

## 4. Present continuous — arreglos fijos

Hay cita, billete o acuerdo concreto:

> She **is meeting** her boss at 3 PM.  
> We **are flying** to Rome on Friday.  
> They **are having** a meeting tomorrow at 9.  
> She **is meeting** her sister at the airport at 5 PM.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/is-meeting.mp3" title="🔊 She is meeting her boss at three PM."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/are-flying.mp3" title="🔊 We are flying to Rome on Friday."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/are-having-meeting.mp3" title="🔊 They are having a meeting tomorrow at nine."></audio>

---

## 5. Present Simple — horarios

> The flight **departs** at 10 AM.  
> The plane **takes off** at 8 o’clock.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/flight-departs.mp3" title="🔊 The flight departs at ten AM."></audio>

No es tu plan: es el **horario** del vuelo / tren.

---

## 6. Vocabulario: Travel & transport

![Vocabulario de viajes](/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/travel-vocab.png)

| Palabra | Idea |
| :--- | :--- |
| airport | aeropuerto |
| passport | pasaporte |
| take off / land | despegar / aterrizar |
| station | estación |
| check in / check out | registrarse / salir del hotel |
| flight | vuelo |
| suitcase | maleta |
| set off | partir / empezar el viaje |
| traveller | viajero/a |
| book | reservar |
| delay | retraso |
| get on / get off | subir / bajar (bus, tren) |
| hotel | hotel |

---

## 7. Reading: Tokyo business trip

![Viaje a Tokio](/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/tokyo-trip.png)

> Next month I am flying to Tokyo for a business trip. I have already booked my flight and hotel. I am meeting my colleagues at the airport at 6 AM. The plane takes off at 8 o’clock. I think I will enjoy the trip because I love travelling. I am going to visit some temples if I have time.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/reading-tokyo.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Tokyo trip"></audio>

Marca las formas: *am flying* / *am meeting* (arreglos), *takes off* (horario), *will enjoy* (predicción), *am going to visit* (intención).

---

## 8. Mini-diálogo

> What are you going to do next month?  
> I am flying to Tokyo for work.  
> Are you meeting anyone there?  
> Yes — I am meeting my colleagues at the airport at six.  
> I think I will enjoy the trip. I am going to visit some temples if I have time.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/dialogue-travel.mp3" title="🔊 Dialogue: travel plans"></audio>

---

## 9. Practica en voz alta

> I am going to visit my parents next weekend. I think it will rain tomorrow. We are flying to Rome on Friday. Wait, I will help you.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-6/practice-four.mp3" title="🔊 Practice four sentences"></audio>

---

## 10. Ejercicios

### Ejercicio 1 — Elige la forma

1. I \_\_\_\_ visit my parents next weekend. (plan)  
2. I think it \_\_\_\_ rain tomorrow.  
3. She \_\_\_\_ meeting her boss at 3 PM.  
4. Wait — I \_\_\_\_ help you.  
5. Look at the clouds! It \_\_\_\_ rain.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **am going to** · 2. **will** · 3. **is** · 4. **will** · 5. **is going to**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Arreglos y horarios

1. We \_\_\_\_ flying to Rome on Friday.  
2. They \_\_\_\_ having a meeting tomorrow at 9.  
3. The flight \_\_\_\_ at 10 AM. (*departs*)  
4. She \_\_\_\_ meeting her sister at the airport at 5.  
5. I promise I \_\_\_\_ call you when I arrive.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **are** · 2. **are** · 3. **departs** · 4. **is** · 5. **will**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Travel vocab

1. Where you wait for a plane = \_\_\_\_  
2. Document to travel abroad = \_\_\_\_  
3. Plane leaves the ground = \_\_\_\_ \_\_\_\_  
4. Reserve a room = \_\_\_\_  
5. Delay in departure = \_\_\_\_

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **airport** · 2. **passport** · 3. **takes off** · 4. **book** · 5. **delay**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Corrección

1. *I will visiting my parents next weekend.* → \_\_\_\_  
2. *Look! It will rain* (nubes negras) → más natural: \_\_\_\_  
3. *The flight is depart at 10.* → \_\_\_\_  
4. *I think I am going to enjoy* (solo opinión) → también: \_\_\_\_

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I **am going to visit**… / I **am visiting**…  
2. It **is going to** rain.  
3. The flight **departs** at 10.  
4. I think I **will** enjoy…
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Reading (Tokyo)

1. The person is flying next \_\_\_\_.  
2. They are meeting colleagues at the airport at \_\_\_\_ AM.  
3. The plane takes off at \_\_\_\_.  
4. They think they \_\_\_\_ enjoy the trip.  
5. They \_\_\_\_ going to visit temples if they have time.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **month** · 2. **6** · 3. **8** · 4. **will** · 5. **are**
</details>

---

## 11. Errores frecuentes

| Evita | Mejor |
| :--- | :--- |
| *I will to go* | I **will go** / I **am going to** go |
| *She meeting her boss tomorrow* | She **is meeting**… |
| *The flight is depart* | The flight **departs** |
| *I think it is going to rain* (solo opinión, sin evidencia) | I think it **will** rain |
| Usar *will* para todo | Mira si hay **plan**, **arreglo** o **opinión** |

---

## 12. Consejos y siguiente paso

1. Pregunta: ¿opinión / promesa? → **will**. ¿plan decidido / evidencia? → **going to**. ¿cita en la agenda? → **continuous**.  
2. Practica con tu próximo viaje real.  
3. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 6](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-6-future-will-going-to-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 6 del curso B1](/curso-b1/unit-6).

La **Unidad 7** introduce **was/were going to** (planes que no se realizaron).

---

## Resumen rápido

| Forma | Señal |
| :--- | :--- |
| will | I think · promise · Wait… · probably |
| going to | plan · intention · Look! (evidencia) |
| present continuous | Friday at 3 · airport at 6 · fixed |
| Present Simple | timetable · departs · takes off |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso B1

En la **Unidad 7** estudiarás **was/were going to**: planes e intenciones del pasado que **no ocurrieron**, con vocabulario de *plans & intentions*.

Guías y curso:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 6 B1 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-6-future-will-going-to-ejercicios-soluciones)

faqs.question: ¿Qué es una subject question?
faqs.answer: Pregunta por el sujeto de la frase. No usa do/does/did: Who called you? What happened? El verbo va en forma normal (called, happens…).

faqs.question: ¿Qué es una object question?
faqs.answer: Pregunta por el objeto (o complemento). Usa do/does/did + infinitivo: Who did you call? What do you want?

faqs.question: ¿Cómo sé si es sujeto u objeto?
faqs.answer: Mira la respuesta. Si la respuesta hace la acción (Tom called me → Who called you?), es sujeto. Si recibe la acción (I called Tom → Who did you call?), es objeto.

faqs.question: ¿Who y What sirven para ambos tipos?
faqs.answer: Sí. Who saw you? / Who did you see? y What happened? / What did you see? Which también aparece en ambos contextos.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 34 del curso A2?
faqs.answer: En el [cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-34-subject-object-questions-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la Unidad 34 del curso A2 de Linguafly: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening, speaking y writing.

content:
En la [Unidad 33](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-33-gerunds-infinitives) practicaste gerundios e infinitivos. En la **Unidad 34 del curso A2** (*Subject & Object Questions*) aprendes a preguntar por el **sujeto** o por el **objeto** — y a no mezclar las dos estructuras.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 34 — Subject & Object Questions](/curso-a2/unit-34)  
> **Antes:** [U33 — Gerundios e infinitivos](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-33-gerunds-infinitives)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 34 (A2)

- Hacer **subject questions** (*Who called you?*) **sin** *do/does/did*.
- Hacer **object questions** (*Who did you call?*) **con** *do/does/did*.
- Usar **who, what, which** en ambos tipos.
- Entender entrevistas y cuestionarios simples.
- Evitar el error típico: ~~Who did call you?~~ / ~~Who you saw?~~

![Subject and object questions](/blog/curso-a2/unit-34/a2-unit34-subject-object.png)

---

## 1. Idea clave: ¿preguntas por quién/qué hace, o por quién/qué recibe?

Frase base: **Tom called Ana.**

| Preguntas por… | Pregunta | Respuesta |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Sujeto** (quién llamó) | **Who called** Ana? | Tom. |
| **Objeto** (a quién llamó) | **Who did** Tom **call**? | Ana. |

Misma idea con *what*:

| | Pregunta | Respuesta |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Sujeto | **What happened?** | An accident. |
| Objeto | **What did** you **see**? | An accident. |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-34/who-called-you.mp3" title="🔊 Who called you?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-34/who-did-you-call.mp3" title="🔊 Who did you call?"></audio>

---

## 2. Subject questions (sin *do/does/did*)

Preguntas por el **sujeto**. El orden es como una frase afirmativa, pero empieza con *Who / What / Which…*

| Tiempo | Estructura | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Present Simple | Who/What + verbo (-s si 3ª) | **Who lives** here? **What causes** this? |
| Past Simple | Who/What + pasado | **Who saw** you? **What happened?** |
| Present Continuous | Who/What + is/are + -ing | **Who is calling**? |
| with *be* | Who/What + am/is/are/was/were | **Who is** the teacher? |

> **Who works** in this office?  
> **What makes** you happy?  
> **Which train** goes to London?

**Importante:** no pongas *do/does/did* delante del verbo principal.

~~Who did call you?~~ → **Who called you?**  
~~Who does live here?~~ → **Who lives here?**

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-34/who-lives-here.mp3" title="🔊 Who lives here?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-34/what-happened.mp3" title="🔊 What happened yesterday?"></audio>

---

## 3. Object questions (con *do/does/did*)

Preguntas por el **objeto** (o un complemento). Aquí sí usas auxiliar + infinitivo:

| Tiempo | Estructura | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Present | Who/What + do/does + sujeto + infinitivo | **Who do** you **know**? **What does** she **want**? |
| Past | Who/What + did + sujeto + infinitivo | **Who did** you **see**? **What did** they **buy**? |

> **Who did** you **call** last night?  
> **What do** you **need**?  
> **Which film did** you **watch**?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-34/what-did-you-buy.mp3" title="🔊 What did you buy?"></audio>

![Who / What two patterns](/blog/curso-a2/unit-34/a2-unit34-who-what.png)

---

## 4. Truco rápido para elegir

1. Piensa en la **respuesta**.  
2. Si la respuesta **hace** la acción → **subject question** (sin *did*).  
3. Si la respuesta **recibe** la acción / es el objeto → **object question** (con *did*).

| Situación | Pregunta |
| :--- | :--- |
| Alguien te llamó; quieres saber quién | **Who called you?** |
| Tú llamaste a alguien; quieres saber a quién | **Who did you call?** |
| Pasó algo; quieres el suceso | **What happened?** |
| Tú viste algo; quieres el objeto | **What did you see?** |

---

## 5. *Who, what, which*

| Palabra | Uso típico | Subject | Object |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Who** | personas | Who phoned you? | Who did you phone? |
| **What** | cosas / hechos | What happened? | What did you say? |
| **Which** | elección (de un grupo) | Which bus stops here? | Which bus did you take? |

> **Which** students **passed** the exam? *(subject)*  
> **Which** students **did** you **help**? *(object)*

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-34/which-bus.mp3" title="🔊 Which bus did you take?"></audio>

---

## 6. Present Simple: *does* solo en object questions

Con *he/she/it* en **object questions**:

> **What does** she **want**?  
> **Who does** Tom **like**?

En **subject questions**, la *-s* va en el verbo principal:

> **Who wants** coffee?  
> **What makes** that noise?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-34/who-wants-coffee.mp3" title="🔊 Who wants coffee?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-34/what-does-she-want.mp3" title="🔊 What does she want?"></audio>

---

## 7. Lectura y diálogo

### Lectura: un mensaje

Someone called me yesterday. **Who called** me? It was Ana. She asked about the party. **What did** she **want**? She wanted my address. **Who did** I **tell**? I told my brother. **What happened** later? We went to the café together.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-34/reading-message.mp3" title="🔊 Someone called me yesterday…"></audio>

### Diálogo: entrevista corta

**A:** **Who lives** in that flat?  
**B:** My cousin.  
**A:** **Who did** you **visit** last weekend?  
**B:** My cousin! **What happened** there?  
**A:** Nothing special — but **what did** you **eat**?  
**B:** Homemade pizza. **Who made** it? My cousin's partner.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-34/dialogue-interview.mp3" title="🔊 Who lives in that flat?"></audio>

![Interview questions](/blog/curso-a2/unit-34/a2-unit34-interview.png)

### Mini práctica (4 frases)

Who called you? Who did you call? What happened? What did you see?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-34/practice-four.mp3" title="🔊 Who called you? Who did you call?"></audio>

---

## 8. Errores frecuentes

1. **Subject + did:** ~~Who did call you?~~ → **Who called you?**  
2. **Object sin auxiliar:** ~~Who you saw?~~ → **Who did you see?**  
3. **Doble pasado:** ~~Who did you saw?~~ → **Who did you see?**  
4. ***-s* + does juntos mal:** ~~Who does wants coffee?~~ → **Who wants coffee?** / **What does she want?**  
5. **Confundir sentido:** *Who saw you?* ≠ *Who did you see?*

---

## 9. Ejercicios (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — ¿Subject (S) u Object (O)?

1. Who called you? ___  
2. Who did you call? ___  
3. What happened? ___  
4. What did you buy? ___  
5. Who lives here? ___  
6. Who do you live with? ___

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. S  
2. O  
3. S  
4. O  
5. S  
6. O  

</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Completa (*did* o nada + forma verbal)

1. Who ___ (call) you yesterday?  
2. Who ___ you ___ (call) yesterday?  
3. What ___ (happen) at school?  
4. What ___ you ___ (see)?  
5. Who ___ (want) tea?

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. called  
2. did / call  
3. happened  
4. did / see  
5. wants  

</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Reescribe como pregunta correcta

Respuesta → pregunta:

1. Tom called me. → Who _______________?  
2. I called Tom. → Who _______________?  
3. An accident happened. → What _______________?  
4. I saw an accident. → What _______________?  
5. Maria lives here. → Who _______________?

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. Who called you?  
2. Who did you call?  
3. What happened?  
4. What did you see?  
5. Who lives here?  

</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Elige la opción correcta

1. ___ you yesterday evening?  
   a) Who called  b) Who did call  c) Who you called  
2. ___ at the party?  
   a) Who you see  b) Who did you see  c) Who saw you did  
3. ___ this noise?  
   a) What does make  b) What makes  c) What did makes  
4. ___ she want?  
   a) What  b) What does  c) What do  
5. ___ the blue bus or the red one?  
   a) Which did you take  b) Which you took  c) Which took you did  

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. a  
2. b  
3. b  
4. b  
5. a  

</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Corrige el error

1. Who did call you?  
2. Who you saw at the cinema?  
3. What did happened?  
4. Who does lives here?  
5. What she want?

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. Who called you?  
2. Who did you see at the cinema?  
3. What happened?  
4. Who lives here?  
5. What does she want?  

</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Traduce al inglés

1. ¿Quién te llamó?  
2. ¿A quién llamaste?  
3. ¿Qué pasó?  
4. ¿Qué compraste?  
5. ¿Quién vive aquí?  
6. ¿Qué quiere ella?

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. Who called you?  
2. Who did you call?  
3. What happened?  
4. What did you buy?  
5. Who lives here?  
6. What does she want?  

</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Completa el diálogo

**A:** ___ (Who / phone) you this morning?  
**B:** My boss.  
**A:** ___ (What / he / want)?  
**B:** He wanted the report.  
**A:** ___ (Who / you / call) after that?  
**B:** Ana. ___ (What / happen) then? We finished the report together.

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

Who phoned  
What did he want  
Who did you call  
What happened  

</details>

### Ejercicio 8 — *Which*

1. ___ train goes to Oxford? *(subject)*  
2. ___ train did you take? *(object)*  
3. ___ students passed? *(subject)*  
4. ___ students did you help? *(object)*

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. Which  
2. Which  
3. Which  
4. Which  

*(La diferencia está en el resto de la pregunta: goes vs did you take; passed vs did you help.)*

</details>

### Ejercicio 9 — Empareja

1. Who broke the window?  
2. Who did you invite?  
3. What caused the delay?  
4. What did the delay cause?  

a) The snow.  
b) Many cancellations.  
c) Tom (he broke it).  
d) My classmates (I invited them).

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1 → c  
2 → d  
3 → a  
4 → b  

</details>

### Ejercicio 10 — Tu entrevista (8–10 preguntas)

Escribe un mini cuestionario con:

- 3 **subject questions**  
- 3 **object questions**  
- al menos un *what* y un *which*

**Modelo:** el diálogo de la sección 7.

---

## 10. Plan de estudio (25–30 minutos)

1. **5 min** — Tabla sujeto vs objeto.  
2. **8 min** — Ejercicios 1–6.  
3. **7 min** — Escucha lectura y diálogo; marca S/O.  
4. **5–8 min** — Escribe el cuestionario (Ejercicio 10) y léelo en voz alta.

### Checklist

- [ ] Sé qué es subject vs object question  
- [ ] No uso *did* en *Who called you?*  
- [ ] Uso *did* + infinitivo en *Who did you call?*  
- [ ] Domino *who / what / which* en ambos tipos  
- [ ] Puedo corregir ~~Who did call you?~~ y ~~Who you saw?~~

---

## 11. Consejos y siguiente paso

1. Practica **pares**: *Who saw you?* / *Who did you see?*  
2. Mira siempre la **respuesta** para elegir la estructura.  
3. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 34](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-34-subject-object-questions-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 34 del curso A2](/curso-a2/unit-34).

La **Unidad 35** revisa **some, any, much, many** (y cantidades A2).

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tipo | ¿Auxiliar? | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Subject | No *do/does/did* | Who called you? What happened? |
| Object | Sí *do/does/did* + base | Who did you call? What did you see? |

---

title: Some, any, much, many A2: cantidades en inglés
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 35 del curso A2: some, any, much, many y cantidades (a lot of, a few, a little), con audios y ejercicios.
description: Repasa some, any, much y many en inglés A2, con a lot of, a few y a little. Contables e incontables. Guía Unidad 35 con audios y ejercicios.
alt: Esquema de some any much many A2

faqs.question: ¿Cuándo uso some y cuándo any?
faqs.answer: Some en afirmativas y ofertas/peticiones (Would you like some tea?). Any en negativas y preguntas normales (I don't have any milk / Do you have any sugar?).

faqs.question: ¿Much o many?
faqs.answer: Many con contables en plural (many apples). Much con incontables (much water). En afirmativas informal suele preferirse a lot of.

faqs.question: ¿A lot of sirve con los dos?
faqs.answer: Sí. A lot of apples y a lot of water. Es muy útil en afirmativas en el inglés cotidiano.

faqs.question: ¿A few y a little?
faqs.answer: A few + contable plural (a few friends). A little + incontable (a little milk). Ambos significan “una pequeña cantidad” (en general positiva).

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 35 del curso A2?
faqs.answer: En el [cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-35-some-any-much-many-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la Unidad 35 del curso A2 de Linguafly: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening, speaking y writing.

content:
En la [Unidad 34](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-34-subject-object-questions) practicaste preguntas de sujeto y objeto. En la **Unidad 35 del curso A2** (*Some, Any, Much, Many*) **repasas cantidades**: cuándo decir *some* o *any*, y cómo elegir *much*, *many*, *a lot of*, *a few* y *a little*.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 35 — Some, Any, Much, Many](/curso-a2/unit-35)  
> **Antes:** [U34 — Subject & Object Questions](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-34-subject-object-questions)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 35 (A2)

- Usar **some** y **any** en afirmativas, negativas, preguntas y ofertas.
- Distinguir **much** (incontable) y **many** (contable).
- Usar **a lot of**, **a few** y **a little**.
- Preguntar con **How much…?** y **How many…?**.
- Hablar de compras, comida y cantidades cotidianas.

![Some any much many](/blog/curso-a2/unit-35/a2-unit35-some-any-much-many.png)

---

## 1. Contable vs incontable (base)

| Contable (puedes contar) | Incontable (no cuentas 1, 2, 3…) |
| :--- | :--- |
| apple**s**, egg**s**, friend**s**, book**s** | water, milk, sugar, rice, money, time |
| *many / a few / a lot of* | *much / a little / a lot of* |

> I bought **three apples**.  
> I need **some water**. *(no: ~~three waters~~ en sentido de líquido general)*

---

## 2. *Some* y *any*

| | Uso principal | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **some** | afirmativas | I have **some** bread. |
| **some** | ofertas / peticiones | Would you like **some** tea? / Can I have **some** water? |
| **any** | negativas | I don't have **any** sugar. |
| **any** | preguntas | Do you have **any** milk? |

> We need **some** eggs.  
> There isn't **any** cheese.  
> Are there **any** tomatoes?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-35/some-bread.mp3" title="🔊 I have some bread."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-35/any-milk.mp3" title="🔊 Do you have any milk?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-35/some-tea-offer.mp3" title="🔊 Would you like some tea?"></audio>

**Nota A2:** en preguntas “neutrales” usa *any*; si ofreces o pides de forma abierta, *some* suena natural.

---

## 3. *Much* y *many*

| Palabra | Con… | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **many** | contables plural | How **many** apples? / Not **many** people. |
| **much** | incontables | How **much** water? / There isn't **much** time. |

En **afirmativas** del inglés cotidiano, *much/many* a veces suenan formales o limitados; suele preferirse **a lot of**:

> I have **a lot of** friends. *(más natural que many friends en habla informal)*  
> We have **a lot of** homework.

En **negativas y preguntas**, *much/many* son muy frecuentes:

> I don't have **much** money.  
> Are there **many** students?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-35/how-many-apples.mp3" title="🔊 How many apples do you need?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-35/how-much-water.mp3" title="🔊 How much water do you drink?"></audio>

![Countable vs uncountable](/blog/curso-a2/unit-35/a2-unit35-countable.png)

---

## 4. *A lot of*, *a few*, *a little*

| Expresión | Tipo | Idea | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **a lot of** | contable e incontable | mucho / mucha cantidad | a lot of books / a lot of rice |
| **a few** | contable plural | unos pocos (en general OK) | a few friends |
| **a little** | incontable | un poco | a little milk |

> I have **a few** emails to answer.  
> There's **a little** milk in the fridge.  
> She has **a lot of** energy.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-35/a-lot-of-friends.mp3" title="🔊 I have a lot of friends."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-35/a-few-a-little.mp3" title="🔊 I have a few apples and a little cheese."></audio>

---

## 5. Mapa rápido

| Quieres decir… | Contable | Incontable |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| algo / un poco (afirm.) | some apples | some milk |
| ninguno / nada (neg.) | any apples | any milk |
| ¿hay…? | any apples? | any milk? |
| ¿cuántos / cuánta? | How many…? | How much…? |
| muchos / mucha | many / a lot of | much / a lot of |
| unos pocos / un poco | a few | a little |

---

## 6. Contenedores (vocabulario útil)

Para “contar” incontables, usa contenedores:

| Contenedor | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| a bottle of | water / milk |
| a cup of | tea / coffee |
| a kilo of | rice / sugar |
| a piece of | cake / cheese |
| a carton of | milk / juice |

> Can I have **a bottle of** water?  
> We need **two kilos of** rice.

---

## 7. Lectura y diálogo

### Lectura: lista de la compra

We need **some** bread and **some** eggs. We don't have **any** milk. How **much** cheese do we need? Just **a little**. How **many** tomatoes? **A few** — maybe four. There's **a lot of** rice already, so we don't need **any** more.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-35/reading-shopping.mp3" title="🔊 We need some bread…"></audio>

### Diálogo: en la tienda

**A:** Do you have **any** fresh bread?  
**B:** Yes — we have **some**. How **much** do you want?  
**A:** Just one loaf. And how **many** oranges are in a bag?  
**B:** Six. Would you like **some** apples too?  
**A:** Yes, please — **a few**.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-35/dialogue-shop.mp3" title="🔊 Do you have any fresh bread?"></audio>

![At the shop](/blog/curso-a2/unit-35/a2-unit35-shopping.png)

### Mini práctica (4 frases)

I have some bread. I don't have any milk. How many eggs? How much water?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-35/practice-four.mp3" title="🔊 I have some bread…"></audio>

---

## 8. Errores frecuentes

1. **Any en afirmativa normal:** ~~I have any bread.~~ → **I have some bread.**  
2. **Much + contable:** ~~much apples~~ → **many apples** / **a lot of apples**.  
3. **Many + incontable:** ~~many water~~ → **much water** / **a lot of water**.  
4. **A few + incontable:** ~~a few milk~~ → **a little milk**.  
5. **How much + plural contable:** ~~How much apples?~~ → **How many apples?**

---

## 9. Ejercicios (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — *some* o *any*

1. I bought ___ apples.  
2. We don't have ___ sugar.  
3. Do you have ___ questions?  
4. Would you like ___ coffee?  
5. There isn't ___ time.

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. some  
2. any  
3. any  
4. some  
5. any  

</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — *much* o *many*

1. How ___ eggs do we need?  
2. How ___ milk is left?  
3. There aren't ___ people here.  
4. I don't have ___ money.  
5. Are there ___ books on the shelf?

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. many  
2. much  
3. many  
4. much  
5. many  

</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — *a lot of / a few / a little*

1. She has ___ friends in Madrid. *(muchos)*  
2. Can I have ___ milk in my tea? *(un poco)*  
3. We waited ___ minutes. *(unos pocos)*  
4. There's ___ traffic today. *(mucho)*  
5. I only need ___ eggs. *(unos pocos)*

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. a lot of  
2. a little  
3. a few  
4. a lot of  
5. a few  

</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Corrige el error

1. I have any bread.  
2. How much apples do you want?  
3. There is many water.  
4. I need a few sugar.  
5. Do you have some idea? *(pregunta neutra)*

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. I have some bread.  
2. How many apples do you want?  
3. There is a lot of water. / There is much water. *(a lot of suena más natural)*  
4. I need a little sugar.  
5. Do you have any idea?  

</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Traduce al inglés

1. Tengo un poco de queso.  
2. No hay ningún tomate.  
3. ¿Cuánta agua bebes?  
4. ¿Cuántos amigos tienes?  
5. ¿Quieres un poco de té?

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. I have a little cheese. / I have some cheese.  
2. There aren't any tomatoes.  
3. How much water do you drink?  
4. How many friends do you have?  
5. Would you like some tea?  

</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Elige la opción

1. There isn't ___ rice.  
   a) some  b) any  c) many  
2. We need ___ tomatoes.  
   a) any  b) much  c) some  
3. How ___ time do we have?  
   a) many  b) much  c) few  
4. I have ___ emails to send.  
   a) a little  b) a few  c) much  
5. There's ___ noise in this street.  
   a) a lot of  b) many  c) a few  

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. b  
2. c  
3. b  
4. b  
5. a  

</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Completa el diálogo

**A:** Do we have ___ milk?  
**B:** No, we don't have ___.  
**A:** How ___ bread is left?  
**B:** Just ___. And how ___ eggs?  
**A:** ___. Maybe three.

<details>
<summary>Soluciones (modelo)</summary>

any  
any  
much  
a little  
many  
A few  

</details>

### Ejercicio 8 — Contable (C) o incontable (U)

1. apple ___  
2. water ___  
3. money ___  
4. egg ___  
5. sugar ___  
6. friend ___

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. C  
2. U  
3. U  
4. C  
5. U  
6. C  

</details>

### Ejercicio 9 — Contenedores

Completa: *bottle / cup / kilo / piece / carton*

1. a ___ of water  
2. a ___ of tea  
3. a ___ of rice  
4. a ___ of cake  
5. a ___ of milk

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. bottle  
2. cup  
3. kilo  
4. piece  
5. carton  

</details>

### Ejercicio 10 — Tu lista (8–12 líneas)

Escribe una lista de la compra o describe tu nevera. Incluye:

- *some / any*  
- *How much / How many*  
- *a lot of* + *a few* o *a little*

**Modelo:** el texto de la sección 7.

---

## 10. Plan de estudio (25–30 minutos)

1. **5 min** — Tabla some/any + much/many.  
2. **8 min** — Ejercicios 1–6.  
3. **7 min** — Escucha compra y tienda; marca cuantificadores.  
4. **5–8 min** — Escribe tu lista (Ejercicio 10) en voz alta.

### Checklist

- [ ] Uso *some* / *any* correctamente  
- [ ] Distingo *much* e *many*  
- [ ] Uso *a lot of*, *a few*, *a little*  
- [ ] Pregunto con *How much / How many*  
- [ ] Sé nombres de contenedores básicos

---

## 11. Consejos y siguiente paso

1. Aprende **pares**: *many apples / much water*; *a few / a little*.  
2. En afirmativas, practica **a lot of** — suena natural.  
3. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 35](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-35-some-any-much-many-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 35 del curso A2](/curso-a2/unit-35).

La **Unidad 36** trabaja **artículos**: *a/an*, *the* y cuando no hay artículo.

---

## Resumen rápido

| | Contable | Incontable |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| afirm. | some / a lot of / a few | some / a lot of / a little |
| neg. | any / many / a lot of | any / much / a lot of |
| ¿? | any / How many…? | any / How much…? |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A2

En la **Unidad 36** verás **Articles: A/An, The, No Article**.

Guía blog:

- [Unidad 36 — Artículos a/an/the](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-36-articles-a-an-the)

Curso:

- [Unidad 36 — Articles](/curso-a2/unit-36)

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 35 A2 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-35-some-any-much-many-ejercicios-soluciones)
- [Unidad 35 — Some, Any, Much, Many](/curso-a2/unit-35)

Guías relacionadas:

- [U34 — Subject & Object Questions](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-34-subject-object-questions)
- [Inglés A2: guía del nivel](/blog/metodos/ingles-a2)

---

## Fuentes

- CEFR/MCER — Nivel A2: https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages
- Cambridge English — A2 Key: https://www.cambridgeenglish.org/exams-and-tests/key/
