title: Clothes & Fashion A2: wear, outfit, too vs enough
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 48 del curso A2: describir ropa y outfits con wear, put on / take off y too vs enough, con audios y ejercicios.
description: Ropa y moda en inglés A2: wear, put on, take off; casual y formal; too vs enough. Guía Unidad 48 con audios, outfits y ejercicios.
alt: Esquema Clothes & Fashion A2

faqs.question: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre wear y put on?
faqs.answer: Wear = llevar puesto (estado). Put on = ponerse (acción). Take off = quitarse. I'm wearing a coat. / Put on your jacket.

faqs.question: ¿Too o enough?
faqs.answer: Too = demasiado (problema). Enough = suficiente. This shirt is too small. / This coat is warm enough.

faqs.question: ¿Clothes es singular o plural?
faqs.answer: Clothes es plural: These clothes are new. Para singular usa an item of clothing / a piece of clothing, o la prenda concreta (a shirt).

faqs.question: ¿Casual o formal?
faqs.answer: Casual = informal (jeans, trainers). Formal = elegante / de trabajo (suit, dress shirt). Smart casual está en medio.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 48 del curso A2?
faqs.answer: En el [cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-48-clothes-fashion-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la Unidad 48 del curso A2 de Linguafly practicarás vocabulario de ropa, estilo y too / enough.

content:
En la [Unidad 47](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-47-health-body) hablaste de salud. En la **Unidad 48 del curso A2** (*Clothes & Fashion*) describes **ropa, tallas y estilo**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 48 — Clothes & Fashion](/curso-a2/unit-48)  
> **Antes:** [U47 — Health & Body](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-47-health-body)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 48 (A2)

- Verbos: **wear**, **put on**, **take off**.
- Estilo: **casual**, **formal**, **outfit**.
- Detalles: **pattern**, **material**, accesorios.
- Repaso: **too** vs **enough**.
- Describir lo que llevas y si te queda bien.

![Clothes & Fashion A2](/blog/curso-a2/unit-48/a2-unit48-clothes-fashion.png)

---

## 1. Vocabulario: ropa y estilo

| Palabra | Idea | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **outfit** | conjunto / look | I love your **outfit**. |
| **casual** | informal | Jeans are **casual**. |
| **formal** | formal / elegante | A suit is **formal**. |
| **pattern** | estampado | A striped **pattern**. |
| **material** | tela / material | This **material** is soft. |
| **size** | talla | What **size** are you? |
| **fit** | quedar (talla) | It **fits** perfectly. |
| **match** | combinar | Does this scarf **match**? |

Prendas útiles: **shirt**, **T-shirt**, **jumper / sweater**, **jacket**, **coat**, **dress**, **skirt**, **trousers / pants**, **jeans**, **shoes**, **trainers / sneakers**.

Accesorios: **bag**, **belt**, **scarf**, **hat**, **glasses**, **jewellery / jewelry**.

---

## 2. Verbos: *wear*, *put on*, *take off*

| Verbo | Idea | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **wear** | llevar puesto | I **wear** jeans at the weekend. |
| **put on** | ponerse | **Put on** your coat — it's cold. |
| **take off** | quitarse | **Take off** your shoes, please. |
| **try on** | probarse | Can I **try on** this jacket? |

> What are you **wearing** today?  
> She's **wearing** a blue dress.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-48/im-wearing-jeans.mp3" title="🔊 I'm wearing jeans."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-48/put-on-your-coat.mp3" title="🔊 Put on your coat."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-48/take-off-your-shoes.mp3" title="🔊 Take off your shoes."></audio>

---

## 3. *Too* vs *enough* (repaso)

| Forma | Idea | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **too** + adjective | demasiado | This shirt is **too small**. |
| adjective + **enough** | suficiente | This coat is **warm enough**. |
| **not** + adjective + **enough** | no suficiente | These shoes aren't **comfortable enough**. |
| **too much / too many** | demasiado (cantidad) | This bag costs **too much**. |

> These trousers are **too long**.  
> Is this jacket **smart enough** for work?

![too vs enough](/blog/curso-a2/unit-48/a2-unit48-too-enough.png)

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-48/too-small.mp3" title="🔊 This shirt is too small."></audio>

---

## 4. Describir un outfit

Orden útil:

1. Estilo general (*casual / formal*)  
2. Prendas principales  
3. Colores / pattern / material  
4. Accesorios  
5. Opinión (*It fits well. / It's comfortable.*)

> Today I'm wearing a **casual outfit**: a white **T-shirt**, blue **jeans** and black **trainers**. I've got a grey **scarf**. It's comfortable and not **too** warm.

---

## 5. Mapa rápido

| Quieres decir… | Usa… | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Llevar puesto | wear | I'm wearing a dress. |
| Ponerse / quitarse | put on / take off | Put on your jumper. |
| Demasiado | too + adj | Too expensive. |
| Suficiente | adj + enough | Big enough. |
| Estilo | casual / formal | A formal outfit. |

![Outfit scene](/blog/curso-a2/unit-48/a2-unit48-outfit-scene.png)

---

## 6. Lectura y diálogo

### Lectura — Dress code tip

For the office, wear a **smart** or **formal outfit**: a shirt, dark trousers and clean shoes. Avoid **casual** clothes like old jeans or trainers. If it's cold, **put on** a jacket. Check that everything **fits** well — not **too tight** and not **too loose**. A simple bag and a belt are enough accessories.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-48/reading-dress-code.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Dress code tip"></audio>

### Diálogo — Choosing an outfit

**Sam:** What should I **wear** to the party?  
**Alex:** Something **smart casual**. Not too formal.  
**Sam:** Are these jeans OK?  
**Alex:** Yes — but that shirt is **too bright**. Try the blue one.  
**Sam:** Is this jacket **warm enough**?  
**Alex:** Perfect. **Put on** those black shoes and you're ready.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-48/dialogue-outfit.mp3" title="🔊 Dialogue: Choosing an outfit"></audio>

### Mini práctica

1. I'm ___ a red jumper. *(llevar)*  
2. ___ on your coat.  
3. These shoes are ___ small.  
4. Is this scarf warm ___ ?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-48/practice-four.mp3" title="🔊 Practice four sentences"></audio>

---

## 7. Errores frecuentes

1. ~~I put a jacket.~~ → **I put on** a jacket. / **I'm wearing** a jacket.  
2. ~~I wear on a hat.~~ → **I put on** a hat. / **I wear** a hat.  
3. ~~This is enough big.~~ → **This is big enough.**  
4. ~~Too much small~~ → **too small**  
5. ~~A clothes~~ → **clothes** (plural) / **a piece of clothing**  
6. ~~It fits to me.~~ → **It fits me.** / **It fits.**

---

## 8. Ejercicios (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — Empareja

1. casual  
2. formal  
3. put on  
4. take off  
5. outfit  

a) remove clothes  
b) smart / for work or events  
c) complete look  
d) relaxed style  
e) dress yourself in something

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1 → d  
2 → b  
3 → e  
4 → a  
5 → c  

</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — *wear*, *put on* o *take off*

1. It's hot — ___ your jumper.  
2. She ___ glasses every day.  
3. Please ___ your coat before you go out.  
4. What are you ___ today?

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. take off  
2. wears  
3. put on  
4. wearing  

</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — *too* o *enough*

1. This dress is ___ expensive.  
2. Are these shoes comfortable ___ ?  
3. The jacket isn't warm ___ for winter.  
4. Those trousers are ___ long.

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. too  
2. enough  
3. enough  
4. too  

</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Corrige el error

1. I put a scarf.  
2. This shirt is enough big.  
3. These clothes is new.  
4. It fits to me well.  
5. Too much tight jeans.

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. I put on a scarf. / I'm wearing a scarf.  
2. This shirt is big enough.  
3. These clothes are new.  
4. It fits me well. / It fits well.  
5. These jeans are too tight.  

</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Traduce al inglés

1. Llevo vaqueros.  
2. Ponte el abrigo.  
3. Quítate los zapatos.  
4. Esta camiseta es demasiado pequeña.  
5. ¿Este jersey es lo bastante abrigado?

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. I'm wearing jeans. / I wear jeans.  
2. Put on your coat.  
3. Take off your shoes.  
4. This T-shirt is too small.  
5. Is this jumper warm enough?  

</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Completa el diálogo

**A:** What are you ___ ?  
**B:** A casual ___: jeans and a white T-shirt.  
**A:** Is that jacket warm ___ ?  
**B:** No — it's ___ thin. I'll ___ on a coat.

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

wearing  
outfit  
enough  
too  
put  

</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Estilo

1. A suit for a job interview → ___  
2. Jeans and trainers at home → ___  
3. Stripes on a shirt → ___  
4. Cotton or wool → ___

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. formal (or smart)  
2. casual  
3. pattern  
4. material  

</details>

### Ejercicio 8 — Ordena

1. wearing / I'm / a / blue / dress  
2. on / Put / your / shoes  
3. small / too / is / This / shirt

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. I'm wearing a blue dress.  
2. Put on your shoes.  
3. This shirt is too small.  

</details>

### Ejercicio 9 — Dress code True / False

> For the office, wear a smart or formal outfit. Avoid old jeans or trainers.

1. Old jeans are perfect for the office.  
2. A formal outfit is a good idea for work.  
3. Trainers are recommended in the tip.

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. False  
2. True  
3. False  

</details>

### Ejercicio 10 — Tu outfit (8–12 líneas)

Describe lo que llevas (o un outfit ideal). Incluye:

- *wear / wearing*  
- 1 *put on* o *take off*  
- *casual* o *formal*  
- 1 *too* y 1 *enough*  
- 1 accesorio

**Modelo:** la lectura / el diálogo de la sección 6.

---

## 9. Plan de estudio (25–30 minutos)

1. **5 min** — Vocabulario + *wear / put on / take off*  
2. **8 min** — Ejercicios 1–6.  
3. **7 min** — Escucha dress code y diálogo.  
4. **5–8 min** — Ejercicio 10.

### Checklist

- [ ] Distingo *wear* / *put on* / *take off*  
- [ ] Uso *casual* y *formal*  
- [ ] Aplico *too* vs *enough*  
- [ ] Describo un *outfit* con prendas y accesorios  
- [ ] Evito *put a jacket* y *enough big*

---

## 10. Consejos y siguiente paso

1. Describe tu ropa en voz alta cada mañana.  
2. Mira etiquetas: *cotton*, *wool*, *size*, *machine wash*.  
3. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 48](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-48-clothes-fashion-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 48 del curso A2](/curso-a2/unit-48).

La **Unidad 49** es **People & Relationships** (personas y relaciones).

---

## Resumen rápido

| | Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Llevar | wear | I'm wearing jeans. |
| Ponerse | put on | Put on your coat. |
| Quitarse | take off | Take off your shoes. |
| Demasiado | too + adj | Too small. |
| Suficiente | adj + enough | Warm enough. |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A2

En la **Unidad 49** verás **People & Relationships**.

- [Unidad 49 — People & Relationships](/curso-a2/unit-49)

title: People & Relationships A2: look like, be like y personalidad

faqs.question: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre look like y be like?
faqs.answer: Look like = parecerse físicamente (apariencia). Be like = cómo es de carácter. She looks like her mother. / What's she like? She's friendly.

faqs.question: ¿How does she look o What does she look like?
faqs.answer: Para apariencia: What does she look like? How does she look? suele preguntar por el aspecto ahora (cansada, elegante…).

faqs.question: ¿Cómo digo “la conozco desde hace años”?
faqs.answer: I've known her for years. / I've known him since 2019. Present Perfect + for/since.

faqs.question: ¿Neighbour o neighbor?
faqs.answer: Neighbour es británico; neighbor americano. Ambos se entienden.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 49 del curso A2?

content:
En la [Unidad 48](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-48-clothes-fashion) describiste ropa. En la **Unidad 49 del curso A2** (*People & Relationships*) describes **personas y relaciones**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 49 — People & Relationships](/curso-a2/unit-49)  
> **Antes:** [U48 — Clothes & Fashion](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-48-clothes-fashion)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 49 (A2)

- **Look like** (apariencia) vs **be like** (carácter).
- Vocabulario de relaciones: **friend**, **colleague**, **neighbour**.
- Adjetivos de **personalidad**.
- Comparar personas (*taller*, *more friendly*).
- **Have known** + *for/since* (cuánto tiempo conoces a alguien).

![People & Relationships A2](/blog/curso-a2/unit-49/a2-unit49-people-relationships.png)

---

## 1. Vocabulario: relaciones

| Palabra | Idea | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **friend** | amigo/a | She's my best **friend**. |
| **colleague** | compañero/a de trabajo | He's a **colleague** from work. |
| **neighbour** | vecino/a | Our **neighbours** are quiet. |
| **classmate** | compañero/a de clase | We were **classmates**. |
| **partner** | pareja / socio | This is my **partner**. |
| **relationship** | relación | We have a good **relationship**. |
| **get on (well) with** | llevarse bien | I **get on well with** my colleagues. |

> I've got a lot of friends, but only a few close ones.

---

## 2. *Look like* vs *be like*

| Forma | Pregunta / uso | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **look like** | apariencia física | She **looks like** her sister. |
| **What does he look like?** | ¿cómo es físicamente? | He's tall with dark hair. |
| **be like** | carácter / personalidad | What's he **like**? He's funny. |
| **What's she like?** | ¿cómo es de carácter? | She's kind and patient. |

> He **looks like** a film star, but he's actually very shy.  
> What's your new boss **like**? — She's strict but fair.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-49/looks-like.mp3" title="🔊 She looks like her sister."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-49/whats-she-like.mp3" title="🔊 What's she like?"></audio>

---

## 3. Adjetivos de personalidad

| Adjetivo | Idea | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **friendly** | amable / sociable | He's very **friendly**. |
| **shy** | tímido | She's a bit **shy**. |
| **funny** | divertido | My uncle is **funny**. |
| **kind** | bueno / amable | They're **kind** people. |
| **hard-working** | trabajador | She's **hard-working**. |
| **quiet** | callado | He's **quiet**. |
| **talkative** | hablador | She's very **talkative**. |
| **patient** | paciente | You need to be **patient**. |
| **honest** | sincero | He's **honest**. |
| **lazy** | vago | Don't be **lazy**! |

![Personality](/blog/curso-a2/unit-49/a2-unit49-personality.png)

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-49/shes-friendly.mp3" title="🔊 She's friendly and hard-working."></audio>

---

## 4. Comparar personas + *have known*

Comparativos (repaso):

> My brother is **taller than** me.  
> She's **more talkative than** her sister.  
> He's the **friendliest** person I know.

Tiempo que conoces a alguien — **Present Perfect**:

| Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| have/has known + for | I've **known** her **for** ten years. |
| have/has known + since | We've **known** each other **since** school. |

> How long have you known him? — **I've known** him **since** 2018.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-49/have-known.mp3" title="🔊 I've known her for ten years."></audio>

---

## 5. Mapa rápido

| Quieres decir… | Usa… | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Apariencia | look like | He looks like his dad. |
| Carácter | be like / What's … like? | What's she like? |
| Relación | friend / colleague… | She's my neighbour. |
| Tiempo | have known + for/since | I've known him for years. |
| Comparar | -er / more … than | More friendly than… |

![Friends scene](/blog/curso-a2/unit-49/a2-unit49-friends-scene.png)

---

## 6. Lectura y diálogo

### Lectura — My neighbour Maya

Maya is my **neighbour**. I've **known** her **for** three years. She **looks like** her mother — same smile and dark hair. What's she **like**? She's **friendly**, **funny** and very **kind**. We **get on well**. She's a bit **quieter** than me, but we talk every weekend over coffee.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-49/reading-maya.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: My neighbour Maya"></audio>

### Diálogo — Talking about a colleague

**Leo:** Have you met the new **colleague**?  
**Nora:** Yes. What's he **like**?  
**Leo:** He's **hard-working** and **honest**. A bit **shy** at first.  
**Nora:** What does he **look like**?  
**Leo:** Tall, short hair. He **looks like** my cousin, actually.  
**Nora:** How long have you **known** him?  
**Leo:** Only **for** two weeks — but we already **get on** well.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-49/dialogue-colleague.mp3" title="🔊 Dialogue: Talking about a colleague"></audio>

### Mini práctica

1. She ___ like her sister. *(apariencia)*  
2. What's he ___ ? *(carácter)*  
3. I've ___ her for five years.  
4. He's more ___ than his brother. *(friendly)*

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-49/practice-four.mp3" title="🔊 Practice four sentences"></audio>

---

## 7. Errores frecuentes

1. ~~How is she like?~~ → **What's she like?**  
2. ~~She is look like her mum.~~ → **She looks like** her mum.  
3. ~~I know her for 10 years.~~ → **I've known** her for 10 years.  
4. ~~What does she like?~~ *(gustos)* ≠ apariencia/carácter → para gustos OK; para carácter: **What's she like?**  
5. ~~He is more tall than me.~~ → **He's taller than** me.  
6. ~~We have a good relation.~~ → **relationship** (más natural aquí)

---

## 8. Ejercicios (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — Empareja

1. colleague  
2. neighbour  
3. look like  
4. be like / What's … like?  
5. get on well with  

a) personality  
b) appearance  
c) person next door  
d) have a good relationship with  
e) person you work with

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1 → e  
2 → c  
3 → b  
4 → a  
5 → d  

</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — *look like* o *be like*

1. She ___ her father — same eyes.  
2. What's your teacher ___ ? — Strict but fair.  
3. What does he ___ ? — Short and blonde.  
4. He doesn't ___ his brother at all. *(apariencia)*

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. looks like  
2. like  
3. look like  
4. look like  

</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Personalidad

Elige: friendly / shy / funny / hard-working / talkative

1. She never stops speaking → ___  
2. He doesn't talk much with new people → ___  
3. She always helps others and smiles → ___  
4. He works late every day → ___  
5. Everyone laughs with him → ___

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. talkative  
2. shy  
3. friendly (or kind)  
4. hard-working  
5. funny  

</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — *have known*

1. I ___ (know) Ana ___ 2015.  
2. We ___ (know) each other ___ ten years.  
3. How long ___ you ___ (know) him?

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. have known / since  
2. have known / for  
3. have / known  

</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Corrige el error

1. How is she like?  
2. She is look like her mum.  
3. I know him for three years.  
4. He is more funny than me.  
5. What's he look like? *(carácter — corrige la pregunta)*

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. What's she like?  
2. She looks like her mum.  
3. I've known him for three years.  
4. He's funnier than me.  
5. What's he like?  

</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Traduce al inglés

1. Se parece a su hermana.  
2. ¿Cómo es él (de carácter)?  
3. La conozco desde hace cinco años.  
4. Nos llevamos bien.  
5. Es más tímido que yo.

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. She looks like her sister.  
2. What's he like?  
3. I've known her for five years.  
4. We get on well.  
5. He's shyer / more shy than me.  

</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Completa el diálogo

**A:** Have you met my new ___ ?  
**B:** Not yet. What's she ___ ?  
**A:** Very ___ and kind.  
**B:** What does she ___ like?  
**A:** Tall, long hair. I've ___ her ___ Monday.

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

colleague (or neighbour / friend)  
like  
friendly  
look  
known / since  

</details>

### Ejercicio 8 — Ordena

1. like / looks / She / her / mother  
2. she / What's / like / ?  
3. known / I've / him / for / years

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. She looks like her mother.  
2. What's she like?  
3. I've known him for years.  

</details>

### Ejercicio 9 — Comparativos

1. My sister is ___ (friendly) than me.  
2. Tom is ___ (tall) than Sam.  
3. She's the ___ (kind) person in the office.

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. more friendly / friendlier  
2. taller  
3. kindest  

</details>

### Ejercicio 10 — Tu descripción (8–12 líneas)

Describe a una persona importante para ti. Incluye:

- relación (*friend / colleague / neighbour…*)  
- *look like* o apariencia  
- *What's … like?* + 2 adjetivos de personalidad  
- *I've known … for/since*  
- 1 comparativo

**Modelo:** la lectura de la sección 6.

---

## 9. Plan de estudio (25–30 minutos)

1. **5 min** — *look like* / *be like* + vocabulario  
2. **8 min** — Ejercicios 1–6.  
3. **7 min** — Escucha lectura y diálogo.  
4. **5–8 min** — Ejercicio 10.

### Checklist

- [ ] Distingo *look like* y *What's … like?*  
- [ ] Uso *friend / colleague / neighbour*  
- [ ] Describo personalidad con adjetivos  
- [ ] Uso *I've known … for/since*  
- [ ] Evito *How is she like?* e *I know her for…*

---

## 10. Consejos y siguiente paso

1. Describe a alguien de tu entorno en voz alta (1 minuto).  
2. Practica el contraste: *looks like* vs *is like*.  
3. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 49](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-49-people-relationships-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 49 del curso A2](/curso-a2/unit-49).

La **Unidad 50** es el **Module 5 Review** (repaso del módulo).

---

## Resumen rápido

| | Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Apariencia | look like | She looks like her mum. |
| Carácter | What's … like? | What's he like? |
| Relación | friend / colleague… | My neighbour |
| Tiempo | have known + for/since | I've known her for years. |
| Comparar | -er / more … than | More friendly than… |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A2

En la **Unidad 50** harás el **Module 5 Review**.

Curso:

- [Unidad 50 — Module 5 Review](/curso-a2/unit-50)

Guías relacionadas:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 49 A2 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-49-people-relationships-ejercicios-soluciones)
- [U48 — Clothes & Fashion](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-48-clothes-fashion)
- [U11 — Present Perfect](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-11-present-perfect-introduccion)
- [U5 — Comparativos](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-5-comparativos-er-more-than)
- [Inglés A2: guía del nivel](/blog/metodos/ingles-a2)

---

faqs.question: ¿Qué se repasa en la Unidad 50 del curso A2?
faqs.answer: El Módulo 5 completo (U41–U49): travel & transport, accommodation, holiday activities, weather, entertainment, shopping, health, clothes y people & relationships.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo pregunto el tiempo atmosférico?
faqs.answer: What's the weather like? Respuestas típicas: It's sunny / rainy / cloudy. Predicciones: It's going to rain / It will be cold.

faqs.question: ¿Look like o What's … like?
faqs.answer: Look like = apariencia. What's she like? = carácter. She looks like her sister. / She's friendly.

faqs.question: ¿Refund o exchange?
faqs.answer: Refund = devolución del dinero. Exchange = cambiar el producto (talla, color…).

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 50 del curso A2?

content:
En la [Unidad 49](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-49-people-relationships) describiste personas. La **Unidad 50 del curso A2** (*Module 5 Review*) **integra** todo el Módulo 5 (U41–U49) en un solo repaso.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 50 — Module 5 Review](/curso-a2/unit-50)  
> **Antes:** [U49 — People & Relationships](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-49-people-relationships)

---

## Qué repasarás en la Unidad 50 (A2)

- **Travel & transport** (U41) y **accommodation** (U42)
- **Holiday activities** (U43) y **weather** (U44)
- **Entertainment & media** (U45) y **shopping** (U46)
- **Health & body** (U47) y **clothes & fashion** (U48)
- **People & relationships** (U49)

![Module 5 Review A2](/blog/curso-a2/unit-50/a2-unit50-module-5-review.png)

---

## 1. Mapa del Módulo 5

| U | Tema | Ejemplo clave |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 41 | Travel & Transport | I go **by train**. / How do I **get to**…? |
| 42 | Accommodation | I'd like to **book** a **double room**. |
| 43 | Holiday Activities | We **went sightseeing**. / Have you ever…? |
| 44 | The Weather | It's **sunny**. / It's **going to rain**. |
| 45 | Entertainment & Media | I **like watching** series. / I **prefer** comedies. |
| 46 | Shopping & Services | **I'm looking for…** / **How much** is it? |
| 47 | Health & Body | I **have a headache**. / You **should** rest. |
| 48 | Clothes & Fashion | I'm **wearing** jeans. / It's **too** small. |
| 49 | People & Relationships | She **looks like** her mum. / What's she **like**? |

![Checklist](/blog/curso-a2/unit-50/a2-unit50-checklist.png)

---

## 2. Viaje y alojamiento (U41–U42)

| Idea | Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Transporte | by + medium | I travel **by bus**. |
| Coger | take the… | **Take the train** to the airport. |
| Llegar | get to / arrive at | How do I **get to** the hotel? |
| Reservar | book / check in / check out | We **checked in** at 3. |
| Habitación | single / double | A **double room**, please. |

Guías: [U41](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-41-travel-transport) · [U42](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-42-accommodation)

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-50/by-train.mp3" title="🔊 I go by train."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-50/book-a-room.mp3" title="🔊 I'd like to book a double room."></audio>

---

## 3. Vacaciones y tiempo (U43–U44)

| Idea | Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Actividades | sightseeing / hiking… | We went **sightseeing**. |
| Experiencia | Present Perfect | **Have you ever** been hiking? |
| Tiempo ahora | It's + adj / -ing | It's **cloudy**. / It's **raining**. |
| Predicción | going to / will | It's **going to rain**. / It **will be** sunny. |

Guías: [U43](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-43-holiday-activities) · [U44](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-44-the-weather)

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-50/whats-the-weather-like.mp3" title="🔊 What's the weather like?"></audio>

---

## 4. Ocio, compras y salud (U45–U47)

| Idea | Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Medios | watch / listen to / read | I **listen to** music. |
| Gustos | like + -ing / prefer | I **prefer** comedies **to** dramas. |
| Tienda | Can I help you? / How much…? | **I'm looking for** a jacket. |
| Devolución | refund / exchange | I'd like a **refund**. |
| Salud | have a… / should | I **have a cold**. You **should** rest. |

Guías: [U45](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-45-entertainment-media) · [U46](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-46-shopping-services) · [U47](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-47-health-body)

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-50/im-looking-for.mp3" title="🔊 I'm looking for a jacket."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-50/you-should-rest.mp3" title="🔊 You should rest."></audio>

---

## 5. Ropa y personas (U48–U49)

| Idea | Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Llevar | wear / put on / take off | I'm **wearing** a coat. |
| Talla | too / enough | It's **too** tight. / It's big **enough**. |
| Apariencia | look like | He **looks like** his dad. |
| Carácter | What's … like? | She's **friendly**. |
| Tiempo | have known + for/since | I've **known** her **for** years. |

Guías: [U48](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-48-clothes-fashion) · [U49](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-49-people-relationships)

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-50/whats-she-like.mp3" title="🔊 What's she like?"></audio>

![Trip scene](/blog/curso-a2/unit-50/a2-unit50-trip-scene.png)

---

## 6. Lectura integrada

### Reading — A weekend in Lisbon

Last Friday we **took the train** to Lisbon and **checked in** at a small hotel. On Saturday it was **sunny**, so we went **sightseeing**. In the evening we **watched** a film — I **prefer comedies** to dramas. On Sunday I bought a scarf: “**How much is it?**” — €12. Later I had a **headache**, so my friend said: “You **should** rest.” Our **neighbour** in the hotel was **friendly**. I've **known** my travel partner **for** ten years — we always **get on** well.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-50/reading-lisbon.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: A weekend in Lisbon"></audio>

### Diálogo — Planning the day

**Mia:** What's the weather **like** today?  
**Omar:** It's **going to be** hot. **Put on** a hat.  
**Mia:** Shall we go **by bus** to the museum?  
**Omar:** Yes. Then I'd like to **watch** a documentary.  
**Mia:** OK — but first **I'm looking for** sunscreen at the pharmacy.  
**Omar:** Good idea. If you feel sick, you **should** drink water.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-50/dialogue-plan.mp3" title="🔊 Dialogue: Planning the day"></audio>

### Mini práctica

1. I go ___ train.  
2. It's ___ to rain.  
3. I'm ___ for a bag.  
4. What's she ___ ?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-50/practice-four.mp3" title="🔊 Practice four sentences"></audio>

---

## 7. Errores frecuentes del módulo

1. ~~I go with train.~~ → **I go by train.**  
2. ~~What's the weather?~~ → **What's the weather like?**  
3. ~~listen music~~ → **listen to music**  
4. ~~How many is it?~~ *(precio)* → **How much is it?**  
5. ~~I have headache.~~ → **I have a headache.**  
6. ~~I put a jacket.~~ → **I put on** a jacket.  
7. ~~How is she like?~~ → **What's she like?**  
8. ~~I know her for years.~~ → **I've known** her for years.

---

## 8. Ejercicios mixtos (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — Empareja unidad y frase

1. Travel  
2. Weather  
3. Shopping  
4. Health  
5. People  

a) I'd like a refund.  
b) You should rest.  
c) Take the bus.  
d) What's she like?  
e) It's going to rain.

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1 → c  
2 → e  
3 → a  
4 → b  
5 → d  

</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Completa

1. How do I ___ to the station?  
2. I'd like to ___ a single room.  
3. Have you ever ___ sightseeing in Rome?  
4. What's the weather ___ ?

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. get  
2. book  
3. been (or gone)  
4. like  

</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Ocio y gustos

1. I ___ films at the weekend. *(watch)*  
2. I listen ___ music every day.  
3. I like ___ (watch) series.  
4. I prefer comedies ___ dramas.

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. watch  
2. to  
3. watching  
4. to  

</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Compras y ropa

1. ___ I help you?  
2. I'm ___ for size M.  
3. This shirt is ___ small.  
4. ___ on your coat — it's cold.

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. Can  
2. looking  
3. too  
4. Put  

</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Salud y personas

1. I have ___ fever.  
2. You ___ go to work today. *(shouldn't)*  
3. She ___ like her mother. *(apariencia)*  
4. I've ___ him since 2020.

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. a  
2. shouldn't  
3. looks  
4. known  

</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Corrige el error

1. I go with bus.  
2. Listen music now.  
3. How many is this bag?  
4. I have cold.  
5. How is he like?

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. I go by bus.  
2. Listen to music now.  
3. How much is this bag?  
4. I have a cold.  
5. What's he like?  

</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Traduce al inglés

1. Voy en tren.  
2. Va a llover.  
3. Busco una chaqueta.  
4. Deberías descansar.  
5. ¿Cómo es ella (de carácter)?

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. I go by train.  
2. It's going to rain.  
3. I'm looking for a jacket.  
4. You should rest.  
5. What's she like?  

</details>

### Ejercicio 8 — Elige la mejor opción

1. We ___ at the hotel at 4.  
   a) arrived  b) got  c) took  
2. I'd like a ___, please. *(dinero de vuelta)*  
   a) exchange  b) refund  c) receipt  
3. These jeans aren't big ___.  
   a) too  b) enough  c) very

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. a  
2. b  
3. b  

</details>

### Ejercicio 9 — Lectura True / False

> Last Friday we took the train to Lisbon and checked in at a small hotel. On Saturday it was sunny, so we went sightseeing.

1. They travelled by train.  
2. They arrived at a hostel.  
3. Saturday was good for outdoor activities.

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. True  
2. False (hotel)  
3. True  

</details>

### Ejercicio 10 — Tu relato de viaje (10–14 líneas)

Escribe sobre un viaje o fin de semana. Incluye al menos:

- transporte (*by / take / get to*)  
- alojamiento o actividad  
- 1 frase del tiempo  
- 1 de ocio o compras  
- 1 de salud **o** ropa **o** personas  
- 1 *should* / *too* / *prefer* / *I've known*

**Modelo:** la lectura de la sección 6.

---

## 9. Plan de estudio (30–35 minutos)

1. **5 min** — Mapa del módulo (sección 1).  
2. **10 min** — Ejercicios 1–6.  
3. **8 min** — Escucha lectura y diálogo.  
4. **7–10 min** — Ejercicio 10.

### Checklist

- [ ] Viaje: *by / take / get to / arrive at*  
- [ ] Tiempo: *It's…* / *going to* / *will*  
- [ ] Ocio: *watch / listen to / like -ing / prefer*  
- [ ] Compras: *looking for / How much / refund*  
- [ ] Salud / ropa / personas: *should*, *too/enough*, *look like / What's … like?*

---

## 10. Consejos y siguiente paso

1. Reescribe el relato de Lisboa con tus datos.  
2. Repasa las guías U41–U49 donde falles más.  
3. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 50](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-50-module-5-review-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 50 del curso A2](/curso-a2/unit-50).

La **Unidad 51** abre el Módulo 6: **Making Suggestions**.

---

## Resumen rápido

| Bloque | Formas clave |
| :--- | :--- |
| Viaje / hotel | by, take, get to, book, check in |
| Vacaciones / tiempo | sightseeing, It's…, going to / will |
| Ocio / compras | watch, listen to, prefer, How much…? |
| Salud / ropa | have a…, should, wear, too / enough |
| Personas | look like, What's … like?, have known |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A2

En la **Unidad 51** verás **Making Suggestions**.

- [Unidad 51 — Making Suggestions](/curso-a2/unit-51)

Guías del módulo:

title: Making Suggestions A2: Shall we…?, Let's…, How about…?
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 51 del curso A2: hacer y responder sugerencias con Shall we, Let's, Why don't we, How about y Would you like to, con audios y ejercicios.
description: Haz sugerencias en inglés A2: Shall we…?, Let's…, Why don't we…?, How about…? y Would you like to…? Guía Unidad 51 con audios, planes y ejercicios.
alt: Esquema Making Suggestions A2

faqs.question: ¿Shall we o Let's?
faqs.answer: Let's + verbo = sugerencia directa (Let's go!). Shall we + verbo? = más pregunta/invitación (Shall we go?). Ambos son comunes en A2.

faqs.question: ¿How about lleva gerundio o infinitivo?
faqs.answer: How about + -ing / noun: How about going to the cinema? / How about a coffee? No uses to después de How about.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo rechazo una sugerencia con educación?
faqs.answer: Sorry, I can't. / I'd love to, but… / Maybe another day. Evita un No seco.

faqs.question: ¿Would you like to es sugerencia o oferta?
faqs.answer: Sirve para invitar o sugerir un plan: Would you like to come with us? También aparece en ofertas (Would you like a drink?).

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 51 del curso A2?
faqs.answer: En el [cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-51-making-suggestions-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la Unidad 51 del curso A2 de Linguafly practicarás sugerencias y respuestas a planes.

content:
Tras el [repaso del Módulo 5](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-50-module-5-review), el **Módulo 6** empieza con la **Unidad 51 del curso A2** (*Making Suggestions*): **proponer planes** y **responder**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 51 — Making Suggestions](/curso-a2/unit-51)  
> **Antes:** [U50 — Module 5 Review](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-50-module-5-review)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 51 (A2)

- Formas: **Shall we…?**, **Let's…**, **Why don't we…?**, **How about…?**
- Invitaciones: **Would you like to…?**
- Respuestas: aceptar, dudar, rechazar con educación.
- Vocabulario de **planes y actividades en grupo**.
- Entender invitaciones y producir un mini diálogo de planes.

![Making Suggestions A2](/blog/curso-a2/unit-51/a2-unit51-making-suggestions.png)

---

## 1. Formas clave para sugerir

| Forma | Estructura | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Shall we…?** | Shall we + verbo base | **Shall we** go to the park? |
| **Let's…** | Let's + verbo base | **Let's** have lunch. |
| **Why don't we…?** | Why don't we + verbo base | **Why don't we** watch a film? |
| **How about…?** | How about + -ing / noun | **How about** meeting at 6? |
| **Would you like to…?** | Would you like to + verbo | **Would you like to** come? |

> **Shall we** take the bus?  
> **Let's** stay at home.  
> **How about** a pizza?

![Ways to suggest](/blog/curso-a2/unit-51/a2-unit51-suggest-forms.png)

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-51/shall-we-go.mp3" title="🔊 Shall we go to the park?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-51/lets-have-lunch.mp3" title="🔊 Let's have lunch."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-51/how-about-meeting.mp3" title="🔊 How about meeting at six?"></audio>

---

## 2. *Would you like to…?* (invitar)

Más suave / educado para invitar:

> **Would you like to** come with us?  
> **Would you like to** see a film tonight?

Relacionado con gustos/pedidos: [Would like vs Like](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-37-would-like-vs-like).

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-51/would-you-like-to.mp3" title="🔊 Would you like to come with us?"></audio>

---

## 3. Responder a una sugerencia

| Tipo | Frases |
| :--- | :--- |
| Aceptar | **Yes, great!** / **Good idea.** / **I'd love to.** / **Sure.** |
| Dudar | **Maybe.** / **I'm not sure.** / **What time?** |
| Rechazar (educado) | **Sorry, I can't.** / **I'd love to, but I'm busy.** / **Maybe another day.** |

> A: Shall we go shopping?  
> B: **I'd love to, but** I have to study.

---

## 4. Vocabulario de planes

| Actividad | Ejemplo de sugerencia |
| :--- | :--- |
| go for a walk | Let's **go for a walk**. |
| have a coffee | Shall we **have a coffee**? |
| see a film / go to the cinema | Why don't we **see a film**? |
| hang out | How about **hanging out** on Saturday? |
| stay in | Let's **stay in** tonight. |
| meet up | Shall we **meet up** at 5? |

---

## 5. Mapa rápido

| Quieres… | Usa… | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Sugerir (directo) | Let's… | Let's go! |
| Preguntar plan | Shall we…? | Shall we leave now? |
| Alternativa suave | Why don't we…? / How about…? | How about pizza? |
| Invitar | Would you like to…? | Would you like to join us? |
| Aceptar / rechazar | Great / Sorry, I can't | I'd love to, but… |

![Plans scene](/blog/curso-a2/unit-51/a2-unit51-plans-scene.png)

---

## 6. Lectura y diálogo

### Lectura — Weekend plans

**Shall we** do something this weekend? **Let's** go to the beach on Saturday if the weather is good. **Why don't we** take the train at 9? **How about** inviting Lara too? **Would you like to** bring some sandwiches? If it rains, **let's** stay in and watch a series instead.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-51/reading-weekend.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Weekend plans"></audio>

### Diálogo — Making plans

**Eva:** **Shall we** go to the cinema tonight?  
**Nico:** **I'd love to, but** I finish work late.  
**Eva:** **How about** tomorrow?  
**Nico:** **Good idea.** **Would you like to** meet at 7?  
**Eva:** Sure. **Let's** have a coffee first.  
**Nico:** Perfect.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-51/dialogue-plans.mp3" title="🔊 Dialogue: Making plans"></audio>

### Mini práctica

1. ___ we go for a walk?  
2. ___ have pizza.  
3. How ___ meeting at 6?  
4. Would you ___ to come?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-51/practice-four.mp3" title="🔊 Practice four sentences"></audio>

---

## 7. Errores frecuentes

1. ~~Let's to go.~~ → **Let's go.**  
2. ~~Shall we to eat?~~ → **Shall we eat?**  
3. ~~How about to go?~~ → **How about going?**  
4. ~~Why we don't go?~~ → **Why don't we go?**  
5. ~~Would you like come?~~ → **Would you like to come?**  
6. ~~No.~~ *(seco)* → **Sorry, I can't.** / **I'd love to, but…**

---

## 8. Ejercicios (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — Empareja

1. Let's…  
2. Shall we…?  
3. How about…?  
4. Would you like to…?  
5. I'd love to, but…  

a) polite invitation  
b) soft alternative (+ -ing / noun)  
c) direct suggestion  
d) polite refusal start  
e) suggestion as a question

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1 → c  
2 → e  
3 → b  
4 → a  
5 → d  

</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Completa

1. ___ we take a taxi?  
2. ___ stay at home.  
3. Why ___ we call her?  
4. How about ___ (go) for a walk?  
5. Would you like ___ (come) with us?

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. Shall  
2. Let's  
3. don't  
4. going  
5. to come  

</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Elige la forma correcta

1. ___ a coffee?  
   a) How about  b) Shall we  c) Let's to  
2. ___ go now!  
   a) How about  b) Let's  c) Would you like  
3. ___ you like to join us?  
   a) Shall  b) Would  c) Let's

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. a  
2. b  
3. b  

</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Corrige el error

1. Let's to watch a film.  
2. Shall we to leave?  
3. How about to meet at 5?  
4. Why we don't eat out?  
5. Would you like come?

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. Let's watch a film.  
2. Shall we leave?  
3. How about meeting at 5?  
4. Why don't we eat out?  
5. Would you like to come?  

</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Traduce al inglés

1. ¿Salimos?  
2. Vamos a tomar un café.  
3. ¿Qué tal si quedamos a las 6?  
4. ¿Te gustaría venir?  
5. Me encantaría, pero estoy ocupado/a.

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. Shall we go out? / Shall we leave?  
2. Let's have a coffee.  
3. How about meeting at 6?  
4. Would you like to come?  
5. I'd love to, but I'm busy.  

</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Completa el diálogo

**A:** ___ we go shopping?  
**B:** Sorry, I ___. How ___ tomorrow?  
**A:** Good idea. Would you ___ to meet at 11?  
**B:** Sure. ___ have lunch after that.

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

Shall  
can't  
about  
like  
Let's  

</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Aceptar o rechazar

Escribe una respuesta educada:

1. Shall we go running? *(rechazar — llueve)*  
2. Would you like to come to my party? *(aceptar)*  
3. How about pizza? *(dudar — hora)*

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. Sorry, I can't — it's raining. / I'd love to, but it's raining.  
2. Yes, I'd love to. / Sure, great!  
3. Maybe — what time? / I'm not sure. What time?

</details>

### Ejercicio 8 — Ordena

1. we / Shall / go / ?  
2. about / How / a / coffee / ?  
3. like / Would / you / to / join / us / ?

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. Shall we go?  
2. How about a coffee?  
3. Would you like to join us?  

</details>

### Ejercicio 9 — Elige según el tono

1. Más directo → ___ go!  
2. Más pregunta → ___ we leave now?  
3. Con gerundio → How about ___ (stay) in?

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. Let's  
2. Shall  
3. staying  

</details>

### Ejercicio 10 — Tu diálogo de planes (8–12 líneas)

Escribe un diálogo entre dos personas. Incluye:

- **Shall we…?** o **Let's…**  
- **How about…?** o **Why don't we…?**  
- **Would you like to…?**  
- 1 aceptación y 1 rechazo educado (o duda)

**Modelo:** el diálogo de la sección 6.

---

## 9. Plan de estudio (25–30 minutos)

1. **5 min** — Formas de sugerir + respuestas  
2. **8 min** — Ejercicios 1–6.  
3. **7 min** — Escucha lectura y diálogo.  
4. **5–8 min** — Ejercicio 10.

### Checklist

- [ ] Uso *Shall we…?* y *Let's…*  
- [ ] Uso *How about + -ing/noun*  
- [ ] Invito con *Would you like to…?*  
- [ ] Acepto / rechazo con educación  
- [ ] Evito *Let's to* y *How about to*

---

## 10. Consejos y siguiente paso

1. Propón 3 planes en voz alta cada día.  
2. Practica rechazos corteses (*I'd love to, but…*).  
3. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 51](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-51-making-suggestions-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 51 del curso A2](/curso-a2/unit-51).

La **Unidad 52** es **Making Offers & Requests** (ofertas y peticiones).

---

## Resumen rápido

| | Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Directo | Let's… | Let's go. |
| Pregunta | Shall we…? | Shall we eat? |
| Suave | Why don't we…? / How about…? | How about pizza? |
| Invitar | Would you like to…? | Would you like to come? |
| Responder | Great / Sorry, I can't | I'd love to, but… |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A2

title: Offers & Requests A2: Can I…?, Could you…?, Would you like me to…?
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 52 del curso A2: ofrecer ayuda y pedir cosas con Can I…?, Could you…? y Would you like me to…?, con audios y ejercicios.
description: Ofertas y peticiones en inglés A2: Can I…?, Could you…?, Would you like me to…? Guía Unidad 52 con audios, diálogos de cortesía y ejercicios.
alt: Esquema Offers & Requests A2

faqs.question: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre una offer y una request?
faqs.answer: Offer = ofreces ayuda o algo (Can I help you? / Would you like me to…?). Request = pides algo a otra persona (Could you open the window?).

faqs.question: ¿Can you o Could you?
faqs.answer: Ambos piden algo. Could you…? suele sonar un poco más educado/formal que Can you…?

faqs.question: ¿Cómo acepto o rechazo una oferta?
faqs.answer: Aceptar: Yes, please. / That would be great. Rechazar: No, thanks. / It's OK, I can manage.

faqs.question: ¿Would you like me to lleva verbo en base?
faqs.answer: Sí: Would you like me to + verbo base (Would you like me to help?).

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 52 del curso A2?
faqs.answer: En el [cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-52-offers-requests-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la Unidad 52 del curso A2 de Linguafly practicarás ofertas y peticiones educadas.

content:
En la [Unidad 51](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-51-making-suggestions) sugeriste planes. En la **Unidad 52 del curso A2** (*Making Offers & Requests*) practicas **ofrecer ayuda** y **pedir cosas con cortesía**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 52 — Making Offers & Requests](/curso-a2/unit-52)  
> **Antes:** [U51 — Making Suggestions](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-51-making-suggestions)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 52 (A2)

- **Offers:** *Can I…?*, *Would you like me to…?*, *Shall I…?*
- **Requests:** *Can you…?*, *Could you…?*, *Could you please…?*
- Respuestas educadas (aceptar / rechazar).
- Vocabulario en **casa, trabajo y tienda**.
- Producir diálogos cortos de cortesía.

![Offers & Requests A2](/blog/curso-a2/unit-52/a2-unit52-offers-requests.png)

---

## 1. Offers: ofrecer ayuda

| Forma | Uso | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Can I…?** | ofrecer hacer algo | **Can I** help you? |
| **Shall I…?** | ofrecer (británico, frecuente) | **Shall I** open the window? |
| **Would you like me to…?** | ofrecer con más cortesía | **Would you like me to** carry that? |
| **Let me…** | ofrecer de forma directa | **Let me** help you. |

> **Can I** get you a drink?  
> **Would you like me to** call a taxi?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-52/can-i-help-you.mp3" title="🔊 Can I help you?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-52/would-you-like-me-to.mp3" title="🔊 Would you like me to carry that?"></audio>

---

## 2. Requests: pedir algo

| Forma | Tono | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Can you…?** | neutro / informal | **Can you** pass the salt? |
| **Could you…?** | más educado | **Could you** open the door? |
| **Could you please…?** | más cortés | **Could you please** wait a minute? |
| **Would you mind + -ing?** | muy educado (A2+) | **Would you mind** helping me?

> **Could you** send me the email?  
> **Can you** help me with this bag?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-52/could-you-open.mp3" title="🔊 Could you open the window?"></audio>

![Offer or request](/blog/curso-a2/unit-52/a2-unit52-offer-vs-request.png)

---

## 3. Respuestas

### A una oferta

| Aceptar | Rechazar |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Yes, please.** | **No, thanks.** |
| **That would be great.** | **It's OK, thanks.** |
| **Thank you!** | **I can manage.** |

### A una petición

| Aceptar | Rechazar (educado) |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Of course.** | **Sorry, I can't right now.** |
| **Sure.** | **I'm afraid I'm busy.** |
| **No problem.** | **Maybe later.** |

> A: Could you help me?  
> B: **Of course.** / **Sorry, I'm busy at the moment.**

---

## 4. Contextos: casa, trabajo, tienda

| Lugar | Offer | Request |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Casa | Shall I make tea? | Could you close the door? |
| Trabajo | Can I help with the report? | Could you send the file? |
| Tienda | Can I help you? | Could you gift-wrap this? |

---

## 5. Mapa rápido

| Quieres… | Usa… | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Ofrecer ayuda | Can I…? / Would you like me to…? | Can I help? |
| Pedir algo | Could you…? / Can you…? | Could you wait? |
| Aceptar oferta | Yes, please. | Yes, please. |
| Rechazar oferta | No, thanks. | No, thanks. |
| Aceptar petición | Of course. / Sure. | Of course. |

![Help scene](/blog/curso-a2/unit-52/a2-unit52-help-scene.png)

---

## 6. Lectura y diálogo

### Lectura — At the office

Good morning. **Can I** help you with those boxes? If you want, **Would you like me to** call reception? Later, **Could you please** send me the report by email? And **Shall I** book a meeting room for 3? Thanks — that would be great.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-52/reading-office.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: At the office"></audio>

### Diálogo — Helping a neighbour

**Alex:** Hi! Those bags look heavy. **Can I** help you?  
**Sam:** **Yes, please.** Thanks!  
**Alex:** **Would you like me to** take them upstairs?  
**Sam:** That would be great.  
**Alex:** **Could you** open the door?  
**Sam:** **Of course.** Here you are.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-52/dialogue-help.mp3" title="🔊 Dialogue: Helping a neighbour"></audio>

### Mini práctica

1. ___ I help you?  
2. Would you like me ___ carry that?  
3. ___ you open the window?  
4. Yes, ___. *(aceptar oferta)*

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-52/practice-four.mp3" title="🔊 Practice four sentences"></audio>

---

## 7. Errores frecuentes

1. ~~Can I to help you?~~ → **Can I help you?**  
2. ~~Could you to open…?~~ → **Could you open…?**  
3. ~~Would you like me help?~~ → **Would you like me to help?**  
4. ~~Please you help me.~~ → **Could you please help me?**  
5. ~~Yes.~~ *(muy seco a oferta)* → **Yes, please.** / **That would be great.**  
6. ~~No.~~ → **No, thanks.** / **It's OK, thanks.**

---

## 8. Ejercicios (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — ¿Offer o request?

1. Can I help you?  
2. Could you wait here?  
3. Would you like me to call a taxi?  
4. Can you pass the salt?  
5. Shall I open the window?

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. offer  
2. request  
3. offer  
4. request  
5. offer  

</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Completa

1. ___ I carry your bag?  
2. Could you ___ close the door? *(please)*  
3. Would you like me ___ help?  
4. ___ I make some tea?

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. Can / Shall  
2. please  
3. to  
4. Shall / Can  

</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Elige la mejor opción

1. Ofrecer ayuda educada:  
   a) Help me!  b) Would you like me to help?  c) You help.  
2. Pedir con cortesía:  
   a) Open the window.  b) Could you open the window?  c) You must open.  
3. Aceptar una oferta:  
   a) No.  b) Yes, please.  c) Of course not.

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. b  
2. b  
3. b  

</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Corrige el error

1. Can I to help you?  
2. Could you to wait?  
3. Would you like me help with this?  
4. Please you send the email.  
5. No. *(rechazo de oferta — hazlo educado)*

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. Can I help you?  
2. Could you wait?  
3. Would you like me to help with this?  
4. Could you please send the email?  
5. No, thanks. / It's OK, thanks.

</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Traduce al inglés

1. ¿Puedo ayudarte?  
2. ¿Te gustaría que te lleve eso?  
3. ¿Podrías abrir la ventana?  
4. Sí, por favor.  
5. Lo siento, ahora no puedo.

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. Can I help you?  
2. Would you like me to carry that?  
3. Could you open the window?  
4. Yes, please.  
5. Sorry, I can't right now.

</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Completa el diálogo

**A:** Those bags look heavy. ___ I help you?  
**B:** Yes, ___.  
**A:** Would you like me ___ take them upstairs?  
**B:** That would be ___.  
**A:** ___ you open the door?  
**B:** Of ___.

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

Can  
please  
to  
great  
Could  
course  

</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Empareja respuesta

1. Can I help you?  
2. Could you send the file?  
3. Would you like me to call a taxi?  

a) Of course.  
b) Yes, please.  
c) No, thanks — I'll walk.

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1 → b (también OK otras)  
2 → a  
3 → c  

</details>

### Ejercicio 8 — Ordena

1. help / I / Can / you / ?  
2. open / Could / you / the / window / ?  
3. me / like / Would / you / to / help / ?

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. Can I help you?  
2. Could you open the window?  
3. Would you like me to help?  

</details>

### Ejercicio 9 — Casa / trabajo / tienda

Escribe una offer y una request para cada lugar:

1. Casa  
2. Trabajo  
3. Tienda

<details>
<summary>Soluciones (modelo)</summary>

1. Shall I make tea? / Could you close the door?  
2. Can I help with the report? / Could you send the email?  
3. Can I help you? / Could you gift-wrap this?

</details>

### Ejercicio 10 — Tu diálogo (8–12 líneas)

Escribe un diálogo con:

- 2 **offers** (*Can I…?* / *Would you like me to…?* / *Shall I…?*)  
- 1 **request** (*Could you…?* / *Can you…?*)  
- 1 aceptación y 1 rechazo educado

**Modelo:** el diálogo de la sección 6.

---

## 9. Plan de estudio (25–30 minutos)

1. **5 min** — Offer vs request + respuestas  
2. **8 min** — Ejercicios 1–6.  
3. **7 min** — Escucha lectura y diálogo.  
4. **5–8 min** — Ejercicio 10.

### Checklist

- [ ] Ofrezco con *Can I…?* / *Would you like me to…?*  
- [ ] Pido con *Could you…?* / *Can you…?*  
- [ ] Respondo *Yes, please* / *No, thanks* / *Of course*  
- [ ] Distingo offer y request  
- [ ] Evito *Can I to* y *Would you like me help*

---

## 10. Consejos y siguiente paso

1. Practica en voz alta: 3 ofertas + 3 peticiones al día.  
2. Graba un mini diálogo y comprueba la cortesía.  
3. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 52](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-52-offers-requests-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 52 del curso A2](/curso-a2/unit-52).

La **Unidad 53** es **Expressing Opinions** (dar opiniones).

---

## Resumen rápido

| | Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Offer | Can I…? | Can I help you? |
| Offer | Would you like me to…? | Would you like me to carry that? |
| Request | Could you…? | Could you open the window? |
| Aceptar oferta | Yes, please. | Yes, please. |
| Aceptar petición | Of course. | Of course. |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A2

En la **Unidad 53** verás **Expressing Opinions**.

Curso:

- [Unidad 53 — Expressing Opinions](/curso-a2/unit-53)

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 52 A2 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-52-offers-requests-ejercicios-soluciones)
- [Unidad 52 — Offers & Requests](/curso-a2/unit-52)

Guías relacionadas:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 52 A2 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-52-offers-requests-ejercicios-soluciones)
- [U51 — Making Suggestions](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-51-making-suggestions)
- [U29 — Could: habilidad y peticiones](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-29-could-habilidad-peticiones)
- [Will: ofertas y peticiones](/blog/gramatica/will-ofertas-peticiones-ingles)
- [Inglés A2: guía del nivel](/blog/metodos/ingles-a2)

---

## Fuentes

- CEFR/MCER — Nivel A2: https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages
- Cambridge English — A2 Key: https://www.cambridgeenglish.org/exams-and-tests/key/
- British Council — Offers and requests: https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/

title: Expressing Opinions A2: I think…, In my opinion…, I agree
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 53 del curso A2: expresar opiniones con I think, In my opinion e I agree/disagree, con audios y ejercicios.
description: Da tu opinión en inglés A2: I think…, I don't think…, In my opinion…, I agree / I disagree. Guía Unidad 53 con audios, reseñas y ejercicios.
alt: Esquema Expressing Opinions A2

faqs.question: ¿Se dice I think that o solo I think?
faqs.answer: Ambas valen. I think it's great. / I think that it's great. En conversación a menudo se omite that.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo digo que no estoy de acuerdo con educación?
faqs.answer: I don't think so. / I'm not sure. / I see your point, but… Evita un I disagree seco si el tono es informal amistoso.

faqs.question: ¿In my opinion necesita that?
faqs.answer: No es obligatorio: In my opinion, the film is too long. También In my opinion, it's too long.

faqs.question: ¿I agree with you o I agree you?
faqs.answer: I agree. / I agree with you. / I agree with that idea. No digas I agree you.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 53 del curso A2?
faqs.answer: En el [cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-53-expressing-opinions-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la Unidad 53 del curso A2 de Linguafly practicarás opiniones y acuerdo/desacuerdo.

content:
En la [Unidad 52](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-52-offers-requests) practicaste ofertas y peticiones. En la **Unidad 53 del curso A2** (*Expressing Opinions*) das **tu opinión** y **reaccionas** a la de otros.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 53 — Expressing Opinions](/curso-a2/unit-53)  
> **Antes:** [U52 — Offers & Requests](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-52-offers-requests)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 53 (A2)

- Dar opinión: **I think…**, **I don't think…**, **In my opinion…**
- Reaccionar: **I agree**, **I disagree**, **I don't think so**
- Vocabulario de temas: películas, música, comida, viajes
- Entender opiniones en reseñas / foros
- Escribir 2–3 frases de opinión

![Expressing Opinions A2](/blog/curso-a2/unit-53/a2-unit53-expressing-opinions.png)

---

## 1. Dar tu opinión

| Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| **I think…** | **I think** this film is great. |
| **I don't think…** | **I don't think** it's funny. |
| **In my opinion…** | **In my opinion**, it's too long. |
| **I believe…** | **I believe** travel is important. |
| **For me…** | **For me**, pizza is the best. |

> **I think** we should go by train.  
> **In my opinion**, the museum is better than the mall.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-53/i-think.mp3" title="🔊 I think this film is great."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-53/in-my-opinion.mp3" title="🔊 In my opinion, it's too long."></audio>

---

## 2. Acordar y discrepar

| Acordar | Discrepar (suave → más claro) |
| :--- | :--- |
| **I agree.** | **I don't think so.** |
| **I agree with you.** | **I'm not sure.** |
| **You're right.** | **I see your point, but…** |
| **Exactly!** | **I disagree.** |

> A: I think the food is delicious.  
> B: **I agree!** / **I don't think so** — it's too spicy for me.

![Agree or disagree](/blog/curso-a2/unit-53/a2-unit53-agree-disagree.png)

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-53/i-agree.mp3" title="🔊 I agree with you."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-53/i-dont-think-so.mp3" title="🔊 I don't think so."></audio>

---

## 3. Vocabulario por tema

| Tema | Opiniones útiles |
| :--- | :--- |
| Películas / series | boring, exciting, funny, too long, brilliant |
| Música | catchy, loud, relaxing, my favourite |
| Comida | delicious, spicy, sweet, healthy, terrible |
| Viajes | expensive, worth it, crowded, amazing |

> **I think** the soundtrack is **catchy**.  
> **In my opinion**, the city is **too crowded** in summer.

---

## 4. Preguntar la opinión

| Pregunta | Respuesta modelo |
| :--- | :--- |
| **What do you think?** | I think it's good. |
| **What's your opinion?** | In my opinion, … |
| **Do you agree?** | Yes, I agree. / Not really. |

---

## 5. Mapa rápido

| Quieres… | Usa… | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Opinar | I think… | I think it's great. |
| Opinar (formal) | In my opinion… | In my opinion, it's long. |
| Negar opinión | I don't think… | I don't think it's funny. |
| Acordar | I agree. | I agree with you. |
| Discrepar | I don't think so. | I don't think so. |

![Opinion scene](/blog/curso-a2/unit-53/a2-unit53-opinion-scene.png)

---

## 6. Lectura y diálogo

### Lectura — Forum review

**What do you think** of the new series? **In my opinion**, episode one is slow, but the story is interesting. **I think** the actors are brilliant. Some people say it's boring — **I don't think so**. **I agree** that it's a bit long, but it's worth watching.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-53/reading-forum.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Forum review"></audio>

### Diálogo — After a film

**Lara:** **What do you think** of the film?  
**Ben:** **I think** it was exciting.  
**Lara:** **I agree.** The ending was amazing.  
**Ben:** **Do you agree** that it was too long?  
**Lara:** **I'm not sure.** **In my opinion**, it was fine.  
**Ben:** Fair enough!

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-53/dialogue-film.mp3" title="🔊 Dialogue: After a film"></audio>

### Mini práctica

1. I ___ this song is catchy.  
2. In my ___, the food is too spicy.  
3. I ___ with you.  
4. I don't think ___.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-53/practice-four.mp3" title="🔊 Practice four sentences"></audio>

---

## 7. Errores frecuentes

1. ~~I am agree.~~ → **I agree.**  
2. ~~I agree you.~~ → **I agree with you.**  
3. ~~In my opinion that the film is bad.~~ → **In my opinion, the film is bad.**  
4. ~~I think yes.~~ → **I think so.** / **Yes, I think so.**  
5. ~~I don't think yes.~~ → **I don't think so.**  
6. ~~According to me…~~ → más natural: **In my opinion…** / **For me…**

---

## 8. Ejercicios (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — Empareja

1. I think…  
2. In my opinion…  
3. I agree.  
4. I don't think so.  
5. What do you think?  

a) ask for an opinion  
b) give an opinion  
c) disagree politely  
d) another way to give an opinion  
e) say you have the same opinion

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1 → b  
2 → d  
3 → e  
4 → c  
5 → a  

</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Completa

1. I ___ the museum is amazing.  
2. I don't ___ it's a good idea.  
3. In my ___, we should stay.  
4. I agree ___ you.  
5. I don't think ___.

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. think  
2. think  
3. opinion  
4. with  
5. so  

</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Agree o disagree

1. You're right. → ___  
2. I'm not sure. → ___  
3. Exactly! → ___  
4. I see your point, but… → ___

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. agree  
2. soft disagree / unsure  
3. agree  
4. soft disagree  

</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Corrige el error

1. I am agree with you.  
2. I agree you.  
3. I think so not.  
4. In my opinion that it's boring.  
5. According to me, it's great.

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. I agree with you.  
2. I agree with you.  
3. I don't think so.  
4. In my opinion, it's boring.  
5. In my opinion, / For me, it's great.

</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Traduce al inglés

1. Creo que la película es genial.  
2. En mi opinión, es demasiado larga.  
3. Estoy de acuerdo contigo.  
4. No lo creo.  
5. ¿Qué opinas?

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. I think the film is great.  
2. In my opinion, it's too long.  
3. I agree with you.  
4. I don't think so.  
5. What do you think? / What's your opinion?

</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Completa el diálogo

**A:** What do you ___ of this restaurant?  
**B:** I ___ the food is delicious.  
**A:** I ___ — but in my ___, it's expensive.  
**B:** I don't think ___ . It's OK for a special day.

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

think  
think  
agree  
opinion  
so  

</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Elige la mejor opción

1. ___ the music is too loud.  
   a) I am think  b) I think  c) I thinking  
2. ___ , we should leave early.  
   a) In my opinion  b) I agree you  c) I think so not  
3. A: It's boring. B: ___ — I loved it.  
   a) I agree  b) I don't think so  c) Exactly

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. b  
2. a  
3. b  

</details>

### Ejercicio 8 — Ordena

1. think / I / it's / great  
2. opinion / In / my / it's / long / too  
3. with / I / agree / you

<details>
<summary>Soluciones</summary>

1. I think it's great.  
2. In my opinion, it's too long.  
3. I agree with you.  

</details>

### Ejercicio 9 — Temas

Escribe 1 opinión (*I think* / *In my opinion*) para cada tema:

1. A film  
2. A song  
3. A city

<details>
<summary>Soluciones (modelo)</summary>

1. I think the film is exciting.  
2. In my opinion, the song is catchy.  
3. I think the city is too crowded.

</details>

### Ejercicio 10 — Tu mini reseña (8–12 líneas)

Elige una película, canción, comida o viaje. Incluye:

- **I think…**  
- **In my opinion…**  
- **I agree** o **I don't think so** (reacción a una idea imaginaria)  
- 2 adjetivos del tema

**Modelo:** la lectura de la sección 6.

---

## 9. Plan de estudio (25–30 minutos)

1. **5 min** — Formas de opinar + agree/disagree  
2. **8 min** — Ejercicios 1–6.  
3. **7 min** — Escucha forum y diálogo.  
4. **5–8 min** — Ejercicio 10.

### Checklist

- [ ] Uso *I think / I don't think*  
- [ ] Uso *In my opinion…*  
- [ ] Digo *I agree with you*  
- [ ] Discrepo con *I don't think so*  
- [ ] Evito *I am agree* e *I agree you*

---

## 10. Consejos y siguiente paso

1. Da tu opinión en voz alta sobre 3 cosas cada día.  
2. Lee comentarios cortos en inglés y marca *I think / I agree*.  
3. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 53](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-53-expressing-opinions-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 53 del curso A2](/curso-a2/unit-53).

La **Unidad 54** es **Feelings & Emotions** (sentimientos).

---

## Resumen rápido

| | Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Opinar | I think… | I think it's great. |
| Opinar | In my opinion… | In my opinion, it's long. |
| Negar | I don't think… | I don't think it's funny. |
| Acordar | I agree (with you). | I agree with you. |
| Discrepar | I don't think so. | I don't think so. |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A2
