title: Repaso A2 → B1: Present Perfect, modales, used to y feelings
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 1 del curso B1: puente A2 → B1 con Present Perfect, modales, used to, who/which, feelings y el texto de Maria en Londres.
description: Empieza el curso B1 con un repaso A2: Present Perfect, comparativos, modales, relative who/which, used to y vocabulario de sentimientos. Guía Unidad 1 con audios y ejercicios.
alt: Puente visual del repaso A2 hacia el nivel B1

faqs.answer: Estructuras clave de A2 que necesitas activas en B1: Present Perfect, comparativos, modales (must, have to, can), relative who/which, used to, first conditional y un primer contacto con Present Perfect Continuous y Past Perfect. También vocabulario de información personal y sentimientos.
faqs.question: ¿Qué se repasa en la Unidad 1 del curso B1?

faqs.answer: En B1 las frases son más largas, combinas tiempos y explicas causas y sentimientos con más precisión (anxious, confident, proud…). No empiezas de cero: consolidas A2 y añades matices.
faqs.question: ¿En qué se diferencia B1 de A2?

faqs.answer: used to + infinitive = hábito o situación del pasado que ya no ocurre: I used to play tennis when I was young. No lo confundas aún con be/get used to (eso se profundiza en la Unidad 9).
faqs.question: ¿Qué es used to en este repaso?

faqs.answer: who para personas (The man who helped me…); which para cosas (The book which I bought…). En B1 luego verás that y cláusulas no definitorias.
faqs.question: ¿who o which en relative clauses?

faqs.answer: En el [cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-1-repaso-a2-b1-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la Unidad 1 del curso B1 de Linguafly: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening, speaking y writing alineados con este repaso A2 → B1.
faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 1 del curso B1?

content:
Si acabas de cerrar el [curso A2](/blog/curso-a2) (o el [Module 6 Review](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-60-module-6-review)), no saltas al vacío: **activas** lo que ya sabes y lo usas en frases más largas. La **Unidad 1 del curso B1** (*Repaso A2 → B1*) es el puente: Present Perfect, comparativos, modales, *who/which*, *used to* y vocabulario de **feelings**, con el texto de Maria en Londres.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 1 — Repaso A2 → B1](/curso-b1/unit-1)  
> **Antes (A2):** [Unidad 60 — Module 6 Review](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-60-module-6-review) · [Guía gramatical B1](/blog/gramatica/gramatica-ingles-b1-guia)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 1 (B1)

- Reactivar **Present Perfect** (*I have lived…*, *She has never been…*).
- Repasar **comparativos**, **modales** (*must*, *have to*, *can*) y **going to**.
- Usar **relative clauses** básicas: *who* (personas) / *which* (cosas).
- Reconocer *used to* (hábitos pasados) y un primer *has been + -ing* / *had + pp*.
- Hablar de **sentimientos** e **información personal** (*confident*, *anxious*, *proud*…).
- Leer y entender un texto B1 corto (Maria en Londres).

![De A2 a B1: puente de repaso](/blog/curso-b1/unit-1/a2-to-b1.png)

---

## 1. De A2 a B1: qué cambia

| Nivel | Enfoque típico |
| :--- | :--- |
| **A2** | Formas claras, frases cortas, un tiempo por vez |
| **B1** | Combinar tiempos, explicar *why*, describir feelings, textos más densos |

No “olvidas” A2: lo **enciendes**. Si una estructura falla aquí, vuelve a su unidad A2 y luego sigue el curso B1.

---

## 2. Present Perfect (repaso rápido)

**have/has + past participle** — experiencia o situación con conexión al presente.

| Sujeto | Auxiliar | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| I / you / we / they | **have** | I **have lived** here for three years. |
| he / she / it | **has** | She **has never been** to Japan. |

> I have lived here for three years.  
> She has never been to Japan.  
> We have visited many countries together.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-1/i-have-lived.mp3" title="🔊 I have lived here for three years."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-1/she-has-never-been.mp3" title="🔊 She has never been to Japan."></audio>

Guía A2 de refuerzo: [Present Perfect: introducción](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-11-present-perfect-introduccion) · [Present Perfect vs Past Simple](/blog/gramatica/present-perfect-vs-past-simple).

---

## 3. Primer vistazo: Present Perfect Continuous

En el repaso aparece *has/have been + -ing* (duración hasta ahora). Lo profundizas en la **Unidad 2**.

> She **has been studying** since nine o’clock.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-1/has-been-studying.mp3" title="🔊 She has been studying since nine o'clock."></audio>

Idea: *continuous* = acción en progreso / duración; *simple* = resultado o experiencia. Más en [Present Perfect Continuous](/blog/gramatica/present-perfect-continuous).

---

## 4. Comparativos y planes (*going to*)

| Estructura | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| *more + adj* (adjetivos largos) | This hotel is **more expensive than** that one. |
| *going to* (plan decidido) | Next weekend I **am going to** visit my parents. |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-1/more-expensive.mp3" title="🔊 This hotel is more expensive than that one."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-1/going-to-visit.mp3" title="🔊 Next weekend I am going to visit my parents."></audio>

---

## 5. Modales: *must*, *have to*, *can*

| Modal | Uso en el repaso | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **must** | obligación fuerte / norma | You **must** wear a seatbelt in the car. |
| **have to** | obligación (externa) | I **have to** work early tomorrow. |
| **can** | capacidad | She **can** speak Spanish very well. |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-1/you-must-wear.mp3" title="🔊 You must wear a seatbelt in the car."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-1/have-to-work.mp3" title="🔊 I have to work early tomorrow."></audio>

En B1 más adelante verás **deducción** (*must / might / can’t*) en la Unidad 8.

---

## 6. Relative clauses: *who* / *which*

| Relativo | Para | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **who** | personas | The man **who** helped me was very kind. |
| **which** | cosas | The book **which** I bought is very interesting. |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-1/who-helped.mp3" title="🔊 The man who helped me was very kind."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-1/which-bought.mp3" title="🔊 The book which I bought is very interesting."></audio>

---

## 7. *used to* + infinitive

Hábitos o situaciones del **pasado** que ya no son verdad:

> I **used to** play tennis when I was young.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-1/used-to-play.mp3" title="🔊 I used to play tennis when I was young."></audio>

En el reading de Maria: *I used to miss my family* / *I got used to living alone*. El trío *used to / be used to / get used to* se estudia a fondo en la **Unidad 9**.

---

## 8. Condicional 1 y Past Perfect (contacto)

| Estructura | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| First conditional | If it rains tomorrow, I **will** stay at home. |
| Past Perfect | He **had finished** his homework before I arrived. |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-1/if-it-rains.mp3" title="🔊 If it rains tomorrow, I will stay at home."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-1/had-finished.mp3" title="🔊 He had finished his homework before I arrived."></audio>

Past Perfect = acción **antes** de otra en el pasado (Unidad 3). Condicionales = Módulo 2.

---

## 9. Vocabulario: personal info + feelings

![Vocabulario de sentimientos B1](/blog/curso-b1/unit-1/feelings-vocab.png)

| Palabra | Idea | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| confident | seguro/a de ti | I feel more **confident** now. |
| nervous / anxious | nervioso / preocupado | At first I felt **anxious**. |
| proud | orgulloso | She is **proud** of her job. |
| satisfied | satisfecho | I’m **satisfied** with the result. |
| embarrassed | avergonzado | I felt **embarrassed**. |
| stressed | estresado | Opposite of *relaxed*. |
| amazing | increíble (positivo) | The trip was **amazing**. |

Profesiones / datos: *journalist*, *architect*, *mechanic*, *degree*, *passport*, *library*, *friendly*, *clever*, *professional*.

> I feel much more confident now.  
> At first I felt very nervous and anxious.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-1/i-feel-confident.mp3" title="🔊 I feel much more confident now."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-1/i-felt-anxious.mp3" title="🔊 At first I felt very nervous and anxious."></audio>

---

## 10. Reading: Maria in London

![Maria en Londres](/blog/curso-b1/unit-1/london-scene.png)

> My name is Maria and I am from Spain. I have been living in London for two years because I work as a journalist. At first I felt very nervous and anxious because I didn’t know anyone. But now I have many friends and I feel much more confident. I used to miss my family a lot, but I got used to living alone. My sister is an architect and she is very proud of her job. We both love travelling and we have visited many countries together.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-1/reading-maria.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Maria in London"></audio>

Comprueba: ¿De dónde es? ¿Cuánto lleva en Londres? ¿Cómo se sentía al principio? ¿Y ahora? ¿Qué hace su hermana?

---

## 11. Mini-diálogo (feelings)

> How do you feel about moving abroad?  
> At first I felt anxious, but now I feel confident.  
> Are you proud of your degree?  
> Yes — and I’m satisfied with my new job.  
> That’s amazing!

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-1/dialogue-feelings.mp3" title="🔊 Dialogue: feelings"></audio>

---

## 12. Practica en voz alta

Une cuatro frases del repaso:

> I have lived here for three years. She has never been to Japan. You must wear a seatbelt. I used to play tennis when I was young.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-1/practice-four.mp3" title="🔊 Practice four sentences"></audio>

---

## 13. Ejercicios

### Ejercicio 1 — Present Perfect

1. I \_\_\_\_ lived here for three years. (*have / has*)  
2. She \_\_\_\_ never been to Japan.  
3. We \_\_\_\_ visited many countries together.  
4. He \_\_\_ finished before I arrived. (Past Perfect)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **have** · 2. **has** · 3. **have** · 4. **had**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Modales y comparativos

1. You \_\_\_\_ wear a seatbelt. (*must / can*)  
2. I \_\_\_\_ work early tomorrow. (*have to / has to*)  
3. This hotel is \_\_\_\_ expensive \_\_\_\_ that one.  
4. Next weekend I \_\_\_\_ \_\_\_\_ \_\_\_\_ visit my parents. (*going to*)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **must** · 2. **have to** · 3. **more** … **than** · 4. **am going to**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — *who* / *which* / *used to*

1. The man \_\_\_\_ helped me was kind.  
2. The book \_\_\_\_ I bought is interesting.  
3. I \_\_\_\_ \_\_\_\_ play tennis when I was young.  
4. If it rains, I \_\_\_\_ stay at home.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **who** · 2. **which** · 3. **used to** · 4. **will**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Feelings / jobs

1. Opposite of *confident* ≈ \_\_\_\_ / \_\_\_\_  
2. Satisfied with a result → you feel \_\_\_\_  
3. Designs buildings → \_\_\_\_  
4. Writes for a newspaper → \_\_\_\_  
5. Document to travel abroad → \_\_\_\_

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **nervous** / **anxious** · 2. **satisfied** · 3. **architect** · 4. **journalist** · 5. **passport**
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Reading (Maria)

1. Maria is from \_\_\_\_.  
2. She has been living in London for \_\_\_\_ years.  
3. At first she felt \_\_\_\_ and \_\_\_\_.  
4. Now she feels more \_\_\_\_.  
5. Her sister is an \_\_\_\_.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Spain** · 2. **two** · 3. **nervous** and **anxious** · 4. **confident** · 5. **architect**
</details>

---

## 14. Errores frecuentes

| Evita | Mejor |
| :--- | :--- |
| *She have lived…* | She **has** lived… |
| *more expensive that* | more expensive **than** |
| *must to wear* | **must** wear / **have to** wear |
| *The man which helped me* | The man **who** helped me |
| *I use to play* | I **used to** play |
| *enough big to* | **big enough** to |

---

## 15. Consejos y siguiente paso

1. Haz el repaso **en voz alta**: B1 pide fluidez, no solo reconocer formas.  
2. Escribe 6–8 frases sobre ti: dónde has vivido, cómo te sentiste al cambiar de ciudad, qué *used to* hacer.  
3. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 1](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-1-repaso-a2-b1-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 1 del curso B1](/curso-b1/unit-1).  
4. Siguiente: **Present Perfect Continuous** (Unidad 2) con *for/since* y contexto de educación.

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Lo esencial |
| :--- | :--- |
| Present Perfect | have/has + pp · experiencia / conexión presente |
| PPC (preview) | has been + -ing · duración |
| Comparativos / planes | more… than · am going to |
| Modales | must · have to · can |
| Relativos | who (people) · which (things) |
| used to | hábitos pasados |
| Feelings | confident · anxious · proud · satisfied |
| Reading | Maria in London |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso B1

En la **Unidad 2** estudiarás **Present Perfect Continuous**: *have/has been + -ing*, *for/since*, y el contraste con Present Perfect Simple (duración vs resultado), con vocabulario de **education**.

Guías y curso:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 1 B1 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-1-repaso-a2-b1-ejercicios-soluciones)
- [Unidad 2 — Present Perfect Continuous](/curso-b1/unit-2)
- [Present Perfect Continuous (guía)](/blog/gramatica/present-perfect-continuous)
- [Cursos online de inglés B1](/blog/metodos/cursos-online-ingles-b1)
- [Gramática inglesa B1: guía](/blog/gramatica/gramatica-ingles-b1-guia)
- [A2 U60 — Module 6 Review](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-60-module-6-review)

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 1 B1 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-1-repaso-a2-b1-ejercicios-soluciones)

---

title: Present Perfect Continuous B1: have/has been + -ing, for/since
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 2 del curso B1: Present Perfect Continuous con have/has been + -ing, for/since, contraste con Simple y vocabulario de education.
description: Aprende Present Perfect Continuous en inglés B1: have/has been + -ing, for/since y contraste con Present Perfect Simple. Guía Unidad 2 con audios y ejercicios (education).
alt: Fórmula have/has been + -ing del Present Perfect Continuous B1

faqs.answer: have/has + been + verbo en -ing. I/you/we/they → have been. He/she/it → has been. Ejemplo: She has been studying for two hours.
faqs.question: ¿Cómo se forma el Present Perfect Continuous?

faqs.answer: for + duración (for three years, for two hours). since + punto de inicio (since 2019, since September, since this morning).
faqs.question: ¿Cuándo uso for y cuándo since?

faqs.answer: Continuous = duración / proceso / resultado visible (She has been gardening — hands dirty). Simple = resultado o cantidad (I have read three books; She has written ten emails).
faqs.question: ¿Continuous o Simple?

faqs.answer: How long have you been + -ing…? Ejemplo: How long have you been studying here?
faqs.question: ¿Cómo pregunto “cuánto tiempo llevas…”?

faqs.answer: En el [cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-2-present-perfect-continuous-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la Unidad 2 del curso B1 de Linguafly: gramática, vocabulario de education, reading, listening, speaking y writing con Present Perfect Continuous.
faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 2 del curso B1?

content:
Tras el [Repaso A2 → B1](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-1-repaso-a2-b1), la **Unidad 2 del curso B1** (*Present Perfect Continuous*) te enseña a hablar de **duración hasta ahora**: ***She has been studying for two hours***. Combina la forma con *for/since*, el contraste con Present Perfect Simple y vocabulario de **education**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 2 — Present Perfect Continuous](/curso-b1/unit-2)  
> **Antes:** [U1 — Repaso A2 → B1](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-1-repaso-a2-b1) · [Guía PPC](/blog/gramatica/present-perfect-continuous)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 2 (B1)

- Formar **have/has been + -ing**.
- Usar **for** (duración) y **since** (punto de inicio).
- Preguntar con **How long have you been…?**
- Elegir **Continuous** (proceso / evidencia) vs **Simple** (resultado / cantidad).
- Aplicarlo al vocabulario de **education** (degree, subject, homework, attend…).

![Fórmula Present Perfect Continuous](/blog/curso-b1/unit-2/ppc-formula.png)

---

## 1. La fórmula

**Present Perfect Continuous = have/has + been + -ing**

| Sujeto | Auxiliar | + been + -ing | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| I / you / we / they | **have been** | studying / working… | They **have been working** all day. |
| he / she / it | **has been** | studying / raining… | She **has been studying** for two hours. |

> She has been studying for two hours.  
> They have been working on the project all day.  
> We have been waiting since 8 o’clock.  
> It has been raining since this morning.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-2/she-has-been-studying.mp3" title="🔊 She has been studying for two hours."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-2/they-have-been-working.mp3" title="🔊 They have been working on the project all day."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-2/it-has-been-raining.mp3" title="🔊 It has been raining since this morning."></audio>

---

## 2. *for* vs *since*

| Palabra | Va con | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **for** | duración | for **three years**, for **two hours**, for **months** |
| **since** | punto de inicio | since **2019**, since **September**, since **this morning** |

> I have been learning English **for** three years.  
> He has been teaching **since** 2019.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-2/for-three-years.mp3" title="🔊 I have been learning English for three years."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-2/since-2019.mp3" title="🔊 He has been teaching since 2019."></audio>

Truco: *for* = “durante cuánto”; *since* = “desde cuándo”.

---

## 3. *How long…?*

> **How long have you been** studying here?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-2/how-long.mp3" title="🔊 How long have you been studying here?"></audio>

Respuestas típicas: *For five years.* / *Since September.* / *Since I started secondary school.*

---

## 4. Continuous vs Simple

![Continuous vs Simple](/blog/curso-b1/unit-2/continuous-vs-simple.png)

| Enfoque | Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Duración / proceso | Continuous | She **has been gardening**. (hands dirty) |
| Evidencia visible | Continuous | Your eyes are red — you **have been crying**. |
| Resultado / cantidad | Simple | I **have read** three books this year. |
| Acciones contadas | Simple | She **has written** ten emails today. |

> Her hands are dirty. She **has been gardening**.  
> Your eyes are red. You **have been crying**.  
> I **have read** three books this year.  
> She **has written** ten emails today.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-2/has-been-gardening.mp3" title="🔊 She has been gardening."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-2/have-been-crying.mp3" title="🔊 You have been crying."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-2/have-read-three.mp3" title="🔊 I have read three books this year."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-2/has-written-ten.mp3" title="🔊 She has written ten emails today."></audio>

Más detalle: [Present Perfect Continuous (guía)](/blog/gramatica/present-perfect-continuous) · [Present Perfect: usos](/blog/gramatica/present-perfect-usos-principales).

---

## 5. Vocabulario: Education

| Palabra | Idea |
| :--- | :--- |
| degree | título universitario |
| subject | asignatura |
| homework | deberes |
| exam | examen |
| course | curso (serie de clases) |
| graduate | graduado/a |
| laboratory | laboratorio |
| essay | ensayo / trabajo escrito |
| practise | practicar (UK spelling) |
| term | trimestre / periodo escolar |
| attend | asistir |
| student | estudiante |
| pass / fail | aprobar / suspender |
| absent | ausente |
| certificate | certificado (de un curso) |

Úsalos con PPC: *I have been attending English classes since September.* · *She has been working on her essay for weeks.*

---

## 6. Reading: James and English

![James estudiando](/blog/curso-b1/unit-2/james-studying.png)

> My name is James and I have been studying English for five years. I started when I was at secondary school and I have been improving ever since. I am currently doing a degree in Engineering at the university and I have been attending English classes since September. My teacher has been teaching here for ten years and she is very patient. I have been working on my pronunciation for months and I think I am getting better.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-2/reading-james.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: James and English"></audio>

Comprueba: ¿Cuánto lleva estudiando inglés? ¿Qué estudia en la universidad? ¿Desde cuándo asiste a clases? ¿Cuánto lleva enseñando su profesora? ¿En qué lleva trabajando meses?

---

## 7. Mini-diálogo

> How long have you been studying English?  
> For five years.  
> Have you been attending classes this term?  
> Yes — since September. I have also been working on my pronunciation.  
> That’s great. Have you passed any exams?  
> Yes — I passed two last term.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-2/dialogue-study.mp3" title="🔊 Dialogue: studying English"></audio>

---

## 8. Practica en voz alta

> She has been studying for two hours. I have been learning English for three years. How long have you been studying here? She has written ten emails today.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-2/practice-four.mp3" title="🔊 Practice four sentences"></audio>

---

## 9. Ejercicios

### Ejercicio 1 — Forma (*have/has been*)

1. She \_\_\_\_ \_\_\_\_ studying for two hours.  
2. They \_\_\_\_ \_\_\_\_ working all day.  
3. We \_\_\_\_ \_\_\_\_ waiting since 8 o’clock.  
4. It \_\_\_\_ \_\_\_\_ raining since this morning.  
5. How long \_\_\_\_ you \_\_\_\_ studying here?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **has been** · 2. **have been** · 3. **have been** · 4. **has been** · 5. **have** … **been**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — *for* / *since*

1. I have been learning English \_\_\_\_ three years.  
2. He has been teaching \_\_\_\_ 2019.  
3. They have been living in Paris \_\_\_\_ last month.  
4. She has been working here \_\_\_\_ five years.  
5. I have been trying to call you \_\_\_\_ an hour.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **for** · 2. **since** · 3. **since** · 4. **for** · 5. **for**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Continuous vs Simple

1. Her hands are dirty. She \_\_\_\_. (*has been gardening / has gardened*)  
2. I \_\_\_\_ three books this year. (*have read / have been reading*) — resultado  
3. Your eyes are red. You \_\_\_\_. (*have been crying / have cried*)  
4. She \_\_\_\_ ten emails today. (*has written / has been writing*)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **has been gardening** · 2. **have read** · 3. **have been crying** · 4. **has written**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Education vocab

1. University qualification = \_\_\_\_  
2. Work you do at home for school = \_\_\_\_  
3. Be present at a lesson = \_\_\_\_  
4. Succeed in an exam = \_\_\_\_  
5. Period of the school year = \_\_\_\_

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **degree** · 2. **homework** · 3. **attend** · 4. **pass** · 5. **term**
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Reading (James)

1. James has been studying English for \_\_\_\_ years.  
2. He started at \_\_\_\_ school.  
3. His degree is in \_\_\_\_.  
4. He has been attending English classes since \_\_\_\_.  
5. His teacher has been teaching there for \_\_\_\_ years.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **five** · 2. **secondary** · 3. **Engineering** · 4. **September** · 5. **ten**
</details>

---

## 10. Errores frecuentes

| Evita | Mejor |
| :--- | :--- |
| *She have been studying* | She **has** been studying |
| *I am been working* | I **have been** working |
| *for 2019* | **since** 2019 |
| *since three years* | **for** three years |
| *How long are you studying?* (duración hasta ahora) | How long **have you been** studying? |
| *I have been knowing her* | I **have known** her (stative) |

---

## 11. Consejos y siguiente paso

1. Cuenta tu historia: *I have been studying… for/since…*  
2. Cuando veas **cantidad** (*three books*, *ten emails*), piensa en **Simple**.  
3. Cuando veas **manos sucias / ojos rojos / all day**, piensa en **Continuous**.  
4. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 2](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-2-present-perfect-continuous-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 2 del curso B1](/curso-b1/unit-2).

La **Unidad 3** introduce el **Past Perfect** (*had + past participle*) para secuencias en el pasado.

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Lo esencial |

| Forma | have/has + been + -ing |
| for | duración (*for two hours*) |

| How long…? | How long have you been + -ing? |
| Continuous | duración / evidencia |
| Simple | resultado / cantidad |
| Vocab | degree · attend · homework · pass · term |

---

title: Past Perfect B1: had + past participle (before, by the time)
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 3 del curso B1: Past Perfect con had + past participle, before/by the time/already y vocabulario de experiencias pasadas.
description: Aprende Past Perfect en inglés B1: had + past participle para secuencias en el pasado (before, by the time, already). Guía Unidad 3 con audios y ejercicios.
alt: Fórmula had + past participle del Past Perfect B1

faqs.answer: had + past participle para todos los sujetos. Ejemplo: He had finished / She had never been / They had already left.
faqs.question: ¿Cómo se forma el Past Perfect?

faqs.answer: Para una acción anterior a otra en el pasado: When she got to the station, the train had already left. También con before, by the time, after y already.
faqs.question: ¿Cuándo uso Past Perfect?

faqs.answer: Past Simple narra el momento pasado (I arrived). Past Perfect marca lo que ya había pasado antes (the film had started). Sin contraste de “antes”, suele bastar Past Simple.
faqs.question: ¿Past Perfect o Past Simple?

faqs.answer: “Para cuando…”. By the time we arrived, the film had already started = la película ya había empezado cuando llegamos.
faqs.question: ¿Qué significa by the time?

faqs.answer: En el [cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-3-past-perfect-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la Unidad 3 del curso B1 de Linguafly: gramática, vocabulario de past experiences, reading, listening, speaking y writing con Past Perfect.
faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 3 del curso B1?

content:
Tras el [Present Perfect Continuous](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-2-present-perfect-continuous), la **Unidad 3 del curso B1** (*Past Perfect*) te enseña a ordenar el pasado: ***He had finished his homework before I arrived***. Usas *had + past participle* con *before*, *by the time* y *already*, y vocabulario de **past experiences**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 3 — Past Perfect](/curso-b1/unit-3)  
> **Antes:** [U2 — Present Perfect Continuous](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-2-present-perfect-continuous) · [Guía Past Perfect](/blog/gramatica/past-perfect-ingles)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 3 (B1)

- Formar **had + past participle** (todos los sujetos).
- Marcar la acción **anterior** en una secuencia pasada.
- Usar *before*, *by the time*, *after*, *already*, *never… before*.
- Contar **experiencias pasadas** (*achievement*, *turning point*, *overcome*…).
- Leer un relato con Past Perfect (viaje a Japón).

![Fórmula Past Perfect](/blog/curso-b1/unit-3/past-perfect-formula.png)

---

## 1. La fórmula

**Past Perfect = had + past participle**

| Sujeto | Auxiliar | + past participle | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| I / you / he / she / it / we / they | **had** | finished / been / left… | He **had finished** before I arrived. |

> He had finished his homework before I arrived.  
> She had never been to Paris before last year.  
> They had never met before that day.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-3/had-finished.mp3" title="🔊 He had finished his homework before I arrived."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-3/had-never-been.mp3" title="🔊 She had never been to Paris before last year."></audio>

Negativa: *had not / hadn’t* + pp. Pregunta: *Had* + sujeto + pp?

---

## 2. ¿Para qué sirve?

Past Perfect = “ya había ocurrido” **antes** de otro momento pasado.

| Idea | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| Secuencia | He **had finished** before I **arrived**. |
| Experiencia antes de un momento pasado | She **had never been** to Paris before last year. |
| Causa en el pasado | I **had forgotten** my keys, so I couldn’t get in. |
| Resultado ya listo | She **had studied** hard, so she passed. |

No es “más pasado” por moda: solo cuando necesitas marcar **qué fue primero**.

---

## 3. *before*, *by the time*, *already*

![Secuencia before / by the time](/blog/curso-b1/unit-3/sequence-before.png)

| Marcador | Uso | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **before** | anterior a… | …before I arrived |
| **by the time** | para cuando… | By the time we arrived, the film **had already started**. |
| **already** | ya (antes) | the train **had already left** |
| **after** | después de que… | After he **had graduated**, he found a job. |

> By the time we arrived, the film had already started.  
> When she got to the station, the train had already left.  
> I had already eaten when she invited me to dinner.  
> After he had graduated, he found a job.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-3/film-had-started.mp3" title="🔊 By the time we arrived, the film had already started."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-3/train-had-left.mp3" title="🔊 When she got to the station, the train had already left."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-3/had-already-eaten.mp3" title="🔊 I had already eaten when she invited me to dinner."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-3/after-graduated.mp3" title="🔊 After he had graduated, he found a job."></audio>

---

## 4. Más ejemplos del curso

> I had forgotten my keys at home so I couldn’t get in.  
> She had been to London twice before she moved there.  
> She had studied hard so she passed the exam.  
> He had left by the time I called.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-3/had-forgotten-keys.mp3" title="🔊 I had forgotten my keys at home…"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-3/had-been-twice.mp3" title="🔊 She had been to London twice…"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-3/had-studied-hard.mp3" title="🔊 She had studied hard so she passed…"></audio>

---

## 5. Past Perfect vs Past Simple

| Tiempo | Rol | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Past Simple | momento / narración | I **arrived** / she **got** to the station |
| Past Perfect | lo anterior | the film **had started** / the train **had left** |

Si solo cuentas una línea temporal sin “antes”, Past Simple basta: *I finished and then I left.*

---

## 6. Vocabulario: Past experiences

| Palabra / frase | Idea |
| :--- | :--- |
| achievement | logro |
| live abroad | vivir en el extranjero |
| challenge | desafío |
| experience | experiencia |
| overcome | superar |
| memory | recuerdo |
| learn from | aprender de |
| setback | contratiempo |
| turn your life around | dar un giro a tu vida |
| first-time experience | primera vez |
| chapter | etapa / capítulo de vida |
| look back on | mirar atrás |
| turning point | punto de inflexión |
| gain experience | ganar experiencia |
| made me stronger | me hizo más fuerte |

Con Past Perfect: *Before that trip, I had always been afraid of travelling alone.* · *That experience had made me stronger.*

---

## 7. Reading: Japan trip

![Viaje a Japón](/blog/curso-b1/unit-3/japan-trip.png)

> Last year I had the best trip of my life. Before I left, I had never been to Asia. I had saved money for two years and I had always dreamed of visiting Japan. When I arrived in Tokyo, I couldn’t believe it because I had never seen such a beautiful city. By the time I left, I had visited many temples and had tried real Japanese food. That trip was a turning point in my life because I had always been afraid of travelling alone. Now I know I can overcome any challenge.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-3/reading-japan.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Japan trip"></audio>

Comprueba: ¿Había estado en Asia antes? ¿Cuánto había ahorrado? ¿Qué había hecho *by the time* se fue? ¿Por qué fue un *turning point*?

---

## 8. Mini-diálogo

> Had you been to Asia before that trip?  
> No — I had never been there.  
> How long had you saved money?  
> For two years.  
> By the time you left, what had you done?  
> I had visited many temples and tried real Japanese food.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-3/dialogue-trip.mp3" title="🔊 Dialogue: Japan trip"></audio>

---

## 9. Practica en voz alta

> He had finished his homework before I arrived. By the time we arrived, the film had already started. When she got to the station, the train had already left. After he had graduated, he found a job.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-3/practice-four.mp3" title="🔊 Practice four sentences"></audio>

---

## 10. Ejercicios

### Ejercicio 1 — Forma (*had* + pp)

1. He \_\_\_\_ finished his homework before I arrived.  
2. She \_\_\_\_ never been to Paris before last year.  
3. They \_\_\_\_ never met before that day.  
4. We \_\_\_\_ finished the project before the deadline.  
5. \_\_\_\_ you already eaten when she invited you?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **had** · 2. **had** · 3. **had** · 4. **had** · 5. **Had**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — *before* / *by the time* / *already*

1. By the time we arrived, the film \_\_\_\_ already \_\_\_\_.  
2. When she got to the station, the train \_\_\_\_ already \_\_\_\_.  
3. I \_\_\_\_ already \_\_\_\_ when she invited me.  
4. After he \_\_\_\_ graduated, he found a job.  
5. He \_\_\_\_ left by the time I called.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **had** … **started** · 2. **had** … **left** · 3. **had** … **eaten** · 4. **had** · 5. **had**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Causa / experiencia

1. I \_\_\_\_ forgotten my keys, so I couldn’t get in.  
2. She \_\_\_\_ studied hard, so she passed.  
3. She \_\_\_\_ been to London twice before she moved there.  
4. I \_\_\_\_ never seen such a beautiful sunset before.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1–4. **had** (+ forgotten / studied / been / seen)
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Vocabulario

1. Something you achieved after effort = \_\_\_\_  
2. A moment that changed everything = \_\_\_\_  
3. Succeed in a difficult situation = \_\_\_\_  
4. Live in another country = \_\_\_\_ \_\_\_\_  
5. Look back at past events = \_\_\_\_ \_\_\_\_ \_\_\_\_

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **achievement** · 2. **turning point** · 3. **overcome** · 4. **live abroad** · 5. **look back on**
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Reading (Japan)

1. Before leaving, the person had never been to \_\_\_\_.  
2. They had saved money for \_\_\_\_ years.  
3. By the time they left, they had visited many \_\_\_\_.  
4. The trip was a \_\_\_\_ \_\_\_\_ because they had been afraid of travelling alone.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Asia** · 2. **two** · 3. **temples** · 4. **turning point**
</details>

---

## 11. Errores frecuentes

| Evita | Mejor |
| :--- | :--- |
| *He has finished before I arrived* | He **had** finished before I arrived |
| *When she arrived, the train already left* (orden poco claro) | …the train **had already left** |
| *By the time we arrive, the film had started* (mezcla de tiempos) | By the time we **arrived**, … |
| *I had went* | I **had gone** / **had been** |
| Usar Past Perfect en toda la historia | Solo en lo **anterior**; el resto en Past Simple |

---

## 12. Consejos y siguiente paso

1. Dibuja dos momentos: primero Past Perfect, después Past Simple.  
2. Practica con *by the time* y *already*.  
3. Cuenta un viaje o un examen: qué **habías** hecho antes.  
4. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 3](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-3-past-perfect-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 3 del curso B1](/curso-b1/unit-3).

La **Unidad 4** contrasta **Past Simple vs Present Perfect** con expresiones de tiempo.

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Lo esencial |
| :--- | :--- |
| Forma | had + past participle |
| Uso | acción anterior a otra en el pasado |
| Marcadores | before · by the time · already · after |
| vs Past Simple | Simple = narración; Perfect = “antes” |
| Vocab | turning point · overcome · achievement · live abroad |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso B1

En la **Unidad 4** estudiarás el contraste **Past Simple vs Present Perfect** (tiempo definido vs conexión con el presente) y *time expressions*.

Guías y curso:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 3 B1 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-3-past-perfect-ejercicios-soluciones)

title: Past Simple vs Present Perfect B1: yesterday, ever, just, already, yet
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 4 del curso B1: contraste Past Simple vs Present Perfect con yesterday, ever, just, already, yet y más expresiones de tiempo.
description: Contrasta Past Simple y Present Perfect en inglés B1 con time expressions: yesterday, last week, ever, never, just, already, yet, for, since. Guía Unidad 4 con audios y ejercicios.
alt: Contraste Past Simple vs Present Perfect con expresiones de tiempo
keywords: Past Simple vs Present Perfect B1
yesterday ever never just already yet

faqs.answer: Con tiempo pasado terminado y concreto: yesterday, last week/month/year, ago, in 2019, last night. Ejemplo: I went to Paris yesterday.
faqs.question: ¿Cuándo uso Past Simple?

faqs.answer: Con experiencias sin fecha concreta o conexión con el presente: ever, never, just, already, yet, for, since. Ejemplo: She has never been to Japan. I have just finished.
faqs.question: ¿Cuándo uso Present Perfect?

faqs.answer: already = ya (afirmativas): She has already booked the hotel. yet = todavía (negativas y preguntas): They haven’t finished yet. / Have you finished yet?
faqs.question: ¿yet o already?

faqs.answer: When… pide un momento concreto → Past Simple (When did you see him?). Ever pregunta por experiencia de vida → Present Perfect (Have you ever been to Italy?).
faqs.question: ¿When did you… o Have you ever…?

faqs.answer: En el [cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-4-past-vs-present-perfect-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la Unidad 4 del curso B1 de Linguafly: contraste Past Simple vs Present Perfect, time expressions, reading, listening, speaking y writing.
faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 4 del curso B1?

content:
Tras el [Past Perfect](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-3-past-perfect), la **Unidad 4 del curso B1** (*Past Simple vs Present Perfect*) te obliga a **elegir**: ¿tiempo acabado (*yesterday*) o conexión con el presente (*ever*, *just*, *already*, *yet*)?

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 4 — Past Simple vs Present Perfect](/curso-b1/unit-4)  
> **Antes:** [U3 — Past Perfect](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-3-past-perfect) · [Guía contraste](/blog/gramatica/present-perfect-vs-past-simple)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 4 (B1)

- Elegir **Past Simple** con tiempo definido (*yesterday*, *last…*, *ago*).
- Elegir **Present Perfect** con *ever/never/just/already/yet* y *for/since*.
- Preguntar *Have you ever…?* vs *When did you…?*
- Usar **time expressions** con el tiempo correcto.
- Leer un texto de viajes que mezcla ambos tiempos.

![Past Simple vs Present Perfect](/blog/curso-b1/unit-4/past-vs-pp.png)

---

## 1. La regla rápida

| Tiempo | Idea | Señales típicas |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Past Simple** | pasado **terminado** y concreto | yesterday, last week/night, ago, in 2019 |
| **Present Perfect** | experiencia / resultado **hasta ahora** | ever, never, just, already, yet, for, since |

> I **went** to Paris **yesterday**.  
> She **has never been** to Japan.  
> I **have just finished** my homework.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-4/went-yesterday.mp3" title="🔊 I went to Paris yesterday."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-4/has-never-been.mp3" title="🔊 She has never been to Japan."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-4/have-just-finished.mp3" title="🔊 I have just finished my homework."></audio>

---

## 2. Past Simple: tiempo acabado

| Expresión | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| yesterday | I **went** to Paris yesterday. |
| last week / month / year / night | They **visited** London last week. · I **went** to the cinema last night. |
| ago | I met him two years ago. |
| in + año | I **met** him in 2019. |
| When…? | **When did** you see him last? |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-4/visited-last-week.mp3" title="🔊 They visited London last week."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-4/went-last-night.mp3" title="🔊 I went to the cinema last night."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-4/when-did-you-see.mp3" title="🔊 When did you see him last?"></audio>

Si la frase **nombra cuándo** (y ese cuándo ya terminó) → Past Simple.

---

## 3. Present Perfect: conexión presente

| Expresión | Uso | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **ever** | ¿alguna vez? | Have you **ever** been to Italy? |
| **never** | nunca (experiencia) | She has **never** been to Japan. |
| **just** | acabo de | I have **just** finished / We have **just** arrived. |
| **already** | ya (afirmativa) | She has **already** booked the hotel. |
| **yet** | todavía (neg. / preg.) | They have **not** finished **yet**. / Have you finished **yet**? |
| **for** | duración | He has lived here **for** five years. |
| **since** | punto de inicio | …**since** 2019 / **since** Monday |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-4/have-you-ever.mp3" title="🔊 Have you ever been to Italy?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-4/has-already-booked.mp3" title="🔊 She has already booked the hotel."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-4/have-not-finished-yet.mp3" title="🔊 They have not finished yet."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-4/has-lived-for.mp3" title="🔊 He has lived here for five years."></audio>

Más: [just / already / yet](/blog/gramatica/present-perfect-just-already-yet).

---

## 4. Vocabulario: Time expressions

![Time expressions](/blog/curso-b1/unit-4/time-expressions.png)

| Con Past Simple | Con Present Perfect |
| :--- | :--- |
| yesterday | ever / never |
| last week / month / year / night | just / already / yet |
| ago | for / since |
| in 2019 | this week / this morning* |

\* *this morning* puede ir con ambos según si la mañana “sigue abierta” o ya cerró el día.

---

## 5. Truco: *When* vs *ever*

| Pregunta | Tiempo | Por qué |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Have you ever** been to Paris? | Present Perfect | experiencia de vida |
| **When did** you go to Paris? | Past Simple | pide fecha / momento |

En el curso también aparece un eco de Past Perfect: *He **had** already left when I called* (acción antes de otra pasada) — refuerzo de la [U3](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-3-past-perfect).

---

## 6. Reading: travel plans

![Planes de viaje](/blog/curso-b1/unit-4/travel-plans.png)

> Last year I visited five countries in Europe. I have never been to Asia yet, but I am planning to go next year. Yesterday I finished reading a book about Japan. I have already booked my flight to Tokyo. I went to Paris last month and I have just received the photos. Have you ever been to Paris?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-4/reading-travel.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: travel plans"></audio>

Marca cada verbo: ¿Past Simple (*visited*, *finished*, *went*) o Present Perfect (*have never been*, *have already booked*, *have just received*)?

---

## 7. Mini-diálogo

> Have you ever been to Paris?  
> Yes — I went last month.  
> Have you booked your flight to Tokyo yet?  
> Yes, I have already booked it. I have just received the photos from Paris too.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-4/dialogue-travel.mp3" title="🔊 Dialogue: travel"></audio>

Fíjate: *Have you ever…?* (experiencia) → respuesta con **Past Simple** + fecha (*I went last month*).

---

## 8. Practica en voz alta

> I went to Paris yesterday. She has never been to Japan. I have just finished my homework. Have you ever been to Italy?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-4/practice-four.mp3" title="🔊 Practice four sentences"></audio>

---

## 9. Ejercicios

### Ejercicio 1 — Elige el tiempo

1. I \_\_\_\_ to Paris yesterday. (*went / have been*)  
2. She \_\_\_\_ never been to Japan. (*has / had*)  
3. They \_\_\_\_ London last week. (*visited / have visited*)  
4. I \_\_\_\_ just finished my homework. (*have / did*)  
5. When \_\_\_\_ you see him last? (*did / have*)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **went** · 2. **has** · 3. **visited** · 4. **have** · 5. **did**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — *just / already / yet / ever*

1. Have you \_\_\_\_ been to Italy?  
2. She has \_\_\_\_ booked the hotel.  
3. They have not finished \_\_\_\_.  
4. We have \_\_\_\_ arrived.  
5. Have you finished the report \_\_\_\_?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **ever** · 2. **already** · 3. **yet** · 4. **just** · 5. **yet**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Time expressions

1. Past Simple: yesterday / last week / \_\_\_\_ (*ago*)  
2. Present Perfect duración: \_\_\_\_ five years  
3. Present Perfect inicio: \_\_\_\_ 2019  
4. “Anoche” = \_\_\_\_ \_\_\_\_  
5. “El mes pasado” = \_\_\_\_ \_\_\_\_

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **ago** · 2. **for** · 3. **since** · 4. **last night** · 5. **last month**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Corrección

1. *I have gone to Paris yesterday.* → \_\_\_\_  
2. *She never was to Japan.* → \_\_\_\_  
3. *Did you ever been to Italy?* → \_\_\_\_  
4. *They didn’t finish yet.* → \_\_\_\_ (más natural con PP)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I **went** to Paris yesterday.  
2. She **has never been** to Japan.  
3. **Have** you ever **been** to Italy?  
4. They **haven’t finished** yet.
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Reading

1. Last year the person visited \_\_\_\_ countries.  
2. They have never been to \_\_\_\_ yet.  
3. Yesterday they finished a book about \_\_\_\_.  
4. They have already booked a flight to \_\_\_\_.  
5. They have just received the \_\_\_\_.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **five** · 2. **Asia** · 3. **Japan** · 4. **Tokyo** · 5. **photos**
</details>

---

## 10. Errores frecuentes

| Evita | Mejor |
| :--- | :--- |
| *I have seen him yesterday* | I **saw** him yesterday |
| *I went to Japan ever* | I have **never/ever** been… / Have you **ever**…? |
| *She already booked* (sin auxiliar, si quieres PP) | She **has already** booked |
| *Did you finish yet?* (posible, pero…) | **Have** you finished **yet**? |
| *for 2019* | **since** 2019 / **for** five years |

---

## 11. Consejos y siguiente paso

1. Subraya la **señal de tiempo** antes de conjugar.  
2. *When* + fecha → Past Simple; *ever/never/just/already/yet* → Present Perfect.  
3. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 4](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-4-past-vs-present-perfect-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 4 del curso B1](/curso-b1/unit-4).  
4. La **Unidad 5** es el **repaso 1–4** (PPC, Past Perfect y este contraste).

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Lo esencial |
| :--- | :--- |
| Past Simple | yesterday · last… · ago · in 2019 · When did…? |
| Present Perfect | ever · never · just · already · yet · for · since |
| already | ya (afirmativa) |
| yet | todavía (neg. / pregunta) |
| just | acabo de |
| Truco | fecha concreta = Simple; experiencia/ahora = Perfect |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso B1

En la **Unidad 5** harás el **Repaso 1–4**: Present Perfect Continuous, Past Perfect y Past Simple vs Present Perfect.

title: Repaso B1 1–4: PPC, Past Perfect y Past vs Present Perfect
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 5 del curso B1: repaso de Present Perfect Continuous, Past Perfect, Past vs Present Perfect y el texto de Laura.
description: Integra las Unidades 1–4 del curso B1: Present Perfect Continuous, Past Perfect, Past Simple vs Present Perfect y vocabulario clave. Guía Unidad 5 con audios y ejercicios.
alt: Mapa de repaso de las unidades 1 a 4 del curso B1

faqs.answer: Las Unidades 1–4: bridge A2→B1, Present Perfect Continuous (for/since), Past Perfect (before/by the time) y el contraste Past Simple vs Present Perfect (yesterday vs ever/just/already/yet), más vocabulario de feelings, education y time expressions.
faqs.question: ¿Qué se repasa en la Unidad 5 del curso B1?

faqs.answer: PPC = duración hasta ahora (has been studying for two hours). Past Perfect = anterior a otro pasado (had finished before I arrived). Past Simple = tiempo acabado (went yesterday). Present Perfect = experiencia/ahora (has never been / have just finished).
faqs.question: ¿Cómo elijo entre PPC, Past Perfect y Past Simple?

faqs.answer: for + duración (for two hours, for five years). since + punto de inicio (since January, since 8 o’clock).
faqs.question: ¿for o since con Present Perfect Continuous?

faqs.answer: Ambos: She has already booked (conexión presente). The film had already started / the train had already left (antes de otro pasado).
faqs.question: ¿already con Present Perfect o Past Perfect?

faqs.answer: En el [cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-5-repaso-1-4-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la Unidad 5 del curso B1 de Linguafly: repaso integrado en gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening, speaking y writing.
faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 5 del curso B1?

content:
La **Unidad 5 del curso B1** (*Repaso 1–4*) no añade gramática nueva: **mezcla** lo de [U1](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-1-repaso-a2-b1)–[U4](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-4-past-vs-present-perfect) para que elijas el tiempo correcto en contexto.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 5 — Repaso 1–4](/curso-b1/unit-5)  
> **Antes:** [U4 — Past vs Present Perfect](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-4-past-vs-present-perfect)

---

## Qué integrarás en la Unidad 5

| Unidad | Tema | Señal clave |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| [U1](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-1-repaso-a2-b1) | Bridge A2→B1 | feelings, who/which, used to… |
| [U2](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-2-present-perfect-continuous) | Present Perfect Continuous | has/have **been** + **-ing** · for/since |
| [U3](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-3-past-perfect) | Past Perfect | **had** + pp · before / by the time |
| [U4](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-4-past-vs-present-perfect) | Past Simple vs Present Perfect | yesterday vs ever/just/already/yet |

![Mapa de repaso U1–U4](/blog/curso-b1/unit-5/review-map.png)

---

## 1. Línea temporal (elige el tiempo)

![Timeline de tiempos](/blog/curso-b1/unit-5/tense-timeline.png)

| Tiempo | Idea en una frase | Ejemplo del repaso |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **PPC** | duración hasta ahora | She **has been studying** for two hours. |
| **Past Perfect** | antes de otro pasado | He **had finished** before I arrived. |
| **Past Simple** | momento acabado | I **went** to Paris yesterday. |
| **Present Perfect** | experiencia / resultado ahora | She **has never been** to Japan. · I **have just finished**. |

---

## 2. Present Perfect Continuous (U2)

> She has been studying for two hours.  
> They have been living in London since January.  
> We have been waiting since 8 o’clock.  
> Your eyes are red — you have been crying.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-5/has-been-studying.mp3" title="🔊 She has been studying for two hours."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-5/have-been-living.mp3" title="🔊 They have been living in London since January."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-5/have-been-crying.mp3" title="🔊 You have been crying."></audio>

Recuerda: cantidad/resultado → Simple (*I **have read** three books this year*), no continuous.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-5/have-read-three.mp3" title="🔊 I have read three books this year."></audio>

---

## 3. Past Perfect (U3)

> He had finished his homework before I arrived.  
> By the time we arrived, the film had already started.  
> When she got to the station, the train had already left.  
> I had already eaten when she invited me.  
> After he had graduated, he found a job.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-5/had-finished.mp3" title="🔊 He had finished his homework before I arrived."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-5/film-had-started.mp3" title="🔊 By the time we arrived, the film had already started."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-5/train-had-left.mp3" title="🔊 When she got to the station, the train had already left."></audio>

---

## 4. Past Simple vs Present Perfect (U4)

| Past Simple | Present Perfect |
| :--- | :--- |
| I **went** yesterday | She **has never been**… |
| They **visited** last week | I **have just finished**… |
| When **did** you see…? | She **has already** booked… |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-5/went-yesterday.mp3" title="🔊 I went to Paris yesterday."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-5/has-never-been.mp3" title="🔊 She has never been to Japan."></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-5/have-just-finished.mp3" title="🔊 I have just finished my report."></audio>

---

## 5. Vocabulario rápido (U1–U4)

| Feelings / personas | Time expressions | Education / jobs |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| confident ↔ nervous | yesterday / last week | degree |
| satisfied / embarrassed | ever / never / just | architect |
| friendly / amazing | already / yet | professional |
| proud | for / since / ago | — |

---

## 6. Reading: Laura

![Laura en el aeropuerto](/blog/curso-b1/unit-5/laura-airport.png)

> My name is Laura and I have been working as a teacher for five years. Last year I decided to travel to Japan. I had never been to Asia before that trip. When I arrived at the airport, my flight had already left because I was delayed. I have just booked another trip for next summer. I am very excited and confident this time everything will go well.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-5/reading-laura.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: Laura"></audio>

Marca los tiempos: PPC (*have been working*), Past Simple (*decided*, *arrived*), Past Perfect (*had never been*, *had already left*), Present Perfect (*have just booked*), feelings (*excited*, *confident*).

---

## 7. Mini-diálogo

> How long have you been working as a teacher?  
> For five years.  
> Had you been to Asia before Japan?  
> No — I had never been there.  
> Have you booked another trip yet?  
> Yes — I have just booked one for next summer.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-5/dialogue-review.mp3" title="🔊 Dialogue: review"></audio>

---

## 8. Practica en voz alta

> She has been studying for two hours. He had finished before I arrived. I went to Paris yesterday. She has never been to Japan.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-b1/unit-5/practice-four.mp3" title="🔊 Practice four sentences"></audio>

---

## 9. Ejercicios

### Ejercicio 1 — Elige el tiempo

1. She \_\_\_\_ studying for two hours. (*has been / had*)  
2. He \_\_\_\_ finished before I arrived.  
3. I \_\_\_\_ to Paris yesterday. (*went / have been*)  
4. They \_\_\_\_ living in London since January.  
5. By the time we arrived, the film \_\_\_\_ already started.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **has been** · 2. **had** · 3. **went** · 4. **have been** · 5. **had**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Señales

1. yesterday → \_\_\_\_  
2. for two hours (duración hasta ahora) → \_\_\_\_  
3. before I arrived → \_\_\_\_  
4. just / already / yet / never (experiencia ahora) → \_\_\_\_  
5. last week → \_\_\_\_

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. Past Simple · 2. Present Perfect Continuous · 3. Past Perfect · 4. Present Perfect · 5. Past Simple
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Completa

1. When she got to the station, the train \_\_\_\_ already \_\_\_\_.  
2. I \_\_\_\_ just finished my report.  
3. She \_\_\_\_ never been to Japan.  
4. I \_\_\_\_ read three books this year.  
5. Your eyes are red — you \_\_\_\_ been crying.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **had** … **left** · 2. **have** · 3. **has** · 4. **have** · 5. **have**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Vocabulario

1. Opposite of confident ≈ \_\_\_\_  
2. “alguna vez” = \_\_\_\_  
3. “acabo de” = \_\_\_\_  
4. “todavía” (neg.) = \_\_\_\_  
5. University qualification = \_\_\_\_

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **nervous** · 2. **ever** · 3. **just** · 4. **yet** · 5. **degree**
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Reading (Laura)

1. Laura has been working as a teacher for \_\_\_\_ years.  
2. She decided to go to Japan \_\_\_\_ year.  
3. Before that trip she \_\_\_\_ never been to Asia.  
4. At the airport her flight \_\_\_\_ already left.  
5. She has \_\_\_\_ booked another trip for next summer.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **five** · 2. **last** · 3. **had** · 4. **had** · 5. **just**
</details>

---

## 10. Checklist antes de seguir

- [ ] Sé formar *has/have been + -ing* y usar *for/since*.  
- [ ] Sé formar *had + pp* con *before / by the time / already*.  
- [ ] Distingo *yesterday/last…* (Past Simple) de *ever/just/already/yet* (Present Perfect).  
- [ ] Elijo Simple (cantidad) vs Continuous (proceso/evidencia).  
- [ ] Uso feelings básicos (*confident*, *excited*, *nervous*…).

Si falla un punto, vuelve a su unidad y luego practícalo en el [curso](/curso-b1/unit-5).

---

## 11. Consejos y siguiente paso

1. En cada frase, pregunta: ¿**hasta ahora**, **antes de otro pasado**, o **fecha acabada**?  
2. Reescribe el texto de Laura marcando cada tiempo.  
3. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 5](/blog/curso-b1/unidad-5-repaso-1-4-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 5 del curso B1](/curso-b1/unit-5).

La **Unidad 6** abre el bloque de **futuros**: *will* vs *going to* vs present continuous, con vocabulario de travel & transport.

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tiempo | Forma | Señal |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| PPC | have/has been + -ing | for / since · evidencia |
| Past Perfect | had + pp | before · by the time · already (pasado) |
| Past Simple | V2 / -ed | yesterday · last… · ago |
| Present Perfect | have/has + pp | ever · never · just · already · yet |

---

En la **Unidad 6** estudiarás el contraste de futuros: **will / going to / present continuous**, con vocabulario de **travel & transport**.

title: Going to A2: planes e intenciones (I am going to…)
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 21 del curso A2: going to para planes e intenciones, afirmativa, negativa e interrogativa, con audios y ejercicios.
description: Aprende going to en inglés A2 para planes e intenciones: afirmativa, negativa e interrogativa. Guía Unidad 21 con audios y ejercicios.
alt: Esquema de going to para planes e intenciones A2

faqs.question: ¿Cuándo uso going to en A2?
faqs.answer: Para planes e intenciones que ya has decidido: I am going to travel to Japan next summer. No es una decisión espontánea en el momento de hablar.

faqs.question: ¿Cuál es la forma de going to?
faqs.answer: am/is/are + going to + infinitivo. Ejemplo: She is going to study engineering. They are going to move next month.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo hago la negativa y la pregunta?
faqs.answer: Negativa: am/is/are + not + going to (We are not going to stay at home). Pregunta: Am/Is/Are + sujeto + going to…? (Are you going to come?)

faqs.question: ¿Qué va después de going to?
faqs.answer: El infinitivo sin to: visit, study, travel, look for. Incorrecto: I am going to visiting. Correcto: I am going to visit.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 21 del curso A2?
faqs.answer: En el [cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-21-going-to-planes-intenciones-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la Unidad 21 del curso A2 de Linguafly: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening, speaking y writing.

content:
En la [Unidad 20](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-20-repaso-modulo-2) cerraste el Módulo 2. En la **Unidad 21 del curso A2** (*Going to: Plans & Intentions*) entras en el **Módulo 3** y aprendes a hablar de **planes e intenciones** con *I'm going to…*

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 21 — Going to: Plans & Intentions](/curso-a2/unit-21)  
> **Antes:** [U20 — Repaso Módulo 2](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-20-repaso-modulo-2)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 21 (A2)

- Usar **going to** para planes e intenciones ya decididos.
- Formar **afirmativa**, **negativa** e **interrogativa**.
- Conjugar *am / is / are* + *going to* + infinitivo.
- Hablar de viajes, estudios, trabajo y familia.
- Evitar errores típicos (*I going to*, *going to to visit*).

![Going to planes e intenciones A2](/blog/curso-a2/unit-21/a2-unit21-going-to.png)

---

## 1. Idea clave

| Uso | Significado | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Plans** | plan que ya tienes | I **am going to** travel to Japan next summer. |
| **Intentions** | intención decidida | She **is going to** look for a new job. |

*Going to* = **ya lo has pensado / decidido** (viaje, estudios, mudanza, fin de semana…).

Más adelante, en la Unidad 22, verás *going to* también para **predicciones con evidencia**. Aquí nos centramos en **planes e intenciones**.

---

## 2. Forma: *am / is / are* + *going to* + infinitivo

![Formas de going to](/blog/curso-a2/unit-21/a2-unit21-forms.png)

| Sujeto | Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| I | **am** going to | I **am going to** visit my family. |
| He / She / It | **is** going to | She **is going to** study English. |
| You / We / They | **are** going to | They **are going to** travel to Spain. |

Después de *going to* va el **infinitivo** (*visit, study, travel, buy, move…*), no *-ing*.

> I **am going to** visit Paris.  
> She **is going to** study at university next year.  
> They **are going to** travel to Spain in August.  
> He **is going to** buy a new car soon.  
> We **are going to** get married when she comes back.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-21/am-going-to-visit.mp3" title="🔊 I am going to visit my family next week"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-21/is-going-to-study.mp3" title="🔊 She is going to study English next year"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-21/are-going-to-travel.mp3" title="🔊 They are going to travel to Spain in August"></audio>

---

## 3. Negativa: *am/is/are not going to*

| Forma | Contracción | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| I am not going to… | I'm not going to… | I **am not going to** stay late. |
| he/she is not going to… | isn't going to… | He **isn't going to** buy a car. |
| we/you/they are not going to… | aren't going to… | We **are not going to** stay at home tonight. |

> We **are not going to** stay at home tonight.  
> I **am not going to** work this weekend.  
> She **isn't going to** move this year.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-21/not-going-to-stay.mp3" title="🔊 We are not going to stay at home tonight"></audio>

---

## 4. Preguntas y respuestas cortas

**Orden:** *Am / Is / Are* + sujeto + *going to* + infinitivo…?

> **Are** you **going to** come? — Yes, I **am**. / No, I **am not**.  
> **Is** she **going to** study engineering? — Yes, she **is**.  
> **What are** you **going to** do this weekend?  
> **Where is** he **going to** apply for jobs?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-21/are-you-going-to-come.mp3" title="🔊 Are you going to come?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-21/what-are-you-going-to-do.mp3" title="🔊 What are you going to do this weekend?"></audio>

Respuestas cortas: *Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.* · *Yes, she is. / No, she isn't.* · *Yes, they are. / No, they aren't.*

---

## 5. Marcadores de tiempo (futuro)

| Marcador | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| this weekend | This weekend I **am going to** visit my grandmother. |
| next week / month / year | Next year he **is going to** study at university. |
| next summer | I **am going to** travel to Japan **next summer**. |
| soon | He **is going to** buy a new car **soon**. |
| in June / in August / in September | I **am going to** finish university **in June**. |
| tonight | We **are not going to** stay at home **tonight**. |

Estos marcadores ayudan a situar el plan: no hablas del pasado, hablas de lo que **vas a hacer**.

---

## 6. Texto modelo: Emma

> My name is Emma. I am going to travel to Japan next summer. I am going to visit Tokyo and Kyoto. My brother is going to study at university next year. He is going to study engineering. My parents are going to move to a small village next month. They are going to buy a house there. This weekend I am going to visit my grandmother. She is going to cook my favourite food. I love making plans and thinking about the future!

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-21/reading-emma.mp3" title="🔊 My name is Emma. I am going to travel to Japan…"></audio>

![Planes de Emma con going to](/blog/curso-a2/unit-21/a2-unit21-emma-plans.png)

| Quién | Plan |
| :--- | :--- |
| Emma | travel to Japan next summer (Tokyo and Kyoto) |
| Brother | study engineering at university next year |
| Parents | move to a small village / buy a house next month |
| Emma (weekend) | visit grandmother |
| Grandmother | cook Emma's favourite food |

---

## 7. Listening: David

> Hi! My name is David. I am going to tell you about my plans for next year. I am going to finish university in June. After that I am going to look for a job. I am going to apply for jobs in London and Manchester. My girlfriend is going to travel to Australia in September. She is going to work there for six months. We are going to get married when she comes back. This weekend I am going to visit my parents. They are going to celebrate their anniversary. I am excited about all my plans!

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-21/dialogue-david.mp3" title="🔊 Hi! My name is David. I am going to tell you…"></audio>

Preguntas rápidas:

1. ¿Cuándo termina la universidad? → *in June*  
2. ¿Qué va a hacer después? → *look for a job*  
3. ¿Dónde solicita trabajo? → *London and Manchester*  
4. ¿A dónde viaja su novia? → *Australia* (en septiembre, 6 meses)  
5. ¿Qué van a hacer cuando ella vuelva? → *get married*

---

## 8. Mini práctica oral

> What are you going to do this weekend?  
> Are you going to travel next summer?  
> Is your family going to move soon?  
> What are you going to study / do next year?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-21/practice-four.mp3" title="🔊 What are you going to do this weekend?…"></audio>

1. Di **4 planes** con *I am going to…*  
2. Haz **2 preguntas** a un compañero (*Are you going to…? / What are you going to…?*).  
3. Incluye **1 negativa** (*I'm not going to…*).

---

## 9. Vocabulario (del curso)

| Inglés | Idea |
| :--- | :--- |
| plan / intention | plan / intención |
| holiday (UK) / vacation (US) | vacaciones |
| travel / visit / move | viajar / visitar / mudarse |
| study / work / look for a job | estudiar / trabajar / buscar trabajo |
| apply for a job | solicitar un trabajo |
| get married / celebrate | casarse / celebrar |
| next week / next month / next year | la próxima semana / mes / año |
| this weekend / soon / tonight | este fin de semana / pronto / esta noche |
| university / engineering | universidad / ingeniería |
| village / house | pueblo / casa |

---

## 10. Errores frecuentes

| Incorrecto | Correcto | Por qué |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| I going to visit Paris. | I **am** going to visit Paris. | Falta *am/is/are* |
| She are going to study. | She **is** going to study. | *she* → *is* |
| They is going to travel. | They **are** going to travel. | *they* → *are* |
| I am going to **to** visit. | I am going to visit. | Un solo *to* (el de *going to*) |
| I am going to **visiting**. | I am going to **visit**. | Infinitivo, no *-ing* |
| Are going you to come? | **Are you going to** come? | Orden: auxiliar + sujeto |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-21/he-is-going-to-buy.mp3" title="🔊 He is going to buy a new car soon"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-21/parents-are-going-to-move.mp3" title="🔊 My parents are going to move to a small village"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-21/look-for-a-job.mp3" title="🔊 I am going to look for a job"></audio>

---

## 11. Ejercicios

### Ejercicio 1 — Elige *am / is / are*

1. I ____ going to visit my family next week.  
2. She ____ going to study English next year.  
3. They ____ going to travel to Spain in August.  
4. He ____ going to buy a new car soon.  
5. We ____ going to stay at home tonight. *(negativa más adelante; aquí solo el verbo)*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **am** · 2. **is** · 3. **are** · 4. **is** · 5. **are**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Completa con *going to* + verbo

Usa: *visit / study / travel / move / cook*

1. I am going to ____ my grandmother this weekend.  
2. He is going to ____ engineering at university.  
3. They are going to ____ to Japan next summer.  
4. My parents are going to ____ to a small village.  
5. She is going to ____ my favourite food.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **visit** · 2. **study** · 3. **travel** · 4. **move** · 5. **cook**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Negativa

1. We ____ going to stay at home tonight. (*are not*)  
2. I ____ going to work this weekend. (*am not*)  
3. She ____ going to buy a car this year. (*is not / isn't*)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. We **are not** / **aren't** going to stay at home tonight.  
2. I **am not** going to work this weekend.  
3. She **is not** / **isn't** going to buy a car this year.
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Preguntas

Ordena / completa:

1. ____ you going to come?  
2. What ____ you going to do this weekend?  
3. ____ she going to study engineering?  
4. Where ____ they going to travel?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Are** you going to come?  
2. What **are** you going to do this weekend?  
3. **Is** she going to study engineering?  
4. Where **are** they going to travel?
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Completa a Emma

My name is Emma. I ____ going to travel to Japan next summer. I am going to ____ Tokyo and Kyoto. My brother ____ going to study engineering. My parents ____ going to move to a small village. This weekend I am going to ____ my grandmother.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**am** · **visit** · **is** · **are** · **visit**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Completa a David

I am going to ____ university in June. After that I am going to ____ for a job. I am going to ____ for jobs in London and Manchester. My girlfriend ____ going to travel to Australia. We ____ going to get married when she comes back.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**finish** · **look** · **apply** · **is** · **are**
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Empareja

1. I am going to…  
2. She is going to…  
3. They are going to…  
4. Are you going to…?  
5. We are not going to…  

a) pregunta · b) *I* · c) *she* · d) *they* · e) negativa (*we*)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1 → **b** · 2 → **c** · 3 → **d** · 4 → **a** · 5 → **e**
</details>

### Ejercicio 8 — Corrige

1. *I going to visit Paris.*  
2. *She are going to study.*  
3. *They is going to travel.*  
4. *I am going to to buy a house.*  
5. *Are going you to come?*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I **am** going to visit Paris.  
2. She **is** going to study.  
3. They **are** going to travel.  
4. I am going to buy a house.  
5. **Are you going to** come?
</details>

### Ejercicio 9 — Traduce

1. Voy a viajar a Japón el próximo verano.  
2. Ella va a estudiar ingeniería.  
3. Ellos van a mudarse el próximo mes.  
4. ¿Vas a venir?  
5. ¿Qué vas a hacer este fin de semana?  
6. No vamos a quedarnos en casa esta noche.  
7. Voy a buscar un trabajo.  
8. Voy a solicitar trabajos en Londres.  
9. Vamos a casarnos cuando ella vuelva.  
10. Este fin de semana voy a visitar a mis padres.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I am going to travel to Japan next summer.  
2. She is going to study engineering.  
3. They are going to move next month.  
4. Are you going to come?  
5. What are you going to do this weekend?  
6. We are not going to stay at home tonight.  
7. I am going to look for a job.  
8. I am going to apply for jobs in London.  
9. We are going to get married when she comes back.  
10. This weekend I am going to visit my parents.
</details>

### Ejercicio 10 — Tus planes

Escribe 8–12 líneas sobre tus planes:

- 3 × *I am going to…* (viaje / estudio / fin de semana)  
- 1 × *He/She is going to…* (alguien de tu familia)  
- 1 × *They are going to…*  
- 1 × negativa (*I'm not going to…*)  
- 1 × pregunta (*What are you going to…?*)

**Modelo:** Emma o David.

---

## 12. Plan de estudio (25–30 minutos)

1. **5 min** — Tabla *am/is/are + going to + infinitivo*.  
2. **8 min** — Ejercicios 1–7.  
3. **7 min** — Escucha a Emma y David; subraya cada *going to*.  
4. **5–8 min** — Graba tus planes (Ejercicio 10).

### Checklist

- [ ] Uso *am/is/are* + *going to* + infinitivo  
- [ ] Formo negativa e interrogativa  
- [ ] Respondo con *Yes, I am / No, I'm not*  
- [ ] Uso marcadores (*next week, this weekend, soon…*)  
- [ ] Puedo hablar de mis planes de viaje, estudio y familia

---

## 13. Consejos y siguiente paso

1. Primero decide el **plan** (¿qué? ¿cuándo?).  
2. Elige *am / is / are* según el sujeto.  
3. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 21](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-21-going-to-planes-intenciones-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 21 del curso A2](/curso-a2/unit-21).

La **Unidad 22** amplía *going to* a **predicciones** con evidencia: *Look at the clouds! It's going to rain.*

---

## Resumen rápido

| Forma | Estructura |
| :--- | :--- |
| Afirmativa | *am/is/are* + *going to* + infinitivo |
| Negativa | *am/is/are* + *not* + *going to* + infinitivo |
| Pregunta | *Am/Is/Are* + sujeto + *going to* + infinitivo…? |
| Uso (U21) | planes e intenciones ya decididos |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A2

En la **Unidad 22** verás **Going to: Predictions**: predicciones basadas en evidencia.

Guía blog:

- [Unidad 22 — Going to: predicciones](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-22-going-to-predicciones)

Curso:

- [Unidad 22 — Going to: Predictions](/curso-a2/unit-22)

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 21 A2 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-21-going-to-planes-intenciones-ejercicios-soluciones)
- [Unidad 21 — Going to: Plans & Intentions](/curso-a2/unit-21)

Guías relacionadas:

- [Repaso Módulo 2 A2 (U20)](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-20-repaso-modulo-2)
