faqs.question: ¿Cómo sé si estoy listo para el Módulo 4?
faqs.answer: Si describes tu casa y barrio, das direcciones, hablas de mascotas, describes el cuerpo con have got y dices qué llevas puesto con I’m wearing…, estás listo para seguir.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 30 del curso A1?
faqs.answer: En la Unidad 30 del curso A1 de Linguafly y en el cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones del blog: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y speaking.

content:
La **Unidad 30 del curso A1** (*Module 3 Review*) cierra el Módulo 3: **mi mundo** (casa, barrio, direcciones, animales, cuerpo y ropa). No introduce gramática nueva: **consolida** las unidades 21–29 para que puedas describir tu entorno y a ti mismo sin dudar.

Esta guía es un **mapa de repaso** con tablas, checklist, audios y ejercicios. Úsala para detectar huecos y volver a la [unidad concreta](/blog/curso-a1) si algo falla.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 30 — Module 3 Review](/curso-a1/unit-30)  
> **Guías del módulo:** [U21](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-21-habitaciones-casa) · [U23](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-23-there-is-there-are) · [U26](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-26-direcciones-imperativos) · [U28](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-28-partes-cuerpo-have-got) · [U29](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-29-ropa-present-continuous)

---

## Qué deberías poder hacer al terminar el Módulo 3

- Describir **habitaciones y muebles** (*living room, sofa, desk…*).
- Usar ***There is / There are*** + preposiciones (*in, on, under, behind, next to, between, opposite*).
- Hablar del **barrio** con *a/an/the* y *some/any*.
- Dar **direcciones**: *Turn left, Go straight, Past the…*.
- Clasificar **animales** (*pet / farm / wild*) y adjetivos (*friendly, cute, dangerous*).
- Describir el **cuerpo** con ***have / has got*** y *this/these*.
- Decir qué **llevas puesto**: ***I am wearing…***.

---

## Mapa rápido del Módulo 3 (U21–U29)

| U | Tema | Idea clave |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 21 | Rooms | kitchen, bedroom, bathroom… |
| 22 | Furniture | sofa, table + **mine/yours** |
| 23 | There is/are | is/are, isn’t/aren’t, Is/Are there…? |
| 24 | Prepositions | next to, between, in front of, opposite |
| 25 | Neighborhood | a/an/the, some/any |
| 26 | Directions | Turn left, Go straight, Past the… |
| 27 | Pets & Animals | pet / farm / wild + adjectives |
| 28 | Body Parts | have/has got, this/these, feet |
| 29 | Clothes | am/is/are **wearing** |

![Mapa Module 3 Review A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-30/a1-unit30-module-map.png)

---

## 1. Casa y muebles (U21–U22)

| Habitación | Muebles típicos |
| :--- | :--- |
| living room | sofa, table, TV |
| kitchen | fridge, table |
| bedroom | bed, wardrobe, desk |
| bathroom | — (lavabo, etc. según vocab) |

> There is a sofa in the living room.  
> There is a lamp on the desk.  
> This book is **mine**. That table is **yours**.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-30/there-is-a-sofa.mp3" title="🔊 There is a sofa in the living room"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-30/lamp-on-desk.mp3" title="🔊 There is a lamp on the desk"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-30/this-book-is-mine.mp3" title="🔊 This book is mine"></audio>

Guías: [U21](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-21-habitaciones-casa) · [U22](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-22-muebles-posesivos-mine-yours)

---

## 2. *There is / There are* + preposiciones (U23–U24)

| Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| There **is** | There is a sofa in the living room. |
| There **are** | There are two chairs in the room. |
| There **isn’t** / **aren’t** | There isn’t a TV. There aren’t any chairs. |
| **Is/Are** there…? | Is there a bathroom? Are there any shops? |

Preposiciones del módulo:

| Grupo | Preposiciones |
| :--- | :--- |
| U23 | in, on, under, behind |
| U24 | next to, between, in front of, opposite |

> The cat is **under** the table.  
> The bank is **next to** the pharmacy.  
> The supermarket is **between** the bank and the library.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-30/there-are-two-chairs.mp3" title="🔊 There are two chairs in the room"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-30/cat-under-table.mp3" title="🔊 The cat is under the table"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-30/bank-next-to.mp3" title="🔊 The bank is next to the pharmacy"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-30/supermarket-between.mp3" title="🔊 The supermarket is between the bank and the library"></audio>

Guías: [U23](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-23-there-is-there-are) · [U24](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-24-preposiciones-lugar-next-to-between)

---

## 3. Barrio: *a/an/the* y *some/any* (U25)

| Regla | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| Primera mención | There is **a** park near my house. |
| Conocido | I go to **the** park every weekend. |
| Afirmativa | There are **some** shops in my street. |
| Negativa / pregunta | There aren’t **any** pharmacies. Are there **any** cafes? |

Guía: [U25](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-25-barrio-the-a-an-some-any)

---

## 4. Direcciones con imperativos (U26)

| Frase | Significado |
| :--- | :--- |
| Turn left / right | Gira a la izquierda / derecha |
| Go straight | Sigue recto |
| Past the… | Pasa el/la… |
| on the left / right | a la izquierda / derecha |

> Turn left at the corner.  
> Go straight past the park.  
> How do I get to the library?  
> You can’t miss it.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-30/turn-left-corner.mp3" title="🔊 Turn left at the corner"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-30/go-straight-past.mp3" title="🔊 Go straight past the park"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-30/directions-park.mp3" title="🔊 Near my flat there are a park and a supermarket. Go straight and turn left at the corner"></audio>

Guía: [U26](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-26-direcciones-imperativos)

---

## 5. Animales (U27)

| Grupo | Ejemplos |
| :--- | :--- |
| pet | dog, cat, rabbit |
| farm | cow, horse, chicken |
| wild | lion, tiger, bear |

Adjetivos: **friendly, cute, dangerous, big, small**

> I have got a pet cat. She is very friendly.  
> Lions are wild and dangerous.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-30/friendly-pet-cat.mp3" title="🔊 I have got a pet cat. She is very friendly"></audio>

Guía: [U27](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-27-mascotas-animales)

---

## 6. Cuerpo: *have/has got* + *this/these* (U28)

| Sujeto | Forma |
| :--- | :--- |
| I/you/we/they | **have got** |
| he/she/it | **has got** |

> I have got two arms and two hands.  
> She has got blue eyes.  
> She has got long legs and big feet.  
> **This** is my hand. **These** are my feet.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-30/i-have-got-two-arms.mp3" title="🔊 I have got two arms and two hands"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-30/she-has-got-blue-eyes.mp3" title="🔊 She has got blue eyes"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-30/long-legs-feet.mp3" title="🔊 She has got long legs and big feet"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-30/this-is-my-hand.mp3" title="🔊 This is my hand. These are my feet"></audio>

Recuerda: **foot → feet**.

Guía: [U28](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-28-partes-cuerpo-have-got)

---

## 7. Ropa: *am/is/are wearing* (U29)

| Sujeto | Forma |
| :--- | :--- |
| I | **am wearing** |
| he/she | **is wearing** |
| you/we/they | **are wearing** |

> I am wearing a red shirt.  
> I am wearing a shirt and trousers.  
> She is wearing a red dress.  
> He is wearing a jacket.  
> What are you wearing today?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-30/i-am-wearing-red.mp3" title="🔊 I am wearing a red shirt"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-30/shirt-and-trousers.mp3" title="🔊 I am wearing a shirt and trousers"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-30/she-is-wearing-dress.mp3" title="🔊 She is wearing a red dress"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-30/he-is-wearing-jacket.mp3" title="🔊 He is wearing a jacket"></audio>

*Trousers* y *shoes* van en **plural**.

Guía: [U29](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-29-ropa-present-continuous)

---

## 8. Checklist gramatical del módulo

![Grammar checklist Module 3 A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-30/a1-unit30-grammar-check.png)

| Bloque | ¿Lo tienes? |
| :--- | :--- |
| There is / There are | ☐ |
| Preposiciones de lugar | ☐ |
| mine / yours | ☐ |
| a/an/the · some/any | ☐ |
| Imperativos de calle | ☐ |
| have got / has got | ☐ |
| this / these | ☐ |
| am/is/are wearing | ☐ |

Si marcas un ☐ vacío, vuelve a esa unidad del blog antes de seguir.

---

## 9. Texto modelo de repaso (todo junto)

> My name is Anna. I live in a small flat. There is a living room, a kitchen, two bedrooms and a bathroom. There is a sofa in the living room and a table next to the window. My room is small but I have got a bed and a desk. I have got a pet cat. She is very friendly. Today I am wearing a blue shirt and jeans. Near my flat there are a park and a supermarket. Go straight and turn left at the corner.

![Anna's flat and neighborhood A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-30/a1-unit30-anna-world.png)

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-30/anna-flat.mp3" title="🔊 I live in a small flat. There is a living room, a kitchen, two bedrooms and a bathroom"></audio>

Léelo dos veces. Luego **ciérralo** y descríbete a ti: casa → mascota → ropa → barrio → dirección.

---

## 10. Diálogo modelo de cierre

> **A:** What is in your living room?  
> **B:** There is a sofa and there are two chairs. The table is next to the window.  
> **A:** Do you have got a pet?  
> **B:** Yes, I have got a dog. He is very friendly.  
> **A:** What are you wearing?  
> **B:** I am wearing a shirt and trousers.  
> **A:** How do I get to the park?  
> **B:** Go straight and turn left.

---

## 11. Errores típicos del Módulo 3 (repaso)

| ❌ | ✅ |
| :--- | :--- |
| *There is two chairs* | *There **are** two chairs* |
| *I has got blue eyes* | *I **have** got blue eyes* |
| *I wearing a shirt* | *I **am** wearing a shirt* |
| *Turn left in the corner* | *Turn left **at** the corner* |
| *This are my feet* | ***These** are my feet* |
| *two foots* | *two **feet*** |
| *a blue trousers* | ***blue trousers*** |
| *The bank is between the pharmacy* | *… **between** A **and** B* |

---

## 12. Mini-diálogos por bloque

**Casa**  
> A: Is there a sofa in the living room?  
> B: Yes, there is. And there are two chairs.

**Barrio**  
> A: Where is the supermarket?  
> B: It’s between the bank and the library.

**Direcciones**  
> A: How do I get to the park?  
> B: Go straight. Turn left at the corner.

**Animales**  
> A: Do you have a pet?  
> B: Yes. I have got a friendly cat.

**Cuerpo**  
> A: This is my hand.  
> B: These are my feet.

**Ropa**  
> A: What are you wearing today?  
> B: I’m wearing a blue shirt and jeans.

---

## 13. Plantillas para autocompletar

1. There is a \_\_\_\_ in the \_\_\_\_.  
2. There are \_\_\_\_ \_\_\_\_ in the \_\_\_\_.  
3. The \_\_\_\_ is next to / opposite / between \_\_\_\_.  
4. Turn left / Go straight / Past the \_\_\_\_.  
5. I have got a \_\_\_\_. It is \_\_\_\_.  
6. She has got \_\_\_\_ eyes / legs / feet.  
7. This is my \_\_\_\_. These are my \_\_\_\_.  
8. I am wearing a \_\_\_\_ and \_\_\_\_.

### Más frases de repaso para memorizar

> There is a sofa in the living room.  
> There are two chairs in the room.  
> This book is mine.  
> She has got blue eyes.  
> He is wearing a jacket.  
> The cat is under the table.  
> Turn left at the corner.  
> The bank is next to the pharmacy.  
> I am wearing a red shirt.  
> There is a lamp on the desk.  
> Go straight past the park.  
> She has got long legs and big feet.  
> I am wearing a shirt and trousers.  
> The supermarket is between the bank and the library.  
> I have got two arms and two hands.  
> She is wearing a red dress.  
> I have got a pet cat. She is very friendly.

### Rutina de repaso de 10 minutos

1. **2 min** — 4 frases *There is/are* + preposición.  
2. **2 min** — 3 pasos de direcciones.  
3. **2 min** — *have got* (cuerpo o mascota).  
4. **2 min** — *I am wearing…* (outfit de hoy).  
5. **2 min** — Lee el texto de Anna sin mirar y resume.

### Checklist mental final

- Singular/plural → *is/are*  
- Lugar → preposición correcta  
- Posesión muebles → *mine/yours*  
- Calle → imperativo sin *you*  
- Cuerpo → *have/has got* · *feet*  
- Ahora ropa → *am/is/are wearing*  
- Barrio → *a* luego *the* · *some/any*

---

## 14. Ejercicios de repaso (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — *is* o *are*

1. There \_\_\_\_ a sofa in the living room.  
2. There \_\_\_\_ two chairs in the room.  
3. She \_\_\_\_ wearing a dress.  
4. I \_\_\_\_ wearing a shirt.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **is**  
2. **are**  
3. **is**  
4. **am**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Elige la estructura

1. This book \_\_\_\_ mine. (is / are)  
2. She \_\_\_\_ got blue eyes. (have / has)  
3. \_\_\_\_ left at the corner. (Turn / Turning)  
4. \_\_\_\_ is my hand. (This / These)  
5. The bank is \_\_\_\_ the pharmacy. (next to / under)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **is**  
2. **has**  
3. **Turn**  
4. **This**  
5. **next to**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Traduce

1. Hay un sofá en la sala.  
2. El gato está debajo de la mesa.  
3. Gira a la izquierda en la esquina.  
4. Ella tiene ojos azules.  
5. Llevo una camisa roja.  
6. Estos son mis pies.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. There is a sofa in the living room.  
2. The cat is under the table.  
3. Turn left at the corner.  
4. She has got blue eyes.  
5. I am wearing a red shirt.  
6. These are my feet.
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Corrige

1. *There is two chairs.*  
2. *I has got two arms.*  
3. *I wearing a jacket.*  
4. *This are my feet.*  
5. *Turn left in the corner.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. There **are** two chairs.  
2. I **have** got two arms.  
3. I **am** wearing a jacket.  
4. **These** are my feet.  
5. Turn left **at** the corner.
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Empareja unidad y tema

1. U23  
2. U26  
3. U28  
4. U29  
5. U24  

a) Directions  
b) Body / have got  
c) There is/are  
d) Clothes / wearing  
e) next to, between, opposite

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1 → **c** · 2 → **a** · 3 → **b** · 4 → **d** · 5 → **e**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Completa el texto de Anna

I live in a small \_\_\_\_. There \_\_\_\_ a living room and a kitchen. There is a sofa in the living room. I have \_\_\_\_ a pet cat. She is very \_\_\_\_. Today I \_\_\_\_ wearing a blue shirt. Go \_\_\_\_ and turn left at the corner.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**flat** · **is** · **got** · **friendly** · **am** · **straight**
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Escribe tu repaso personal

Escribe 10–12 frases que incluyan:

- 2 × *There is/are*  
- 2 preposiciones distintas  
- 1 dirección (*Turn… / Go…*)  
- 1 *have got* (cuerpo o mascota)  
- 2 × *I am wearing…* / *She is wearing…*

**Modelo:** el texto de Anna (sección 9).

### Ejercicio 8 — Elige la opción correcta

1. There \_\_\_\_ two bedrooms. (is / are)  
2. The table is \_\_\_\_ the window. (next to / under — “al lado”)  
3. She \_\_\_\_ got long legs. (have / has)  
4. What \_\_\_\_ you wearing? (am / is / are)  
5. \_\_\_\_ are my feet. (This / These)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **are**  
2. **next to**  
3. **has**  
4. **are**  
5. **These**
</details>

---

## 15. Plan de repaso (30–40 minutos)

1. **8 min** — Relee el mapa U21–U29 y marca 2 unidades débiles.  
2. **10 min** — Haz los ejercicios 1–4 de esta guía.  
3. **8 min** — Escucha y repite 10 audios de esta página.  
4. **8–10 min** — Escribe tu párrafo “Anna” personalizado y grábate.

### Checklist final

- [ ] Describo mi casa con *There is/are*  
- [ ] Uso 6+ preposiciones de lugar  
- [ ] Doy 4 pasos de direcciones  
- [ ] Hablo de una mascota o animal  
- [ ] Uso *have got* con el cuerpo  
- [ ] Digo qué llevo puesto hoy

---

## 16. Consejos antes del Módulo 4

1. No memorices listas sueltas: **une** casa + barrio + ropa en un solo texto.  
2. Si fallas solo en preposiciones, vuelve a [U23](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-23-there-is-there-are)–[U24](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-24-preposiciones-lugar-next-to-between).  
3. Si fallas en *wearing*, vuelve a [U29](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-29-ropa-present-continuous).  
4. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 30](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-30-repaso-modulo-3-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 30 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-30).

---

## Resumen rápido

| Bloque | Lo esencial |
| :--- | :--- |
| Casa | rooms + furniture + mine/yours |
| Existencia | There is / There are |
| Lugar | in/on/under/behind + next to/between/opposite |
| Barrio | a/the · some/any |
| Calle | Turn left · Go straight · Past the… |
| Animales | pet / farm / wild |
| Cuerpo | have/has got · this/these · feet |
| Ropa | am/is/are wearing |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

Tras el Módulo 3, el curso continúa con el **Módulo 4**. La siguiente unidad es **Can for Ability** (*can/can’t*).

Practica ahora:

title: Can for Ability A1: can / can't para habilidades
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 31 del curso A1: can y can't para habilidades (swim, cook, drive, speak), con preguntas, respuestas cortas, audios y ejercicios.
description: Aprende can y can't en inglés A1 para hablar de habilidades: swim, cook, drive, speak a language. Guía Unidad 31 con afirmativa, negativa, preguntas, audios y ejercicios.
alt: Esquema can can't para habilidad en inglés nivel A1

faqs.question: ¿Cómo se forma can para habilidad en A1?
faqs.answer: Can + verbo en forma base (sin to y sin -s): I can swim. She can speak French. Negativa: can't / cannot. Pregunta: Can you swim?

faqs.question: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre can de habilidad y Can I have…?
faqs.answer: En la Unidad 31 can expresa habilidad (I can cook). En la cafetería (U16) Can I have…? pide algo con educación. Misma palabra, usos distintos.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo respondo a Can you…?
faqs.answer: Yes, I can. / No, I can't. No uses Yes, I do ni Yes, I am para esta pregunta de habilidad.

faqs.question: ¿Qué verbos de habilidad practico en la Unidad 31?
faqs.answer: Swim, cook, drive y speak (a language), más well / very well y yet (I can't drive yet).

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 31 del curso A1?
faqs.answer: En la Unidad 31 del curso A1 de Linguafly y en el cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones del blog: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y speaking.

content:
Tras el [repaso del Módulo 3](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-30-repaso-modulo-3), el **Módulo 4** empieza con la **Unidad 31 del curso A1** (*Can for Ability*): ***can / can't*** para decir **qué sabes hacer**.

No confundas con *Can I have…?* de la [cafetería (U16)](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-16-cafeteria-can-i-have-id-like): aquí el foco es **habilidad**. Incluye **audios**, **esquemas** y **ejercicios**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 31 — Can for Ability](/curso-a1/unit-31)  
> **Repaso útil:** [Unidad 30 — Repaso Módulo 3](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-30-repaso-modulo-3) · [Unidad 16 — Can I have…?](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-16-cafeteria-can-i-have-id-like)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 31 (A1)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Usar ***can*** + verbo base (afirmativa).
- Formar la negativa: ***can't / cannot***.
- Preguntar: ***Can you / she / they…?***.
- Responder: ***Yes, I can. / No, I can't.***.
- Hablar de: ***swim, cook, drive, speak*** (+ idiomas).

---

## 1. La regla de oro de *can*

```
can + base form (infinitivo sin to)
```

| ✅ Correcto | ❌ Incorrecto |
| :--- | :--- |
| She **can speak** French. | She can **speaks** French. |
| I **can swim**. | I can **to swim**. |
| He **can cook**. | He **cans** cook. |

***Can*** es igual para todos los sujetos: *I/you/he/she/it/we/they can…*

![Esquema can can't A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-31/a1-unit31-can-cant.png)

---

## 2. Afirmativa: *can*

| Sujeto | Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| I / you / we / they | can + verb | I can swim very well. |
| he / she / it | can + verb | She can speak three languages. |

> She **can** speak three languages.  
> My brother **can** cook very well.  
> I **can** swim very well.  
> I **can** cook pasta.  
> My dad **can** drive a bus.  
> My mum **can** speak three languages: English, Spanish and French.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-31/she-can-speak.mp3" title="🔊 She can speak three languages"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-31/brother-can-cook.mp3" title="🔊 My brother can cook very well"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-31/i-can-swim-well.mp3" title="🔊 I can swim very well"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-31/i-can-cook-pasta.mp3" title="🔊 I can cook pasta"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-31/dad-can-drive.mp3" title="🔊 My dad can drive a bus"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-31/mum-three-languages.mp3" title="🔊 My mum can speak three languages: English, Spanish and French"></audio>

### Tip

Añade ***well / very well*** para matizar: *I can swim very well.*

---

## 3. Negativa: *can't / cannot*

| Forma | Uso |
| :--- | :--- |
| **can't** | Habla y escritura informal (la más frecuente en A1) |
| **cannot** | Más formal / enfática |

> I **can't** drive. I don't have a licence.  
> She **can't** drive.  
> Penguins **can't** fly.  
> I **can't** drive yet because I am only fifteen.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-31/i-cant-drive.mp3" title="🔊 I can't drive. I don't have a licence"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-31/she-cant-drive.mp3" title="🔊 She can't drive"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-31/penguins-cant-fly.mp3" title="🔊 Penguins can't fly"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-31/cant-drive-yet.mp3" title="🔊 I can't drive yet because I am only fifteen"></audio>

### No digas

| ❌ | ✅ |
| :--- | :--- |
| *I don't can drive* | *I **can't** drive* |
| *She not can cook* | *She **can't** cook* |
| *He cans't swim* | *He **can't** swim* |

---

## 4. Preguntas: *Can you…?*

```
Can + subject + base verb…?
```

> **Can** you swim?  
> **Can** you speak English?  
> **Can** you cook?  
> **Can** your sister cook?  
> **Can** you drive?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-31/can-you-swim.mp3" title="🔊 Can you swim?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-31/can-you-speak-english.mp3" title="🔊 Can you speak English?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-31/can-you-cook.mp3" title="🔊 Can you cook? Yes, I can"></audio>

### Respuestas cortas

| Pregunta | Sí | No |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Can you swim? | Yes, **I can**. | No, **I can't**. |
| Can she cook? | Yes, **she can**. | No, **she can't**. |
| Can they drive? | Yes, **they can**. | No, **they can't**. |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-31/yes-i-can.mp3" title="🔊 Yes, I can"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-31/no-i-cant.mp3" title="🔊 No, I can't"></audio>

No respondas *Yes, I do* ni *Yes, I am* a *Can you…?* (eso es para *Do you…?* / *Are you…?*).

---

## 5. Vocabulario de habilidades

| Verbo | Significado | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **swim** | nadar | I can swim very well. |
| **cook** | cocinar | I can cook pasta. |
| **drive** | conducir | My dad can drive a bus. |
| **speak** | hablar (idioma) | She can speak Spanish. |
| **fly** | volar | Penguins can't fly. |

Otras útiles: *language, pool, licence/license, yet, well, talented*.

![Vocabulario abilities A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-31/a1-unit31-abilities.png)

### *Speak* + idioma

> She can **speak** English.  
> Can you **speak** French?  
> My mum can speak three **languages**.

---

## 6. Texto modelo (familia con talento)

> My name is Lisa. I can swim very well because I go to the pool every week. My brother can cook. He makes pasta and salad. My mum can speak three languages: English, Spanish and French. My dad can drive a bus. I can't drive yet because I am only fifteen. We are a talented family.

![Familia talented A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-31/a1-unit31-family.png)

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-31/lisa-swim.mp3" title="🔊 I can swim very well because I go to the pool every week"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-31/brother-pasta.mp3" title="🔊 My brother can cook. He makes pasta and salad"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-31/talented-family.mp3" title="🔊 We are a talented family"></audio>

### Diálogo modelo

> **A:** Can you swim?  
> **B:** Yes, I can. I go to the pool every Saturday.  
> **A:** Can your sister cook?  
> **B:** No, she can't. But she can speak Spanish and English.  
> **A:** Can you drive?  
> **B:** No, not yet. I am seventeen next month. Then I can start driving lessons.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-31/sister-speak.mp3" title="🔊 No, she can't cook. But she can speak Spanish and English"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-31/not-yet-seventeen.mp3" title="🔊 Can you drive? No, not yet. I am seventeen next month"></audio>

### *Yet* = aún / todavía

> I can't drive **yet**.  
> No, **not yet**.

---

## 7. *Can* habilidad vs *Can I have…?* (U16)

| Uso | Ejemplo | Idea |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Ability** (U31) | I can swim. | Sé / puedo hacer algo |
| **Request** (U16) | Can I have a coffee? | Pedir con educación |

Ambos usan *can*, pero el contexto cambia el significado. En esta unidad practica siempre **habilidad**.

---

## 8. Errores típicos de hispanohablantes

| ❌ Incorrecto | ✅ Correcto | Explicación |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *She can speaks English* | *She can **speak** English* | Sin -s |
| *I can to swim* | *I can swim* | Sin *to* |
| *He cans cook* | *He **can** cook* | Sin -s en can |
| *I don't can drive* | *I **can't** drive* | Negativa = can't |
| *Do you can swim?* | ***Can** you swim?* | Can delante del sujeto |
| *Yes, I do* (a Can you…?) | *Yes, **I can*** | Respuesta corta con can |
| *She can cooking* | *She can **cook*** | Forma base, no -ing |

---

## 9. Pronunciación útil

| Forma | Tip A1 |
| :--- | :--- |
| **can** (frase) | A menudo débil: *kən* (*I can swim*). |
| **can** (respuesta / énfasis) | Fuerte: *kan* (*Yes, I **can***). |
| **can't** | UK *kant* · US *kænt*. |
| **swim / cook / drive** | Practica *can* + verbo enlazado. |
| **licence** (UK) / **license** (US) | Carné de conducir. |

Practica el contraste: *I can swim* (débil) → *Yes, I can* (fuerte).

---

## 9b. Mini-diálogos para memorizar

> **A:** Can you swim?  
> **B:** Yes, I can. Very well!  
> **A:** Can you drive?  
> **B:** No, I can't. Not yet.

> **A:** Can she cook?  
> **B:** Yes, she can. She makes pasta.  
> **A:** Can she speak French?  
> **B:** No, she can't. But she can speak English.

> **A:** Can your dad drive a bus?  
> **B:** Yes, he can.  
> **A:** Can penguins fly?  
> **B:** No, they can't!

Cambia solo el verbo: fijas *can / can't* y las respuestas cortas.

---

## 9c. Plantillas para copiar

1. I can \_\_\_\_.  
2. She / He can \_\_\_\_ very well.  
3. I can't \_\_\_\_ (yet).  
4. Can you \_\_\_\_? — Yes, I can. / No, I can't.  
5. My mum can speak \_\_\_\_.  
6. Penguins can't \_\_\_\_.  
7. I can \_\_\_\_ because…  
8. We are a talented family.

### Más frases para memorizar

> She can speak three languages.  
> I can't drive. I don't have a licence.  
> Can you swim?  
> Penguins can't fly.  
> My brother can cook very well.  
> I can swim very well.  
> Can you speak English?  
> She can't drive.  
> I can cook pasta.  
> Yes, I can.  
> No, I can't.  
> Can you cook? Yes, I can.  
> My dad can drive a bus.  
> My mum can speak three languages: English, Spanish and French.  
> I can swim very well because I go to the pool every week.  
> My brother can cook. He makes pasta and salad.  
> I can't drive yet because I am only fifteen.  
> We are a talented family.

Lee la lista dos veces. Luego escribe **8 frases** sobre tu familia (can / can't).

### Rutina de 2 minutos

1. Di 3 habilidades con *I can…*.  
2. Di 2 con *I can't…* (+ *yet* si aplica).  
3. Pregunta y responde: *Can you…?* × 4.  
4. Di 2 frases sobre otra persona: *She can / can't…*.

Si lo haces en voz alta, la forma base del verbo se automatiza.

### Tour guiado (modelo)

> My name is Lisa. I can swim very well because I go to the pool every week. My brother can cook. He makes pasta and salad. My mum can speak three languages: English, Spanish and French. My dad can drive a bus. I can't drive yet because I am only fifteen. We are a talented family.

Grábate leyéndolo. Luego improvisa con **tu** familia.

### Frases extra para practicar en voz alta

> Can you swim?  
> Yes, I can. I go to the pool every Saturday.  
> Can your sister cook?  
> No, she can't. But she can speak Spanish and English.  
> Can you drive?  
> No, not yet.  
> He can cook very well.  
> She can speak three languages.  
> Penguins can't fly.  
> I can cook pasta.

Personaliza con tus habilidades reales. Cuanto más verdad digas, mejor recuerdas *can/can't*.

### Checklist mental

- *can* + forma base (sin *to*, sin *-s*)  
- Negativa → *can't* (no *don't can*)  
- Pregunta → *Can* + sujeto + verbo  
- Respuesta → *Yes, I can* / *No, I can't*  
- *yet* = aún no  
- Habilidad ≠ petición (*Can I have…?*)

### Mapa rápido del módulo

| Unidad | Enfoque |
| :--- | :--- |
| U16 | *Can I have…?* (petición) |
| U30 | Repaso Módulo 3 |
| **U31** | *can/can't* habilidad |
| U32 | Sports & Hobbies (*play/go/do*) |

### Comparación rápida con otros auxiliares A1

| Pregunta | Respuesta corta | Uso |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Can** you swim? | Yes, I **can**. / No, I **can't**. | Habilidad |
| **Do** you like swimming? | Yes, I **do**. / No, I **don't**. | Gustos / hábitos |
| **Are** you a good swimmer? | Yes, I **am**. / No, I'm **not**. | Descripción con *be* |

Si mezclas las respuestas (*Yes, I do* a *Can you…?*), el oyente nota el error al instante. Practica el trío en voz alta.

### *Can* + *very well* / *a little*

| Matiz | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| Muy bien | I can swim **very well**. |
| Un poco | I can speak French **a little**. |
| Nada / aún no | I can't drive **at all** / **yet**. |

Estos matices hacen tu inglés más natural sin gramática nueva.

### Conecta con *because* (repaso U18)

> I can swim very well **because** I go to the pool every week.  
> I can't drive yet **because** I am only fifteen.  
> She can cook well **because** she works in a restaurant.

Una frase de habilidad + *because* = mini-texto listo para speaking.

---

## 10. Ejercicios prácticos (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — *can* o *can't*

1. She \_\_\_\_ speak three languages. (afirmativa)  
2. I \_\_\_\_ drive. I don't have a licence.  
3. Penguins \_\_\_\_ fly.  
4. My brother \_\_\_\_ cook very well.  
5. I \_\_\_\_ drive yet. I'm only fifteen.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **can**  
2. **can't**  
3. **can't**  
4. **can**  
5. **can't**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Forma la pregunta

1. you / swim → \_\_\_\_  
2. she / cook → \_\_\_\_  
3. they / drive → \_\_\_\_  
4. he / speak English → \_\_\_\_

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Can you swim?**  
2. **Can she cook?**  
3. **Can they drive?**  
4. **Can he speak English?**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Traduce

1. Puedo nadar muy bien.  
2. Ella puede hablar tres idiomas.  
3. No puedo conducir.  
4. ¿Puedes nadar? — Sí.  
5. ¿Puede ella cocinar? — No.  
6. Los pingüinos no pueden volar.  
7. Mi padre puede conducir un autobús.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I can swim very well.  
2. She can speak three languages.  
3. I can't drive.  
4. Can you swim? — Yes, I can.  
5. Can she cook? — No, she can't.  
6. Penguins can't fly.  
7. My dad can drive a bus.
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Corrige

1. *She can speaks English.*  
2. *I can to swim.*  
3. *He cans cook.*  
4. *I don't can drive.*  
5. *Do you can swim?*  
6. *Yes, I do.* (respuesta a *Can you cook?*)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. She can **speak** English.  
2. I can swim.  
3. He **can** cook.  
4. I **can't** drive.  
5. **Can** you swim?  
6. Yes, **I can**.
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Empareja

1. swim  
2. cook  
3. drive  
4. speak  
5. can't  

a) cocinar  
b) no poder  
c) nadar  
d) hablar  
e) conducir

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1 → **c** · 2 → **a** · 3 → **e** · 4 → **d** · 5 → **b**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Completa el texto

My name is Lisa. I \_\_\_\_ swim very well. My brother \_\_\_\_ cook. My mum can \_\_\_\_ three languages. My dad can \_\_\_\_ a bus. I \_\_\_\_ drive yet. We are a \_\_\_\_ family.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**can** · **can** · **speak** · **drive** · **can't** · **talented**
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Escribe sobre habilidades

Escribe 8–10 frases. Incluye:

- 3 × *can* (tú u otras personas)  
- 2 × *can't*  
- 2 preguntas *Can…?* con respuesta corta  
- al menos los verbos *swim, cook, drive* o *speak*

**Modelo:** el texto de Lisa (sección 6).

### Ejercicio 8 — Elige la opción correcta

1. She can \_\_\_\_ French. (speak / speaks / to speak)  
2. \_\_\_\_ you swim? (Can / Do / Are)  
3. I \_\_\_\_ drive yet. (can't / don't can / not can)  
4. Can you cook? Yes, \_\_\_\_. (I can / I do / I am)  
5. He \_\_\_\_ cook very well. (can / cans / can to)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **speak**  
2. **Can**  
3. **can't**  
4. **I can**  
5. **can**
</details>

---

## 11. Plan de práctica (15 minutos)

1. **3 min** — 6 frases *I can / I can't*.  
2. **3 min** — 6 preguntas *Can you/she…?* + respuestas cortas.  
3. **4 min** — Reescribe el texto de Lisa con tu familia.  
4. **5 min** — Grábate y comprueba: sin *to*, sin *-s*, sin *don't can*.

### Checklist

- [ ] Uso *can* + forma base  
- [ ] Formo *can't* correctamente  
- [ ] Pregunto *Can…?*  
- [ ] Respondo *Yes, I can / No, I can't*  
- [ ] Conozco swim, cook, drive, speak

---

## 12. Consejos para practicar

1. **Lista de 10 habilidades:** marca *can* / *can't* en voz alta.  
2. **Entrevista** a un compañero: 5 × *Can you…?*  
3. **Combina** U16: *I can cook. Can I have a coffee?* (dos usos).  
4. Prepárate para la [Unidad 32](/curso-a1/unit-32): *Sports & Hobbies* (*play/go/do*).  
5. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 31](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-31-can-habilidad-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 31 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-31).

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Lo esencial |
| :--- | :--- |
| Forma | can + base verb |
| Negativa | can't / cannot |
| Pregunta | Can + subject + verb? |
| Respuestas | Yes, I can. / No, I can't. |
| Vocab | swim · cook · drive · speak |
| Tip | sin *to*, sin *-s*, sin *don't can* |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

Continúa con la [**Unidad 32 — Deportes y hobbies: play, go, do**](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-32-deportes-hobbies-play-go-do): *play football*, *go swimming*, *do yoga*.

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 31 A1 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-31-can-habilidad-ejercicios-soluciones)

Guías relacionadas:

- [Can / Could en inglés](/blog/gramatica/can-could-ingles)
- [Verbos modales: guía](/blog/gramatica/verbos-modales-ingles-guia)
- [Inglés A1: guía para empezar](/blog/metodos/ingles-a1)

---

## Fuentes

- CEFR/MCER — Nivel A1: https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages
- British Council — Can / can't: https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/grammar/a1-a2-grammar/can-cant
- British Council — Ability: https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/grammar/english-grammar-reference/can-ability

title: Sports & Hobbies A1: play, go y do con deportes
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 32 del curso A1: deportes y hobbies con play, go y do, más like + painting/reading, con audios y ejercicios.
description: Aprende play football, go swimming y do yoga en inglés A1, más hobbies como painting y reading. Guía Unidad 32 con audios, esquemas y ejercicios.
alt: Esquema play go do con deportes y hobbies en inglés A1

faqs.question: ¿Cuándo uso play, go y do con deportes?
faqs.answer: Play + deportes de pelota (play football, play tennis). Go + actividad en -ing (go swimming, go running). Do + yoga, exercise, gymnastics.

faqs.question: ¿Se dice play swimming o go swimming?
faqs.answer: Go swimming. Con natación, running o cycling usamos go + -ing, no play.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo hablo de hobbies como reading o painting?
faqs.answer: Suele usarse like / love / enjoy + -ing: She likes reading and painting. No hace falta play/go/do con estos hobbies.

faqs.question: ¿Qué vocabulario practico en la Unidad 32?
faqs.answer: Football, tennis, swimming, yoga, painting, reading, basketball, running, exercise, team, pool, active.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 32 del curso A1?
faqs.answer: En la Unidad 32 del curso A1 de Linguafly y en el cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones del blog: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y speaking.

content:
En la [Unidad 31](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-31-can-habilidad) dijiste qué **puedes** hacer (*I can swim*). En la **Unidad 32 del curso A1** (*Sports & Hobbies*) aprendes a hablar de **deportes y hobbies** con la tríada ***play / go / do***.

Combina bien con *like + -ing* de la [Unidad 18](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-18-gustos-like-ing-because) y con los [días de la semana](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-12-dias-semana). Incluye **audios**, **esquemas** y **ejercicios**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 32 — Sports & Hobbies](/curso-a1/unit-32)  
> **Repaso útil:** [Unidad 31 — Can](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-31-can-habilidad) · [Unidad 18 — Gustos](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-18-gustos-like-ing-because)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 32 (A1)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Usar ***play*** con deportes de pelota.
- Usar ***go + -ing*** (*go swimming, go running*).
- Usar ***do*** con *yoga, exercise…*.
- Hablar de hobbies: ***painting, reading*** (+ *like*).
- Combinar con días y frecuencia: *every Saturday, twice a week*.

---

## 1. La regla *play / go / do*

| Verbo | Con qué | Ejemplos |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **play** | deportes de pelota / juegos | play football, play tennis, play basketball |
| **go** | actividades en **-ing** | go swimming, go running, go cycling |
| **do** | actividades sin pelota / “hacer” | do yoga, do exercise, do gymnastics |

![Esquema play go do A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-32/a1-unit32-play-go-do.png)

```
play + sport (ball)
go + -ing activity
do + yoga / exercise / …
```

### Tip

No digas *play swimming* ni *go football*. Elige el verbo según el tipo de actividad.

---

## 2. *Play* — football, tennis, basketball

> I **play** football every Saturday.  
> They **play** tennis at the club.  
> I **play** football with my friends.  
> I **play** tennis and football.  
> They **play** basketball at school.  
> My mum **plays** tennis twice a week.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-32/play-football-saturday.mp3" title="🔊 I play football every Saturday"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-32/play-tennis-club.mp3" title="🔊 They play tennis at the club"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-32/play-football-friends.mp3" title="🔊 I play football with my friends"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-32/play-tennis-football.mp3" title="🔊 I play tennis and football"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-32/play-basketball.mp3" title="🔊 They play basketball at school"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-32/mum-tennis.mp3" title="🔊 My mum plays tennis twice a week"></audio>

### Nota UK/US

*Football* (UK) ≈ *soccer* (US). En el curso usamos ***football***.

---

## 3. *Go* — swimming, running, cycling

> She **goes** swimming on Mondays.  
> She **goes** swimming every weekend.  
> On Sundays I **go** swimming at the pool.  
> I **go** running in the park.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-32/goes-swimming-mondays.mp3" title="🔊 She goes swimming on Mondays"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-32/goes-swimming-weekend.mp3" title="🔊 She goes swimming every weekend"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-32/jake-swimming.mp3" title="🔊 On Sundays I go swimming at the pool"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-32/go-running.mp3" title="🔊 I go running in the park"></audio>

### Concordancia Present Simple

| Sujeto | Forma |
| :--- | :--- |
| I / you / we / they | go swimming |
| he / she / it | **goes** swimming |

---

## 4. *Do* — yoga, exercise

> We **do** yoga in the morning.  
> My sister **does** yoga every morning.  
> We **do** exercise every day.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-32/do-yoga-morning.mp3" title="🔊 We do yoga in the morning"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-32/sister-yoga.mp3" title="🔊 My sister does yoga every morning"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-32/do-exercise.mp3" title="🔊 We do exercise every day"></audio>

He/she → ***does*** yoga / exercise.

---

## 5. Hobbies: *painting* y *reading*

Con hobbies creativos o de ocio suele usarse ***like / love / enjoy + -ing*** (repaso U18), no *play/go/do*:

> My sister **likes** painting and reading.  
> He **likes** painting and reading.  
> She **likes** reading and painting.  
> She doesn’t like football but she likes reading and painting.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-32/likes-painting-reading.mp3" title="🔊 My sister likes painting and reading"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-32/likes-painting.mp3" title="🔊 He likes painting and reading"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-32/likes-reading-painting.mp3" title="🔊 She likes reading and painting"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-32/sister-reading.mp3" title="🔊 She doesn't like football but she likes reading and painting"></audio>

![Vocabulario sports hobbies A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-32/a1-unit32-sports-hobbies.png)

| Hobby | Frase típica |
| :--- | :--- |
| painting | I like painting. |
| reading | She likes reading. |
| football | I play football. |
| swimming | I go swimming. |
| yoga | I do yoga. |

---

## 6. Preguntas útiles

> **What sports do you play?**  
> I play football and tennis.  
> **Do you go swimming?** — Yes, I do. / No, I don’t.  
> **Does she do yoga?** — Yes, she does.  
> **What do you like doing** at the weekend?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-32/what-do-you-play.mp3" title="🔊 What sports do you play? I play football and tennis"></audio>

### Combina con *can* (U31)

> I **can** swim. I **go** swimming every Sunday.  
> She **can** play tennis. She **plays** tennis twice a week.

---

## 7. Texto modelo (familia activa)

> My name is Jake. I love sport. I play football every Saturday with my team. On Sundays I go swimming at the pool. My sister does yoga every morning. She doesn’t like football but she likes reading and painting. My mum plays tennis twice a week. We are an active family.

![Active family sports hobbies A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-32/a1-unit32-active-family.png)

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-32/jake-football.mp3" title="🔊 I play football every Saturday with my team"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-32/active-family.mp3" title="🔊 We are an active family"></audio>

### Diálogo modelo

> **A:** What sports do you play?  
> **B:** I play football every Saturday. And you?  
> **A:** I go swimming on Sundays. Does your sister play football?  
> **B:** No, she doesn’t. She does yoga and she likes reading and painting.  
> **A:** Nice! Does your mum play tennis?  
> **B:** Yes, she does — twice a week. We’re an active family.

---

## 8. Errores típicos de hispanohablantes

| ❌ Incorrecto | ✅ Correcto | Explicación |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *play swimming* | ***go** swimming* | -ing → go |
| *go football* | ***play** football* | pelota → play |
| *do tennis* | ***play** tennis* | pelota → play |
| *play yoga* | ***do** yoga* | yoga → do |
| *She go swimming* | *She **goes** swimming* | 3.ª persona |
| *I play the football* | *I play football* | Sin *the* (A1 general) |
| *I do painting* (A1) | *I **like** painting* | Hobby → like + -ing |

---

## 9. Pronunciación útil

| Forma | Tip A1 |
| :--- | :--- |
| **play / plays** | *plei* · *pleiz*. |
| **go / goes** | *gou* · *gouz*. |
| **do / does** | *duː* · *daz*. |
| **swimming** | *SWI-ming* (doble m). |
| **football** | UK *FUT-bool*. |
| **yoga** | *IOU-ga*. |

Practica el trío: *play football → go swimming → do yoga*.

---

## 9b. Mini-diálogos para memorizar

> **A:** Do you play football?  
> **B:** Yes, I do. Every Saturday.  
> **A:** Do you go swimming?  
> **B:** Yes — on Sundays.

> **A:** Does she do yoga?  
> **B:** Yes, she does. Every morning.  
> **A:** Does she like football?  
> **B:** No. She likes reading and painting.

> **A:** What sports do you play?  
> **B:** Football and tennis. My mum plays tennis twice a week.

Cambia solo el deporte: fijas *play / go / do*.

---

## 9c. Plantillas para copiar

1. I play \_\_\_\_ every \_\_\_\_.  
2. She / He goes \_\_\_\_ing on \_\_\_\_.  
3. We do \_\_\_\_ in the morning.  
4. I like \_\_\_\_ing and \_\_\_\_ing.  
5. What sports do you play?  
6. Do you go swimming? — Yes, I do.  
7. Does she do yoga? — Yes, she does.  
8. We are an active family.

### Más frases para memorizar

> I play football every Saturday.  
> She goes swimming on Mondays.  
> We do yoga in the morning.  
> They play tennis at the club.  
> My sister likes painting and reading.  
> I play football with my friends.  
> She goes swimming every weekend.  
> He likes painting and reading.  
> I play tennis and football.  
> She likes reading and painting.  
> I go running in the park.  
> We do exercise every day.  
> They play basketball at school.  
> I play football every Saturday with my team.  
> On Sundays I go swimming at the pool.  
> My sister does yoga every morning.  
> My mum plays tennis twice a week.  
> We are an active family.

Lee la lista dos veces. Luego describe **tu** semana deportiva en 8 frases.

### Rutina de 2 minutos

1. Di 2 frases *play…*.  
2. Di 2 frases *go …ing*.  
3. Di 2 frases *do…*.  
4. Di 2 hobbies con *like + -ing*.

Si lo unes a días (*on Monday, every Saturday*), practicas U12 + U32 a la vez.

### Combinar *can* (U31) con *play / go / do* (U32)

En la unidad anterior practicaste habilidad (*I can swim*). Aquí hablas de **hábito**: *I go swimming*. Las dos ideas van juntas en la vida real:

| Habilidad (can) | Hábito (play/go/do) |
| :--- | :--- |
| I can swim. | I go swimming on Sundays. |
| She can play tennis. | She plays tennis twice a week. |
| We can do yoga. | We do yoga in the morning. |
| He can run. | He goes running in the park. |

Modelo corto:

> I can swim very well. On Sundays I go swimming at the pool.  
> My mum can play tennis. She plays tennis twice a week.  
> My sister can paint. She likes painting and reading.

Así unes **capacidad** + **rutina** sin mezclar las formas: *can* no lleva *-s*; *plays / goes / does* sí.

### Mini-historia para reescribir

Lee y sustituye los deportes por los tuyos:

> Every Saturday I play football with my friends. On Sunday I go swimming. On Monday I do exercise at home. In the evening I like reading. My brother plays basketball at school. My dad goes cycling at the weekend. We are an active family.

Cambia *football → tennis*, *swimming → running*, *exercise → yoga*, y vuelve a decirlo en voz alta. El verbo (*play / go / do*) debe quedarse bien elegido.

### Tour guiado (modelo)

> My name is Jake. I love sport. I play football every Saturday with my team. On Sundays I go swimming at the pool. My sister does yoga every morning. She doesn’t like football but she likes reading and painting. My mum plays tennis twice a week. We are an active family.

Grábate leyéndolo. Luego improvisa con **tu** familia.

### Frases extra para practicar en voz alta

> What sports do you play?  
> I play football and tennis.  
> Do you go swimming?  
> Yes, I do — every weekend.  
> Does she do yoga?  
> Yes, she does.  
> I go running in the park.  
> We do exercise every day.  
> She likes reading and painting.  
> We’re an active family.

Personaliza con tus hobbies reales. Cuanto más concreto el día, mejor.

### Checklist mental

- Pelota → **play**  
- Actividad *-ing* (swim/run/cycle) → **go**  
- Yoga / exercise → **do**  
- Painting / reading → **like + -ing**  
- he/she → *plays / goes / does*  
- Pregunta → *What sports do you play?*

### Combina U18 + U31 + U32

| Idea | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| Gusto | I **like** swimming. |
| Habilidad | I **can** swim. |
| Actividad | I **go** swimming on Sundays. |

Las tres juntas dan un speaking A1 completo sobre ocio.

### Mapa rápido

| Unidad | Enfoque |
| :--- | :--- |
| U18 | like + -ing |
| U31 | can / can't |
| **U32** | play / go / do |
| U33 | Adverbs of frequency |

---

## 10. Ejercicios prácticos (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — *play / go / do*

1. I \_\_\_\_ football every Saturday.  
2. She \_\_\_\_ swimming on Mondays. (goes)  
3. We \_\_\_\_ yoga in the morning.  
4. They \_\_\_\_ tennis at the club.  
5. We \_\_\_\_ exercise every day.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **play**  
2. **goes**  
3. **do**  
4. **play**  
5. **do**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Elige el verbo

1. swimming → play / **go** / do  
2. football → **play** / go / do  
3. yoga → play / go / **do**  
4. running → play / **go** / do  
5. basketball → **play** / go / do

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **go** · 2. **play** · 3. **do** · 4. **go** · 5. **play**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Traduce

1. Juego al fútbol cada sábado.  
2. Ella va a nadar los lunes.  
3. Hacemos yoga por la mañana.  
4. Le gusta leer y pintar.  
5. ¿Qué deportes practicas?  
6. Mi madre juega al tenis dos veces a la semana.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I play football every Saturday.  
2. She goes swimming on Mondays.  
3. We do yoga in the morning.  
4. She likes reading and painting.  
5. What sports do you play?  
6. My mum plays tennis twice a week.
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Corrige

1. *I play swimming.*  
2. *She go swimming every week.*  
3. *We play yoga.*  
4. *I go football.*  
5. *He do exercise.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I **go** swimming.  
2. She **goes** swimming every week.  
3. We **do** yoga.  
4. I **play** football.  
5. He **does** exercise.
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Empareja

1. play  
2. go  
3. do  
4. like  

a) yoga, exercise  
b) football, tennis  
c) painting, reading  
d) swimming, running

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1 → **b** · 2 → **d** · 3 → **a** · 4 → **c**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Completa el texto

My name is Jake. I \_\_\_\_ football every Saturday. On Sundays I \_\_\_\_ swimming at the pool. My sister \_\_\_\_ yoga every morning. She likes \_\_\_\_ and painting. My mum \_\_\_\_ tennis twice a week. We are an \_\_\_\_ family.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**play** · **go** · **does** · **reading** · **plays** · **active**
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Escribe tu semana

Escribe 8–10 frases. Incluye:

- 2 × *play*  
- 2 × *go …ing*  
- 1 × *do*  
- 2 hobbies con *like*  
- al menos 2 días o frecuencias (*every Saturday, twice a week*)

**Modelo:** el texto de Jake (sección 7).

### Ejercicio 8 — Elige la opción correcta

1. She \_\_\_\_ swimming every weekend. (go / goes / play)  
2. I \_\_\_\_ football with my friends. (play / go / do)  
3. We \_\_\_\_ yoga in the morning. (do / play / go)  
4. He likes \_\_\_\_. (painting / paint / paints)  
5. What sports \_\_\_\_ you play? (do / does / are)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **goes**  
2. **play**  
3. **do**  
4. **painting**  
5. **do**
</details>

---

## 11. Plan de práctica (15 minutos)

1. **3 min** — Tabla mental: 5 *play*, 5 *go*, 3 *do*.  
2. **3 min** — Preguntas *Do you play/go/do…?*  
3. **4 min** — Reescribe el texto de Jake.  
4. **5 min** — Grábate y comprueba 3.ª persona (*plays/goes/does*).

### Checklist

- [ ] Sé elegir *play / go / do*  
- [ ] Uso *goes / plays / does* con he/she  
- [ ] Hablo de painting/reading con *like*  
- [ ] Pregunto *What sports do you play?*  
- [ ] Combino con días y frecuencia

---

## 12. Consejos para practicar

1. **Calendario semanal:** escribe un deporte/hobby por día.  
2. **Pareja:** entrevista con 6 preguntas *Do you…?*  
3. **Combina** U31: *I can swim → I go swimming.*  
4. Prepárate para la [Unidad 33](/curso-a1/unit-33): *Adverbs of Frequency*.  
5. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 32](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-32-deportes-hobbies-play-go-do-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 32 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-32).

---

## Resumen rápido

| Verbo | Uso | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **play** | pelota | play football |
| **go** | -ing | go swimming |
| **do** | yoga / exercise | do yoga |
| **like** | hobbies | like reading |
| **Tip** | he/she | plays / goes / does |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

Continúa con la [**Unidad 33 — Adverbios de frecuencia**](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-33-adverbios-frecuencia): *always, usually, often, sometimes, never*.

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 32 A1 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-32-deportes-hobbies-play-go-do-ejercicios-soluciones)

Antes de pasar de unidad, escribe ocho frases reales sobre tu semana: dos con *play*, dos con *go …ing*, dos con *do*, y dos hobbies con *like + -ing*. Léelas en voz alta y comprueba la *-s* de la tercera persona.

Guías relacionadas:

- [Inglés para deportes](/blog/metodos/ingles-para-deportes)
- [Inglés en playas y deportes acuáticos](/blog/viajes/ingles-playas-deportes-acuaticos)
- [Inglés A1: guía para empezar](/blog/metodos/ingles-a1)

---

## Fuentes

- CEFR/MCER — Nivel A1: https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages
- British Council — Play, go, do: https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/grammar/a1-a2-grammar/play-go-do
- British Council — Sports vocabulary: https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/vocabulary/a1-a2-vocabulary

faqs.question: ¿Cuáles son los adverbios de frecuencia en A1?
faqs.answer: Los cinco básicos son always (siempre), usually (normalmente), often (a menudo), sometimes (a veces) y never (nunca).

faqs.question: ¿Dónde va el adverbio con Present Simple?
faqs.answer: Antes del verbo principal: I always get up at 7. She often goes running.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde va el adverbio con am/is/are?
faqs.answer: Después de be: She is never late. They are always busy.

faqs.question: ¿Qué vocabulario practico en la Unidad 33?
faqs.answer: Always, usually, often, sometimes, never, get up, have breakfast, go running, meet friends, eat late, relax, read books, how often.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 33 del curso A1?
faqs.answer: En la Unidad 33 del curso A1 de Linguafly y en el cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones del blog: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y speaking.

content:
En la [Unidad 32](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-32-deportes-hobbies-play-go-do) hablaste de deportes y hobbies (*I play football, I go swimming*). En la **Unidad 33 del curso A1** (*Adverbs of Frequency*) aprendes a decir **con qué frecuencia** haces esas cosas: ***always, usually, often, sometimes, never***.

Encaja con la [rutina diaria](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-13-rutina-diaria) y el [Present Simple](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-5-present-simple-rutinas). Incluye **audios**, **esquemas** y **ejercicios**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 33 — Adverbs of Frequency](/curso-a1/unit-33)  
> **Repaso útil:** [Unidad 32 — Sports & Hobbies](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-32-deportes-hobbies-play-go-do) · [Unidad 13 — Rutina diaria](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-13-rutina-diaria)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 33 (A1)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Usar ***always, usually, often, sometimes, never***.
- Colocar el adverbio **antes del verbo** en Present Simple.
- Colocar el adverbio **después de** *am / is / are*.
- Hablar de hábitos: *get up, have breakfast, go running…*.
- Preguntar frecuencia: ***How often…?*** (introducción A1).

---

## 1. La escala de frecuencia

De más a menos frecuente:

| Adverbio | Significado | % aproximado |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **always** | siempre | 100% |
| **usually** | normalmente / casi siempre | ~80–90% |
| **often** | a menudo / muchas veces | ~60–70% |
| **sometimes** | a veces | ~30–40% |
| **never** | nunca | 0% |

![Escala adverbios de frecuencia A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/a1-unit33-frequency-scale.png)

```
always > usually > often > sometimes > never
```

### Tip

No memorices solo la traducción: asocia cada adverbio a **tu** vida (*I always… / I never…*).

---

## 2. Posición con Present Simple (verbo normal)

Regla A1: **sujeto + adverbio + verbo + …**

> I **always** get up at 7.  
> I **usually** have breakfast with my family.  
> I **often** go running before work.  
> I **sometimes** meet friends for lunch.  
> I **never** eat late at night.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/always-get-up.mp3" title="🔊 I always get up at 7 in the morning"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/usually-breakfast.mp3" title="🔊 I usually have breakfast with my family"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/often-go-running.mp3" title="🔊 I often go running before work"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/sometimes-meet-friends.mp3" title="🔊 I sometimes meet friends for lunch"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/never-eat-late.mp3" title="🔊 I never eat late at night"></audio>

### Más ejemplos

> I **always** have breakfast at 8.  
> I **usually** get up at 7.  
> I **often** watch TV in the evening.  
> We **sometimes** go to the cinema.  
> She **never** eats meat.  
> I **usually** drink coffee in the morning.  
> She **never** forgets her keys.  
> I **often** go to the gym.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/i-always-have-breakfast.mp3" title="🔊 I always have breakfast at 8"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/i-usually-get-up.mp3" title="🔊 I usually get up at 7"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/i-often-watch-tv.mp3" title="🔊 I often watch TV in the evening"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/we-sometimes-cinema.mp3" title="🔊 We sometimes go to the cinema"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/she-never-eats-meat.mp3" title="🔊 She never eats meat"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/we-usually-drink-coffee.mp3" title="🔊 I usually drink coffee in the morning"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/never-forget-keys.mp3" title="🔊 She never forgets her keys"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/i-often-go-gym.mp3" title="🔊 I often go to the gym"></audio>

### Cuidado con la 3.ª persona

El adverbio **no** lleva *-s*. El verbo sí:

| Incorrecto | Correcto |
| :--- | :--- |
| She always **get** up | She always **gets** up |
| He never **eat** meat | He never **eats** meat |
| She often **go** running | She often **goes** running |

---

## 3. Posición con *be* (*am / is / are*)

Con *be*, el adverbio va **después**: **sujeto + am/is/are + adverbio + …**

> She **is never** late.  
> He **is never** late.  
> They **are always** busy.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/she-is-never-late.mp3" title="🔊 She is never late"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/he-is-never-late.mp3" title="🔊 He is never late"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/they-are-always-busy.mp3" title="🔊 They are always busy"></audio>

![Posición del adverbio A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/a1-unit33-adverb-position.png)

```
I always get up.     → adverbio ANTES del verbo
She is never late.   → adverbio DESPUÉS de be
```

### Contraste rápido

| Tipo | Orden | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Verbo normal | subject + **adv** + verb | I **often** go running |
| *be* | subject + **be** + adv | She **is** never late |

No digas *She never is late* ni *I get always up* en A1 estándar.

---

## 4. Vocabulario útil de hábitos

| Inglés | Español | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| get up | levantarse | I always get up at 7. |
| have breakfast | desayunar | I usually have breakfast. |
| go running | ir a correr | I often go running. |
| meet friends | quedar con amigos | I sometimes meet friends. |
| eat late | cenar / comer tarde | I never eat late at night. |
| relax | relajarse | I always relax at weekends. |
| read books | leer libros | I always read books. |
| watch TV | ver la tele | I often watch TV. |
| go to the cinema | ir al cine | We sometimes go to the cinema. |
| go to the gym | ir al gimnasio | I often go to the gym. |

Combina con U32: *I often **play** football. / I usually **go** swimming. / I always **do** yoga.*

---

## 5. Preguntar *How often…?*

Pregunta A1 muy útil:

> **How often** do you go running?  
> I **often** go running. / Three times a week.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/how-often-do-you.mp3" title="🔊 How often do you go running?"></audio>

### Respuestas posibles

| Pregunta | Respuesta con adverbio | Respuesta con tiempo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| How often do you play football? | I **always** play on Saturdays. | Every Saturday. |
| How often do you go swimming? | I **sometimes** go swimming. | Twice a week. |
| How often do you eat meat? | I **never** eat meat. | Never. |

*Every day / twice a week / at weekends* (U10–U13) + adverbios (U33) = hábitos claros.

---

## 6. Reading modelo: Emma

![Rutina de Emma A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/a1-unit33-emma-routine.png)

> My name is Emma. I **always** get up at 7 in the morning. I **usually** have breakfast with my family. I **often** go running before work. I **sometimes** meet friends for lunch. I **never** eat late at night because I like to sleep early. At weekends I **always** relax and read books.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/emma-routine.mp3" title="🔊 I always get up at 7. I usually have breakfast with my family"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/always-relax-weekends.mp3" title="🔊 At weekends I always relax and read books"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-33/always-usually-often.mp3" title="🔊 I always get up early. I usually have breakfast. I often go running"></audio>

### Comprueba

1. ¿A qué hora se levanta? → **At 7** (*always*).  
2. ¿Desayuna con la familia? → **Usually**.  
3. ¿Qué hace a menudo antes del trabajo? → **Go running**.  
4. ¿Come tarde por la noche? → **Never**.  
5. ¿Qué hace los fines de semana? → **Always relax and read books**.

---

## 7. Diálogo modelo

> **A:** How often do you get up early?  
> **B:** I **always** get up at 7. And you?  
> **A:** I **usually** get up at 8. Do you go running?  
> **B:** Yes — I **often** go running before work.  
> **A:** Nice! Do you eat late at night?  
> **B:** No, I **never** eat late. I like to sleep early.  
> **A:** At weekends I **always** relax and read books.  
> **B:** Me too sometimes… but I **often** meet friends!

---

## 8. Errores típicos de hispanohablantes

| ❌ Incorrecto | ✅ Correcto | Explicación |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *I get always up* | *I **always** get up* | Adv. antes del verbo |
| *She never is late* | *She **is never** late* | Adv. después de *be* |
| *I am always get up* | *I always get up* | No mezcles *be* + verbo |
| *She always go* | *She always **goes*** | 3.ª persona en el verbo |
| *I never don't eat* | *I **never** eat* | *Never* ya es negativo |
| *Always I get up* | *I always get up* | Orden A1 estándar |

### Tip *never*

*Never* = negativo. No uses *don't/doesn't* juntos en A1 básico:

> I **never** eat meat. ✅  
> I don’t never eat meat. ❌

---

## 9. Pronunciación útil

| Forma | Tip A1 |
| :--- | :--- |
| **always** | *OL-weiz* (2 sílabas). |
| **usually** | *IU-zhu-li* (cuidado con /ʒ/). |
| **often** | UK a menudo *OF-ən* (t muda frecuente). |
| **sometimes** | *SAM-taimz*. |
| **never** | *NE-və*. |

Practica la cadena: *always → usually → often → sometimes → never*.

---

## 9b. Mini-diálogos para memorizar

> **A:** Do you always have breakfast?  
> **B:** Yes, I usually have breakfast with my family.  
> **A:** How often do you go running?  
> **B:** I often go running before work.

> **A:** Is she ever late?  
> **B:** No. She is never late.  
> **A:** Are they busy?  
> **B:** Yes — they are always busy.

> **A:** Do you eat late at night?  
> **B:** Never. I like to sleep early.  
> **A:** What do you do at weekends?  
> **B:** I always relax and read books.

Cambia solo el adverbio: fijas la **posición**.

---

## 9c. Plantillas para copiar

1. I always \_\_\_\_ at \_\_\_\_.  
2. I usually \_\_\_\_ with \_\_\_\_.  
3. I often \_\_\_\_ before \_\_\_\_.  
4. I sometimes \_\_\_\_.  
5. I never \_\_\_\_.  
6. She / He is never \_\_\_\_.  
7. They are always \_\_\_\_.  
8. How often do you \_\_\_\_?

### Más frases para memorizar

> I always get up at 7 in the morning.  
> I usually have breakfast with my family.  
> I often go running before work.  
> I sometimes meet friends for lunch.  
> I never eat late at night.  
> At weekends I always relax and read books.  
> She is never late.  
> They are always busy.  
> I usually get up at 7.  
> We sometimes go to the cinema.  
> He is never late.  
> I always have breakfast at 8.  
> I often watch TV in the evening.  
> She never eats meat.  
> I usually drink coffee in the morning.  
> She never forgets her keys.  
> I often go to the gym.  
> How often do you go running?

Lee la lista dos veces. Luego escribe **tu** rutina con los cinco adverbios.

### Rutina de 2 minutos

1. Di 1 frase con *always*.  
2. Di 1 con *usually*.  
3. Di 1 con *often*.  
4. Di 1 con *sometimes*.  
5. Di 1 con *never*.  
6. Di 1 con *be* (*is/are* + adverbio).

Si lo unes a deportes (U32), practicas *I often play football / I usually go swimming*.

### Combinar U32 + U33

| Deporte / hobby | + frecuencia |
| :--- | :--- |
| I play football | I **always** play football on Saturdays. |
| I go swimming | I **usually** go swimming on Sundays. |
| I do yoga | I **often** do yoga in the morning. |
| I like reading | I **always** read books at weekends. |

### Mini-historia para reescribir

> I always get up at 7. I usually have breakfast. I often go running. I sometimes meet friends. I never eat late. At weekends I always relax.

Cambia los verbos por los tuyos y mantén los adverbios en el sitio correcto.

### Tour guiado (modelo Emma)

> My name is Emma. I always get up at 7 in the morning. I usually have breakfast with my family. I often go running before work. I sometimes meet friends for lunch. I never eat late at night because I like to sleep early. At weekends I always relax and read books.

Grábate leyéndolo. Luego improvisa con **tu** día.

### Frases extra para practicar en voz alta

> How often do you get up early?  
> I always get up at 7.  
> I usually have breakfast with my family.  
> I often go running before work.  
> I sometimes meet friends for lunch.  
> I never eat late at night.  
> She is never late.  
> They are always busy.  
> At weekends I always relax and read books.  
> How often do you go to the gym?

Personaliza horas y actividades. Cuanto más real, mejor.

### Checklist mental

- Escala: always → usually → often → sometimes → never  
- Verbo normal → adverbio **antes**  
- *be* → adverbio **después**  
- 3.ª persona: *-s* en el **verbo**, no en el adverbio  
- *never* = sin *don't*  
- Pregunta: *How often…?*

### Mapa rápido

| Unidad | Enfoque |
| :--- | :--- |
| U5 / U13 | Present Simple + rutina |
| U32 | play / go / do |
| **U33** | Adverbs of frequency |
| U34 | and / but / because |

---

## 10. Ejercicios prácticos (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — Elige el adverbio

1. I \_\_\_\_ get up at 7. (100%)  
2. She \_\_\_\_ eats meat. (0%)  
3. We \_\_\_\_ go to the cinema. (a veces)  
4. I \_\_\_\_ go running before work. (a menudo)  
5. I \_\_\_\_ have breakfast with my family. (normalmente)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **always**  
2. **never**  
3. **sometimes**  
4. **often**  
5. **usually**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Posición (ordena)

1. always / I / get up / at 7  
2. never / she / is / late  
3. often / I / go / running  
4. are / they / always / busy  
5. sometimes / we / go / to the cinema

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **I always get up at 7.**  
2. **She is never late.**  
3. **I often go running.**  
4. **They are always busy.**  
5. **We sometimes go to the cinema.**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Traduce

1. Siempre me levanto a las 7.  
2. Ella nunca llega tarde.  
3. A menudo voy a correr.  
4. A veces quedo con amigos.  
5. Normalmente desayuno con mi familia.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **I always get up at 7.**  
2. **She is never late.**  
3. **I often go running.**  
4. **I sometimes meet friends.**  
5. **I usually have breakfast with my family.**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — *be* o verbo normal

1. He \_\_\_\_ never late. (*is*)  
2. They \_\_\_\_ always busy. (*are*)  
3. I \_\_\_\_ always get up early. (— / adverbio solo)  
4. She \_\_\_\_ never eats meat.  
5. We \_\_\_\_ sometimes go to the cinema.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **is**  
2. **are**  
3. (nada: *I always get up early*)  
4. (nada: *She never eats meat*)  
5. (nada: *We sometimes go…*)
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Reading corto

Lee el texto de Emma (sección 6). Contesta:

1. What time does she get up?  
2. Does she usually have breakfast alone?  
3. What does she often do before work?  
4. Does she eat late at night?  
5. What does she always do at weekends?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **At 7**  
2. **No — with her family**  
3. **Go running**  
4. **No — never**  
5. **Relax and read books**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Completa con *always / usually / often / sometimes / never*

1. I \_\_\_\_ drink coffee in the morning. (casi siempre)  
2. She \_\_\_\_ forgets her keys. (nunca)  
3. We \_\_\_\_ eat out at weekends. (a veces)  
4. He \_\_\_\_ goes to the gym. (a menudo)  
5. At weekends I \_\_\_\_ relax. (siempre)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **usually**  
2. **never**  
3. **sometimes**  
4. **often**  
5. **always**
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Escribe sobre ti

Escribe 8–10 frases. Incluye:

- los cinco adverbios  
- al menos una frase con *be*  
- una pregunta *How often…?*  
- un deporte de la U32

**Modelo:** el texto de Emma (sección 6).

### Ejercicio 8 — Elige la opción correcta

1. She \_\_\_\_ late. (never is / is never / never)  
2. I \_\_\_\_ get up at 7. (always / am always / get always)  
3. They \_\_\_\_ busy. (always are / are always / always)  
4. He never \_\_\_\_ meat. (eat / eats / eating)  
5. How often \_\_\_\_ you go running? (do / does / are)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **is never**  
2. **always**  
3. **are always**  
4. **eats**  
5. **do**
</details>

---

## 11. Plan de práctica (15 minutos)

1. **3 min** — Escala en voz alta: always → never.  
2. **3 min** — 5 frases verbo + 3 frases con *be*.  
3. **4 min** — Reescribe el texto de Emma.  
4. **5 min** — Preguntas *How often…?* + respuestas.

### Checklist

- [ ] Conozco always / usually / often / sometimes / never  
- [ ] Pongo el adverbio antes del verbo  
- [ ] Pongo el adverbio después de *be*  
- [ ] Uso *-s* en 3.ª persona del verbo  
- [ ] Pregunto *How often…?*

---

## 12. Consejos para practicar

1. **Tabla personal:** una columna por adverbio, 2 hábitos en cada una.  
2. **Pareja:** 6 × *How often do you…?*  
3. **Combina** U32: *I often play football / I usually go swimming.*  
4. Prepárate para la [Unidad 34](/curso-a1/unit-34): *and, but, because*.  
5. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 33](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-33-adverbios-frecuencia-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 33 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-33).

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Lo esencial |
| :--- | :--- |
| Escala | always → usually → often → sometimes → never |
| Verbo | subject + **adv** + verb |
| *be* | subject + **be** + adv |
| Negativo | *never* (sin *don't*) |
| Pregunta | How often…? |
| Tip | *-s* en el verbo, no en el adverbio |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 33 A1 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-33-adverbios-frecuencia-ejercicios-soluciones)
- [Unidad 33 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-33)

Continúa con la [**Unidad 34 — And, but, because**](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-34-and-but-because): suma ideas, contraste y razones.

Antes de pasar de unidad, escribe ocho frases reales: una con cada adverbio, más dos con *be*, y léelas en voz alta comprobando la posición.

Guías relacionadas:

- [Gramática inglesa: guía por niveles](/blog/gramatica/gramatica-inglesa-guia)
- [Inglés A1: guía para empezar](/blog/metodos/ingles-a1)
- [A2 U19 — How Questions](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-19-how-questions)

---
