title: Asking for Permission A1: Can I…? y May I…?
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 38 del curso A1: Can I…? y May I…? para pedir permiso, con audios y ejercicios.
description: Aprende a pedir permiso en inglés A1 con Can I…? y May I…?, más please, excuse me y of course. Guía Unidad 38 con audios, esquemas y ejercicios.
alt: Esquema Can I y May I para pedir permiso en inglés A1

faqs.question: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre Can I y May I?
faqs.answer: Ambos piden permiso. Can I…? es más informal y frecuente. May I…? suena más formal (clase, trabajo, situaciones educadas).

faqs.question: ¿Cómo respondo a Can I…?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can. / No, you can't. También Of course. o Sorry, not right now.

faqs.question: ¿Can I have…? es lo mismo que Can I use…?
faqs.answer: Ambos usan Can I, pero Can I have…? (U16) suele pedir algo en un pedido; Can I use / borrow…? pide permiso para hacer o usar algo.

faqs.question: ¿Qué vocabulario practico en la Unidad 38?
faqs.answer: Can I, May I, please, excuse me, of course, borrow, use, open, sit, ask a question, bathroom, pen, permission.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 38 del curso A1?
faqs.answer: En la Unidad 38 del curso A1 de Linguafly y en el cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones del blog: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y speaking.

content:
En la [Unidad 37](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-37-talent-skills) dijiste *cómo de bien* haces algo (*I can sing very well*). En la **Unidad 38 del curso A1** (*Asking for Permission*) usas ***Can I…?*** y ***May I…?*** para **pedir permiso**.

Conecta con *can* de la [Unidad 31](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-31-can-habilidad) y con *Can I have…?* de la [cafetería (U16)](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-16-cafeteria-can-i-have-id-like). Incluye **audios**, **esquemas** y **ejercicios**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 38 — Asking for Permission](/curso-a1/unit-38)  
> **Repaso útil:** [Unidad 37 — Talent & Skills](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-37-talent-skills) · [Unidad 31 — Can](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-31-can-habilidad)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 38 (A1)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Pedir permiso con ***Can I…?*** (informal).
- Pedir permiso con ***May I…?*** (más formal).
- Responder: ***Yes, you can / No, you can't / Of course***.
- Usar frases educadas: ***please, excuse me, thank you***.
- Pedir en clase y en el trabajo: *borrow a pen, ask a question, come in…*.

---

## 1. Dos fórmulas, mismo objetivo

| Fórmula | Registro | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Can I** + verb…? | informal / cotidiano | Can I use the bathroom? |
| **May I** + verb…? | más formal / educado | May I ask a question? |

![Esquema Can I May I A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/a1-unit38-can-may.png)

```
Can I + base verb…?
May I + base verb…?
→ Yes, you can. / No, you can't. / Of course.
```

### Tip

Tras *Can I / May I* va el **verbo en forma base** (sin *-s*, sin *to*): *open, borrow, use, sit, ask*.

---

## 2. *Can I…?* — permiso informal

> **Can I** use the bathroom?  
> **Can I** borrow your pen?  
> **Can I** use the phone?  
> **Can I** sit here?  
> **Can I** please use the computer?  
> **Can I** borrow your eraser?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/can-i-use-bathroom.mp3" title="🔊 Can I use the bathroom?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/can-i-borrow-pen.mp3" title="🔊 Can I borrow your pen?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/can-i-use-phone.mp3" title="🔊 Can I use the phone?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/can-i-sit-here.mp3" title="🔊 Can I sit here?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/can-i-please-computer.mp3" title="🔊 Can I please use the computer?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/can-i-borrow-eraser.mp3" title="🔊 Can I borrow your eraser?"></audio>

### Tres usos de *can* (no los mezcles)

| Unidad | Uso | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| U31 | habilidad | Can you swim? |
| U16 | pedido | Can I have a coffee? |
| **U38** | permiso | Can I use the bathroom? |

---

## 3. *May I…?* — más formal

> **May I** open the door?  
> **May I** come in?  
> **May I** ask a question?  
> Excuse me, **may I** come in?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/may-i-open-door.mp3" title="🔊 May I open the door?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/may-i-come-in.mp3" title="🔊 May I come in?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/may-i-ask-question.mp3" title="🔊 May I ask a question?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/excuse-me-come-in.mp3" title="🔊 Excuse me, may I come in?"></audio>

### ¿Cuándo usar *May I*?

- En **clase** con el profesor.  
- En el **trabajo** o con desconocidos.  
- Cuando quieres sonar **más educado**.

En conversación cotidiana, *Can I…?* es perfectamente correcto.

### Extra A1: *Could I…?*

Más suave/educado que *Can I*:

> **Could I** please open the window?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/could-i-please.mp3" title="🔊 Could I please open the window?"></audio>

---

## 4. Respuestas

| Respuesta | Significado |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Yes, you can.** | Sí, puedes. |
| **No, you can't.** | No, no puedes. |
| **No, you can't right now.** | Ahora no. |
| **Of course.** | Por supuesto. |
| **Of course. Here you are.** | Claro. Aquí tienes. |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/yes-you-can.mp3" title="🔊 Yes, you can"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/no-you-cant.mp3" title="🔊 No, you can't right now"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/of-course.mp3" title="🔊 Of course. Here you are"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/of-course-short.mp3" title="🔊 Of course"></audio>

---

## 5. Frases educadas

![Frases educadas A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/a1-unit38-polite-phrases.png)

| Inglés | Español | Uso |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| please | por favor | Can I **please**…? |
| excuse me | perdón / con permiso | para llamar la atención |
| of course | por supuesto | respuesta positiva |
| thank you | gracias | después del permiso |
| borrow | pedir prestado | borrow your pen |
| permission | permiso | ask for permission |
| right now | ahora mismo | not right now |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/excuse-me-borrow.mp3" title="🔊 Excuse me — can I borrow your pen?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/please-and-thank-you.mp3" title="🔊 Please and thank you"></audio>

### Verbos útiles de petición

| Verbo | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| use | Can I use the bathroom / phone / computer? |
| borrow | Can I borrow your pen / eraser / book? |
| open | May I open the door / window? |
| sit | Can I sit here? |
| ask | May I ask a question? |
| come in | May I come in? |

---

## 6. En clase y en el trabajo

![Escenas de permiso A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/a1-unit38-permission-scenes.png)

> In class we use polite phrases.  
> At work we say please and thank you.  
> When we ask for permission we are polite.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/in-class-polite.mp3" title="🔊 In class we use polite phrases"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/at-work-please.mp3" title="🔊 At work we say please and thank you"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-38/when-ask-permission.mp3" title="🔊 When we ask for permission we are polite"></audio>

### Mini-guía rápida

| Situación | Frase modelo |
| :--- | :--- |
| Baño (clase) | Can I use the bathroom? |
| Pregunta (clase) | May I ask a question? |
| Entrar | Excuse me, may I come in? |
| Bolígrafo | Excuse me — can I borrow your pen? |
| Ordenador | Can I please use the computer? |

---

## 7. Reading modelo

> In class we use polite phrases. **Can I** use the bathroom? **May I** ask a question? At work we say **please** and **thank you**. **Excuse me** — can I borrow your pen? **Of course**. When we ask for **permission** we are polite.

### Comprueba

1. ¿Dónde se usan primero las frases educadas? → **In class**.  
2. Ejemplo de baño → **Can I use the bathroom?**  
3. Ejemplo de pregunta → **May I ask a question?**  
4. ¿Qué se dice en el trabajo? → **Please and thank you**.  
5. Respuesta a *borrow your pen* → **Of course**.

---

## 8. Diálogo modelo

> **A:** Excuse me — can I borrow your pen?  
> **B:** Of course. Here you are.  
> **A:** Thank you! May I ask a question?  
> **B:** Yes, you can.  
> **A:** Can I use the bathroom?  
> **B:** Yes, you can.  
> **A:** And later… may I come in after the break?  
> **B:** Of course.

---

## 9. Errores típicos de hispanohablantes

| ❌ Incorrecto | ✅ Correcto | Explicación |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *Can I to use…?* | *Can I **use**…?* | Sin *to* |
| *Can I using…?* | *Can I **use**…?* | Forma base |
| *Yes, I can.* (como permiso a otro) | *Yes, **you** can.* | Respondes al oyente |
| *May I opens…?* | *May I **open**…?* | Sin *-s* |
| *Borrow me your pen* | *Can I **borrow your** pen?* | Estructura inglesa |

---

## 9b. Pronunciación útil

| Forma | Tip A1 |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Can I** | a menudo /kən aɪ/ débil. |
| **May I** | *mei aɪ*. |
| **borrow** | *BO-rou*. |
| **excuse me** | *ik-SKIUZ mi*. |
| **of course** | *əv KORS*. |

Practica: *Can I…? → May I…? → Of course.*

---

## 9c. Mini-diálogos para memorizar

> **A:** Can I use the bathroom?  
> **B:** Yes, you can.  
> **A:** May I ask a question?  
> **B:** Of course.

> **A:** Excuse me — can I borrow your pen?  
> **B:** Of course. Here you are.  
> **A:** Thank you!  
> **B:** You're welcome.

> **A:** May I come in?  
> **B:** Yes, you can.  
> **A:** Can I sit here?  
> **B:** Sorry — no, you can't right now.

Cambia solo el verbo/objeto: fijas la **estructura**.

---

## 9d. Plantillas para copiar

1. Can I \_\_\_\_?  
2. May I \_\_\_\_?  
3. Excuse me — can I borrow your \_\_\_\_?  
4. Can I please use the \_\_\_\_?  
5. Yes, you can. / No, you can't. / Of course.  
6. May I ask a question?  
7. May I come in?

### Más frases para memorizar

> Can I use the bathroom?  
> May I open the door?  
> Can I borrow your pen?  
> May I come in?  
> Yes, you can.  
> No, you can't right now.  
> Can I use the phone?  
> May I ask a question?  
> Can I sit here?  
> Excuse me — can I borrow your pen?  
> Of course. Here you are.  
> Excuse me, may I come in?  
> Can I borrow your eraser?  
> Can I please use the computer?  
> Please and thank you.  
> In class we use polite phrases.  
> At work we say please and thank you.  
> When we ask for permission we are polite.  
> Of course.  
> Could I please open the window?

Lee la lista dos veces. Luego improvisa 8 peticiones de tu día (clase, casa, trabajo).

### Rutina de 2 minutos

1. Di 3 × *Can I…?*  
2. Di 3 × *May I…?*  
3. Di 3 respuestas (*Yes, you can / No, you can't / Of course*).  
4. Une con *Excuse me — …*

Si lo combinas con U16: *Can I have a coffee?* (pedido) vs *Can I use the bathroom?* (permiso).

### Combinar U16 + U31 + U38

| Uso de *can* | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| Habilidad | I can swim. |
| Pedido | Can I have a tea? |
| Permiso | Can I borrow your pen? |

### Mini-historia para reescribir

> In class I say: Can I use the bathroom? May I ask a question? Excuse me — can I borrow your pen? Of course. At work we say please and thank you. When we ask for permission we are polite.

Cambia *pen → book*, *bathroom → phone*, y mantén *Can I / May I*.

### Tour guiado (modelo del reading)

> In class we use polite phrases. Can I use the bathroom? May I ask a question? At work we say please and thank you. Excuse me — can I borrow your pen? Of course. When we ask for permission we are polite.

Grábate leyéndolo. Luego inventa un diálogo de 6 líneas.

### Frases extra para practicar en voz alta

> Excuse me.  
> Can I borrow your pen?  
> May I ask a question?  
> Can I sit here?  
> May I come in?  
> Yes, you can.  
> No, you can't right now.  
> Of course. Here you are.  
> Thank you.  
> Could I please open the window?

Personaliza objetos y lugares de tu rutina.

### Checklist mental

- *Can I* + verbo base  
- *May I* = más formal  
- Respuestas: *you can / you can't / of course*  
- *Excuse me* + petición  
- *please / thank you*

### Mapa rápido

| Unidad | Enfoque |
| :--- | :--- |
| U16 | Can I have…? (pedido) |
| U31 | can / can't (habilidad) |
| **U38** | Can I / May I (permiso) |
| U39 | Outdoor Activities |

---

## 10. Ejercicios prácticos (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — Completa *Can / May*

1. \_\_\_\_ I use the bathroom? (informal)  
2. \_\_\_\_ I ask a question? (formal / clase)  
3. \_\_\_\_ I borrow your pen?  
4. \_\_\_\_ I come in? (educado)  
5. \_\_\_\_ I sit here?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Can**  
2. **May** (también *Can*)  
3. **Can**  
4. **May** (también *Can*)  
5. **Can**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Forma base del verbo

1. May I \_\_\_\_ the door? (open)  
2. Can I \_\_\_\_ your pen? (borrow)  
3. May I \_\_\_\_ a question? (ask)  
4. Can I \_\_\_\_ the phone? (use)  
5. May I \_\_\_\_ in? (come)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **open**  
2. **borrow**  
3. **ask**  
4. **use**  
5. **come**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Traduce

1. ¿Puedo usar el baño?  
2. ¿Puedo hacer una pregunta?  
3. ¿Puedo pedir prestado tu bolígrafo?  
4. Sí, puedes.  
5. Por supuesto. Aquí tienes.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Can I use the bathroom?**  
2. **May I ask a question?**  
3. **Can I borrow your pen?**  
4. **Yes, you can.**  
5. **Of course. Here you are.**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Respuestas

1. Can I sit here? → \_\_\_\_ (sí)  
2. Can I use the computer now? → \_\_\_\_ (ahora no)  
3. Can I borrow your eraser? → \_\_\_\_ (por supuesto)  
4. May I come in? → \_\_\_\_ (sí)  
5. Can I open the window? → \_\_\_\_ (no)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Yes, you can.**  
2. **No, you can't right now.**  
3. **Of course.**  
4. **Yes, you can. / Of course.**  
5. **No, you can't.**
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Reading corto

Lee el texto de la sección 7. Contesta:

1. Where do we use polite phrases first in the text?  
2. Give one *Can I…* example.  
3. Give one *May I…* example.  
4. What do we say at work?  
5. What does *Of course* mean here?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **In class**  
2. **Can I use the bathroom?** / **Can I borrow your pen?**  
3. **May I ask a question?**  
4. **Please and thank you**  
5. **Yes / sure**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Une con *Excuse me*

1. can I borrow your pen  
2. may I come in  
3. can I pass

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Excuse me — can I borrow your pen?**  
2. **Excuse me, may I come in?**  
3. **Excuse me — can I pass?**
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Escribe diálogos

Escribe 2 mini-diálogos (4–6 líneas cada uno):

1. En **clase** (*May I ask…? / bathroom / borrow*).  
2. En el **trabajo** o con un desconocido (*Excuse me / please / of course*).

### Ejercicio 8 — Elige la opción correcta

1. Can I \_\_\_\_ the bathroom? (use / uses / using)  
2. May I \_\_\_\_ a question? (ask / asks / asking)  
3. Yes, \_\_\_\_ can. (you / I / we)  
4. \_\_\_\_ me — can I borrow your pen? (Excuse / Please / Sorry)  
5. Which is more formal? (Can I / **May I** / Do I)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **use**  
2. **ask**  
3. **you**  
4. **Excuse**  
5. **May I**
</details>

---

## 11. Plan de práctica (15 minutos)

1. **3 min** — 5 × *Can I…?* + 5 × *May I…?*  
2. **3 min** — Respuestas rápidas.  
3. **4 min** — Diálogo clase + diálogo trabajo.  
4. **5 min** — Reescribe el reading con tus objetos.

### Checklist

- [ ] Formo *Can I + verbo base*  
- [ ] Uso *May I* en contextos formales  
- [ ] Respondo *you can / you can't / of course*  
- [ ] Uso *excuse me* y *please*  
- [ ] Distingo permiso (U38) de habilidad (U31) y pedido (U16)

---

## 12. Consejos para practicar

1. **Lista del día:** 8 cosas para las que pediste (o pedirías) permiso.  
2. **Pareja:** uno pide, el otro concede o niega.  
3. **Combina** U16: *Can I have…?* vs *Can I use…?*  
4. Prepárate para la [Unidad 39](/curso-a1/unit-39): *Outdoor Activities*.  
5. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 38](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-38-pedir-permiso-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 38 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-38).

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Lo esencial |
| :--- | :--- |
| Informal | Can I + verb…? |
| Formal | May I + verb…? |
| Sí | Yes, you can. / Of course. |
| No | No, you can't. |
| Educación | please · excuse me · thank you |
| Tip | verbo en forma base |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 38 A1 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-38-pedir-permiso-ejercicios-soluciones)
- [Unidad 38 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-38)

Continúa con la [**Unidad 39 — Outdoor Activities**](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-39-outdoor-activities): *I'm going camping*, *hiking*, *cycling*, *fishing*.

Antes de pasar de unidad, escribe 10 frases de permiso reales (casa, clase, trabajo) con *Can I* y *May I*.

Guías relacionadas:

- [Can / Could en inglés](/blog/gramatica/can-could-ingles)
- [May / Might en inglés](/blog/gramatica/may-might-ingles)

---

title: Outdoor Activities A1: Present Continuous para planes (camping, hiking…)
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 39 del curso A1: actividades al aire libre y Present Continuous para planes, con audios y ejercicios.
description: Aprende a hablar de planes al aire libre en inglés A1 con Present Continuous: I'm going camping, hiking, cycling, fishing. Guía Unidad 39 con audios y ejercicios.
alt: Esquema Present Continuous para planes outdoor en inglés A1

faqs.question: ¿Cómo hablo de planes futuros en A1 con outdoor activities?
faqs.answer: Con Present Continuous + marcador de futuro: I'm going camping next week. She is going hiking on Saturday.

faqs.question: ¿Es lo mismo que el Present Continuous de ropa (U29)?
faqs.answer: Misma forma (am/is/are + -ing), distinto uso: U29 describe ahora (ropa); U39 habla de planes ya decididos para el futuro cercano.

faqs.question: ¿Qué vocabulario outdoor practico?
faqs.answer: Hiking, camping, cycling, fishing, tent, backpack, trail, mountains, outdoor, next week, tomorrow.

faqs.question: ¿Se dice go camping o going camping?
faqs.answer: Para planes: I'm going camping. Para hábitos también existe I go camping every summer; en esta unidad priorizamos going + activity para planes.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 39 del curso A1?
faqs.answer: En la Unidad 39 del curso A1 de Linguafly y en el cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones del blog: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y speaking.

content:
En la [Unidad 38](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-38-pedir-permiso) pediste permiso (*Can I…?*). En la **Unidad 39 del curso A1** (*Outdoor Activities*) hablas de **planes al aire libre** con ***Present Continuous***: *I'm going camping next week*.

Repasas la forma de la [Unidad 29](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-29-ropa-present-continuous) y *go + -ing* de la [Unidad 32](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-32-deportes-hobbies-play-go-do). Incluye **audios**, **esquemas** y **ejercicios**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 39 — Outdoor Activities](/curso-a1/unit-39)  
> **Repaso útil:** [Unidad 38 — Pedir permiso](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-38-pedir-permiso) · [Unidad 29 — Present Continuous](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-29-ropa-present-continuous)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 39 (A1)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Usar ***am / is / are + going + activity*** para planes.
- Hablar de ***camping, hiking, cycling, fishing***.
- Usar marcadores: ***tomorrow, on Saturday, next week, next weekend***.
- Preguntar: ***What are you doing next weekend?***
- Describir planes familiares outdoor.

---

## 1. Present Continuous para planes futuros

| Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| I **'m going** + activity | I'm going camping next week. |
| She / He **is going** + activity | She is going hiking on Saturday. |
| We / They **are going** + activity | We are going cycling tomorrow. |

![Present Continuous planes A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/a1-unit39-present-continuous-plans.png)

```
am / is / are + going + camping / hiking / cycling / fishing
+ tomorrow / on Saturday / next week / next weekend
```

### Tip

No es “ahora mismo”: es un **plan ya decidido**. La clave está en el tiempo futuro (*next week*, *tomorrow*…).

Con un marcador claro, el oyente entiende que hablas del futuro aunque la forma sea Present Continuous. Sin marcador (*I'm going camping*), a veces suena a “ahora / en camino”; por eso en A1 conviene añadir **cuándo**.

### Marcadores de tiempo útiles

| Marcador | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| tomorrow | We're going cycling **tomorrow**. |
| on Saturday / on Sunday | She's going hiking **on Saturday**. |
| next week | I'm going camping **next week**. |
| next weekend | We're going to the mountains **next weekend**. |
| in July | They're going camping **in July**. |

Memoriza 4 marcadores y reutilízalos con las 4 actividades outdoor.

---

## 2. Ejemplos con audio

> **I'm going camping** next week.  
> She **is going hiking** on Saturday.  
> We **are going cycling** tomorrow.  
> **He's going fishing** next weekend.

| Hábito | I **go** cycling every Sunday. | U32 / Present Simple |

## 3. Vocabulario outdoor

![Vocabulario outdoor A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/a1-unit39-outdoor-vocab.png)

| Inglés | Español | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| outdoor | al aire libre | outdoor activities |
| hiking | senderismo | going hiking |
| camping | camping / acampar | going camping |

| fishing | pesca | going fishing |

| backpack | mochila | backpacks |

| mountains | montañas | to the mountains |
| next week | la próxima semana | next week |
| next weekend | el próximo fin de semana | next weekend |
| tomorrow | mañana | tomorrow |

---

## 4. Preguntas y respuestas

> **What are you doing** next weekend?  
> **I'm going hiking.**

> **Are you going camping** next week?

| Pregunta | Respuesta corta |
| :--- | :--- |
| Are you going camping? | Yes, I am. / No, I'm not. |

## 5. Reading modelo: planes en familia

![Familia outdoor A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/a1-unit39-family-outdoors.png)

> **I'm going camping** next week with my family. We love outdoor activities. My brother **is going hiking** on Saturday and my sister **is going cycling** on Sunday. My dad **is going fishing** tomorrow. We have a tent and backpacks. Next weekend we are all **going to the mountains**.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/im-going-camping-family.mp3" title="🔊 I'm going camping next week with my family"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/love-outdoor.mp3" title="🔊 We love outdoor activities"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/brother-hiking.mp3" title="🔊 My brother is going hiking on Saturday"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/sister-cycling.mp3" title="🔊 My sister is going cycling on Sunday"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/dad-fishing.mp3" title="🔊 My dad is going fishing tomorrow"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/tent-backpacks.mp3" title="🔊 We have a tent and backpacks"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-39/going-mountains.mp3" title="🔊 Next weekend we are all going to the mountains"></audio>

### Comprueba

1. ¿Qué hace el narrador la próxima semana? → **Going camping**.  
2. ¿Con quién? → **Family**.  
3. ¿Hermano el sábado? → **Hiking**.  
4. ¿Hermana el domingo? → **Cycling**.  
5. ¿Padre mañana? → **Fishing**.  
6. ¿Próximo finde? → **To the mountains**.

---

## 6. Diálogo modelo

> **A:** What are you doing next weekend?  
> **B:** I'm going camping with my family. And you?  
> **A:** I'm going hiking on Saturday.  
> **B:** Nice! Is your sister going too?  
> **A:** No — she's going cycling on Sunday.  
> **B:** And your dad?  
> **A:** He's going fishing tomorrow. We love outdoor activities.

---

## 7. Errores típicos de hispanohablantes

| ❌ Incorrecto | ✅ Correcto | Explicación |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *I going camping* | *I**'m** going camping* | Falta *am* |
| *She going hiking* | *She **is** going hiking* | Falta *is* |
| *We go camping next week* (plan fijo A1) | *We **are going** camping next week* | PC para planes |
| *I'm go camping* | *I'm **going** camping* | *-ing* |
| *next week I camping* | *I'm going camping **next week*** | Orden + *going* |

---

## 8. Pronunciación útil

| Forma | Tip A1 |
| :--- | :--- |
| **I'm going** | une: *aimˈgoing*. |
| **hiking** | *HAI-king*. |
| **camping** | *KAM-ping*. |
| **cycling** | *SAI-kling*. |
| **fishing** | *FI-shing*. |
| **outdoor** | *AUT-dor*. |

Practica: *camping → hiking → cycling → fishing*.

---

## 9. Mini-diálogos para memorizar

> **A:** Are you going camping next week?  
> **B:** Yes, we are — with my family.  
> **A:** What are you doing on Saturday?  
> **B:** I'm going hiking.

> **A:** Is she going cycling on Sunday?  
> **B:** Yes, she is.  
> **A:** Is he going fishing tomorrow?  
> **B:** Yes — my dad loves fishing.

> **A:** What are you doing next weekend?  
> **B:** We're going to the mountains. We have a tent and backpacks.

Cambia solo el día o la actividad: fijas ***am/is/are going***.

---

## 9b. Plantillas para copiar

1. I'm going \_\_\_\_ next week.  
2. She / He is going \_\_\_\_ on \_\_\_\_.  
3. We are going \_\_\_\_ tomorrow.  
4. What are you doing next weekend?  
5. Are you going camping? — Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.  
6. Next weekend we are going to the mountains.

### Más frases para memorizar

> I'm going camping next week.  
> She is going hiking on Saturday.  
> We are going cycling tomorrow.  
> He's going fishing next weekend.  
> They are going camping in July.  
> I am going hiking on Saturday.  
> We are going cycling next week.  
> They are going fishing tomorrow.  
> My brother is going hiking on Saturday.  
> My sister is going cycling on Sunday.  
> My dad is going fishing tomorrow.  
> We have a tent and backpacks.  
> Next weekend we are all going to the mountains.  
> We love outdoor activities.  
> I'm going camping next week with my family.  
> What are you doing next weekend?  
> I'm going hiking.  
> Are you going camping next week?  
> Yes, we are.  
> She is going cycling on Sunday.

Lee la lista dos veces. Luego escribe **tus** planes outdoor de la semana.

### Rutina de 2 minutos

1. Di 4 frases *I'm going…* con actividades distintas.  
2. Di 3 con *he/she is going…*.  
3. Pregunta *What are you doing next weekend?* y responde.  
4. Añade *tent / backpack / mountains*.

Si lo unes a U33: *I'm often going hiking at weekends* (más natural: *I often go hiking* para hábitos; *I'm going hiking on Saturday* para un plan concreto).

### Combinar U29 + U32 + U39

| Unidad | Aporta | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| U29 | am/is/are + -ing | form |
| U32 | go + -ing activities | go cycling |
| **U39** | plans | I'm **going** cycling **tomorrow** |

### Mini-historia para reescribir

> I'm going camping next week with my family. My brother is going hiking on Saturday. My sister is going cycling on Sunday. My dad is going fishing tomorrow. Next weekend we are going to the mountains.

Cambia días y actividades; mantén *am/is/are going*.

### Tour guiado (modelo)

> I'm going camping next week with my family. We love outdoor activities. My brother is going hiking on Saturday and my sister is going cycling on Sunday. My dad is going fishing tomorrow. We have a tent and backpacks. Next weekend we are all going to the mountains.

Grábate leyéndolo. Luego improvisa con **tus** planes.

### Frases extra para practicar en voz alta

> What are you doing next weekend?  
> I'm going camping.  
> Are you going hiking on Saturday?  
> Yes, I am.  
> She's going cycling on Sunday.  
> He's going fishing tomorrow.  
> We're going to the mountains.  
> We have a tent and backpacks.

Personaliza lugares y días reales.

### Checklist mental

- *am/is/are + going + activity*  
- Marcador de futuro (*tomorrow / next week…*)  
- Vocab: camping · hiking · cycling · fishing  
- Pregunta: *What are you doing…?*  
- Respuestas cortas: *Yes, I am / No, I'm not*

### Mapa rápido

| Unidad | Enfoque |
| :--- | :--- |
| U29 | Present Continuous (ahora) |
| U32 | go + -ing (hábitos/ocio) |
| **U39** | PC para planes outdoor |
| U40 | Module 4 Review |

---

## 10. Ejercicios prácticos (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — Completa *am / is / are*

1. I \_\_\_\_ going camping next week.  
2. She \_\_\_\_ going hiking on Saturday.  
3. We \_\_\_\_ going cycling tomorrow.  
4. He \_\_\_\_ going fishing next weekend.  
5. They \_\_\_\_ going camping in July.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **am** / **'m**  
2. **is**  
3. **are**  
4. **is** / **'s**  
5. **are**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Elige la actividad

1. sleeping in a tent → \_\_\_\_  
2. walking in the mountains → \_\_\_\_  
3. riding a bicycle → \_\_\_\_  
4. catching fish → \_\_\_\_

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **camping**  
2. **hiking**  
3. **cycling**  
4. **fishing**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Traduce

1. Voy de camping la próxima semana.  
2. Ella va de senderismo el sábado.  
3. Vamos en bici mañana.  
4. Él va a pescar mañana.  
5. ¿Qué haces el próximo fin de semana?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **I'm going camping next week.**  
2. **She is going hiking on Saturday.**  
3. **We are going cycling tomorrow.**  
4. **He is going fishing tomorrow.**  
5. **What are you doing next weekend?**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Ordena

1. camping / I'm / next week / going  
2. hiking / is / she / on Saturday / going  
3. fishing / going / dad / is / tomorrow / my  
4. mountains / going / we / are / to the

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **I'm going camping next week.**  
2. **She is going hiking on Saturday.**  
3. **My dad is going fishing tomorrow.**  
4. **We are going to the mountains.**
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Reading corto

Lee el texto de la sección 5. Contesta:

1. What is the writer doing next week?  
2. What is the brother doing on Saturday?  
3. What is the sister doing on Sunday?  
4. What is dad doing tomorrow?  
5. Where are they going next weekend?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Going camping (with family)**  
2. **Hiking**  
3. **Cycling**  
4. **Fishing**  
5. **To the mountains**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Preguntas sí/no

1. Are you going camping next week? → Yes, \_\_\_\_.  
2. Is she going hiking? → No, \_\_\_\_.  
3. Are they going fishing tomorrow? → Yes, \_\_\_\_.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **I am** / **we are**  
2. **she isn't** / **she's not**  
3. **they are**
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Escribe tus planes

Escribe 8–10 frases. Incluye:

- las 4 actividades (*camping, hiking, cycling, fishing*)  
- *tomorrow / on Saturday / next week / next weekend*  
- 1 pregunta *What are you doing…?*  
- *tent* o *backpack*

**Modelo:** el texto de la sección 5.

### Ejercicio 8 — Elige la opción correcta

1. I \_\_\_\_ going camping next week. ('m / is / are)  
2. She is \_\_\_\_ hiking on Saturday. (go / going / goes)  
3. What \_\_\_\_ you doing next weekend? (are / is / do)  
4. We \_\_\_\_ going to the mountains. (are / is / am)  
5. He \_\_\_\_ going fishing tomorrow. (is / are / am)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **'m**  
2. **going**  
3. **are**  
4. **are**  
5. **is**
</details>

---

## 11. Plan de práctica (15 minutos)

1. **3 min** — Di las 4 actividades con *I'm going…*.  
2. **3 min** — Cambia sujeto (*he/she/we*).  
3. **4 min** — Reescribe el reading.  
4. **5 min** — Mini-entrevista *What are you doing…?*

### Checklist

- [ ] Formo *am/is/are going + activity*  
- [ ] Uso marcadores de futuro  
- [ ] Conozco hiking / camping / cycling / fishing  
- [ ] Pregunto planes con Present Continuous  
- [ ] Distingo hábito (I go…) vs plan (I'm going…)

---

## 12. Consejos para practicar

1. **Agenda de la semana:** un plan outdoor por día en inglés.  
2. **Pareja:** planes del finde + preguntas sí/no.  
3. **Combina** U32: *I go cycling every Sunday* vs *I'm going cycling tomorrow*.  
4. Prepárate para la [Unidad 40](/curso-a1/unit-40): *Module 4 Review*.  
5. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 39](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-39-outdoor-activities-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 39 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-39).

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Lo esencial |
| :--- | :--- |
| Forma | am/is/are + going + activity |
| Uso | planes futuros decididos |
| Vocab | camping · hiking · cycling · fishing |
| Tiempo | tomorrow · next week · on Saturday |
| Pregunta | What are you doing…? |
| Tip | no olvides *am/is/are* |

---

content:
La **Unidad 40 del curso A1** (*Module 4 Review*) cierra el Módulo 4: **habilidades e intereses**. No introduce gramática nueva: **consolida** las unidades 31–39 para que puedas hablar de lo que sabes hacer, de tus hobbies, de la frecuencia, de la cortesía y de tus planes.

Esta guía es un **mapa de repaso** con tablas, checklist, audios y ejercicios. Úsala para detectar huecos y volver a la [unidad concreta](/blog/curso-a1) si algo falla.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 40 — Module 4 Review](/curso-a1/unit-40)  
> **Guías del módulo:** [U31](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-31-can-habilidad) · [U32](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-32-deportes-hobbies-play-go-do) · [U33](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-33-adverbios-frecuencia) · [U38](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-38-pedir-permiso) · [U39](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-39-outdoor-activities)

---

## Qué deberías poder hacer al terminar el Módulo 4

- Hablar de **habilidades** con ***can / can't*** (*I can swim*).
- Elegir bien ***play / go / do*** según el deporte o hobby.
- Usar **adverbios de frecuencia**: *always, usually, often, sometimes, never*.
- Unir ideas con ***and / but / because***.
- Hablar de **tiempo libre** (*go for a walk, go shopping, like + -ing*).
- Decir instrumentos: ***play the*** + guitar / piano / drums…
- Graduar skills: ***very well / quite well / not at all***.
- Pedir permiso: ***Can I…? / May I…?***
- Hablar de **planes outdoor**: ***I'm going camping next week***.

---

## Mapa rápido del Módulo 4 (U31–U39)

| U | Tema | Idea clave |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | Can for Ability | can / can't + verbo base |
| 32 | Sports & Hobbies | **play** / **go** / **do** |
| 33 | Adverbs of Frequency | always → never |
| 34 | And, But, Because | unión, contraste, razón |
| 35 | Free Time | go for a walk, like + -ing |
| 36 | Musical Instruments | play **the** guitar |
| 37 | Talent & Skills | very well / quite well |
| 38 | Asking for Permission | Can I…? / May I…? |
| 39 | Outdoor Activities | I'm **going** camping |

![Mapa Module 4 Review A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-40/a1-unit40-module-map.png)

---

## 1. *Can* para habilidad (U31)

| Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| I / you / we / they **can** | I can swim. |
| He / she **can** | She can dance. |
| Negativa | I **can't** drive. |
| Pregunta | **Can** you swim? |

Recuerda: *can* + **verbo base** (sin *to*). No digas *\*can to swim*.

> I can swim.  
> She can play football.  
> Can you cook?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-40/i-can-swim.mp3" title="🔊 I can swim"></audio>

Guía: [U31 — Can for Ability](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-31-can-habilidad)

---

## 2. *Play / go / do* (U32)

Esta es una de las reglas más útiles del módulo. El verbo cambia según el tipo de actividad:

| Verbo | Tipo de actividad | Ejemplos |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **play** | deportes con pelota / juegos | football, tennis, chess |
| **go** | actividades en *-ing* / movimiento | cycling, swimming, running |
| **do** | actividades sin pelota / “hacer” | yoga, gymnastics, karate |

> She plays football on Saturdays.  
> They go cycling every weekend.  
> He does yoga twice a week.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-40/plays-football.mp3" title="🔊 She plays football on Saturdays"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-40/go-cycling.mp3" title="🔊 They go cycling every weekend"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-40/does-yoga.mp3" title="🔊 He does yoga twice a week"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-40/play-go-do.mp3" title="🔊 Play football, go swimming, do yoga"></audio>

Truco rápido: **pelota → play**; ***-ing* de movimiento → go**; **yoga/artes marciales → do**.

Guía: [U32 — Sports & Hobbies](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-32-deportes-hobbies-play-go-do)

---

## 3. Adverbios de frecuencia (U33)

Orden habitual (del más frecuente al menos):

| Adverbio | Significado aproximado |
| :--- | :--- |
| always | siempre (~100 %) |
| usually | normalmente |
| often | a menudo |
| sometimes | a veces |
| never | nunca (~0 %) |

Posición típica: **antes del verbo principal** (*I always have breakfast*) y **después de *be*** (*She is usually late*).

> I always have breakfast at 8.  
> I never eat late.  
> She usually goes running on Mondays.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-40/always-breakfast.mp3" title="🔊 I always have breakfast at 8"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-40/never-eat-late.mp3" title="🔊 I never eat late"></audio>

Guía: [U33 — Adverbios de frecuencia](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-33-adverbios-frecuencia)

---

## 4. *And / but / because* (U34)

| Conector | Función | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **and** | suma / añade | I can play the guitar **and** I play football. |
| **but** | contraste | I like tea **but** I don't like coffee. |
| **because** | razón | I always do yoga **because** I like it. |

> I like tea but I don't like coffee.  
> I always do yoga in the morning because I like it.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-40/tea-but-coffee.mp3" title="🔊 I like tea but I don't like coffee"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-40/always-yoga-because.mp3" title="🔊 I always do yoga because I like it"></audio>

Consejo: en un mismo párrafo usa los tres. Así demuestras que sabes **unir**, **contrastar** y **explicar**.

Guía: [U34 — And, but, because](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-34-and-but-because)

---

## 5. Free time activities (U35)

En tiempo libre combinas *go + activity*, *like + -ing* y vocabulario de ocio:

| Expresión | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| go for a walk | I go for a walk in the park. |
| go shopping | We go shopping on Saturdays. |
| like + -ing | I like reading. |
| love + -ing | They love dancing. |

Relaciona con U32: *go swimming / go cycling* sigue la misma lógica de *go + -ing*.

Guía: [U35 — Free Time Activities](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-35-free-time-activities)

---

## 6. Instrumentos musicales (U36)

Patrón clave: ***play the*** + instrumento.

| Correcto | Incorrecto típico |
| :--- | :--- |
| play **the** guitar | *play guitar* (en A1 priorizamos *the*) |
| play **the** piano | *play piano* |
| play **the** drums | *do the drums* |

> I can play the guitar quite well.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-40/can-play-guitar.mp3" title="🔊 I can play the guitar quite well"></audio>

Diferencia importante con deportes: *play football* (sin *the*) vs *play **the** guitar* (con *the*).

Guía: [U36 — Instrumentos musicales](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-36-instrumentos-musicales)

---

## 7. Talent & skills (U37)

Gradúa cómo de bien haces algo:

| Nivel | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| **very well** | She sings very well. |
| **quite well** | I play the guitar quite well. |
| **not … well** / **not at all** | He can't dance at all. |

> She sings very well.  
> We all have different skills.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-40/sings-very-well.mp3" title="🔊 She sings very well"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-40/module4-skills.mp3" title="🔊 We all have different skills"></audio>

Combina con *can*: *I can cook very well* / *I can't draw at all*.

Guía: [U37 — Talent & Skills](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-37-talent-skills)

---

## 8. Pedir permiso (U38)

| Pregunta | Respuesta típica |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Can I** use the bathroom? | Yes, of course. / Yes, you can. |
| **May I** ask a question? | Yes, you may. / Of course. |
| Excuse me — can I borrow your pen? | Here you are. |

*May I…?* suena un poco más formal; *Can I…?* es muy frecuente en la vida diaria. Ambos son correctos en A1.

> Can I use the bathroom?  
> May I ask a question?  
> Excuse me — can I borrow your pen?  
> We use polite phrases every day.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-40/can-i-bathroom.mp3" title="🔊 Can I use the bathroom?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-40/may-i-question.mp3" title="🔊 May I ask a question?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-40/excuse-me-borrow.mp3" title="🔊 Excuse me — can I borrow your pen?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-40/we-are-polite.mp3" title="🔊 We use polite phrases every day"></audio>

Guía: [U38 — Pedir permiso](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-38-pedir-permiso)

---

## 9. Outdoor activities y planes (U39)

Misma forma que el Present Continuous de ropa (U29), **otro uso**: planes futuros ya decididos.

| Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| I **'m going** + activity | I'm going camping next week. |
| She **is going** + activity | She is going hiking on Saturday. |
| We **are going** + activity | We are going cycling tomorrow. |

Marcadores útiles: *tomorrow, on Saturday, next week, next weekend*.

> I'm going camping next week.  
> She is going hiking on Saturday.  
> I am going camping next weekend because I love nature.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-40/im-going-camping.mp3" title="🔊 I'm going camping next week"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-40/going-hiking-saturday.mp3" title="🔊 She is going hiking on Saturday"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-40/love-nature-camping.mp3" title="🔊 I'm going camping because I love nature"></audio>

Guía: [U39 — Outdoor Activities](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-39-outdoor-activities)

---

## 10. Reading modelo: Tom

Lee el texto del curso. Une casi todo el módulo en un solo párrafo.

> My name is Tom. I can play the guitar quite well and I play football every Saturday. I always do yoga in the morning because I like it. Next week I'm going camping with my friends. Can I use the bathroom? Yes, of course — we use polite phrases every day.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-40/tom-intro.mp3" title="🔊 Reading: My name is Tom…"></audio>

![Tom hobbies and outdoor plans](/blog/curso-a1/unit-40/a1-unit40-tom-interests.png)

### Qué estructuras ves en el texto

| Fragmento | Tema del módulo |
| :--- | :--- |
| I can play the guitar quite well | U31 + U36 + U37 |
| I play football every Saturday | U32 |
| I always do yoga… because I like it | U33 + U32 + U34 |
| I'm going camping with my friends | U39 |
| Can I use the bathroom? / of course | U38 |

Marca en tu cuaderno cada estructura. Si alguna te cuesta, vuelve a esa unidad del blog antes de seguir al Módulo 5.

---

## 11. Checklist visual del módulo

![Checklist Module 4 Review](/blog/curso-a1/unit-40/a1-unit40-grammar-check.png)

Usa esta lista para autoevaluarte en 5 minutos:

- [ ] *can / can't* + verbo base  
- [ ] *play / go / do* sin mezclar  
- [ ] 5 adverbios de frecuencia en posición correcta  
- [ ] *and / but / because* en el mismo texto  
- [ ] *play the* + instrumento  
- [ ] *very well / quite well / not at all*  
- [ ] *Can I…?* y *May I…?* con respuesta cortés  
- [ ] *I'm going…* + marcador de futuro  

---

## 12. Errores frecuentes del Módulo 4

| Incorrecto | Correcto | Por qué |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *I can to swim* | I can swim | *can* + base |
| *I go football* | I play football | pelota → *play* |
| *I play yoga* | I do yoga | yoga → *do* |
| *I play guitar* (A1) | I play **the** guitar | instrumento + *the* |
| *I going camping* | I **am** going camping | falta *am/is/are* |
| *Always I eat* | I **always** eat | adverbio antes del verbo |
| *I like tea because I don't like coffee* | I like tea **but** I don't like coffee | contraste = *but* |

---

## 13. Mini diálogos de repaso

### Diálogo A — Habilidades

**A:** Can you swim?  
**B:** Yes, I can. And I can play the guitar quite well.  
**A:** Wow! I can't play the guitar at all.

### Diálogo B — Permiso

**A:** Excuse me — can I borrow your pen?  
**B:** Of course. Here you are.  
**A:** Thank you.

### Diálogo C — Planes

**A:** What are you doing next weekend?  
**B:** I'm going camping with my friends because I love nature.  
**A:** Nice! I'm going hiking on Saturday.

Practica en voz alta. Grábate y compara con los audios de esta guía.

---

## 14. Ejercicios de repaso (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — *can* o *can't*

1. I \_\_\_\_ swim. (puedo)  
2. She \_\_\_\_ drive. (no puede)  
3. \_\_\_\_ you cook?  
4. They \_\_\_\_ play tennis.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **can**  
2. **can't** / **cannot**  
3. **Can**  
4. **can**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — *play / go / do*

1. She \_\_\_\_ football on Saturdays.  
2. They \_\_\_\_ cycling every weekend.  
3. He \_\_\_\_ yoga twice a week.  
4. We \_\_\_\_ swimming on Sundays.  
5. I \_\_\_\_ the guitar.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **plays**  
2. **go**  
3. **does**  
4. **go**  
5. **play** (*play the guitar*)
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Frecuencia y conectores

1. I \_\_\_\_ have breakfast at 8. (siempre)  
2. I like tea \_\_\_\_ I don't like coffee.  
3. I do yoga \_\_\_\_ I like it.  
4. I can sing \_\_\_\_ I can dance.  
5. I \_\_\_\_ eat late. (nunca)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **always**  
2. **but**  
3. **because**  
4. **and**  
5. **never**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Skills y permiso

1. She sings \_\_\_\_ well. (muy)  
2. I play the guitar \_\_\_\_ well. (bastante)  
3. \_\_\_\_ I use the bathroom?  
4. \_\_\_\_ I ask a question?  
5. He can't dance \_\_\_\_ all.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **very**  
2. **quite**  
3. **Can**  
4. **May** / **Can**  
5. **at**
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Planes (Present Continuous)

1. I \_\_\_\_ going camping next week.  
2. She \_\_\_\_ going hiking on Saturday.  
3. We \_\_\_\_ going cycling tomorrow.  
4. What \_\_\_\_ you doing next weekend?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **'m** / **am**  
2. **is**  
3. **are**  
4. **are**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Corrige

1. *I can to swim.*  
2. *I go football.*  
3. *I play yoga.*  
4. *I going camping next week.*  
5. *Always I have breakfast.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I can swim.  
2. I **play** football.  
3. I **do** yoga.  
4. I **am** going camping next week.  
5. I **always** have breakfast.
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Empareja unidad y tema

1. U31  
2. U32  
3. U33  
4. U36  
5. U38  
6. U39  

a) play the guitar  
b) Can I…? / May I…?  
c) can / can't  
d) I'm going camping  
e) play / go / do  
f) always / usually / never

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1 → **c** · 2 → **e** · 3 → **f** · 4 → **a** · 5 → **b** · 6 → **d**
</details>

### Ejercicio 8 — Completa el texto de Tom

My name is Tom. I \_\_\_\_ play the guitar quite well \_\_\_\_ I play football every Saturday. I \_\_\_\_ do yoga in the morning \_\_\_\_ I like it. Next week I \_\_\_\_ going camping with my friends. \_\_\_\_ I use the bathroom? Yes, of course.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**can** · **and** · **always** · **because** · **'m / am** · **Can**
</details>

### Ejercicio 9 — Traduce

1. Puedo nadar.  
2. Ella juega al fútbol los sábados.  
3. Hago yoga porque me gusta.  
4. ¿Puedo usar el baño?  
5. La próxima semana voy de camping.  
6. Canta muy bien.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I can swim.  
2. She plays football on Saturdays.  
3. I do yoga because I like it.  
4. Can I use the bathroom?  
5. I'm going camping next week.  
6. She sings very well. / He sings very well.
</details>

### Ejercicio 10 — Escribe tu repaso personal

Escribe 10–12 frases que incluyan:

- 2 × *can / can't*  
- 1 × *play*, 1 × *go*, 1 × *do*  
- 2 adverbios de frecuencia  
- *and*, *but* y *because* (al menos una vez cada uno)  
- 1 × *play the* + instrumento o *very/quite well*  
- 1 × *Can I…?*  
- 2 × *I'm going… / She is going…*

**Modelo:** el texto de Tom (sección 10).

---

## 15. Plan de repaso (30–40 minutos)

1. **8 min** — Relee el mapa U31–U39 y marca 2 unidades débiles.  
2. **10 min** — Haz los ejercicios 1–6 de esta guía.  
3. **8 min** — Escucha y repite 10 audios de esta página (incluye el de Tom).  
4. **8–10 min** — Escribe tu párrafo “Tom” personalizado y grábate.

### Checklist final

- [ ] Hablo de 3 habilidades con *can/can't*  
- [ ] Uso *play/go/do* sin confusión  
- [ ] Coloco bien *always/usually/never*  
- [ ] Uno ideas con *and/but/because*  
- [ ] Pido permiso con *Can I…?* / *May I…?*  
- [ ] Describo 2 planes con *I'm going…*

---

## 16. Consejos antes del Módulo 5

1. No memorices listas sueltas: **une** skills + hobbies + planes en un solo texto (como Tom).  
2. Si fallas solo en *play/go/do*, vuelve a [U32](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-32-deportes-hobbies-play-go-do).  
3. Si fallas en permiso o cortesía, vuelve a [U38](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-38-pedir-permiso).  
4. Si fallas en planes futuros, vuelve a [U39](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-39-outdoor-activities).  
5. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 40](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-40-repaso-modulo-4-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 40 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-40).

El Módulo 5 empieza en el aeropuerto (*At the Airport*): *must/should*, *passport*, *check-in*, *gate*. Llevarás contigo *can*, la cortesía y la capacidad de explicar planes.

---

## Resumen rápido

| Bloque | Lo esencial |
| :--- | :--- |
| Habilidad | can / can't + base |
| Deportes | play / go / do |
| Frecuencia | always → never |
| Conectores | and · but · because |
| Free time | go for a walk · like + -ing |
| Música | play **the** + instrumento |
| Skills | very well · quite well · not at all |
| Permiso | Can I…? · May I…? |
| Planes | am/is/are going + activity |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 40 A1 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-40-repaso-modulo-4-ejercicios-soluciones)
- [Unidad 40 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-40)

Tras el Módulo 4, el curso continúa con el **Módulo 5** (*Places & Travel*). La siguiente unidad es **At the Airport** (*must/should*, *passport*, *ticket*, *check-in*).

Guía dedicada y curso:

title: At the Airport A1: must/should, passport, check-in y boarding
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 41 del curso A1: en el aeropuerto con must/should, passport, check-in, gate y boarding, con audios y ejercicios.
description: Aprende inglés de aeropuerto nivel A1: must (obligación) y should (consejo), passport, ticket, check-in, gate y boarding. Guía Unidad 41 con audios y ejercicios.
alt: Esquema must vs should en el aeropuerto para inglés A1

faqs.question: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre must y should en A1?
faqs.answer: Must expresa obligación (debes): You must show your passport. Should expresa consejo o recomendación (deberías): You should arrive early.

faqs.question: ¿Qué va después de must y should?
faqs.answer: El verbo en forma base, sin to y sin -ing: must show, should go. No digas must to show ni should going.

faqs.question: ¿Qué vocabulario de aeropuerto practico en la Unidad 41?
faqs.answer: Passport, ticket, check-in, boarding pass, gate, boarding, flight, luggage, suitcase y frases como Go to gate number ten.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde muestro el pasaporte y dónde embarco?
faqs.answer: En check-in muestras passport y ticket y obtienes la boarding pass. En la gate embarcas (boarding) al avión.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 41 del curso A1?
faqs.answer: En la Unidad 41 del curso A1 de Linguafly y en el cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones del blog: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y speaking.

content:
Tras el [repaso del Módulo 4](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-40-repaso-modulo-4), empieza el **Módulo 5** (*Places & Travel*). En la **Unidad 41 del curso A1** (*At the Airport*) usas ***must*** (obligación) y ***should*** (consejo) con vocabulario de aeropuerto: *passport*, *ticket*, *check-in*, *gate*, *boarding*.

Conecta con *can* de la [Unidad 31](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-31-can-habilidad) y la cortesía de la [Unidad 38](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-38-pedir-permiso). Incluye **audios**, **esquemas** y **ejercicios**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 41 — At the Airport](/curso-a1/unit-41)  
> **Repaso útil:** [Unidad 40 — Repaso Módulo 4](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-40-repaso-modulo-4) · [Unidad 38 — Pedir permiso](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-38-pedir-permiso)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 41 (A1)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Usar ***must + verbo base*** para obligaciones en el aeropuerto.
- Usar ***should + verbo base*** para consejos y recomendaciones.
- Nombrar ***passport, ticket, check-in, boarding pass, gate, boarding***.
- Seguir el flujo: facturación → tarjeta de embarque → puerta → embarque.
- Entender y producir instrucciones simples de aeropuerto.

---

## 1. Must vs should

| Modal | Significado | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **must** | obligación (debes) | You **must** show your passport. |
| **should** | consejo (deberías) | You **should** arrive early. |

![Must vs should A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-41/a1-unit41-must-should.png)

```
must / should + base verb
→ must show · should go · must have · should arrive
(NO: must to show / should going)
```

### Tip

**Must** = regla o necesidad fuerte (*tienes que*).  
**Should** = buena idea (*conviene*). En el aeropuerto: *must show passport*; *should go to the gate early*.

### Contraste con can (U31) y Can I…? (U38)

| Forma | Uso | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **can** | habilidad | I **can** swim. |
| **Can I…?** | permiso | **Can I** use the bathroom? |
| **must** | obligación | You **must** show your passport. |
| **should** | consejo | You **should** arrive early. |

---

## 2. Ejemplos con audio

> You **must show** your passport at check-in.  
> Passengers **should go** to the gate before boarding.  
> I **must have** my ticket ready.  
> You **should arrive** early for your flight.  
> We **must show** our boarding pass at the gate.  
> You **should go** to the gate now.  
> Go to **gate number ten**.  
> I **must show** my passport and ticket.  
> You **should go** early; boarding starts soon.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-41/must-show-passport.mp3" title="🔊 You must show your passport at check-in"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-41/should-go-gate.mp3" title="🔊 Passengers should go to the gate before boarding"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-41/must-have-ticket.mp3" title="🔊 I must have my ticket ready"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-41/should-arrive-early.mp3" title="🔊 You should arrive early for your flight"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-41/must-show-boarding-pass.mp3" title="🔊 We must show our boarding pass at the gate"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-41/should-go-now.mp3" title="🔊 You should go to the gate now"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-41/gate-number-ten.mp3" title="🔊 Go to gate number ten"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-41/must-passport-ticket.mp3" title="🔊 I must show my passport and ticket"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-41/should-go-early-boarding.mp3" title="🔊 You should go early; boarding starts soon"></audio>

### Regla rápida

| Correcto | Incorrecto |
| :--- | :--- |
| must **show** | must **to** show |
| should **go** | should **going** |
| must **have** | must **having** |

---

## 3. Vocabulario de aeropuerto

![Vocabulario aeropuerto A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-41/a1-unit41-airport-vocab.png)

| Inglés | Español | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| airport | aeropuerto | at the airport |
| passport | pasaporte | show your passport |
| ticket | billete | passport and ticket |
| check-in | facturación | at check-in |
| boarding pass | tarjeta de embarque | get your boarding pass |
| gate | puerta de embarque | gate number twenty-two |
| boarding | embarque | boarding starts at… |
| flight | vuelo | my flight is at ten |
| luggage | equipaje | my luggage is not heavy |
| suitcase | maleta | one suitcase |
| arrive early | llegar temprano | You should arrive early. |
| have a good flight | buen vuelo | Have a good flight! |

---

## 4. Flujo en el aeropuerto

![Flujo aeropuerto A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-41/a1-unit41-airport-flow.png)

| Paso | Inglés | Qué haces |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | **Check-in** | You **must** show your passport and ticket. |
| 2 | **Boarding pass** | You get your boarding pass. |
| 3 | **Gate** | You **should** go to the gate early. |
| 4 | **Boarding** | You show your boarding pass and board the plane. |

### Frases del flujo

> Where is the check-in?  
> You must show your passport and ticket.  
> What gate for the flight to London?  
> Gate twenty-two.  
> You should go now; boarding starts in ten minutes.  
> I have my boarding pass.  
> Have a good flight!

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-41/where-is-check-in.mp3" title="🔊 Where is the check-in?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-41/gate-twenty-two.mp3" title="🔊 Gate twenty-two"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-41/boarding-ten-minutes.mp3" title="🔊 Boarding starts in ten minutes"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-41/have-good-flight.mp3" title="🔊 Have a good flight"></audio>

---

## 5. Reading modelo: en el aeropuerto

> **I am at the airport today.** My flight is at ten o'clock. I **must show** my passport and my ticket at check-in. After that I get my boarding pass. I **should go** to the gate early. Boarding starts at half past nine. I have one suitcase. My luggage is not heavy.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-41/reading-at-airport.mp3" title="🔊 I am at the airport today"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-41/reading-must-show.mp3" title="🔊 I must show my passport and my ticket at check-in"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-41/reading-should-gate.mp3" title="🔊 I should go to the gate early"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-41/reading-boarding-half-past.mp3" title="🔊 Boarding starts at half past nine"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-41/reading-one-suitcase.mp3" title="🔊 I have one suitcase"></audio>

### Comprueba

1. ¿Dónde está el narrador? → **At the airport**.  
2. ¿A qué hora es el vuelo? → **At ten o'clock**.  
3. ¿Qué debe mostrar en check-in? → **Passport and ticket**.  
4. ¿Qué obtiene después? → **Boarding pass**.  
5. ¿Cuándo empieza el embarque? → **At half past nine**.  
6. ¿Cuántas maletas? → **One**.  
7. ¿El equipaje es pesado? → **No**.

---

## 6. Diálogo modelo

> **A:** Where is the check-in?  
> **B:** Over there. You **must** show your passport and ticket.  
> **A:** Thank you. What gate for the flight to London?  
> **B:** Gate twenty-two. You **should** go now; boarding starts in ten minutes.  
> **A:** I have my boarding pass.  
> **B:** Perfect. Have a good flight!

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-41/dialogue-where-check-in.mp3" title="🔊 Where is the check-in?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-41/dialogue-must-show.mp3" title="🔊 You must show your passport and ticket"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-41/dialogue-gate-london.mp3" title="🔊 What gate for the flight to London?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-41/dialogue-should-go-now.mp3" title="🔊 You should go now; boarding starts in ten minutes"></audio>

---

## 7. Errores típicos de hispanohablantes

| ❌ Incorrecto | ✅ Correcto | Explicación |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *You must **to** show* | *You must **show*** | sin *to* |
| *You should **going*** | *You should **go*** | verbo base |
| *You must show **the** passport* (siempre) | *You must show **your** passport* | posesivo habitual |
| *Go to the gate **number the** ten* | *Go to gate **number ten*** | *gate number + número* |
| *I must **can** show* | *I must show* | un modal por frase en A1 |
| Confundir *must* y *should* | *must* = obligación; *should* = consejo | significado distinto |

---

## 8. Pronunciación útil

| Palabra / frase | Tip A1 |
| :--- | :--- |
| **must** | corta y firme: *mast*. |
| **should** | *shud* (la *l* casi no suena). |
| **passport** | *PAS-port*. |
| **check-in** | *CHEK-in* (dos partes). |
| **boarding** | *BOR-ding*. |
| **gate** | *gueit*. |
| **luggage** | *LA-guich*. |
| **suitcase** | *SUT-keis*. |

Practica: *must show → should go → check-in → boarding pass → gate*.

---

## 9. Mini-diálogos para memorizar

> **A:** Where is check-in?  
> **B:** Over there. You must show your passport.  
> **A:** What gate?  
> **B:** Gate ten. You should go early.

> **A:** Do I need my ticket?  
> **B:** Yes — you must have your ticket ready.  
> **A:** And then?  
> **B:** You get your boarding pass and go to the gate.

> **A:** Should I go to the gate now?  
> **B:** Yes. Boarding starts in ten minutes.  
> **A:** I have my boarding pass.  
> **B:** Perfect. Have a good flight!

Cambia solo el número de puerta o la ciudad: fijas ***must / should + base verb***.

---

## 9b. Plantillas para copiar

1. You must \_\_\_\_ your passport at check-in.  
2. You should \_\_\_\_ to the gate early.  
3. I must have my \_\_\_\_ ready.  
4. Go to gate number \_\_\_\_.  
5. Where is the check-in?  
6. Have a good flight!

### Más frases para memorizar

> You must show your passport at check-in.  
> Passengers should go to the gate before boarding.  
> I must have my ticket ready.  
> You should arrive early for your flight.  
> We must show our boarding pass at the gate.  
> You should go to the gate now.  
> Go to gate number ten.  
> I must show my passport and ticket.  
> Where is the check-in?  
> Over there.  
> What gate for the flight to London?  
> Gate twenty-two.  
> Boarding starts in ten minutes.  
> I have my boarding pass.  
> Have a good flight!  
> I am at the airport today.  
> My flight is at ten o'clock.  
> After check-in I get my boarding pass.  
> Boarding starts at half past nine.  
> I have one suitcase.  
> My luggage is not heavy.

Lee la lista dos veces. Luego describe **tu** viaje al aeropuerto en 6–8 frases.

### Rutina de 2 minutos

1. Di 3 frases con *must* (passport / ticket / boarding pass).  
2. Di 3 con *should* (arrive early / go to the gate / go now).  
3. Pregunta *Where is the check-in?* y *What gate?*  
4. Cierra con *Have a good flight!*

### Combinar U31 + U38 + U41

| Unidad | Aporta | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| U31 | can (habilidad) | I **can** speak English. |
| U38 | Can I…? (permiso) | **Can I** ask a question? |
| **U41** | must / should | You **must** show… / You **should** go… |

### Mini-historia para reescribir

> I am at the airport today. My flight is at ten o'clock. I must show my passport and my ticket at check-in. After that I get my boarding pass. I should go to the gate early. Boarding starts at half past nine. I have one suitcase.

Cambia horas y número de puerta; mantén *must* y *should*.

### Tour guiado (modelo)

> I am at the airport today. My flight is at ten o'clock. I must show my passport and my ticket at check-in. After that I get my boarding pass. I should go to the gate early. Boarding starts at half past nine. I have one suitcase. My luggage is not heavy.

Grábate leyéndolo. Luego improvisa con **tu** vuelo.

### Frases extra para practicar en voz alta

> Where is the check-in?  
> You must show your passport.  
> What gate for London?  
> Gate twenty-two.  
> You should go now.  
> I have my boarding pass.  
> Have a good flight!

Personaliza ciudad y número de puerta.

### Checklist mental

- *must* = obligación · *should* = consejo  
- *must/should + verbo base*  
- Vocab: passport · ticket · check-in · boarding pass · gate  
- Flujo: check-in → boarding pass → gate → boarding  
- Cierre: *Have a good flight!*

### Mapa rápido

| Unidad | Enfoque |
| :--- | :--- |
| U40 | Module 4 Review |
| **U41** | At the Airport — must/should |
| U42 | Transport — *by* + transporte |

---

## 10. Ejercicios prácticos (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — Elige *must* o *should*

1. You \_\_\_\_ show your passport at check-in. (obligación)  
2. You \_\_\_\_ arrive early for your flight. (consejo)  
3. Passengers \_\_\_\_ go to the gate before boarding. (consejo)  
4. We \_\_\_\_ show our boarding pass at the gate. (obligación)  
5. You \_\_\_\_ go now; boarding starts in ten minutes. (consejo)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **must**  
2. **should**  
3. **should**  
4. **must**  
5. **should**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Completa el vocabulario

1. Document for travel → \_\_\_\_  
2. Where you get your boarding pass → \_\_\_\_  
3. Where you board the plane → \_\_\_\_  
4. Getting on the plane → \_\_\_\_  
5. Bags / suitcases → \_\_\_\_

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **passport**  
2. **check-in**  
3. **gate**  
4. **boarding**  
5. **luggage**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Traduce

1. Debes mostrar tu pasaporte en facturación.  
2. Deberías llegar temprano a tu vuelo.  
3. Ve a la puerta número diez.  
4. Tengo mi tarjeta de embarque.  
5. ¿Dónde está la facturación?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **You must show your passport at check-in.**  
2. **You should arrive early for your flight.**  
3. **Go to gate number ten.**  
4. **I have my boarding pass.**  
5. **Where is the check-in?**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Ordena

1. passport / must / You / show / your  
2. early / should / You / arrive  
3. gate / to / Go / number / ten  
4. boarding pass / have / I / my

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **You must show your passport.**  
2. **You should arrive early.**  
3. **Go to gate number ten.**  
4. **I have my boarding pass.**
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Reading corto

Lee el texto de la sección 5. Contesta:

1. Where is the writer today?  
2. What time is the flight?  
3. What must the writer show at check-in?  
4. When does boarding start?  
5. How many suitcases does the writer have?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **At the airport**  
2. **At ten o'clock**  
3. **Passport and ticket**  
4. **At half past nine**  
5. **One**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Forma correcta del verbo

1. You must \_\_\_\_ your passport. (show / to show / showing)  
2. You should \_\_\_\_ to the gate early. (go / to go / going)  
3. I must \_\_\_\_ my ticket ready. (have / to have / having)  
4. Passengers should \_\_\_\_ early. (arrive / arriving / to arrive)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **show**  
2. **go**  
3. **have**  
4. **arrive**
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Escribe tu viaje

Escribe 8–10 frases. Incluye:

- *must* (2 veces) y *should* (2 veces)  
- *passport, ticket, check-in, boarding pass, gate*  
- hora del vuelo  
- *Have a good flight!*

**Modelo:** el texto de la sección 5.

### Ejercicio 8 — Elige la opción correcta

1. You \_\_\_\_ show your passport. (must / must to / musts)  
2. You should \_\_\_\_ early. (arrive / arriving / to arrive)  
3. Go to \_\_\_\_ twenty-two. (gate / the gates / gating)  
4. I have my \_\_\_\_ pass. (boarding / board / boarded)  
5. Where is the \_\_\_\_? (check-in / checking / checked)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **must**  
2. **arrive**  
3. **gate**  
4. **boarding**  
5. **check-in**
</details>

---

## 11. Plan de práctica (15 minutos)

1. **3 min** — Di 5 frases *must* + aeropuerto.  
2. **3 min** — Di 5 frases *should* + consejos.  
3. **4 min** — Reescribe el reading con tu vuelo.  
4. **5 min** — Practica el diálogo (check-in / gate / boarding).

### Checklist

- [ ] Distingo *must* (obligación) y *should* (consejo)  
- [ ] Uso verbo base después del modal  
- [ ] Conozco passport / ticket / check-in / gate / boarding  
- [ ] Explico el flujo del aeropuerto  
- [ ] Digo *Have a good flight!*

---

## 12. Consejos para practicar

1. **Checklist mental en el aeropuerto:** *passport → ticket → check-in → boarding pass → gate*.  
2. **Pareja:** uno pregunta *Where is check-in?* / *What gate?*; el otro responde con *must/should*.  
3. **Combina** U38: *Excuse me — where is the check-in?* (cortesía + aeropuerto).  
4. Prepárate para la [Unidad 42](/curso-a1/unit-42): *Transport* (*by bus*, *take the train*).  
5. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 41](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-41-aeropuerto-must-should-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 41 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-41).

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Lo esencial |
| :--- | :--- |
| must | obligación + verbo base |
| should | consejo + verbo base |
| Vocab | passport · ticket · check-in · gate · boarding |
| Flujo | check-in → boarding pass → gate → boarding |
| Tip | no uses *to* ni *-ing* después de must/should |
| Cierre | Have a good flight! |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 41 A1 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-41-aeropuerto-must-should-ejercicios-soluciones)
- [Unidad 41 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-41)

En la **Unidad 42** hablas de **transporte**: *by bus / by train / by plane* y *take the bus / take the train*.

Guía dedicada y curso:

- [Unidad 42 — Transport (by / take the)](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-42-transporte-by-take-the)
- [Unidad 42 — Transport](/curso-a1/unit-42)

Antes de pasar de unidad, escribe un párrafo de 6–8 frases con tu llegada al aeropuerto (*must* + *should* + vocabulario).

faqs.question: ¿Cómo se dice «en autobús» en inglés A1?
faqs.answer: Se dice by bus (sin artículo). También puedes decir take the bus (con the). Las dos formas son correctas y muy frecuentes.

faqs.question: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre by bus y take the bus?
faqs.answer: Significan casi lo mismo. By + transporte va sin artículo (by bus). Take the + transporte usa the (take the bus). Ejemplo: I go by bus. / I take the bus.

faqs.question: ¿Se dice by the train o by train?
faqs.answer: By train, sin the. Con take sí usas the: take the train. Incorrecto: by the train / take bus.

faqs.question: ¿Qué medios de transporte practico en la Unidad 42?
faqs.answer: Bus, train, plane, taxi, bicycle y también car. Frases: by bus, by train, by plane, by taxi, by bicycle, by car; take the bus, take the train.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 42 del curso A1?
faqs.answer: En la Unidad 42 del curso A1 de Linguafly y en el cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones del blog: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y speaking.

content:
En la [Unidad 41](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-41-aeropuerto-must-should) estuviste en el aeropuerto (*must/should*). En la **Unidad 42 del curso A1** (*Transport*) explicas **cómo te mueves**: ***by bus***, ***by train***, ***take the bus***.

Repasas *go* y hábitos del Present Simple y conectas con viajes del Módulo 5. Incluye **audios**, **esquemas** y **ejercicios**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 42 — Transport](/curso-a1/unit-42)  
> **Repaso útil:** [Unidad 41 — At the Airport](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-41-aeropuerto-must-should) · [Unidad 32 — Sports & Hobbies](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-32-deportes-hobbies-play-go-do)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 42 (A1)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Usar ***by + transporte*** sin artículo (*by bus*, *by train*).
- Usar ***take the + transporte*** (*take the bus*, *take the train*).
- Nombrar ***bus, train, plane, taxi, bicycle, car***.
- Preguntar: ***How do you go to work?***
- Hablar de viajes diarios y de vacaciones.

---

## 1. By + transporte (sin artículo)

| Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| by **bus** | I go to work **by bus**. |
| by **train** | She travels **by train** to London. |
| by **plane** | We travel **by plane** for holidays. |
| by **car** | He goes **by car** to the office. |
| by **taxi** | I went to the airport **by taxi**. |
| by **bicycle** | He goes to school **by bicycle**. |

![By + transporte A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-42/a1-unit42-by-transport.png)

```
by + transport (NO article)
→ by bus · by train · by plane · by car · by taxi · by bicycle
(NO: by the bus / by a train)
```

### Tip

Después de ***by*** no pongas *the* ni *a*. Piensa: *by + medio* = «en + medio».

---

## 2. Take the + transporte

| Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| take **the bus** | I **take the bus** every day. |
| take **the train** | She **takes the train** every Monday. |
| take **the plane** | They **take the plane** to Spain. |

![by vs take the A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-42/a1-unit42-by-vs-take.png)

```
take the + transport
→ take the bus · take the train · take the plane
(con "the")
```

### Misma idea, dos estructuras

| by… | take the… |
| :--- | :--- |
| I go **by bus**. | I **take the bus**. |
| She travels **by train**. | She **takes the train**. |
| We travel **by plane**. | We **take the plane**. |

En A1 las dos valen. Elige una y practícala hasta que salga automática; luego añade la otra.

---

## 3. Ejemplos con audio

> I go to work **by bus** every day.  
> She travels **by train** to London.  
> We **take the bus** every day.  
> She **takes the train** every Monday.  
> We travel **by plane** to Spain.  
> He goes **by car** to the office.  
> I went to the airport **by taxi**.  
> My brother goes to school **by bicycle**.  
> How do you go to work?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-42/go-by-bus.mp3" title="🔊 I go to work by bus every day"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-42/travel-by-train.mp3" title="🔊 She travels by train to London"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-42/take-the-bus.mp3" title="🔊 We take the bus every day"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-42/takes-the-train.mp3" title="🔊 She takes the train every Monday"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-42/travel-by-plane.mp3" title="🔊 We travel by plane to Spain"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-42/go-by-car.mp3" title="🔊 He goes by car to the office"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-42/by-taxi-airport.mp3" title="🔊 I went to the airport by taxi"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-42/by-bicycle-school.mp3" title="🔊 My brother goes to school by bicycle"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-42/how-do-you-go.mp3" title="🔊 How do you go to work?"></audio>

### Regla rápida

| Correcto | Incorrecto |
| :--- | :--- |
| by **bus** | by **the** bus |
| by **train** | by **a** train |
| take **the** bus | take bus |
| take **the** train | take **a** train (menos natural en A1 aquí) |

---

## 4. Vocabulario de transporte

![Vocabulario transporte A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-42/a1-unit42-transport-vocab.png)

| Inglés | Español | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| bus | autobús | by bus / take the bus |
| train | tren | by train / take the train |
| plane | avión | by plane |
| taxi | taxi | by taxi |
| bicycle | bicicleta | by bicycle |
| car | coche | by car |
| travel | viajar | We travel by plane. |
| go to work | ir al trabajo | I go to work by bus. |
| every day | cada día | every day |
| holidays | vacaciones | for holidays |
| fast | rápido | It is fast. |
| cheap | barato | It is cheap. |

---

## 5. Preguntas y respuestas

> **How do you go** to work?  
> **I take the bus.** / **I go by bus.**

> **How does she travel** to London?  
> **She travels by train.**

> **Do you ever go by plane?**  
> **Yes, for holidays.**

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-42/i-take-the-bus.mp3" title="🔊 I take the bus"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-42/she-travels-by-train.mp3" title="🔊 She travels by train"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-42/yes-for-holidays.mp3" title="🔊 Yes, for holidays"></audio>

### Tabla de preguntas

| Pregunta | Respuesta |
| :--- | :--- |
| How do you go to work? | I go by bus. / I take the bus. |
| How does he go to school? | He goes by bicycle. |
| Do you travel by plane? | Yes, for holidays. |
| How did you go to the airport? | By taxi. |

---

## 6. Reading modelo: cómo viajamos

> **I go to work by bus every day.** My sister **takes the train** to London. We sometimes travel **by plane** for holidays. Last week I went to the airport **by taxi**. My brother goes to school **by bicycle**. He likes it because it is fast and cheap.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-42/reading-go-by-bus.mp3" title="🔊 I go to work by bus every day"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-42/reading-sister-train.mp3" title="🔊 My sister takes the train to London"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-42/reading-by-plane-holidays.mp3" title="🔊 We sometimes travel by plane for holidays"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-42/reading-by-taxi.mp3" title="🔊 Last week I went to the airport by taxi"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-42/reading-by-bicycle.mp3" title="🔊 My brother goes to school by bicycle"></audio>

### Comprueba

1. ¿Cómo va el narrador al trabajo? → **By bus**.  
2. ¿Qué toma la hermana a Londres? → **The train**.  
3. ¿Cuándo viajan en avión? → **For holidays**.  
4. ¿Cómo fue al aeropuerto? → **By taxi**.  
5. ¿Cómo va el hermano al colegio? → **By bicycle**.  
6. ¿Por qué le gusta la bici? → **Fast and cheap**.

---

## 7. Diálogo modelo

> **A:** How do you go to work?  
> **B:** I take the bus.  
> **A:** I go by car. What about your sister?  
> **B:** She travels by train to London.  
> **A:** Do you ever go by plane?  
> **B:** Yes, for holidays. Last time I went to the airport by taxi.  
> **A:** My son goes to school by bicycle.
