title: At the Supermarket A1: plurales, fruta, verdura y pasillos
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 51 del curso A1: supermercado con plurales, fruta, verdura, carne, pescado y pasillos, con audios y ejercicios.
description: Aprende inglés A1 en el supermercado: plurales regulares e irregulares, fruit, vegetables, meat, fish, aisle y checkout. Guía Unidad 51 con audios y ejercicios.
alt: Esquema de plurales regulares e irregulares en el supermercado A1

faqs.question: ¿Qué se aprende en la Unidad 51 del curso A1?
faqs.answer: At the Supermarket: plurales regulares (apples, tomatoes, potatoes) e irregulares básicos (children, people), vocabulario de fruit, vegetables, meat, fish, aisle, trolley y checkout.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo se forma el plural de tomato y potato?
faqs.answer: Añaden -es: tomato → tomatoes, potato → potatoes. No digas *tomatos* ni *potatos*.

faqs.question: ¿Cuál es el plural de fish como comida?
faqs.answer: En A1, fish suele quedar igual: two fish / two pieces of fish. Fishes se usa más para tipos de animales.

faqs.question: ¿Qué significa aisle en el supermercado?
faqs.answer: Aisle = pasillo entre estantes. Ejemplo: The apples are in aisle five. / Where are the vegetables? — In aisle two.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 51 del curso A1?
faqs.answer: En el cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones y en la Unidad 51 del curso A1 de Linguafly: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening, speaking y writing.

content:
Tras el [repaso del Módulo 5](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-50-repaso-modulo-5), el **Módulo 6** (*Shopping & Food*) empieza en la tienda. En la **Unidad 51 del curso A1** (*At the Supermarket*) practicas **plurales** y vocabulario de **fruit, vegetables, meat, fish** y **aisles**.

Conecta con plurales de la [Unidad 4](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-4-articulos-plurales-demostrativos) y comidas de la [Unidad 17](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-17-comidas-breakfast-lunch-dinner). Incluye **audios**, **esquemas** y **ejercicios**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 51 — At the Supermarket](/curso-a1/unit-51)  
> **Repaso útil:** [Unidad 50 — Repaso Módulo 5](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-50-repaso-modulo-5) · [Unidad 4 — Plurales](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-4-articulos-plurales-demostrativos)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 51 (A1)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Formar **plurales regulares**: *apple → apples*, *egg → eggs*.
- Usar **-es** cuando la palabra termina en *-o* frecuente del supermercado: *tomatoes, potatoes*.
- Recordar irregulares básicos: *child → children*, *person → people*.
- Usar *fish* (igual en plural como comida) y *pieces of fish*.
- Nombrar **fruit, vegetables, meat, fish**.
- Orientarte en la tienda: ***aisle, shelf, basket, trolley, checkout***.
- Preguntar: ***Where are the vegetables?*** / ***Where is the fruit section?***

---

## 1. Plurales regulares en el supermercado

| Singular | Plural | Regla |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| apple | **apples** | + **-s** |
| banana | **bananas** | + **-s** |
| egg | **eggs** | + **-s** |
| carrot | **carrots** | + **-s** |
| vegetable | **vegetables** | + **-s** |
| tomato | **tomatoes** | + **-es** |
| potato | **potatoes** | + **-es** |

> I need two **tomatoes** for the salad.  
> We have three **potatoes** in the fridge.  
> There are many **apples** in the fruit section.  
> How many **eggs** do you need?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-51/two-tomatoes.mp3" title="🔊 I need two tomatoes for the salad"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-51/three-potatoes.mp3" title="🔊 We have three potatoes in the fridge"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-51/many-apples.mp3" title="🔊 There are many apples in the fruit section"></audio>

También añadimos **-es** tras *-s, -ch, -sh, -x* (*boxes, dishes*). En esta unidad el foco práctico es *tomatoes / potatoes / apples / eggs*.

![Plurales en el supermercado A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-51/a1-unit51-plurals.png)

---

## 2. Plurales irregulares y casos especiales

| Singular | Plural | Nota |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| child | **children** | irregular |
| person | **people** | irregular (prioridad A1) |
| fish | **fish** | igual como comida |
| piece | **pieces** | *two pieces of fish* |

> There are many **children** in the supermarket today.  
> How many **people** are in the queue?  
> I want two **pieces** of fish.  
> We say **two fish** for two pieces of fish.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-51/two-pieces-fish.mp3" title="🔊 I want two pieces of fish"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-51/two-fish.mp3" title="🔊 We say two fish for two pieces of fish"></audio>

*Meat* y *fish* (como comida) a menudo van con *some*: *I need **some** meat and fish* (verás *some/any* más a fondo en U52–53).

---

## 3. Vocabulario: fruit, vegetables, meat, fish

| Categoría | Palabras A1 |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Fruit** | apple, banana, orange |
| **Vegetables** | carrot, tomato, potato |
| **Meat** | chicken, beef, pork |
| **Fish** | salmon, tuna, cod |

> Fruit = apples, bananas, oranges.  
> Vegetables = carrots, tomatoes, potatoes.  
> Meat = chicken, beef, pork.  
> Fish = salmon, tuna, cod.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-51/fruit-list.mp3" title="🔊 Fruit = apples, bananas, oranges"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-51/vegetables-list.mp3" title="🔊 Vegetables = carrots, tomatoes, potatoes"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-51/meat-list.mp3" title="🔊 Meat = chicken, beef, pork"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-51/fish-list.mp3" title="🔊 Fish = salmon, tuna, cod"></audio>

![Vocabulario supermercado A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-51/a1-unit51-supermarket-vocab.png)

---

## 4. La tienda: aisle, trolley, checkout

| Palabra | Significado | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **aisle** | pasillo | The apples are in aisle five. |
| **shelf** | estante | The eggs are on the shelf. |
| **basket** | cesta | I get a basket for a few things. |
| **trolley** | carrito | Get a trolley if you have many things. |
| **checkout** | caja | Then I pay at the checkout. |
| **section** | sección | Where is the fruit section? |
| **at the back** | al fondo | Meat and fish are at the back. |
| **entrance** | entrada | Aisle one, next to the entrance. |

> The apples are in aisle five.  
> Where are the vegetables?  
> Where is the fruit section?  
> Get a trolley if you have many things.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-51/apples-aisle-five.mp3" title="🔊 The apples are in aisle five"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-51/where-vegetables.mp3" title="🔊 Where are the vegetables?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-51/get-trolley.mp3" title="🔊 Get a trolley if you have many things"></audio>

![Mapa de pasillos A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-51/a1-unit51-aisles.png)

---

## 5. Preguntas útiles en el supermercado

| Pregunta | Respuesta típica |
| :--- | :--- |
| Where **are** the vegetables? | In aisle two. |
| Where **is** the fruit section? | Aisle one, next to the entrance. |
| Where **are** the apples? | On the shelf / In aisle five. |
| Where **is** the checkout? | Over there. |
| How many eggs do you need? | Six, please. |

Recuerda: *vegetables / apples* → **Where are…?**; *fruit section / checkout* → **Where is…?**

> Where are the vegetables? — In aisle two.  
> And the fruit? — Aisle one, next to the entrance.  
> I need some chicken and fish. — Meat and fish are at the back.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-51/dialogue-where-veg.mp3" title="🔊 Where are the vegetables? In aisle two"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-51/meat-at-back.mp3" title="🔊 Meat and fish are at the back"></audio>

---

## 6. Texto modelo: una compra del sábado

> I go to the supermarket every Saturday. First I get a trolley. The fruit and vegetables are in aisle one. I buy apples, bananas and tomatoes. The meat and fish are at the back. I need some chicken and two pieces of fish. Then I pay at the checkout.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-51/reading-saturday.mp3" title="🔊 I go to the supermarket every Saturday…"></audio>

Marca en el texto:

- plurales: *apples, bananas, tomatoes, pieces*  
- lugares: *aisle one, at the back, checkout*  
- *some chicken* + *two pieces of fish*

---

## 7. Diálogo de listening

> **A:** Where are the vegetables?  
> **B:** In aisle two.  
> **A:** And the fruit?  
> **B:** Aisle one, next to the entrance.  
> **A:** I need some chicken and fish.  
> **B:** Meat and fish are at the back.  
> **A:** Thank you. Where is the checkout?  
> **B:** Over there. Get a trolley if you have many things.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-51/dialogue-full.mp3" title="🔊 Where are the vegetables?…"></audio>

---

## 8. Errores frecuentes

| Incorrecto | Correcto | Por qué |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| two tomatos | two **tomatoes** | *tomato* → *tomatoes* |
| three potatos | three **potatoes** | *potato* → *potatoes* |
| two fishs | two **fish** / two **pieces of fish** | *fish* no cambia (comida) |
| Where is the vegetables? | Where **are** the vegetables? | plural → *are* |
| childs | **children** | irregular |
| persons (prioridad A1) | **people** | forma más natural en A1 |

---

## 9. Mini prácticas orales

1. Nombra 3 frutas y 3 verduras en inglés.  
2. Di dónde está la carne en tu supermercado habitual (*at the back / in aisle…*).  
3. Pregunta a alguien: *Where are the eggs?*  
4. Di tu lista: *I need some chicken, two tomatoes and six eggs.*

> I need some beef and chicken.  
> The vegetables are in aisle three.  
> Where is the fruit section?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-51/need-beef-chicken.mp3" title="🔊 I need some beef and chicken"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-51/veg-aisle-three.mp3" title="🔊 The vegetables are in aisle three"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-51/where-fruit-section.mp3" title="🔊 Where is the fruit section?"></audio>

---

## 10. Ejercicios

### Ejercicio 1 — Plurales regulares

1. apple → \_\_\_\_  
2. tomato → \_\_\_\_  
3. potato → \_\_\_\_  
4. egg → \_\_\_\_  
5. banana → \_\_\_\_

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **apples** · 2. **tomatoes** · 3. **potatoes** · 4. **eggs** · 5. **bananas**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Completa

1. I need two \_\_\_\_ for the salad. (tomate)  
2. We have three \_\_\_\_ in the fridge. (patata)  
3. There are many \_\_\_\_ in the fruit section. (manzana)  
4. How many \_\_\_\_ do you need? (huevo)  
5. I want two \_\_\_\_ of fish.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **tomatoes**  
2. **potatoes**  
3. **apples**  
4. **eggs**  
5. **pieces**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Irregulares y especiales

1. child → \_\_\_\_  
2. person → \_\_\_\_  
3. Plural de *fish* (comida) → \_\_\_\_  
4. Correcto: ____  

a) two fishs · b) two fish · c) two fisheses

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **children** · 2. **people** · 3. **fish** · 4. **b**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Categorías

Escribe **fruit / vegetables / meat / fish**:

1. banana → \_\_\_\_  
2. carrot → \_\_\_\_  
3. chicken → \_\_\_\_  
4. salmon → \_\_\_\_  
5. tomato → \_\_\_\_  
6. beef → \_\_\_\_

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **fruit** · 2. **vegetables** · 3. **meat** · 4. **fish** · 5. **vegetables** · 6. **meat**
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Tienda

1. The apples are in \_\_\_\_ five.  
2. First I get a \_\_\_\_. (carrito)  
3. Then I pay at the \_\_\_\_.  
4. Meat and fish are at the \_\_\_\_.  
5. Where \_\_\_\_ the vegetables?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **aisle**  
2. **trolley**  
3. **checkout**  
4. **back**  
5. **are**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Corrige

1. *I need two tomatos.*  
2. *Where is the vegetables?*  
3. *I want two fishs.*  
4. *There are many childs.*  
5. *The apples is in aisle five.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I need two **tomatoes**.  
2. Where **are** the vegetables?  
3. I want two **fish** / two **pieces of fish**.  
4. There are many **children**.  
5. The apples **are** in aisle five.
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Empareja

1. aisle  
2. checkout  
3. trolley  
4. basket  
5. shelf  

a) caja · b) carrito · c) pasillo · d) estante · e) cesta

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1 → **c** · 2 → **a** · 3 → **b** · 4 → **e** · 5 → **d**
</details>

### Ejercicio 8 — Completa el texto

I go to the supermarket every Saturday. First I get a \_\_\_\_. The fruit and vegetables are in \_\_\_\_ one. I buy \_\_\_\_, bananas and \_\_\_\_. The meat and fish are at the \_\_\_\_. I need some \_\_\_\_ and two \_\_\_\_ of fish. Then I pay at the \_\_\_\_.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**trolley** · **aisle** · **apples** · **tomatoes** · **back** · **chicken** · **pieces** · **checkout**
</details>

### Ejercicio 9 — Traduce

1. Necesito dos tomates para la ensalada.  
2. ¿Dónde están las verduras?  
3. La fruta está en el pasillo uno.  
4. Quiero dos trozos de pescado.  
5. Luego pago en la caja.  
6. Coge un carrito si tienes muchas cosas.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I need two tomatoes for the salad.  
2. Where are the vegetables?  
3. The fruit is in aisle one. / Fruit is in aisle one.  
4. I want two pieces of fish.  
5. Then I pay at the checkout.  
6. Get a trolley if you have many things.
</details>

### Ejercicio 10 — Escribe tu compra

Escribe 8–10 frases sobre una compra. Incluye:

- 3 plurales (*apples / tomatoes / eggs…*)  
- 1 × *aisle*  
- 1 × *trolley* o *basket*  
- 1 × *meat* o *fish*  
- 1 × *checkout*  
- 1 pregunta *Where is…?* o *Where are…?*

**Modelo:** el texto de la sección 6.

---

## 11. Plan de estudio (25–30 minutos)

1. **5 min** — Repasa las tablas de plurales y vocabulario.  
2. **8 min** — Haz los ejercicios 1–6.  
3. **7 min** — Escucha y repite 8 audios (incluye el diálogo).  
4. **5–8 min** — Escribe tu lista de compra y léela en voz alta.

### Checklist

- [ ] Formo *tomatoes / potatoes / apples / eggs*  
- [ ] Recuerdo *children / people / fish*  
- [ ] Clasifico fruit / vegetables / meat / fish  
- [ ] Uso *aisle, trolley, checkout*  
- [ ] Pregunto *Where are the…?* / *Where is the…?*

---

## 12. Consejos y siguiente paso

1. Practica plurales **con lista real** de la nevera, no solo con tablas.  
2. Si confundes *Where is / Where are*, mira el sustantivo: plural → *are*.  
3. *Some meat / some fish* prepara U52–53 (*countable / uncountable*, *some / any*).  
4. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 51](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-51-supermercado-plurales-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 51 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-51).

La **Unidad 52** profundiza en **contables e incontables** (*a banana* vs *some milk*).

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Lo esencial |
| :--- | :--- |
| Regular + -s | apples · bananas · eggs |
| + -es | tomatoes · potatoes |
| Irregular | children · people |
| Fish | fish / pieces of fish |
| Comida | fruit · vegetables · meat · fish |
| Tienda | aisle · trolley · checkout · at the back |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 51 A1 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-51-supermercado-plurales-ejercicios-soluciones)
- [Unidad 51 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-51)

En la **Unidad 52** estudiarás **Countable & Uncountable** (contables e incontables): *an apple* vs *some milk / some rice*.

Guía dedicada y curso:

- [Unidad 52 — Contables e incontables](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-52-contables-incontables)
- [Unidad 52 — Countable & Uncountable](/curso-a1/unit-52)

Guías relacionadas:

- [Inglés para compras](/blog/viajes/ingles-para-compras)
- [Inglés en mercados y regateo](/blog/viajes/ingles-mercados-regateo-viaje)
- [Inglés en la cocina](/blog/viajes/ingles-en-la-cocina)

---

## Fuentes

title: Countable & Uncountable A1: much, many y a lot of

faqs.question: ¿Qué se aprende en la Unidad 52 del curso A1?

faqs.question: ¿Cuándo uso many y cuándo much?

content:
En la [Unidad 51](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-51-supermercado-plurales) compraste *tomatoes* y *apples*. En la **Unidad 52 del curso A1** (*Countable & Uncountable*) aprendes a medir cantidad: ***much / many / a lot of*** con ***milk, water, bread, rice*** frente a ***apples, eggs***.

Conecta con comidas de la [Unidad 17](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-17-comidas-breakfast-lunch-dinner). Incluye **audios**, **esquemas** y **ejercicios**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 52 — Countable & Uncountable](/curso-a1/unit-52)  
> **Repaso útil:** [Unidad 51 — Supermercado](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-51-supermercado-plurales) · [Unidad 17 — Comidas](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-17-comidas-breakfast-lunch-dinner)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 52 (A1)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Distinguir **countable** (*apple, egg*) e **uncountable** (*milk, water, bread, rice*).
- Usar ***many*** con plurales contables.
- Usar ***much*** con incontables (sobre todo en negativas y preguntas).
- Usar ***a lot of*** con ambos tipos.
- Preguntar: ***How many…?*** / ***How much…?***
- Hablar de una **lista de compra** con cantidades naturales.

---

## 1. Countable vs uncountable

| Tipo | Idea | Ejemplos | Cantidad |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Countable** | se pueden contar | apple, egg, orange, banana | one apple, two eggs, many apples |
| **Uncountable** | sin plural normal | milk, water, bread, rice, sugar, coffee | some milk, much water, a lot of rice |

> Apples and eggs are **countable** — we say two apples.  
> Milk, water, bread and rice are **uncountable**.  
> We don't usually say *two milks* or *three rices* in A1.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-52/apples-countable.mp3" title="🔊 Apples and eggs are countable"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-52/milk-uncountable.mp3" title="🔊 Milk, water, bread and rice are uncountable"></audio>

![Countable vs Uncountable A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-52/a1-unit52-countable-uncountable.png)

---

## 2. *Many* + contable plural

Usa ***many*** con cosas que puedes contar (plural):

| Correcto | Incorrecto típico |
| :--- | :--- |
| How **many** eggs do you need? | *How much eggs?* |
| I need **many** apples. | *I need much apples.* |
| There aren't **many** oranges. | *There isn't many oranges.* |

> How many eggs do you need?  
> How many apples do you want?  
> She has a lot of apples in the basket. / She has many apples.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-52/how-many-eggs.mp3" title="🔊 How many eggs do you need?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-52/how-many-apples.mp3" title="🔊 How many apples do you want?"></audio>

---

## 3. *Much* + incontable

Usa ***much*** con incontables. En A1 es muy frecuente en **negativas** y **preguntas**:

| Correcto | Incorrecto típico |
| :--- | :--- |
| I don't have **much** milk left. | *I don't have many milk.* |
| There isn't **much** bread left. | *There aren't much bread.* |
| Do we have **much** milk? | *Do we have many milk?* |

> I don't have much milk left.  
> There isn't much bread left.  
> Do we have much milk? — No, we don't have much.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-52/dont-have-much-milk.mp3" title="🔊 I don't have much milk left"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-52/isnt-much-bread.mp3" title="🔊 There isn't much bread left"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-52/do-we-have-much-milk.mp3" title="🔊 Do we have much milk?"></audio>

Pregunta con incontable: ***How much*** milk / water / rice / sugar…?

> How much milk do we have?  
> How much water do you want?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-52/how-much-milk.mp3" title="🔊 How much milk do we have?"></audio>

---

## 4. *A lot of* — contables e incontables

***A lot of*** funciona con **ambos**. Es la opción más cómoda en afirmativas:

| Con contable | Con incontable |
| :--- | :--- |
| a lot of apples | a lot of water |
| a lot of eggs | a lot of bread |
| a lot of oranges | a lot of rice / milk |

> We have a lot of water in the fridge.  
> We have a lot of water and bread.  
> I'll buy water and many apples. / I'll buy a lot of apples.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-52/alot-of-water.mp3" title="🔊 We have a lot of water in the fridge"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-52/alot-water-bread.mp3" title="🔊 We have a lot of water and bread"></audio>

![much many a lot of A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-52/a1-unit52-much-many-alot.png)

### Tabla rápida

| Cuantificador | Contable plural | Incontable | Uso típico A1 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **many** | ✅ many eggs | ❌ | preguntas / negativas / afirmativas |
| **much** | ❌ | ✅ much milk | preguntas / negativas |
| **a lot of** | ✅ a lot of eggs | ✅ a lot of milk | especialmente afirmativas |

---

## 5. Vocabulario esencial

| Uncountable | Countable |
| :--- | :--- |
| milk | apple / apples |
| water | egg / eggs |
| bread | orange / oranges |
| rice | banana / bananas |
| sugar | tomato / tomatoes |
| coffee | carrot / carrots |

> I need some milk and bread.  
> How many eggs do you want?  
> There is a lot of water in the fridge.  
> We say some rice, a lot of bread — not two rices.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-52/need-milk-bread.mp3" title="🔊 I need some milk and bread"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-52/some-rice-alot-bread.mp3" title="🔊 We say some rice, a lot of bread"></audio>

*Some* aparece aquí de forma natural (*some milk, some rice*). Lo profundizarás con *any* en la [Unidad 53](/curso-a1/unit-53).

---

## 6. Lista de compra modelo

![Shopping list countable uncountable A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-52/a1-unit52-shopping-list.png)

> I need to buy some food today. We don't have much milk or bread left. I want a lot of water and some rice. For fruit I need many apples and six eggs. We have too much sugar at home so I won't buy any. How many oranges do we need? Maybe four or five.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-52/reading-shopping.mp3" title="🔊 I need to buy some food today…"></audio>

Marca en el texto:

- *much milk / bread* (incontable + negativa)  
- *a lot of water* / *some rice*  
- *many apples* / *six eggs* / *How many oranges?*

---

## 7. Diálogo de listening

> **A:** Do we have much milk?  
> **B:** No, we don't have much.  
> **A:** How many eggs do we need?  
> **B:** Six eggs and a lot of bread. We have some rice but not much water.  
> **A:** I'll buy water and many apples.  
> **B:** Good. Don't buy too much sugar; we have a lot already.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-52/dialogue-full.mp3" title="🔊 Do we have much milk?…"></audio>

---

## 8. *Too much* (aviso A1)

En el reading aparece ***too much*** = demasiado (incontable):

> We have **too much** sugar at home.  
> Don't buy **too much** sugar.

Con contables, más adelante verás *too many* (*too many apples*). En esta unidad prioriza *too much* + incontable.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-52/too-much-sugar.mp3" title="🔊 Don't buy too much sugar"></audio>

---

## 9. Errores frecuentes

| Incorrecto | Correcto | Por qué |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| How much eggs? | How **many** eggs? | *eggs* = contable plural |
| How many milk? | How **much** milk? | *milk* = incontable |
| I don't have many milk. | I don't have **much** milk. | incontable → *much* |
| two rices / three breads | some rice / some bread | incontables sin plural normal |
| a lot of of water | **a lot of** water | una sola *of* |
| There aren't much bread. | There **isn't much** bread. | incontable → *isn't* + *much* |

---

## 10. Mini prácticas orales

1. Nombra 4 incontables y 4 contables de tu cocina.  
2. Pregunta: *How much milk do we have?* / *How many eggs do we need?*  
3. Di qué te falta: *We don't have much bread left.*  
4. Di qué compras: *I'll buy a lot of water and many apples.*

> We don't have much water.  
> I'll buy water and many apples.  
> We have a lot of sugar already.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-52/dont-have-much-water.mp3" title="🔊 We don't have much water"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-52/buy-water-apples.mp3" title="🔊 I'll buy water and many apples"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-52/alot-sugar-already.mp3" title="🔊 We have a lot of sugar already"></audio>

---

## 11. Ejercicios

### Ejercicio 1 — ¿Contable o incontable?

1. milk → \_\_\_\_  
2. apple → \_\_\_\_  
3. rice → \_\_\_\_  
4. eggs → \_\_\_\_  
5. bread → \_\_\_\_  
6. water → \_\_\_\_

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **uncountable** · 2. **countable** · 3. **uncountable** · 4. **countable** · 5. **uncountable** · 6. **uncountable**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — *much* / *many* / *a lot of*

1. I don't have \_\_\_\_ milk left.  
2. How \_\_\_\_ eggs do you need?  
3. We have \_\_\_\_ water in the fridge.  
4. There isn't \_\_\_\_ bread left.  
5. She has \_\_\_\_ apples in the basket.  
6. How \_\_\_\_ milk do we have?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **much**  
2. **many**  
3. **a lot of**  
4. **much**  
5. **a lot of** / **many**  
6. **much**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Elige la correcta

1. ____  
   a) How many milk? · b) How much milk? · c) How much milks?  
2. ____  
   a) How many eggs? · b) How much eggs? · c) How many egg?  
3. ____  
   a) a lot of rice · b) many rice · c) much rices  
4. Which is uncountable?  
   a) apple · b) egg · c) rice

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **b** · 2. **a** · 3. **a** · 4. **c**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Completa con vocabulario

1. I need some \_\_\_\_ and bread. (leche)  
2. How many \_\_\_\_ do you want? (huevos)  
3. There is a lot of \_\_\_\_ in the fridge. (agua)  
4. We have some \_\_\_\_ but not much water. (arroz)  
5. Don't buy too much \_\_\_\_. (azúcar)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **milk** · 2. **eggs** · 3. **water** · 4. **rice** · 5. **sugar**
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Corrige

1. *How much eggs do you need?*  
2. *I don't have many milk.*  
3. *We have two rices.*  
4. *How many water do you want?*  
5. *There aren't much bread left.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. How **many** eggs do you need?  
2. I don't have **much** milk.  
3. We have **some** rice. / We have **a lot of** rice.  
4. How **much** water do you want?  
5. There **isn't much** bread left.
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Empareja

1. many  
2. much  
3. a lot of  
4. How many…?  
5. How much…?  

a) milk / water / bread  
b) eggs / apples (pregunta)  
c) contable e incontable  
d) eggs / apples (afirm./neg./preg.)  
e) milk / rice (pregunta)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1 → **d** · 2 → **a** · 3 → **c** · 4 → **b** · 5 → **e**
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Completa el diálogo

A: Do we have \_\_\_\_ milk?  
B: No, we don't have \_\_\_\_.  
A: How \_\_\_\_ eggs do we need?  
B: Six eggs and \_\_\_\_ \_\_\_\_ bread.  
A: I'll buy water and \_\_\_\_ apples.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**much** · **much** · **many** · **a lot** · **of** · **many** / **a lot of**
</details>

### Ejercicio 8 — Completa el texto

I need to buy some food today. We don't have \_\_\_\_ milk or bread left. I want \_\_\_\_ \_\_\_\_ water and some rice. For fruit I need \_\_\_\_ apples and six \_\_\_\_. We have too \_\_\_\_ sugar at home. How \_\_\_\_ oranges do we need?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**much** · **a lot** · **of** · **many** · **eggs** · **much** · **many**
</details>

### Ejercicio 9 — Traduce

1. No tengo mucha leche.  
2. ¿Cuántos huevos necesitas?  
3. Tenemos mucha agua en la nevera.  
4. No queda mucho pan.  
5. Compraré agua y muchas manzanas.  
6. No compres demasiado azúcar.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I don't have much milk. / I don't have much milk left.  
2. How many eggs do you need?  
3. We have a lot of water in the fridge.  
4. There isn't much bread left.  
5. I'll buy water and many apples. / I'll buy water and a lot of apples.  
6. Don't buy too much sugar.
</details>

### Ejercicio 10 — Escribe tu lista

Escribe 8–10 frases sobre tu nevera o compra. Incluye:

- 2 × *much* + incontable  
- 2 × *many* o *How many…?*  
- 2 × *a lot of*  
- 1 × *How much…?*  
- al menos *milk, bread/rice/water* y *eggs/apples*

**Modelo:** el texto de la sección 6.

---

## 12. Plan de estudio (25–30 minutos)

1. **5 min** — Repasa las tablas countable / uncountable y *much/many/a lot of*.  
2. **8 min** — Haz los ejercicios 1–5.  
3. **7 min** — Escucha y repite 8 audios (incluye el diálogo).  
4. **5–8 min** — Escribe tu lista y léela en voz alta.

### Checklist

- [ ] Clasifico milk/rice vs apples/eggs  
- [ ] Uso *many* con plurales contables  
- [ ] Uso *much* con incontables en negativas/preguntas  
- [ ] Uso *a lot of* con ambos  
- [ ] Pregunto con *How many…?* / *How much…?*

---

## 13. Consejos y siguiente paso

1. Si dudas en afirmativa, usa ***a lot of***: funciona casi siempre.  
2. Pregunta mental: ¿puedo decir *two ___?* → contable → *many*.  
3. *Some / any* se practican a fondo en la Unidad 53.  
4. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 52](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-52-contables-incontables-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 52 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-52).

La **Unidad 53** trabaja ***some & any*** en afirmativas, negativas y preguntas.

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Lo esencial |
| :--- | :--- |
| Countable | apples · eggs · oranges |
| Uncountable | milk · water · bread · rice · sugar |
| many | + plural contable |
| much | + incontable (neg./preg.) |
| a lot of | contable e incontable |
| Preguntas | How many…? · How much…? |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 52 A1 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-52-contables-incontables-ejercicios-soluciones)
- [Unidad 52 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-52)

En la **Unidad 53** estudiarás ***some & any***: *I need some milk* / *We don't have any eggs* / *Do you have any rice?*

Guía dedicada y curso:

- [Unidad 53 — Some & Any](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-53-some-any)
- [Unidad 53 — Some & Any](/curso-a1/unit-53)

Guías relacionadas:

- [Inglés para compras](/blog/viajes/ingles-para-compras)
- [Gramática inglesa: guía por niveles](/blog/gramatica/gramatica-inglesa-guia)
- [Inglés en la cocina](/blog/viajes/ingles-en-la-cocina)

---

title: Some & Any A1: afirmativas, negativas y contenedores
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 53 del curso A1: some y any con afirmativas, negativas, preguntas y contenedores, con audios y ejercicios.
description: Aprende some y any en inglés A1: afirmativas, negativas y preguntas, más bottle, box, bag y can. Guía Unidad 53 con audios y ejercicios.
alt: Esquema some y any en afirmativas negativas y preguntas A1

faqs.question: ¿Cuándo uso some y cuándo any en A1?
faqs.answer: Some en afirmativas (I have some milk). Any en negativas y preguntas (There isn't any bread / Do you have any eggs?).

faqs.question: ¿Puedo usar some en preguntas?
faqs.answer: Sí, en ofertas o peticiones: Would you like some tea? / Can I have some water? En preguntas neutras de información prioriza any.

faqs.question: ¿Some y any van con contables o incontables?
faqs.answer: Con ambos: some milk / some apples; any rice / any eggs. Van antes de incontables o plurales.

faqs.question: ¿Qué son bottle, box, bag y can?
faqs.answer: Contenedores: a bottle of water, a box of cereal, a bag of apples, a can of cola. Patrón: a + contenedor + of + producto.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 53 del curso A1?
faqs.answer: En el cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones y en la Unidad 53 del curso A1 de Linguafly: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening, speaking y writing.

content:
En la [Unidad 52](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-52-contables-incontables) mediste cantidad con *much / many / a lot of*. En la **Unidad 53 del curso A1** (*Some & Any*) eliges la forma correcta según el tipo de frase: ***some*** en afirmativas, ***any*** en negativas y preguntas — más ***bottle, box, bag, can***.

Incluye **audios**, **esquemas** y **ejercicios**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 53 — Some & Any](/curso-a1/unit-53)  
> **Repaso útil:** [Unidad 52 — Contables](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-52-contables-incontables) · [Unidad 51 — Supermercado](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-51-supermercado-plurales)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 53 (A1)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Usar ***some*** en oraciones afirmativas.
- Usar ***any*** en negativas y preguntas.
- Ofrecer con ***Would you like some…?***
- Combinar *some/any* con **incontables** y **plurales**.
- Nombrar contenedores: ***bottle, box, bag, can***.
- Formar: ***a bottle of water / a box of cereal / a bag of apples / a can of cola***.

---

## 1. Regla rápida: *some* vs *any*

| Tipo de frase | Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Afirmativa** | **some** | I have **some** milk in the fridge. |
| **Negativa** | **any** | There isn't **any** bread left. |
| **Pregunta** | **any** | Do you have **any** eggs? |
| **Oferta / petición** | **some** (frecuente) | Would you like **some** tea? |

> I have some milk in the fridge.  
> There isn't any bread left.  
> Do you have any eggs?  
> She doesn't have any rice.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-53/have-some-milk.mp3" title="🔊 I have some milk in the fridge"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-53/isnt-any-bread.mp3" title="🔊 There isn't any bread left"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-53/have-any-eggs.mp3" title="🔊 Do you have any eggs?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-53/doesnt-have-any-rice.mp3" title="🔊 She doesn't have any rice"></audio>

![some and any A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-53/a1-unit53-some-any.png)

---

## 2. *Some* en afirmativas

*Some* = “algo de / algunos” (cantidad no exacta).

| Con incontable | Con plural contable |
| :--- | :--- |
| some milk | some eggs |
| some water | some apples |
| some rice | some cans |
| some bread | some bottles |

> We need some water and some apples.  
> There is some milk and some water in bottles.  
> I have some rice in a box.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-53/need-some-water-apples.mp3" title="🔊 We need some water and some apples"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-53/some-rice-in-box.mp3" title="🔊 I have some rice in a box"></audio>

No digas normalmente *\*I have any milk* en afirmativa.

---

## 3. *Any* en negativas y preguntas

| Negativa | Pregunta |
| :--- | :--- |
| There isn't **any** bread. | Do you have **any** bread? |
| I don't have **any** eggs. | Do we have **any** fruit? |
| She doesn't have **any** rice. | Is there **any** milk? |

> Do you have any bread? — No, I don't have any.  
> There isn't any rice left.  
> Do you want any? — No, thanks.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-53/dont-have-any.mp3" title="🔊 No, I don't have any"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-53/isnt-any-rice.mp3" title="🔊 There isn't any rice left"></audio>

Respuesta corta típica: *I don't have any* (sin repetir el sustantivo).

---

## 4. Ofertas: *some* en preguntas

Cuando **ofreces** o **pides** algo, *some* suena natural:

| Oferta / petición | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| Would you like **some**…? | Would you like some tea? |
| Can I have **some**…? | Can I have some water? |
| Do you need **some**…? | Do you need some milk? |

> Do you need a bottle of water or some milk? — Some milk, please.  
> Would you like some tea?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-53/some-milk-please.mp3" title="🔊 Some milk, please"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-53/would-like-some-tea.mp3" title="🔊 Would you like some tea?"></audio>

En A1 del curso, para preguntas de información neutras prioriza ***any***; guarda ***some*** para ofertas y peticiones.

---

## 5. Contenedores: *bottle, box, bag, can*

Patrón: ***a + contenedor + of + producto***

| Contenedor | Uso típico | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **bottle** | líquidos | a bottle of water / milk |
| **box** | cartón / caja | a box of cereal |
| **bag** | bolsa | a bag of apples / potatoes |
| **can** | lata | a can of cola / beans |

> I need a bottle of water.  
> There is a box of cereal on the table.  
> Buy a can of cola.  
> There are some apples in the bag.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-53/bottle-of-water.mp3" title="🔊 I need a bottle of water"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-53/box-of-cereal.mp3" title="🔊 There is a box of cereal on the table"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-53/can-of-cola.mp3" title="🔊 Buy a can of cola"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-53/apples-in-bag.mp3" title="🔊 There are some apples in the bag"></audio>

![Containers A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-53/a1-unit53-containers.png)

Plurales útiles: *bottles, boxes, bags, cans* → *some cans of beans*, *some bottles of water*.

---

## 6. Texto modelo: abro la nevera

![Fridge check some any A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-53/a1-unit53-fridge-check.png)

> I open the fridge. There is some milk and some water in bottles. There isn't any bread left. In the cupboard I have some rice in a box and some cans of beans. Do we have any fruit? Yes, there are some apples in the bag. I need to buy some bread and some eggs.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-53/reading-fridge.mp3" title="🔊 I open the fridge…"></audio>

Marca:

- afirmativas con *some*  
- negativa con *any*  
- pregunta con *any*  
- contenedores: *bottles, box, cans, bag*

---

## 7. Diálogo de listening

> **A:** Do you have any bread?  
> **B:** No, I don't have any.  
> **A:** I have some in the bag. Do you need a bottle of water or some milk?  
> **B:** Some milk, please.  
> **A:** There are some cans of cola in the fridge. Do you want any?  
> **B:** No, thanks. I need to buy some eggs and a box of cereal.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-53/dialogue-full.mp3" title="🔊 Do you have any bread?…"></audio>

---

## 8. Errores frecuentes

| Incorrecto | Correcto | Por qué |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| I have any milk. | I have **some** milk. | afirmativa → *some* |
| I don't have some bread. | I don't have **any** bread. | negativa → *any* |
| Do you have some eggs? (neutra) | Do you have **any** eggs? | pregunta neutra → *any* |
| a bottle water | a bottle **of** water | falta *of* |
| box of cereal (sin artículo) | **a** box of cereal | *a* + contenedor |
| There isn't some rice. | There isn't **any** rice. | negativa → *any* |

---

## 9. Mini prácticas orales

1. Abre tu nevera mental y di 3 frases con *some*.  
2. Di 2 cosas que no hay: *There isn't any…*  
3. Pregunta a alguien: *Do you have any…?*  
4. Ofrece: *Would you like some…?*  
5. Nombra 4 contenedores con *a … of …*

> Do we have any milk? — Yes, we have some.  
> There aren't any eggs left.  
> I need a bag of potatoes.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-53/have-any-milk-yes.mp3" title="🔊 Do we have any milk? Yes, we have some"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-53/arent-any-eggs.mp3" title="🔊 There aren't any eggs left"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-53/bag-of-potatoes.mp3" title="🔊 I need a bag of potatoes"></audio>

---

## 10. Ejercicios

### Ejercicio 1 — *some* o *any*

1. I have \_\_\_\_ milk in the fridge.  
2. There isn't \_\_\_\_ bread left.  
3. Do you have \_\_\_\_ eggs?  
4. We need \_\_\_\_ water and \_\_\_\_ apples.  
5. She doesn't have \_\_\_\_ rice.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **some** · 2. **any** · 3. **any** · 4. **some**, **some** · 5. **any**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Tipo de frase

Elige **afirmativa / negativa / pregunta**:

1. I have some milk. → \_\_\_\_  
2. Do you have any bread? → \_\_\_\_  
3. There isn't any rice. → \_\_\_\_  
4. Would you like some tea? → \_\_\_\_ (oferta)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **afirmativa** · 2. **pregunta** · 3. **negativa** · 4. **pregunta (oferta)**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Contenedores

1. I need a \_\_\_\_ of water.  
2. There is a \_\_\_\_ of cereal on the table.  
3. Buy a \_\_\_\_ of cola.  
4. There are some apples in the \_\_\_\_.  
5. I have some rice in a \_\_\_\_.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **bottle** · 2. **box** · 3. **can** · 4. **bag** · 5. **box**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Empareja

1. bottle  
2. box  
3. bag  
4. can  
5. some  
6. any  

a) cola, beans · b) water, milk · c) affirmative · d) cereal · e) apples, potatoes · f) negative / question

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1 → **b** · 2 → **d** · 3 → **e** · 4 → **a** · 5 → **c** · 6 → **f**
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Corrige

1. *I have any milk.*  
2. *I don't have some bread.*  
3. *Do you have some eggs?* (pregunta neutra)  
4. *a bottle water*  
5. *There isn't some rice left.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I have **some** milk.  
2. I don't have **any** bread.  
3. Do you have **any** eggs?  
4. a bottle **of** water  
5. There isn't **any** rice left.
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Completa el diálogo

A: Do you have \_\_\_\_ bread?  
B: No, I don't have \_\_\_\_.  
A: I have \_\_\_\_ in the bag. Do you need a \_\_\_\_ of water or \_\_\_\_ milk?  
B: \_\_\_\_ milk, please.  
A: There are \_\_\_\_ cans of cola. Do you want \_\_\_\_?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**any** · **any** · **some** · **bottle** · **some** · **Some** · **some** · **any**
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Completa el texto

I open the fridge. There is \_\_\_\_ milk and \_\_\_\_ water in bottles. There isn't \_\_\_\_ bread left. I have \_\_\_\_ rice in a \_\_\_\_ and \_\_\_\_ cans of beans. Do we have \_\_\_\_ fruit? Yes, there are \_\_\_\_ apples in the bag.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**some** · **some** · **any** · **some** · **box** · **some** · **any** · **some**
</details>

### Ejercicio 8 — Elige la correcta

1. ____  
   a) I have any milk · b) I have some milk · c) I have many milk  
2. ____  
   a) Do you have any eggs? · b) Do you have much eggs? · c) Have you some eggs?  
3. ____  
   a) a can of cola · b) a can cola · c) can of a cola  
4. We use any in ____.  
   a) affirmatives only · b) negatives and questions · c) never

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **b** · 2. **a** · 3. **a** · 4. **b**
</details>

### Ejercicio 9 — Traduce

1. Tengo algo de leche en la nevera.  
2. No queda pan.  
3. ¿Tienes huevos?  
4. Necesito una botella de agua.  
5. Hay una caja de cereales en la mesa.  
6. ¿Quieres un poco de té?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I have some milk in the fridge.  
2. There isn't any bread left. / There is no bread left.  
3. Do you have any eggs?  
4. I need a bottle of water.  
5. There is a box of cereal on the table.  
6. Would you like some tea?
</details>

### Ejercicio 10 — Escribe tu nevera

Escribe 8–10 frases. Incluye:

- 3 × *some* (afirmativa)  
- 2 × *any* (negativa)  
- 2 × *any* (pregunta)  
- 1 oferta con *some*  
- 3 contenedores distintos (*bottle / box / bag / can*)

**Modelo:** el texto de la sección 6.

---

## 11. Plan de estudio (25–30 minutos)

1. **5 min** — Repasa la tabla *some/any* y los contenedores.  
2. **8 min** — Haz los ejercicios 1–5.  
3. **7 min** — Escucha y repite 8 audios (incluye el diálogo).  
4. **5–8 min** — Escribe tu “fridge check” y léelo en voz alta.

### Checklist

- [ ] Uso *some* en afirmativas  
- [ ] Uso *any* en negativas y preguntas  
- [ ] Ofrezco con *Would you like some…?*  
- [ ] Formo *a bottle/box/bag/can of…*  
- [ ] Combino *some/any* con milk, eggs, rice, apples

---

## 12. Consejos y siguiente paso

1. Pregunta mental: ¿afirmativa? → *some*. ¿negativa/pregunta? → *any*.  
2. Si ofreces algo, *some* suena más natural.  
3. Contenedores ayudan a “contar” incontables: *a bottle of milk*.  
4. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 53](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-53-some-any-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 53 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-53).

La **Unidad 54** trabaja ***How much & How many*** con precios y cantidades.

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Lo esencial |
| :--- | :--- |
| Afirmativa | some |
| Negativa | any |
| Pregunta | any |
| Oferta | some (Would you like some…?) |
| Contenedores | bottle · box · bag · can |
| Patrón | a + container + of + product |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 53 A1 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-53-some-any-ejercicios-soluciones)
- [Unidad 53 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-53)

En la **Unidad 54** estudiarás ***How much & How many*** (precios y cantidades): *How much is it?* / *How many do you need?*

Guía dedicada y curso:

- [Unidad 54 — How Much & How Many](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-54-how-much-how-many)
- [Unidad 54 — How Much & How Many](/curso-a1/unit-54)

Guías relacionadas:

- [Inglés para compras](/blog/viajes/ingles-para-compras)
- [Inglés en la cocina](/blog/viajes/ingles-en-la-cocina)
- [Inglés A1: guía para empezar](/blog/metodos/ingles-a1)

---

## Fuentes

- CEFR/MCER — Nivel A1: https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages

title: How Much & How Many A1: precio, cantidad y moneda
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 54 del curso A1: How much y How many para precio y cantidad, con audios y ejercicios.
description: Aprende How much y How many en inglés A1: precio, incontables, contables, pound, dollar, euro, cheap y expensive. Guía Unidad 54 con audios y ejercicios.
alt: Esquema How much y How many para precio y cantidad en A1

faqs.question: ¿Cuándo uso How much y cuándo How many?
faqs.answer: How much para precio e incontables (How much is the bread? / How much water?). How many para contables en plural (How many eggs do you need?).

faqs.question: ¿Cómo pregunto el precio en A1?
faqs.answer: How much is it? / How much is the milk? / How much does it cost? Respuesta típica: It's two pounds. / It costs one pound fifty.

faqs.question: ¿Qué monedas practico en la Unidad 54?
faqs.answer: Pound (£), dollar ($) y euro (€), más vocabulario de precio: cost, price, cheap, expensive, total.

faqs.question: ¿How much lleva is o are?
faqs.answer: Para un producto/precio suele ir con is: How much is the bread? Con plurales de productos a veces How much are the apples? (precio del conjunto); en A1 prioriza How much is…? y How many + plural.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 54 del curso A1?
faqs.answer: En el cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones y en la Unidad 54 del curso A1 de Linguafly: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening, speaking y writing.

content:
En la [Unidad 53](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-53-some-any) elegiste *some/any*. En la **Unidad 54 del curso A1** (*How Much & How Many*) preguntas **precio** y **cantidad**: ***How much is it?*** / ***How many eggs do you need?***

Conecta con números y precios de la [Unidad 8](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-8-numeros-edad-precios) y con contables de la [Unidad 52](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-52-contables-incontables). Incluye **audios**, **esquemas** y **ejercicios**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 54 — How Much & How Many](/curso-a1/unit-54)  
> **Repaso útil:** [Unidad 53 — Some & Any](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-53-some-any) · [Unidad 52 — Contables](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-52-contables-incontables)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 54 (A1)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Preguntar **precio** con ***How much is…?*** / ***How much does it cost?***
- Preguntar **cantidad de incontables** con ***How much + milk/water…?***
- Preguntar **cantidad de contables** con ***How many + plural?***
- Responder con **precios** (*two pounds*, *one pound fifty*).
- Usar vocabulario: ***pound, dollar, euro, cost, price, cheap, expensive, total***.

---

## 1. Regla rápida: *How much* vs *How many*

| Pregunta | Uso | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **How much…?** | precio | How much is the bread? |
| **How much…?** | incontable | How much water do you want? |
| **How many…?** | contable plural | How many eggs do you need? |

> How much is the bread?  
> How many eggs do you need?  
> How much water do you want?  
> How many apples are there?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-54/how-much-bread.mp3" title="🔊 How much is the bread?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-54/how-many-eggs.mp3" title="🔊 How many eggs do you need?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-54/how-much-water.mp3" title="🔊 How much water do you want?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-54/how-many-apples.mp3" title="🔊 How many apples are there?"></audio>

![How much and How many A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-54/a1-unit54-how-much-many.png)

---

## 2. *How much* para precio

Patrones A1:

| Pregunta | Respuesta típica |
| :--- | :--- |
| **How much is** the milk? | It's one pound fifty. |
| **How much is** it? | Two pounds. |
| **How much does** the bread **cost**? | It costs two pounds. |
| **How much does** it **cost**? | One euro. |

> How much is the milk? — It's one pound fifty.  
> How much does the bread cost? — Two pounds.  
> How much does it cost?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-54/how-much-milk.mp3" title="🔊 How much is the milk?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-54/one-pound-fifty.mp3" title="🔊 It's one pound fifty"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-54/how-much-does-bread.mp3" title="🔊 How much does the bread cost?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-54/how-much-does-it-cost.mp3" title="🔊 How much does it cost?"></audio>

Recuerda: *How much **is**…?* (verbo singular) es la forma más frecuente para un producto.

---

## 3. *How many* para contables

Siempre + **plural**:

| Correcto | Incorrecto típico |
| :--- | :--- |
| How many **eggs** do you need? | *How much eggs?* |
| How many **oranges** do you want? | *How many orange?* |
| How many **apples** are there? | *How much apples?* |

> How many eggs do you need? — Six, please.  
> How many oranges do you want? — Maybe six.  
> How many apples are there?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-54/six-please.mp3" title="🔊 Six, please"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-54/how-many-oranges.mp3" title="🔊 How many oranges do you want?"></audio>

---

## 4. *How much* + incontable (cantidad)

No es solo precio: también cantidad de *milk, water, rice, bread…*

> How much water do we have? — We have a lot.  
> How much milk do you want?  
> How much rice do we need?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-54/how-much-water-have.mp3" title="🔊 How much water do we have?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-54/we-have-a-lot.mp3" title="🔊 We have a lot"></audio>

Truco: si no puedes decir *two ___* fácilmente → *How much*. Si dices *two/six ___* → *How many*.

---

## 5. Moneda y vocabulario de precio

| Palabra | Idea | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **pound** (£) | libra | two pounds |
| **dollar** ($) | dólar | three dollars |
| **euro** (€) | euro | five euros |
| **cost** | costar | It costs two pounds. |
| **price** | precio | The price is high. |
| **cheap** | barato | That's cheap. |
| **expensive** | caro | That is not expensive. |
| **total** | total | The total is five pounds fifty. |

> The total for my shopping is fifteen pounds.  
> That is not expensive.  
> The milk costs one pound fifty.  
> That's cheap. Thank you.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-54/total-fifteen.mp3" title="🔊 The total for my shopping is fifteen pounds"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-54/not-expensive.mp3" title="🔊 That is not expensive"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-54/thats-cheap.mp3" title="🔊 That's cheap. Thank you"></audio>

![Price and money A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-54/a1-unit54-price-money.png)

---

## 6. Texto modelo: en el mercado

![Shop dialogue A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-54/a1-unit54-shop-dialogue.png)

> I am at the market. I want to buy some fruit and vegetables. How much is the bread? It costs two pounds. How many oranges do I need? Maybe six. How much water do we have? We have a lot. The total for my shopping is fifteen pounds. That is not expensive. The milk costs one pound fifty.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-54/reading-market.mp3" title="🔊 I am at the market…"></audio>

Marca:

- *How much is…?* / *It costs…*  
- *How many oranges…?*  
- *How much water…?*  
- *total / expensive / pound*

---

## 7. Diálogo de listening

> **A:** How much is the milk?  
> **B:** It's one pound fifty.  
> **A:** How many eggs do you need?  
> **B:** Six, please.  
> **A:** How much does the bread cost?  
> **B:** Two pounds. The total is five pounds fifty.  
> **A:** That's cheap. Thank you.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-54/dialogue-full.mp3" title="🔊 How much is the milk?…"></audio>

---

## 8. Errores frecuentes

| Incorrecto | Correcto | Por qué |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| How many is the bread? | How **much** is the bread? | precio → *much* |
| How much eggs do you need? | How **many** eggs…? | contable plural → *many* |
| How many water…? | How **much** water…? | incontable → *much* |
| How much are the bread? | How much **is** the bread? | *bread* + *is* |
| How many egg…? | How many **eggs**…? | plural obligatorio |
| It cost two pounds. | It **costs** two pounds. | 3.ª persona *-s* |

---

## 9. Mini prácticas orales

1. Pregunta el precio de 3 productos de tu cocina.  
2. Pregunta cantidades: *How many…?* / *How much…?*  
3. Di un total: *The total is…*  
4. Opina: *That's cheap* / *That's expensive*.

> How much is the bread? — Two pounds.  
> How many apples do you want? — Six.  
> The total is five pounds fifty.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-54/two-pounds.mp3" title="🔊 Two pounds"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-54/total-five-fifty.mp3" title="🔊 The total is five pounds fifty"></audio>

---

## 10. Ejercicios

### Ejercicio 1 — *much* o *many*

1. How \_\_\_\_ is the bread?  
2. How \_\_\_\_ eggs do you need?  
3. How \_\_\_\_ water do you want?  
4. How \_\_\_\_ does the milk cost?  
5. How \_\_\_\_ apples are there?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **much** · 2. **many** · 3. **much** · 4. **much** · 5. **many**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Completa las preguntas

1. \_\_\_\_ \_\_\_\_ is the milk?  
2. \_\_\_\_ \_\_\_\_ eggs do you need?  
3. \_\_\_\_ \_\_\_\_ does it cost?  
4. \_\_\_\_ \_\_\_\_ oranges do you want?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **How much**  
2. **How many**  
3. **How much**  
4. **How many**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Precio y moneda

1. It costs two \_\_\_\_. (£)  
2. The \_\_\_\_ is five pounds fifty.  
3. That's \_\_\_\_. (barato)  
4. That is not \_\_\_\_. (caro)  
5. The milk \_\_\_\_ one pound fifty.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **pounds** · 2. **total** · 3. **cheap** · 4. **expensive** · 5. **costs**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Empareja

1. How much is it?  
2. How many eggs…?  
3. pound  
4. cheap  
5. expensive  
6. total  

a) £ · b) precio bajo · c) precio · d) contable · e) precio alto · f) todo junto

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1 → **c** · 2 → **d** · 3 → **a** · 4 → **b** · 5 → **e** · 6 → **f**
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Corrige

1. *How many is the bread?*  
2. *How much eggs do you need?*  
3. *How many water do you want?*  
4. *It cost two pounds.*  
5. *How many egg do you need?*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. How **much** is the bread?  
2. How **many** eggs do you need?  
3. How **much** water do you want?  
4. It **costs** two pounds.  
5. How many **eggs** do you need?
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Completa el diálogo

A: How \_\_\_\_ is the milk?  
B: It's one pound fifty.  
A: How \_\_\_\_ eggs do you need?  
B: Six, please.  
A: How much \_\_\_\_ the bread \_\_\_\_?  
B: Two pounds. The \_\_\_\_ is five pounds fifty.  
A: That's \_\_\_\_. Thank you.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**much** · **many** · **does** · **cost** · **total** · **cheap**
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Completa el texto

I am at the market. How \_\_\_\_ is the bread? It \_\_\_\_ two pounds. How \_\_\_\_ oranges do I need? Maybe six. How \_\_\_\_ water do we have? We have a lot. The \_\_\_\_ for my shopping is fifteen pounds. That is not \_\_\_\_.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**much** · **costs** · **many** · **much** · **total** · **expensive**
</details>

### Ejercicio 8 — Elige la correcta

1. ____  
   a) How many is the milk? · b) How much is the milk? · c) How much are the milk?  
2. ____  
   a) How many eggs…? · b) How much eggs…? · c) How many egg…?  
3. Currency in the UK often:  
   a) dollar · b) pound · c) only euro  
4. We use How much for ____.  
   a) price and uncountable · b) only countable · c) never price

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **b** · 2. **a** · 3. **b** · 4. **a**
</details>

### Ejercicio 9 — Traduce

1. ¿Cuánto cuesta el pan?  
2. ¿Cuántos huevos necesitas?  
3. ¿Cuánta agua quieres?  
4. Cuesta dos libras.  
5. El total es cinco libras cincuenta.  
6. Eso es barato.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. How much is the bread? / How much does the bread cost?  
2. How many eggs do you need?  
3. How much water do you want?  
4. It costs two pounds. / It's two pounds.  
5. The total is five pounds fifty.  
6. That's cheap. / That is cheap.
</details>

### Ejercicio 10 — Escribe tu compra

Escribe 8–10 frases de una compra. Incluye:

- 2 × *How much is…?* o *How much does… cost?*  
- 2 × *How many…?*  
- 1 × *How much* + incontable (cantidad)  
- *costs / total / cheap* o *expensive*  
- al menos una moneda (*pounds / euros / dollars*)

**Modelo:** el texto de la sección 6.

---

## 11. Plan de estudio (25–30 minutos)

1. **5 min** — Repasa la tabla *How much / How many* y monedas.  
2. **8 min** — Haz los ejercicios 1–5.  
3. **7 min** — Escucha y repite 8 audios (incluye el diálogo).  
4. **5–8 min** — Representa una compra en voz alta con precios.

### Checklist

- [ ] Pregunto precio con *How much is…?* / *does it cost?*  
- [ ] Uso *How many* + plural  
- [ ] Uso *How much* + incontable  
- [ ] Respondo con *pounds / euros* y *total*  
- [ ] Uso *cheap / expensive*

---

## 12. Consejos y siguiente paso

1. Precio → casi siempre ***How much***.  
2. Contable plural → ***How many***.  
3. Practica números de precio en voz alta (*one pound fifty*).  
4. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 54](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-54-how-much-how-many-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 54 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-54).

La **Unidad 55** te lleva a la tienda de ropa: ***too*** vs ***enough***.

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Lo esencial |
| :--- | :--- |
| Precio | How much is…? · How much does it cost? |
| Incontable | How much milk / water…? |
| Contable | How many eggs / apples…? |
| Moneda | pound £ · dollar $ · euro € |
| Opinión | cheap · expensive |
| Compra | cost · price · total |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 54 A1 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-54-how-much-how-many-ejercicios-soluciones)
