faqs.question: ¿Cuándo uso ever en Present Perfect?
faqs.answer: Sobre todo en preguntas sobre experiencias: Have you ever been to Japan? Has she ever tried Italian food? Ever = “alguna vez (en tu vida)”.

faqs.question: ¿Cuándo uso never?
faqs.answer: En afirmaciones negativas de experiencia: I have never eaten sushi. He has never been to the beach. Never va entre have/has y el past participle.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo respondo a Have you ever…?
faqs.answer: Respuestas cortas: Yes, I have. / No, I haven't. Puedes ampliar: Yes, I have. I have been to London. / No, I haven't. I have never been there.

faqs.question: ¿Puedo decir I never have been?
faqs.answer: En A2 prioriza I have never been… (have/has + never + past participle). Evita never have been y have been never.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 12 del curso A2?
faqs.answer: En el cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones y en la Unidad 12 del curso A2 de Linguafly: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening, speaking y writing.

content:
En la [Unidad 11](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-11-present-perfect-introduccion) formaste *I have been / She has seen*. En la **Unidad 12 del curso A2** (*Present Perfect: Ever & Never*) **preguntas y niegas** experiencias: ***Have you ever…?*** / ***I have never…***

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 12 — Present Perfect: Ever & Never](/curso-a2/unit-12)  
> **Antes:** [U11 — Present Perfect: Introducción](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-11-present-perfect-introduccion)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 12 (A2)

- Preguntar con **ever**: *Have you ever been to Japan?*
- Negar con **never**: *I have never eaten sushi.*
- Responder: **Yes, I have** / **No, I haven't**.
- Colocar *never* entre *have/has* y el past participle.
- Hablar de experiencias (viaje, comida, ocio) en encuestas y diálogos.

![Ever y never Present Perfect A2](/blog/curso-a2/unit-12/a2-unit12-ever-never.png)

---

## 1. Repaso rápido de la forma

Sigues usando **have/has + past participle**.

| | Pregunta con *ever* | Negativa con *never* |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| I / you / we / they | **Have** you **ever** been…? | I **have never** been… |
| he / she / it | **Has** she **ever** tried…? | He **has never** been… |

Participios útiles en esta unidad: *been, eaten, tried, flown, ridden, seen*.

---

## 2. *Ever* en preguntas

**Ever** = “alguna vez (en la vida)”. Va en preguntas, normalmente **después del sujeto**:

> **Have you ever** been to Japan?  
> **Has she ever** tried Italian food?  
> **Have you ever** ridden a horse?  
> **Have you ever** flown in a plane?  
> **Have you ever** eaten sushi?  
> **Have you ever** been to a concert?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-12/have-you-ever-japan.mp3" title="🔊 Have you ever been to Japan?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-12/has-she-ever-tried.mp3" title="🔊 Has she ever tried Italian food?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-12/have-you-ever-ridden.mp3" title="🔊 Have you ever ridden a horse?"></audio>

Estructura:

**Have/Has + sujeto + ever + past participle + …?**

---

## 3. *Never* en frases

**Never** = “nunca / ni una vez”. Va **entre** *have/has* y el past participle:

> I **have never** eaten sushi.  
> He **has never** been to the beach.  
> I **have never** seen snow.  
> I **have never** been to a concert.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-12/have-never-eaten-sushi.mp3" title="🔊 I have never eaten sushi"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-12/has-never-been-beach.mp3" title="🔊 He has never been to the beach"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-12/have-never-seen-snow.mp3" title="🔊 I have never seen snow"></audio>

| Correcto | Incorrecto típico |
| :--- | :--- |
| I have **never** eaten sushi. | *I never have eaten sushi.* |
| I have never seen snow. | *I have seen never snow.* |
| He has never been… | *He never has been…* *(prioridad A2: have + never)* |

Con *never* **no** hace falta *not*: *I have never…* (no *I haven't never…*).

---

## 4. Respuestas cortas: *Yes, I have* / *No, I haven't*

![Respuestas cortas Yes I have No I haven't](/blog/curso-a2/unit-12/a2-unit12-short-answers.png)

| Pregunta | Respuesta corta | Ampliación opcional |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Have you ever been to London? | **Yes, I have.** | I have been to London. |
| Have you ever been there? | **No, I haven't.** | I have never been there. |
| Has she ever tried sushi? | **Yes, she has.** / **No, she hasn't.** | — |

> Yes, I have. I have been to London.  
> No, I haven't. I have never been there.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-12/yes-i-have.mp3" title="🔊 Yes, I have. I have been to London"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-12/no-i-havent.mp3" title="🔊 No, I haven't. I have never been there"></audio>

Truco: la respuesta corta usa el mismo auxiliar (*have/has*), no el past participle.

---

## 5. *Ever* vs *never* (mapa mental)

| Palabra | Tipo de frase | Posición | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **ever** | pregunta | after subject | Have you **ever** flown…? |
| **never** | “negativa” de experiencia | after have/has | I have **never** flown… |

Regla del curso: ***ever* en preguntas · *never* en negativas**.

---

## 6. Texto modelo: encuesta a compañeros

> Have you ever wondered what your friends have or haven't done? I asked my classmates some questions. Have you ever flown in a plane? Most of them said Yes, I have. Have you ever eaten sushi? Some said Yes and some said No, I haven't. Have you ever been to a concert? Many said Yes. One friend said: "I have never been to a concert. I would like to go one day." It was interesting to learn about their experiences.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-12/reading-classmates.mp3" title="🔊 Have you ever wondered what your friends…"></audio>

![Encuesta de experiencias](/blog/curso-a2/unit-12/a2-unit12-experience-survey.png)

Marca: *Have you ever…? · Yes, I have · No, I haven't · I have never been…*

---

## 7. Listening: survey

> Hi! I am doing a survey about experiences. Can I ask you some questions? Great! Have you ever tried sushi? Yes, I have. I tried it in Tokyo last year. It was amazing. Have you ever ridden a horse? No, I haven't. I would like to try one day. Have you ever been to a football match? Yes, I have. Many times! I love football. Thank you for your answers!

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-12/dialogue-survey.mp3" title="🔊 Hi! I am doing a survey about experiences…"></audio>

Nota A2: tras *Yes, I have* a veces aparece Past Simple con fecha (*I tried it in Tokyo last year*). La pregunta de experiencia va en Present Perfect; el detalle con tiempo concreto puede ir en pasado.

---

## 8. Mini práctica oral

> Have you ever been to Japan?  
> I have never eaten sushi.  
> Yes, I have.  
> No, I haven't.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-12/practice-four.mp3" title="🔊 Have you ever been to Japan?…"></audio>

1. Haz 4 preguntas *Have you ever…?* (comida, viaje, deporte, ocio).  
2. Responde a cada una: *Yes, I have* o *No, I haven't* + ampliación.  
3. Di 3 frases *I have never…*

---

## 9. Errores frecuentes

| Incorrecto | Correcto | Por qué |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Ever you have been to Japan? | **Have you ever** been to Japan? | orden: Have + you + ever |
| I never have eaten sushi. | I **have never** eaten sushi. | *never* tras *have* |
| I haven't never been there. | I have **never** been there. / No, I **haven't**. | no dobles negaciones |
| Yes, I do. *(a Have you ever…?)* | **Yes, I have.** | auxiliar *have* |
| No, I don't. | **No, I haven't.** | auxiliar *haven't* |
| Have you never been to Japan? *(pregunta A2 prioritaria)* | **Have you ever** been…? | *ever* en preguntas |
| I have ever been to Japan. *(afirmativa)* | I **have been**… / I **have never**… | *ever* no va en afirmativas normales A2 |

---

## 10. Ejercicios

### Ejercicio 1 — *ever* o *never*

1. ____ have you been to Japan? → *Have you ____ been…*  
2. I have ____ eaten sushi.  
3. Has she ____ tried Italian food?  
4. He has ____ been to the beach.  
5. Have you ____ ridden a horse?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **ever** · 2. **never** · 3. **ever** · 4. **never** · 5. **ever**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Respuestas cortas

1. Have you ever been to London? → ____, I ____. *(sí)*  
2. Have you ever been there? → ____, I ____. *(no)*  
3. Has she ever tried sushi? → Yes, she ____.  
4. Has he ever flown? → No, he ____.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Yes, I have.** · 2. **No, I haven't.** · 3. **has** · 4. **hasn't**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Ordena / coloca *never*

Elige la correcta:

1. ____  
   a) I never have seen snow. · b) I have never seen snow. · c) I have seen never snow.  
2. ____  
   a) Have you ever been to Japan? · b) Ever have you been to Japan? · c) Have ever you been to Japan?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **b** · 2. **a**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Completa la encuesta de compañeros

____ you ever flown in a plane? Most said ____, I ____. Have you ever eaten sushi? Some said No, I ____. One friend said: I have ____ been to a concert.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**Have** · **Yes** · **have** · **haven't** · **never**
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Completa el listening

Have you ever ____ sushi? ____, I have. Have you ever ____ a horse? ____, I haven't. Have you ever ____ to a football match? Yes, I ____.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**tried** · **Yes** · **ridden** · **No** · **been** · **have**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Corrige

1. *I never have eaten sushi.*  
2. *Ever you have been to Japan?*  
3. *Yes, I do.* *(respuesta a Have you ever…?)*  
4. *No, I don't.*  
5. *I haven't never been there.*  
6. *I have seen never snow.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I **have never** eaten sushi.  
2. **Have you ever** been to Japan?  
3. **Yes, I have.**  
4. **No, I haven't.**  
5. I have **never** been there. / No, I haven't.  
6. I have **never** seen snow.
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Empareja

1. Have you ever been to Japan?  
2. I have never eaten sushi.  
3. Yes, I have.  
4. No, I haven't.  
5. Has she ever tried Italian food?  

a) respuesta corta afirmativa · b) pregunta con *ever* (you) · c) negativa con *never* · d) respuesta corta negativa · e) pregunta con *Has… ever*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1 → **b** · 2 → **c** · 3 → **a** · 4 → **d** · 5 → **e**
</details>

### Ejercicio 8 — Elige la correcta

1. *Ever* se usa sobre todo en: ____  
   a) preguntas · b) afirmativas · c) solo con *yesterday*  
2. Posición de *never*: ____  
   a) al final · b) entre have/has y el past participle · c) antes del sujeto  
3. ____  
   a) Have you ever flown in a plane? · b) Have you never flown in a plane? *(prioridad A2 pregunta)* · c) Did you ever fly yesterday Present Perfect  
4. Respuesta a *Have you ever…?*: ____  
   a) Yes, I have. · b) Yes, I do. · c) Yes, I ever.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a** · 2. **b** · 3. **a** · 4. **a**
</details>

### Ejercicio 9 — Traduce

1. ¿Has estado alguna vez en Japón?  
2. Nunca he comido sushi.  
3. ¿Ha probado ella alguna vez comida italiana?  
4. Él nunca ha estado en la playa.  
5. Sí, he estado en Londres.  
6. No, no he. Nunca he estado allí.  
7. ¿Has montado alguna vez a caballo?  
8. Nunca he visto la nieve.  
9. ¿Has volado alguna vez en un avión?  
10. Nunca he ido a un concierto.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. Have you ever been to Japan?  
2. I have never eaten sushi.  
3. Has she ever tried Italian food?  
4. He has never been to the beach.  
5. Yes, I have. I have been to London.  
6. No, I haven't. I have never been there.  
7. Have you ever ridden a horse?  
8. I have never seen snow.  
9. Have you ever flown in a plane?  
10. I have never been to a concert.
</details>

### Ejercicio 10 — Haz tu encuesta

Escribe 8–12 líneas:

- 4 × preguntas *Have you ever…?*  
- 2 × *Yes, I have* (+ detalle)  
- 2 × *No, I haven't* / *I have never…*  

**Modelo:** reading (classmates) o listening (survey).

---

## 11. Plan de estudio (25–30 minutos)

1. **5 min** — Repasa *ever* (preguntas) y *never* (entre have/has y participio).  
2. **8 min** — Ejercicios 1–7.  
3. **7 min** — Escucha la encuesta; practica *Yes, I have / No, I haven't*.  
4. **5–8 min** — Graba tu mini-encuesta.

### Checklist

- [ ] Pregunto con *Have/Has… ever…?*  
- [ ] Niego con *have/has never + past participle*  
- [ ] Respondo *Yes, I have* / *No, I haven't*  
- [ ] No digo *I never have* ni *haven't never*  
- [ ] Puedo hacer una encuesta de 4 preguntas

---

## 12. Consejos y siguiente paso

1. Plantilla: *Have you ever + past participle…?* → *Yes, I have.* / *No, I haven't. I have never…*  
2. Lista: *been to Japan, eaten sushi, flown, ridden a horse, been to a concert, seen snow, tried Italian food, been to a football match*.  
3. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 12](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-12-present-perfect-ever-never-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 12 del curso A2](/curso-a2/unit-12).

La **Unidad 13** añade **already** y **yet**: *I have already…* / *I haven't… yet*.

---

## Resumen rápido

| Caso | Forma |
| :--- | :--- |
| Pregunta | **Have/Has + sujeto + ever + PP…?** |
| Nunca | **have/has + never + PP** |
| Sí | **Yes, I have.** / **Yes, she has.** |
| No | **No, I haven't.** / **No, she hasn't.** |
| Posición *never* | entre *have/has* y el participio |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A2

En la **Unidad 13** estudiarás **Present Perfect: Already & Yet**: *I have already finished* / *I haven't finished yet*.

Guía blog:

- [Unidad 13 — Present Perfect: Already & Yet](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-13-present-perfect-already-yet)

Curso:

- [Unidad 13 — Present Perfect: Already & Yet](/curso-a2/unit-13)

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 12 A2 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-12-present-perfect-ever-never-ejercicios-soluciones)
- [Unidad 12 — Present Perfect: Ever & Never](/curso-a2/unit-12)

Guías relacionadas:

- [Present Perfect: ever / never](/blog/gramatica/present-perfect-ever-never)
- [Present Perfect: usos principales](/blog/gramatica/present-perfect-usos-principales)
- [Present Perfect vs Past Simple](/blog/gramatica/present-perfect-vs-past-simple)

---

title: Past Simple A2: verbos regulares (-ed), yesterday, last week y ago
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 2 del curso A2: Past Simple con verbos regulares (-ed) y expresiones yesterday, last week y ago, con audios y ejercicios.
description: Aprende el Past Simple con verbos regulares en inglés A2: walked, visited, played, finished; yesterday, last week y ago. Guía Unidad 2 con audios y ejercicios.
alt: Esquema Past Simple verbos regulares con -ed para inglés A2

faqs.question: ¿Cómo se forma el Past Simple de los verbos regulares?
faqs.answer: Añades -ed al verbo base: walk → walked, visit → visited, play → played, finish → finished. Con yesterday, last week o ago usas esa forma.

faqs.question: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre yesterday, last week y ago?
faqs.answer: Yesterday = ayer. Last week / last night = la semana / noche pasada. Ago va después de un periodo: two hours ago, three days ago.

faqs.question: ¿Se usa la misma forma con I, he y they?
faqs.answer: Sí. En Past Simple afirmativo el verbo regular es igual para todos: I walked, she walked, they walked.

faqs.question: ¿Qué verbos practico en la Unidad 2 del curso A2?
faqs.answer: Sobre todo regulares: walked, visited, played, finished, watched, cleaned, talked, rested, cooked — con relatos de ayer o la semana pasada.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 2 del curso A2?
faqs.answer: En el cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones y en la Unidad 2 del curso A2 de Linguafly: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening, speaking y writing.

content:
En la [Unidad 1](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-1-saludos-introducciones-repaso) te presentaste en presente. En la **Unidad 2 del curso A2** (*Past Simple: Regular Verbs*) cuentas **lo que ya pasó**: ***walked, visited, played, finished*** + marcas de tiempo ***yesterday, last week, ago***.

Esta guía cubre la **afirmativa con *-ed***, las **expresiones de tiempo**, textos modelo del curso y **ejercicios** con audios.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 2 — Past Simple: verbos regulares](/curso-a2/unit-2)  
> **Antes:** [Unidad 1 — Saludos e introducciones](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-1-saludos-introducciones-repaso)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 2 (A2)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Formar el **Past Simple** de verbos regulares con ***-ed***.
- Usar la misma forma con *I / you / he / she / we / they*.
- Señalar el pasado con ***yesterday***, ***last week / last night***, ***ago***.
- Contar un día o una semana ocupada con varios verbos regulares.
- Evitar el error *\*I walk yesterday* → **I walked yesterday**.

Los verbos irregulares (*went, saw, had…*) llegan en la [Unidad 3](/curso-a2/unit-3).

---

## 1. Forma básica: verbo + *-ed*

| Base | Past Simple | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| walk | **walked** | I **walked** to the park yesterday. |
| visit | **visited** | She **visited** her grandmother last week. |
| play | **played** | We **played** football yesterday. |
| finish | **finished** | He **finished** his homework two hours ago. |
| watch | **watched** | They **watched** a film last night. |
| clean | **cleaned** | I **cleaned** my room yesterday. |
| talk | **talked** | We **talked** for two hours. |
| rest | **rested** | I **rested** at home yesterday. |
| cook | **cooked** | I **cooked** dinner last night. |

Regla A2 prioritaria: **añade *-ed***. Con verbos que ya terminan en *-e* (como *like* → *liked*) solo añades *-d*; en esta unidad el foco son formas claras como *walked / visited / played*.

![Past Simple regular verbs -ed A2](/blog/curso-a2/unit-2/a2-unit2-past-simple-ed.png)

> I walked to the park yesterday.  
> She visited her grandmother last week.  
> We played football yesterday.  
> He finished his homework two hours ago.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-2/walked-yesterday.mp3" title="🔊 I walked to the park yesterday"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-2/visited-last-week.mp3" title="🔊 She visited her grandmother last week"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-2/played-football.mp3" title="🔊 We played football yesterday"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-2/finished-ago.mp3" title="🔊 He finished his homework two hours ago"></audio>

**Importante:** la forma no cambia con la persona:

- I **walked** · She **walked** · They **walked**

---

## 2. Expresiones de tiempo pasado

| Expresión | Significado | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **yesterday** | ayer | I walked to work **yesterday**. |
| **last week** | la semana pasada | I visited my grandmother **last week**. |
| **last night** | anoche | They watched a film **last night**. |
| **last weekend** | el fin de semana pasado | We played football **last weekend**. |
| **… ago** | hace… | He finished two hours **ago**. |
| **on Monday** | el lunes (pasado, en un relato) | **On Monday** I walked to work. |

Con estas marcas → **Past Simple**, no Present Simple.

| Incorrecto | Correcto |
| :--- | :--- |
| I walk to school yesterday. | I **walked** to school yesterday. |
| She visit her grandmother last week. | She **visited** her grandmother last week. |

![Verbos regulares y expresiones de tiempo A2](/blog/curso-a2/unit-2/a2-unit2-verbs-time.png)

> They watched a film last night.  
> I cleaned my room yesterday.  
> We talked for two hours.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-2/watched-last-night.mp3" title="🔊 They watched a film last night"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-2/cleaned-room.mp3" title="🔊 I cleaned my room yesterday"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-2/talked-two-hours.mp3" title="🔊 We talked for two hours"></audio>

---

## 3. Negativa y preguntas (mapa rápido)

El curso A2 trabaja sobre todo la **afirmativa** en esta unidad; conviene tener el mapa completo:

| Tipo | Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Afirmativa | sujeto + verbo-**ed** | I **walked** to the shop. |
| Negativa | sujeto + **didn't** + base | I **didn't walk** to the shop. |
| Pregunta | **Did** + sujeto + base? | **Did** you **walk** to the shop? |

En negativa y pregunta el verbo vuelve a la **base** (*walk*, no *walked*).

---

## 4. Texto modelo: una semana ocupada

> Last week I had a busy week. On Monday I walked to work because my car was broken. On Tuesday I visited my grandmother in the hospital. She was happy to see me. On Wednesday I played football with my friends. We won the match! On Thursday I finished my project at work. My boss was very happy. Yesterday I rested at home and watched a film.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-2/reading-busy-week.mp3" title="🔊 Last week I had a busy week…"></audio>

![A busy week Past Simple A2](/blog/curso-a2/unit-2/a2-unit2-busy-week.png)

Marca los regulares: *walked · visited · played · finished · rested · watched*.  
(*had, was, won* son irregulares — los verás a fondo en la Unidad 3.)

---

## 5. Listening: lo que hice ayer

> Hi! I want to tell you about what I did yesterday. In the morning I walked to the shop and picked up some bread. Then I visited my friend Sarah. We played cards and talked for two hours. In the afternoon I cleaned my room and finished my homework. Last night I watched a film on TV. It was very good!

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-2/dialogue-yesterday.mp3" title="🔊 Hi! I want to tell you about yesterday…"></audio>

Orden del día: **morning** (*walked, visited, played, talked*) → **afternoon** (*cleaned, finished*) → **last night** (*watched*).

---

## 6. Más ejemplos del curso

> Yesterday I walked to work. In the afternoon I visited my friend. In the evening I cooked dinner and watched TV.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-2/yesterday-routine.mp3" title="🔊 Yesterday I walked to work…"></audio>

> Last weekend I walked in the park and played football. On Sunday I visited my grandmother and cooked lunch with her.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-2/last-weekend.mp3" title="🔊 Last weekend I walked in the park…"></audio>

---

## 7. Errores frecuentes

| Incorrecto | Correcto | Por qué |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| I walk yesterday. | I **walked** yesterday. | *yesterday* → Past Simple |
| She visit her grandmother last week. | She **visited** … | falta *-ed* |
| He finish his homework two hours ago. | He **finished** … | *ago* → pasado |
| They watch a film last night. | They **watched** … | *last night* → pasado |
| I didn't walked. | I didn't **walk**. | tras *didn't* → base |
| Did you walked? | Did you **walk**? | tras *Did* → base |

---

## 8. Mini prácticas orales

1. Di tres cosas que hiciste **yesterday** (*walked / visited / watched…*).  
2. Cuenta tu **last week** día a día (como el texto de la sección 4).  
3. Usa **ago**: *I finished… two hours ago.*  
4. Pregunta a alguien: *Did you play football yesterday?*

> I walked to the shop yesterday.  
> I visited my friend last week.  
> I finished my homework two hours ago.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-2/practice-three.mp3" title="🔊 I walked… I visited… I finished…"></audio>

---

## 9. Ejercicios

### Ejercicio 1 — Forma *-ed*

1. I \_\_\_\_ to the park yesterday. (walk)  
2. She \_\_\_\_ her grandmother last week. (visit)  
3. We \_\_\_\_ football yesterday. (play)  
4. He \_\_\_\_ his homework two hours ago. (finish)  
5. They \_\_\_\_ a film last night. (watch)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **walked** · 2. **visited** · 3. **played** · 4. **finished** · 5. **watched**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Expresiones de tiempo

1. \_\_\_\_ = ayer  
2. \_\_\_\_ week = la semana pasada  
3. two hours \_\_\_\_ = hace dos horas  
4. last \_\_\_\_ = anoche  
5. Con estas palabras usamos \_\_\_\_ Simple.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **yesterday** · 2. **last** · 3. **ago** · 4. **night** · 5. **Past**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Elige la correcta

1. ____  
   a) I walk to school yesterday. · b) I walked to school yesterday. · c) I walking to school yesterday.  
2. ____  
   a) She visited her grandmother last week. · b) She visit her grandmother last week.  
3. "Two days ago" requiere: ____  
   a) Present Simple · b) Past Simple · c) Future

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **b** · 2. **a** · 3. **b**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Completa el texto (semana)

Last week I had a busy week. On Monday I \_\_\_\_ to work. On Tuesday I \_\_\_\_ my grandmother. On Wednesday I \_\_\_\_ football. On Thursday I \_\_\_\_ my project. Yesterday I \_\_\_\_ at home and \_\_\_\_ a film.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**walked** · **visited** · **played** · **finished** · **rested** · **watched**
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Completa el listening

In the morning I \_\_\_\_ to the shop. Then I \_\_\_\_ my friend Sarah. We \_\_\_\_ cards and \_\_\_\_ for two hours. In the afternoon I \_\_\_\_ my room and \_\_\_\_ my homework. Last night I \_\_\_\_ a film on TV.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**walked** · **visited** · **played** · **talked** · **cleaned** · **finished** · **watched**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Empareja

1. walk  
2. visit  
3. play  
4. finish  
5. watch  

a) finished · b) played · c) walked · d) watched · e) visited

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1 → **c** · 2 → **e** · 3 → **b** · 4 → **a** · 5 → **d**
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Corrige

1. *I walk to work yesterday.*  
2. *She visit her grandmother last week.*  
3. *He finish his homework two hours ago.*  
4. *They watch a film last night.*  
5. *I didn't walked to the shop.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I **walked** to work yesterday.  
2. She **visited** her grandmother last week.  
3. He **finished** his homework two hours ago.  
4. They **watched** a film last night.  
5. I didn't **walk** to the shop.
</details>

### Ejercicio 8 — Negativa / pregunta

1. Affirmative: I cleaned my room. → Negative: I \_\_\_\_ clean my room.  
2. Affirmative: She played football. → Question: \_\_\_\_ she play football?  
3. Did you \_\_\_\_ TV last night? (watch)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **didn't** · 2. **Did** · 3. **watch**
</details>

### Ejercicio 9 — Traduce

1. Ayer caminé al parque.  
2. La semana pasada visité a mi abuela.  
3. Jugamos al fútbol ayer.  
4. Terminó los deberes hace dos horas.  
5. Anoche vieron una película.  
6. Limpié mi habitación ayer.  
7. Hablamos durante dos horas.  
8. Ayer descansé en casa.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I walked to the park yesterday.  
2. I visited my grandmother last week. / She visited…  
3. We played football yesterday.  
4. He finished his homework two hours ago.  
5. They watched a film last night.  
6. I cleaned my room yesterday.  
7. We talked for two hours.  
8. I rested at home yesterday.
</details>

### Ejercicio 10 — Escribe tu día / semana

Escribe 8–12 frases en Past Simple regular. Incluye:

- al menos 5 verbos con *-ed* (*walked, visited, played, finished, watched, cleaned, talked, rested, cooked…*)  
- *yesterday* o *last night*  
- *last week* o *last weekend*  
- una expresión con *ago*

**Modelo:** el texto de la sección 4 o el listening de la sección 5.

---

## 10. Plan de estudio (25–30 minutos)

1. **5 min** — Repasa la tabla *-ed* y las expresiones de tiempo.  
2. **8 min** — Haz los ejercicios 1–7.  
3. **7 min** — Escucha la semana ocupada y el día de ayer; repite en voz alta.  
4. **5–8 min** — Escribe y graba tu propio *yesterday*.

### Checklist

- [ ] Formo regulares con *-ed*  
- [ ] Uso la misma forma con *I/she/they*  
- [ ] Combino con *yesterday / last… / ago*  
- [ ] Evito *\*I walk yesterday*  
- [ ] Sé que tras *didn't / Did* va el verbo **base**

---

## 11. Consejos y siguiente paso

1. Cuenta **un día real**: morning → afternoon → evening.  
2. Cada vez que digas *yesterday*, comprueba que el verbo lleva *-ed*.  
3. Lista de 10 regulares en una hoja y di una frase con cada uno.  
4. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 2](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-2-past-simple-verbos-regulares-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 2 del curso A2](/curso-a2/unit-2).

La **Unidad 3** entra en los **verbos irregulares**: *went, saw, had, made, wrote, bought…*

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Lo esencial |
| :--- | :--- |
| Forma | base + **-ed** (igual para todas las personas) |
| Tiempo | yesterday · last week/night · ago · on Monday |
| Afirmativa | I walked / She visited |
| Negativa | didn't + base |
| Pregunta | Did + sujeto + base? |
| Siguiente | irregulares (U3) |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A2

En la **Unidad 3** estudiarás **Past Simple: Irregular Verbs**: *went, saw, had, made* y otros frecuentes para relatos del pasado.

Guía dedicada y curso:

- [Unidad 3 — Past Simple: verbos irregulares](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-3-past-simple-verbos-irregulares)
- [Unidad 3 — Past Simple: verbos irregulares](/curso-a2/unit-3)

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 2 A2 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-2-past-simple-verbos-regulares-ejercicios-soluciones)
- [Unidad 2 — Past Simple: verbos regulares](/curso-a2/unit-2)

Guías relacionadas:

- [Past Simple: usos y reglas](/blog/gramatica/past-simple-usos-reglas)
- [Errores de tiempos de pasado](/blog/gramatica/errores-tiempos-pasado-espanoles)
- [Pronunciación de -ed y -s](/blog/gramatica/pronunciacion-ed-s-ingles)
- [A1 U47 — Vacaciones: was/were](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-47-vacaciones-was-were)

---

## Fuentes

title: Past Simple A2: verbos irregulares (went, saw, had, made, wrote, bought)
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 3 del curso A2: Past Simple con verbos irregulares went, saw, had, made, wrote y bought, con audios y ejercicios.
description: Aprende los verbos irregulares del Past Simple en inglés A2: go-went, see-saw, have-had, make-made, write-wrote, buy-bought. Guía Unidad 3 con audios y ejercicios.
alt: Tabla de verbos irregulares del Past Simple para inglés A2
keywords: go went see saw have had
make made write wrote buy bought

faqs.question: ¿Cuáles son los irregulares clave de la Unidad 3 A2?
faqs.answer: go → went, see → saw, have → had, make → made, write → wrote, buy → bought. No uses *goed, *seed, *buyed ni *writed.

faqs.question: ¿La forma irregular cambia con he/she?
faqs.answer: No. En Past Simple afirmativo es la misma para todas las personas: I went, she went, they went.

faqs.question: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre saw y seen?
faqs.answer: Saw es Past Simple (She saw a film last night). Seen es el participio (más adelante con Present Perfect: I have seen…). En esta unidad usa saw.

faqs.question: ¿Puedo mezclar regulares e irregulares en el mismo relato?
faqs.answer: Sí. Es normal: I went to the market and bought fruit. Then I talked to my friend (talked = regular de la U2).

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 3 del curso A2?
faqs.answer: En el cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones y en la Unidad 3 del curso A2 de Linguafly: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening, speaking y writing.

content:
En la [Unidad 2](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-2-past-simple-verbos-regulares) añadiste *-ed*. En la **Unidad 3 del curso A2** (*Past Simple: Irregular Verbs*) memoritas las formas especiales: ***went, saw, had, made, wrote, bought***.

No hay regla mágica: **hay que aprenderlas**. Esta guía las organiza con tablas, textos del curso, audios y ejercicios.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 3 — Past Simple: verbos irregulares](/curso-a2/unit-3)  
> **Antes:** [Unidad 2 — Verbos regulares](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-2-past-simple-verbos-regulares)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 3 (A2)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Usar ***go → went***, ***see → saw***, ***have → had***.
- Usar ***make → made***, ***write → wrote***, ***buy → bought***.
- Contar un **fin de semana** o un **viaje** con irregulares.
- Evitar *\*goed*, *\*buyed*, *\*writed*, *\*maked*.
- Distinguir Past Simple (*saw*) del participio (*seen*) — este último no es el foco aún.

---

## 1. Los 6 irregulares prioritarios

| Base | Past Simple | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **go** | **went** | I **went** to the cinema yesterday. |
| **see** | **saw** | She **saw** a film last night. |
| **have** | **had** | We **had** a great time at the party. |
| **make** | **made** | He **made** a cake for his birthday. |
| **write** | **wrote** | I **wrote** a letter last week. |
| **buy** | **bought** | She **bought** a new dress yesterday. |

Misma forma para todas las personas: *I went / she went / they went*.

![Irregular verbs Past Simple A2](/blog/curso-a2/unit-3/a2-unit3-irregular-verbs.png)

> I went to the cinema yesterday.  
> She saw a film last night.  
> We had a great time at the party.  
> He made a cake for his birthday.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-3/went-cinema.mp3" title="🔊 I went to the cinema yesterday"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-3/saw-film.mp3" title="🔊 She saw a film last night"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-3/had-great-time.mp3" title="🔊 We had a great time at the party"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-3/made-cake.mp3" title="🔊 He made a cake for his birthday"></audio>

> I wrote a letter to my friend last week.  
> She bought a new dress yesterday.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-3/wrote-letter.mp3" title="🔊 I wrote a letter last week"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-3/bought-dress.mp3" title="🔊 She bought a new dress yesterday"></audio>

---

## 2. Regular vs irregular

| Tipo | Cómo se forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Regular** (U2) | base + *-ed* | walk → **walked** |
| **Irregular** (U3) | forma especial | go → **went** (no *goed*) |

![Regular vs irregular Past Simple A2](/blog/curso-a2/unit-3/a2-unit3-regular-vs-irregular.png)

En un mismo relato mezclas ambos:

> I **went** to the market and **bought** fruit. Then I **talked** to my friend. (*talked* = regular)

---

## 3. Errores típicos (¡no los escribas!)

| Incorrecto | Correcto |
| :--- | :--- |
| I goed to London. | I **went** to London. |
| She seed a film. | She **saw** a film. |
| We haved a great time. | We **had** a great time. |
| He maked a cake. | He **made** a cake. |
| I writed a letter. | I **wrote** a letter. |
| She buyed a dress. | She **bought** a dress. |
| I gone to the shop. | I **went** to the shop. (*gone* ≠ Past Simple aquí) |
| I seen a film yesterday. | I **saw** a film yesterday. |

*Gone* y *seen* son **participios** (aparecen más adelante con *have/has*). En Past Simple afirmativo de esta unidad: **went** y **saw**.

---

## 4. Negativa y preguntas (igual que con regulares)

| Tipo | Forma | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Afirmativa | sujeto + irregular | I **went** to London. |
| Negativa | **didn't** + base | I **didn't go** to London. |
| Pregunta | **Did** + sujeto + base? | **Did** you **go** to London? |

Tras *didn't / Did* vuelve la **base**: *go, see, buy* — no *went, saw, bought*.

---

## 5. Texto modelo: last weekend

> Last weekend I had a wonderful time. On Saturday morning I went to the market and bought some fresh fruit and vegetables. Then I saw my old friend Tom at the cafe. We had coffee together and talked for hours. In the afternoon I went home and made a delicious cake for my family. My sister wrote a letter to our grandmother and I helped her with it. In the evening we saw a film on TV. It was very good!

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-3/reading-weekend.mp3" title="🔊 Last weekend I had a wonderful time…"></audio>

![Last weekend irregular verbs A2](/blog/curso-a2/unit-3/a2-unit3-weekend-story.png)

Marca: *had · went · bought · saw · made · wrote* (+ *talked / helped* regulares).

---

## 6. Listening: viaje a Londres

> Hi! I want to tell you about my trip last month. I went to London with my family. We had a wonderful time! On the first day we went to the British Museum. I saw many interesting things there. Then we bought some souvenirs from a shop near the museum. My sister wrote postcards to her friends. In the evening we made dinner at our hotel. It was delicious! I really enjoyed the trip.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-3/dialogue-london.mp3" title="🔊 Hi! I want to tell you about my trip…"></audio>

Patrón de viaje: **went** → **saw** → **bought** → **wrote** → **made** → **had** a wonderful time.

---

## 7. Más modelos del curso

> Last week I went to the park. I saw many people there.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-3/went-park.mp3" title="🔊 Last week I went to the park…"></audio>

> Last time I went shopping I bought a new shirt and some books.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-3/bought-shirt.mp3" title="🔊 Last time I went shopping…"></audio>

> Yesterday I made pasta for dinner. I had it with salad.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-3/made-pasta.mp3" title="🔊 Yesterday I made pasta…"></audio>

> Last summer I went to Barcelona. I saw the Sagrada Familia. I bought some souvenirs. I had a wonderful time!

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-3/barcelona-trip.mp3" title="🔊 Last summer I went to Barcelona…"></audio>

---

## 8. Mini prácticas orales

1. Di dónde **went** la semana pasada.  
2. Di qué **saw** (cine, TV, ciudad).  
3. Di qué **bought** la última vez que fuiste de compras.  
4. Di qué **made** para comer ayer.  
5. Une todo en un mini-viaje: *went / saw / bought / had*.

> I went to the shop yesterday.  
> She bought a new book last week.  
> He made a delicious dinner last night.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-3/practice-three.mp3" title="🔊 I went… She bought… He made…"></audio>

---

## 9. Ejercicios

### Ejercicio 1 — Elige el pasado

1. I \_\_\_\_ to the cinema yesterday. (go)  
2. She \_\_\_\_ a film last night. (see)  
3. We \_\_\_\_ a great time at the party. (have)  
4. He \_\_\_\_ a cake for his birthday. (make)  
5. I \_\_\_\_ a letter last week. (write)  
6. She \_\_\_\_ a new dress yesterday. (buy)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **went** · 2. **saw** · 3. **had** · 4. **made** · 5. **wrote** · 6. **bought**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Empareja

1. go  
2. see  
3. have  
4. make  
5. write  
6. buy  

a) made · b) went · c) bought · d) saw · e) wrote · f) had

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1 → **b** · 2 → **d** · 3 → **f** · 4 → **a** · 5 → **e** · 6 → **c**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Elige la correcta

1. ____  
   a) I go to London last year. · b) I went to London last year. · c) I gone to London last year.  
2. Past of buy = ____  
   a) buyed · b) bought · c) buied  
3. Past of write = ____  
   a) writed · b) written · c) wrote

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **b** · 2. **b** · 3. **c**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Completa el fin de semana

Last weekend I \_\_\_\_ a wonderful time. On Saturday I \_\_\_\_ to the market and \_\_\_\_ some fruit. Then I \_\_\_\_ my friend Tom. We \_\_\_\_ coffee together. In the afternoon I \_\_\_\_ a cake. My sister \_\_\_\_ a letter. In the evening we \_\_\_\_ a film.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**had** · **went** · **bought** · **saw** · **had** · **made** · **wrote** · **saw**
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Completa el viaje

I \_\_\_\_ to London with my family. We \_\_\_\_ a wonderful time. We \_\_\_\_ to the British Museum. I \_\_\_\_ many interesting things. We \_\_\_\_ souvenirs. My sister \_\_\_\_ postcards. In the evening we \_\_\_\_ dinner at our hotel.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**went** · **had** · **went** · **saw** · **bought** · **wrote** · **made**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Corrige

1. *I goed to the shop yesterday.*  
2. *She seed a film last night.*  
3. *He maked a cake.*  
4. *I writed a letter.*  
5. *She buyed a dress.*  
6. *I seen a film yesterday.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I **went** to the shop yesterday.  
2. She **saw** a film last night.  
3. He **made** a cake.  
4. I **wrote** a letter.  
5. She **bought** a dress.  
6. I **saw** a film yesterday.
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Negativa / pregunta

1. Affirmative: I went to London. → Negative: I \_\_\_\_ go to London.  
2. Affirmative: She bought a book. → Question: \_\_\_\_ she buy a book?  
3. Did you \_\_\_\_ a film last night? (see)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **didn't** · 2. **Did** · 3. **see**
</details>

### Ejercicio 8 — Regular o irregular

Escribe **R** o **I**:

1. walked ____  
2. went ____  
3. visited ____  
4. bought ____  
5. played ____  
6. made ____

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **R** · 2. **I** · 3. **R** · 4. **I** · 5. **R** · 6. **I**
</details>

### Ejercicio 9 — Traduce

1. Ayer fui al cine.  
2. Ella vio una película anoche.  
3. Tuvimos un gran rato en la fiesta.  
4. Él hizo una tarta para su cumpleaños.  
5. Escribí una carta la semana pasada.  
6. Ella compró un vestido nuevo ayer.  
7. Fui a Londres con mi familia.  
8. Compré algunos souvenirs.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I went to the cinema yesterday.  
2. She saw a film last night.  
3. We had a great time at the party.  
4. He made a cake for his birthday.  
5. I wrote a letter last week.  
6. She bought a new dress yesterday.  
7. I went to London with my family.  
8. I bought some souvenirs.
</details>

### Ejercicio 10 — Escribe tu fin de semana / viaje

Escribe 8–12 frases. Incluye al menos:

- 2 × *went*  
- 1 × *saw*  
- 1 × *had*  
- 1 × *made* o *wrote*  
- 1 × *bought*  
- (opcional) 1–2 regulares de la U2 (*talked, visited…*)

**Modelo:** sección 5 (weekend) o sección 6 (London).

---

## 10. Plan de estudio (25–30 minutos)

1. **5 min** — Memoriza la tabla de 6 verbos en voz alta.  
2. **8 min** — Ejercicios 1–7.  
3. **7 min** — Escucha el weekend y el viaje; repite.  
4. **5–8 min** — Escribe y graba tu propio relato.

### Checklist

- [ ] Recito go/went, see/saw, have/had  
- [ ] Recito make/made, write/wrote, buy/bought  
- [ ] Evito *goed / buyed / writed*  
- [ ] Uso *saw* (no *seen*) en Past Simple  
- [ ] Tras *didn't / Did* uso la base

---

## 11. Consejos y siguiente paso

1. Haz tarjetas: cara A = *go*, cara B = *went*.  
2. Cada día cuenta un mini-viaje con *went / saw / bought / had*.  
3. Si aún dudas con *-ed*, vuelve a [U2 regulares](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-2-past-simple-verbos-regulares).  
4. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 3](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-3-past-simple-verbos-irregulares-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 3 del curso A2](/curso-a2/unit-3).

La **Unidad 4** trabaja **Wh-questions in the Past**: *What did you do?*, *Where did you go?*, *When / Who / Why / How did…?*

---

## Resumen rápido

| Base | Past | Recuerda |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| go | **went** | no *goed* |
| see | **saw** | no *seen* (aquí) |
| have | **had** | |
| make | **made** | no *maked* |
| write | **wrote** | no *writed* |
| buy | **bought** | no *buyed* |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A2

En la **Unidad 4** estudiarás **Wh-questions en Past Simple**: preguntar y responder sobre el pasado (*What/Where/When/Who/Why/How did…?*).

Guía dedicada y curso:

- [Unidad 4 — Wh-questions en Past Simple](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-4-wh-questions-past-simple)
- [Unidad 4 — Wh-questions en Past Simple](/curso-a2/unit-4)

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 3 A2 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-3-past-simple-verbos-irregulares-ejercicios-soluciones)
- [Unidad 3 — Past Simple: verbos irregulares](/curso-a2/unit-3)

Guías relacionadas:

- [Past Simple: verbos irregulares](/blog/gramatica/past-simple-verbos-irregulares)
- [Past Simple: usos y reglas](/blog/gramatica/past-simple-usos-reglas)
- [Errores de tiempos de pasado](/blog/gramatica/errores-tiempos-pasado-espanoles)

---

title: Wh-questions en Past Simple A2: What/Where/When/Who/Why/How did…?
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 4 del curso A2: Wh-questions en Past Simple (What/Where/ When/Who/Why/How did…?) y conectores First, Then, Finally, con audios y ejercicios.
description: Aprende a preguntar en pasado en inglés A2: What did you do?, Where did you go?, When/Who/Why/How did…? Guía Unidad 4 con First/Then/Finally, audios y ejercicios.
alt: Esquema de Wh-questions en Past Simple para inglés A2

faqs.question: ¿Cómo se forma una Wh-question en Past Simple?
faqs.answer: Wh-word + did + sujeto + verbo en base: What did you do? Where did she go? No uses el pasado después de did (*What did you did? → What did you do?).

faqs.question: ¿Qué pregunta cada Wh-word?
faqs.answer: What = qué/acción; Where = dónde; When = cuándo; Who = quién; Why = por qué; How = cómo.

faqs.question: ¿Para qué sirven First, Then, After that y Finally?
faqs.answer: Ordenan un relato o una entrevista: First… Then… After that… Finally…

faqs.question: ¿Cuál es el error más frecuente?
faqs.answer: Invertir did y el sujeto (*Where you did go?) o poner el verbo en pasado tras did (*What did you went?). Correcto: Where did you go? / What did you do?

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 4 del curso A2?
faqs.answer: En el cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones y en la Unidad 4 del curso A2 de Linguafly: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening, speaking y writing.

content:
En las [Unidades 2](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-2-past-simple-verbos-regulares) y [3](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-3-past-simple-verbos-irregulares) contaste el pasado. En la **Unidad 4 del curso A2** (*Wh-questions in the Past*) **preguntas** sobre ese pasado: ***What / Where / When / Who / Why / How did…?***

También ordenas relatos con ***First, Then, After that, Finally*** — útil para entrevistas y para contar un fin de semana.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 4 — Wh-questions en Past Simple](/curso-a2/unit-4)  
> **Antes:** [U3 — Irregulares](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-3-past-simple-verbos-irregulares) · [U2 — Regulares](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-2-past-simple-verbos-regulares)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 4 (A2)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Formar preguntas: ***Wh-word + did + sujeto + base verb***.
- Elegir bien ***What / Where / When / Who / Why / How***.
- Responder con frases largas (*I went to Valencia with my friends*).
- Ordenar una historia con ***First, Then, After that, Finally***.
- Evitar *\*Where you did go?* y *\*What did you went?*

---

## 1. Fórmula: Wh + did + sujeto + base

| Parte | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| Wh-word | **What** |
| did | **did** |
| sujeto | **you** |
| verbo base | **do** |
| complemento | yesterday? |

> **What did you do** yesterday?  
> **Where did you go** last weekend?  
> **When did she leave**?

![Wh-questions Past Simple A2](/blog/curso-a2/unit-4/a2-unit4-wh-questions.png)

Tras ***did***, el verbo va en **base** (*do, go, see*), no en pasado (*did, went, saw*).

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-4/what-did-you-do.mp3" title="🔊 What did you do yesterday?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-4/where-did-you-go.mp3" title="🔊 Where did you go last weekend?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-4/when-did-she-leave.mp3" title="🔊 When did she leave?"></audio>

---

## 2. Qué pregunta cada Wh-word

| Wh-word | Pregunta por… | Ejemplo | Respuesta típica |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **What** | acción / cosa | What did you do yesterday? | I went to the beach. |
| **Where** | lugar | Where did you go? | I went to Valencia. |
| **When** | tiempo | When did you leave? | On Sunday afternoon. |
| **Who** | persona | Who did you go with? | With Ana and Pablo. |
| **Why** | razón | Why did you leave early? | Because I was tired. |
| **How** | manera / cómo fue | How did the trip go? | It was amazing! |

> Who did you see at the party?  
> Why did he leave early?  
> How did the exam go?  
> What did you buy at the shop?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-4/who-did-you-see.mp3" title="🔊 Who did you see at the party?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-4/why-did-he-leave.mp3" title="🔊 Why did he leave early?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-4/how-did-it-go.mp3" title="🔊 How did the exam go?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-4/what-did-you-buy.mp3" title="🔊 What did you buy at the shop?"></audio>

---

## 3. Conectores de relato: First, Then, After that, Finally

| Conector | Uso |
| :--- | :--- |
| **First** | primer paso |
| **Then** | siguiente |
| **After that** | después de eso |
| **Finally** | al final |

![Sequence connectors A2](/blog/curso-a2/unit-4/a2-unit4-sequence.png)

> First I went to the beach.  
> Then I swam.  
> After that we had lunch.  
> Finally we went home.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-4/sequence-beach.mp3" title="🔊 First I went to the beach…"></audio>

En entrevistas del curso también organizan las preguntas: *First she asked… Then she asked… Finally she asked…*

---

## 4. Texto modelo: entrevista de trabajo (Carlos)

> Last month my friend Carlos had an interview for a new job. I asked him many questions about it. First I asked what he did to prepare. He said he studied the company online. Then I asked where the interview took place. He said it was at the office in Madrid. I asked when it happened. He said last Tuesday at 10 o'clock. I asked who he met there. He said he met two managers and the HR director. I asked why he wanted the job. He said because it was interesting and near his home. Finally I asked how it went. He said it went very well and he got the job!

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-4/reading-interview.mp3" title="🔊 Last month my friend Carlos…"></audio>

Preguntas equivalentes en forma directa:

| Wh | Pregunta |
| :--- | :--- |
| What | What did he do to prepare? |
| Where | Where did the interview take place? |
| When | When did it happen? |
| Who | Who did he meet there? |
| Why | Why did he want the job? |
| How | How did it go? |

![Asking about the past A2](/blog/curso-a2/unit-4/a2-unit4-interview.png)

---

## 5. Listening: un día de preguntas

> Hi! Yesterday I had a really strange day. My sister called me in the morning and asked me many questions. First she asked what I did last weekend. I said I went to the beach. Then she asked where I went exactly. I said I went to Valencia. She asked when I left. I said I left on Sunday afternoon. She asked who I went with. I said I went with my friends Ana and Pablo. She asked why I did not tell her before. I said because I forgot! Finally she asked how the trip went. I said it was amazing!

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-4/dialogue-sister.mp3" title="🔊 Hi! Yesterday I had a really strange day…"></audio>

Parejas pregunta → respuesta:

- What did you do last weekend? → I went to the beach.  
- Where did you go? → Valencia.  
- When did you leave? → On Sunday afternoon.  
- Who did you go with? → Ana and Pablo.  
- Why didn't you tell her? → Because I forgot.  
- How did the trip go? → It was amazing!

---

## 6. Errores frecuentes

| Incorrecto | Correcto | Por qué |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Where you did go? | **Where did you go?** | *did* delante del sujeto |
| What did you did? | What did you **do**? | base tras *did* |
| What did you went? | What did you **go**? / What did you **do**? | base, no pasado |
| Where did you went? | Where did you **go**? | *go*, no *went* |
| Who you see? | **Who did you see?** | falta *did* |
| How the trip went? | **How did the trip go?** | *did* + base |

---

## 7. Mini prácticas orales

Haz estas 6 preguntas a un compañero (o a ti mismo) sobre el último fin de semana:

1. What did you do?  
2. Where did you go?  
3. When did you leave / arrive?  
4. Who did you go with?  
5. Why did you choose that place?  
6. How did it go?

> What did you do last weekend?  
> Where did you go?  
> Who did you go with?  
> How did the trip go?

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-4/practice-four.mp3" title="🔊 What did you do last weekend?…"></audio>

---

## 8. Ejercicios

### Ejercicio 1 — Elige el Wh-word

1. \_\_\_\_ did you do yesterday?  
2. \_\_\_\_ did you go last weekend?  
3. \_\_\_\_ did she leave?  
4. \_\_\_\_ did you see at the party?  
5. \_\_\_\_ did he leave early?  
6. \_\_\_\_ did the exam go?

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **What** · 2. **Where** · 3. **When** · 4. **Who** · 5. **Why** · 6. **How**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Ordena

1. did / What / you / do / yesterday  
2. go / did / Where / you  
3. you / Who / did / see  
4. did / Why / leave / he / early

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **What did you do yesterday?**  
2. **Where did you go?**  
3. **Who did you see?**  
4. **Why did he leave early?**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Completa con la base correcta

1. What did you \_\_\_\_ yesterday? (do)  
2. Where did she \_\_\_\_? (go)  
3. Who did you \_\_\_\_ at the party? (see)  
4. What did you \_\_\_\_ at the shop? (buy)  
5. How did the trip \_\_\_\_? (go)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **do** · 2. **go** · 3. **see** · 4. **buy** · 5. **go**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Empareja pregunta y respuesta

1. What did you do?  
2. Where did you go?  
3. When did you leave?  
4. Who did you go with?  
5. How did it go?  

a) To Valencia. · b) It was amazing! · c) I went to the beach. · d) On Sunday afternoon. · e) Ana and Pablo.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1 → **c** · 2 → **a** · 3 → **d** · 4 → **e** · 5 → **b**
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Conectores

Completa: First / Then / After that / Finally

\_\_\_\_ I went to the beach. \_\_\_\_ I swam. \_\_\_\_ we had lunch. \_\_\_\_ we went home.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**First** · **Then** · **After that** · **Finally**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Completa la entrevista (Carlos)

First I asked \_\_\_\_ he did to prepare. Then I asked \_\_\_\_ the interview took place. I asked \_\_\_\_ it happened. I asked \_\_\_\_ he met there. I asked \_\_\_\_ he wanted the job. Finally I asked \_\_\_\_ it went.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**what** · **where** · **when** · **who** · **why** · **how**
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Corrige

1. *Where you did go?*  
2. *What did you did yesterday?*  
3. *Where did you went?*  
4. *Who you see at the party?*  
5. *How the trip went?*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Where did you go?**  
2. What did you **do** yesterday?  
3. Where did you **go**?  
4. **Who did you see** at the party?  
5. **How did the trip go?**
</details>

### Ejercicio 8 — Completa el listening

First she asked \_\_\_\_ I did last weekend. Then she asked \_\_\_\_ I went. She asked \_\_\_\_ I left. She asked \_\_\_\_ I went with. She asked \_\_\_\_ I did not tell her. Finally she asked \_\_\_\_ the trip went.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**what** · **where** · **when** · **who** · **why** · **how**
</details>

### Ejercicio 9 — Traduce

1. ¿Qué hiciste ayer?  
2. ¿Dónde fuiste el fin de semana pasado?  
3. ¿Cuándo se fue ella?  
4. ¿A quién viste en la fiesta?  
5. ¿Por qué se fue temprano?  
6. ¿Cómo fue el viaje?  
7. Primero fui a la playa.  
8. Finalmente volvimos a casa.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. What did you do yesterday?  
2. Where did you go last weekend?  
3. When did she leave?  
4. Who did you see at the party?  
5. Why did he/she leave early?  
6. How did the trip go?  
7. First I went to the beach.  
8. Finally we went home.
</details>

### Ejercicio 10 — Escribe tu entrevista

Escribe 8–12 frases: incluye las 6 Wh-questions (o sus respuestas) sobre tu último fin de semana / viaje, y usa **First, Then, Finally** (y si puedes *After that*).

**Modelo:**

> Last weekend I went to the beach. First I packed my bag. Then I went to Valencia with Ana and Pablo. After that we had lunch. Finally we went home. It was amazing!

---

## 9. Plan de estudio (25–30 minutos)

1. **5 min** — Repasa la fórmula y la tabla Wh.  
2. **8 min** — Ejercicios 1–7.  
3. **7 min** — Escucha la entrevista y el diálogo de la hermana; repite las preguntas.  
4. **5–8 min** — Graba tus 6 preguntas + respuestas sobre el fin de semana.

### Checklist

- [ ] Uso *Wh + did + sujeto + base*  
- [ ] Distingo What / Where / When / Who / Why / How  
- [ ] No pongo pasado tras *did*  
- [ ] Ordeno con First / Then / After that / Finally  
- [ ] Puedo preguntar y responder sobre un viaje corto

---

## 10. Consejos y siguiente paso

1. Memoriza el esqueleto: ***did + sujeto + base*** — el Wh solo cambia el tipo de información.  
2. Practica en pareja: uno pregunta, otro responde con *went / saw / had* (U3).  
3. Si fallas el verbo en pasado, vuelve a [U2](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-2-past-simple-verbos-regulares) / [U3](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-3-past-simple-verbos-irregulares).  
4. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 4](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-4-wh-questions-past-simple-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 4 del curso A2](/curso-a2/unit-4).

La **Unidad 5** entra en **comparativos**: *bigger than*, *more expensive than*, *as… as*.

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Lo esencial |
| :--- | :--- |
| Fórmula | Wh + **did** + sujeto + **base** |
| Wh-words | What · Where · When · Who · Why · How |
| Relato | First · Then · After that · Finally |
| Error típico | *Where you did go?* / *What did you went?* |
| Respuesta | frase completa en Past Simple |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A2

En la **Unidad 5** estudiarás **Comparatives**: *-er*, *more… than* y una introducción a *as… as*.

Guía dedicada y curso:

- [Unidad 5 — Comparativos](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-5-comparativos-er-more-than)
- [Unidad 5 — Comparativos](/curso-a2/unit-5)

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 4 A2 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-4-wh-questions-past-simple-ejercicios-soluciones)
- [Unidad 4 — Wh-questions Past Simple](/curso-a2/unit-4)

Guías relacionadas:

- [Past Simple: usos y reglas](/blog/gramatica/past-simple-usos-reglas)
- [Past Simple vs Past Continuous](/blog/gramatica/past-simple-vs-past-continuous)
- [Past Simple: verbos irregulares](/blog/gramatica/past-simple-verbos-irregulares)

---

## Fuentes

- CEFR/MCER — Nivel A2: https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages
- Cambridge English — A2 Key: https://www.cambridgeenglish.org/exams-and-tests/key/
- British Council — Question forms: https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/grammar/a1-a2-grammar
- British Council — Past simple questions: https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/grammar/a1-a2-grammar/past-simple-questions

title: Comparativos A2: -er, more… than, better y as… as
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 5 del curso A2: comparativos con -er, more… than, better / worse y as… as, con audios y ejercicios.
description: Aprende comparativos en inglés A2: taller than, more expensive than, better / worse y as… as. Guía Unidad 5 con audios, ortografía y ejercicios.
alt: Esquema de comparativos -er y more than para inglés A2

faqs.question: ¿Cuándo uso -er y cuándo more?
faqs.answer: Adjetivos cortos (1 sílaba, a veces 2): -er (taller, bigger, hotter). Adjetivos largos: more + adjetivo (more interesting, more expensive). Siempre puedes cerrar con than.

faqs.question: ¿Cuál es el comparativo de good y bad?
faqs.answer: good → better (no *gooder*). bad → worse (no *badder*). Ejemplos: a better camera; worse than yesterday.

faqs.question: ¿Qué significa as… as?
faqs.answer: Igualdad: She is as tall as her sister = tan alta como su hermana. No compares “más”, compares “igual de”.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo se escribe bigger y happier?
faqs.answer: big → bigger (consonante doble). happy → happier (y → i + er). nice → nicer (solo -r si ya termina en -e).

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 5 del curso A2?
faqs.answer: En el cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones y en la Unidad 5 del curso A2 de Linguafly: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening, speaking y writing.

content:
En la [Unidad 4](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-4-wh-questions-past-simple) preguntaste sobre el pasado. En la **Unidad 5 del curso A2** (*Comparatives*) **comparas** dos cosas o personas: ***taller than***, ***more expensive than***, ***better*** y una intro a ***as… as***.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 5 — Comparativos](/curso-a2/unit-5)  
> **Antes:** [U4 — Wh-questions](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-4-wh-questions-past-simple)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 5 (A2)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Formar comparativos cortos con ***-er*** (*taller, bigger, hotter*).
- Formar comparativos largos con ***more + adjective*** (*more interesting*).
- Usar ***than*** para completar la comparación.
- Usar irregulares ***better*** / ***worse***.
- Expresar igualdad con ***as… as*** (introducción).

Los **superlativos** (*the tallest, the most beautiful*) llegan en la [Unidad 6](/curso-a2/unit-6).

---

## 1. Dos caminos: *-er* o *more*

| Tipo de adjetivo | Comparativo | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Corto** (tall, big, hot, fast, cheap…) | adj + **-er** | taller, bigger, hotter |
| **Largo** (interesting, expensive, beautiful…) | **more** + adj | more interesting |
| Cierre | **than** | taller **than** me |

![Comparatives -er and more than A2](/blog/curso-a2/unit-5/a2-unit5-comparatives.png)

> My brother is **taller than** me.  
> This book is **more interesting than** that one.  
> Summer is **hotter than** winter.  
> My car is **more expensive than** yours.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-5/taller-than.mp3" title="🔊 My brother is taller than me"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-5/more-interesting.mp3" title="🔊 This book is more interesting than that one"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-5/hotter-than.mp3" title="🔊 Summer is hotter than winter"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-5/more-expensive.mp3" title="🔊 My car is more expensive than yours"></audio>

---

## 2. Adjetivos cortos frecuentes

| Adjetivo | Comparativo | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| tall | **taller** | Maria is taller than me. |
| short | **shorter** | Sofia is shorter than both of us. |
| big | **bigger** | Our house is bigger than grandmother's. |
| long | **longer** | She has longer hair than I do. |
| hot | **hotter** | Summer is hotter than winter. |
| cold | **colder** | Winter is colder than summer. |
| fast | **faster** | She is faster than us. / The new phone is faster. |
| light | **lighter** | The old phone is lighter than the new one. |
| new | **newer** | My phone is newer than yours. |
| quiet | **quieter** | The village is quieter than the city. |
| cheap | **cheaper** | This bag is cheaper than that one. |

---

## 3. Adjetivos largos: *more…*

| Adjetivo | Comparativo | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| interesting | **more interesting** | The city is more interesting than the village. |
| expensive | **more expensive** | The new phone is more expensive than the old one. |
| beautiful | **more beautiful** | Grandmother's garden is more beautiful than ours. |
| difficult | **more difficult** | This exercise is more difficult than the last. |
| powerful | **more powerful** | The battery is more powerful than before. |
| useful | **more useful** | It is much more useful than that one. |

> Our city is more interesting than the village.  
> This exercise is more difficult than the last.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-5/more-interesting-city.mp3" title="🔊 Our city is more interesting than the village"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-5/more-difficult.mp3" title="🔊 This exercise is more difficult than the last"></audio>

---

## 4. Irregulares: *good → better*, *bad → worse*

| Adjetivo | Comparativo | Incorrecto |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| good | **better** | *gooder* / *more good* |
| bad | **worse** | *badder* / *more bad* |

> This film is **better than** the other.  
> The new phone has a **better** camera than the old one.  
> Today the weather is **worse than** yesterday.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-5/better-than.mp3" title="🔊 This film is better than the other"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-5/better-camera.mp3" title="🔊 The new phone has a better camera"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-5/worse-than.mp3" title="🔊 Today the weather is worse than yesterday"></audio>

---

## 5. Ortografía y *as… as* (intro)

![Spelling and as as A2](/blog/curso-a2/unit-5/a2-unit5-spelling-asas.png)

### Ortografía de *-er*

| Regla | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| + **-er** | tall → taller |
| termina en **-e** → + **-r** | nice → nicer |
| consonante + **y** → **-ier** | happy → happier |
| CVC corto → doble consonante | big → **bigger**, hot → **hotter** |

### *as… as* = igualdad

| Forma | Idea | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **as** + adj + **as** | igual de… que | She is **as tall as** her sister. |

No digas *\*as taller as*. Con igualdad el adjetivo va en forma base.

> She is as tall as her sister.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-5/as-tall-as.mp3" title="🔊 She is as tall as her sister"></audio>

---

## 6. Texto modelo: Laura y sus hermanas

> My name is Laura and I have two sisters. My older sister Maria is taller than me and she has longer hair than I do. My younger sister Sofia is shorter than both of us but she is faster than us when we run. Our house is bigger than our grandmother's house but grandmother's garden is more beautiful than ours. I think our city is more interesting than the village where grandmother lives but the village is quieter than the city.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-5/reading-sisters.mp3" title="🔊 My name is Laura…"></audio>

![Comparing people places things A2](/blog/curso-a2/unit-5/a2-unit5-compare-scenes.png)

Marca: *taller / longer / shorter / faster / bigger / more beautiful / more interesting / quieter*.

---

## 7. Listening: dos móviles

> Hi! I want to tell you about my two phones. I have an old phone and a new one. The new phone is bigger than the old one but the old one is lighter than the new one. The new phone has a better camera than the old one. The battery is more powerful than before. I think the new phone is more expensive than the old one but it is much more useful than that one. Overall I prefer the new one because it is faster than my old phone.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-5/dialogue-phones.mp3" title="🔊 Hi! I want to tell you about my two phones…"></audio>

Patrones: *bigger / lighter / better / more powerful / more expensive / more useful / faster*.

---

## 8. Más modelos del curso

> My city is bigger than Valencia. Valencia is more beautiful than my city.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-5/city-valencia.mp3" title="🔊 My city is bigger than Valencia…"></audio>

> Summer is hotter than winter. Winter is colder than summer.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-5/summer-winter.mp3" title="🔊 Summer is hotter than winter…"></audio>

> Reading books is more interesting than watching films for me. Books are better because you use your imagination more.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-5/books-films.mp3" title="🔊 Reading books is more interesting…"></audio>

---

## 9. Errores frecuentes

| Incorrecto | Correcto | Por qué |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| more taller | **taller** | corto → *-er*, no *more* |
| interestinger | **more interesting** | largo → *more* |
| gooder | **better** | irregular |
| badder | **worse** | irregular |
| bigger that | bigger **than** | *than*, no *that* |
| as taller as | **as tall as** | igualdad → adjetivo base |
| more big | **bigger** | *big* es corto |

---

## 10. Mini prácticas orales

1. Compara dos personas (*taller / younger / older*).  
2. Compara dos sitios (*bigger / more beautiful / quieter*).  
3. Compara dos objetos (*more expensive / better / lighter*).  
4. Di una igualdad: *as… as*.

> My brother is taller than me.  
> This phone is more expensive than that one.  
> She is as tall as her sister.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a2/unit-5/practice-three.mp3" title="🔊 My brother is taller… This phone is more expensive… She is as tall as…"></audio>

---

## 11. Ejercicios

### Ejercicio 1 — *-er* o *more*

1. My brother is \_\_\_\_ than me. (tall)  
2. This book is \_\_\_\_ than that one. (interesting)  
3. Summer is \_\_\_\_ than winter. (hot)  
4. My car is \_\_\_\_ than yours. (expensive)  
5. She runs \_\_\_\_ than me. (fast)  
6. This exercise is \_\_\_\_ than the last. (difficult)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **taller** · 2. **more interesting** · 3. **hotter** · 4. **more expensive** · 5. **faster** · 6. **more difficult**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — *better / worse*

1. This film is \_\_\_\_ than the other. (good)  
2. Today the weather is \_\_\_\_ than yesterday. (bad)  
3. The new phone has a \_\_\_\_ camera. (good)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **better** · 2. **worse** · 3. **better**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Completa con *than*

1. Maria is taller \_\_\_\_ me.  
2. The garden is more beautiful \_\_\_\_ ours.  
3. The new phone is faster \_\_\_\_ my old phone.  
4. Books are better \_\_\_\_ films for me.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1–4. **than**
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Empareja

1. tall  
2. big  
3. interesting  
4. good  
5. bad  
6. happy  

a) bigger · b) better · c) taller · d) happier · e) worse · f) more interesting

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1 → **c** · 2 → **a** · 3 → **f** · 4 → **b** · 5 → **e** · 6 → **d**
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Completa el texto de Laura

Maria is \_\_\_\_ than me. Sofia is \_\_\_\_ than both of us but \_\_\_\_ than us when we run. Our house is \_\_\_\_ than grandmother's house. The garden is \_\_\_\_ beautiful than ours. The city is \_\_\_\_ interesting than the village. The village is \_\_\_\_ than the city.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**taller** · **shorter** · **faster** · **bigger** · **more** · **more** · **quieter**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Completa el listening (phones)

The new phone is \_\_\_\_ than the old one. The old one is \_\_\_\_ than the new one. The new phone has a \_\_\_\_ camera. The battery is \_\_\_\_ powerful than before. The new phone is \_\_\_\_ expensive but \_\_\_\_ useful. It is \_\_\_\_ than my old phone.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

**bigger** · **lighter** · **better** · **more** · **more** · **more** · **faster**
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Corrige

1. *She is more taller than me.*  
2. *This book is interestinger.*  
3. *This film is gooder than that one.*  
4. *My car is more expensive that yours.*  
5. *She is as taller as her sister.*  
6. *This box is more big than that.*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. She is **taller** than me.  
2. This book is **more interesting**.  
3. This film is **better** than that one.  
4. My car is more expensive **than** yours.  
5. She is **as tall as** her sister.  
6. This box is **bigger** than that.
</details>

### Ejercicio 8 — *as… as*

1. She is \_\_\_\_ tall \_\_\_\_ her sister.  
2. This bag is not \_\_\_\_ cheap \_\_\_\_ that one.  
3. Incorrecto: as more expensive as → Correcto: ____

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **as** · **as**  
2. **as** · **as**  
3. **as expensive as** / o usa *more expensive than*
</details>

### Ejercicio 9 — Traduce

1. Mi hermano es más alto que yo.  
2. Este libro es más interesante que ese.  
3. El verano es más caluroso que el invierno.  
4. Mi coche es más caro que el tuyo.  
5. Esta película es mejor que la otra.  
6. Hoy el tiempo está peor que ayer.  
7. Ella es tan alta como su hermana.  
8. El pueblo es más tranquilo que la ciudad.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. My brother is taller than me.  
2. This book is more interesting than that one.  
3. Summer is hotter than winter.  
4. My car is more expensive than yours.  
5. This film is better than the other.  
6. Today the weather is worse than yesterday.  
7. She is as tall as her sister.  
8. The village is quieter than the city.
</details>

### Ejercicio 10 — Escribe tus comparaciones

Escribe 8–12 frases. Incluye:

- 3 × *-er* + *than*  
- 2 × *more… than*  
- 1 × *better* o *worse*  
- 1 × *as… as*

**Modelo:** el texto de Laura (sección 6) o el de los móviles (sección 7).

---

## 12. Plan de estudio (25–30 minutos)

1. **5 min** — Repasa *-er* vs *more* y *better/worse*.  
2. **8 min** — Ejercicios 1–7.  
3. **7 min** — Escucha a Laura y los móviles; marca cada comparativo.  
4. **5–8 min** — Escribe y graba 8 comparaciones personales.

### Checklist

- [ ] Uso *-er* con adjetivos cortos  
- [ ] Uso *more* con adjetivos largos  
- [ ] Cierro con *than*  
- [ ] Recuerdo *better / worse*  
- [ ] Sé formar *as… as* para igualdad

---

## 13. Consejos y siguiente paso

1. Pregunta rápida: ¿1 sílaba? → prueba *-er*. ¿3+ sílabas? → *more*.  
2. Di en voz alta pares: *big–bigger, hot–hotter, happy–happier*.  
3. Compara tu ciudad con otra (como en los modelos del curso).  
4. Practica en el [cuaderno de ejercicios de la Unidad 5](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-5-comparativos-er-more-than-ejercicios-soluciones) y en la [Unidad 5 del curso A2](/curso-a2/unit-5).

La **Unidad 6** entra en **superlativos**: *the tallest*, *the most beautiful*, *in / of*.

---

## Resumen rápido

| Caso | Forma |
| :--- | :--- |
| Corto | adj + **-er** + than |
| Largo | **more** + adj + than |
| good / bad | **better** / **worse** |
| Igualdad | **as** + adj + **as** |
| Ortografía | bigger · hotter · happier · nicer |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A2

En la **Unidad 6** estudiarás **Superlatives**: *-est*, *the most*, y el uso de *in* / *of*.

Guía dedicada y curso:

- [Unidad 6 — Superlativos](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-6-superlativos-est-the-most)
- [Unidad 6 — Superlativos](/curso-a2/unit-6)

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 5 A2 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a2/unidad-5-comparativos-er-more-than-ejercicios-soluciones)
- [Unidad 5 — Comparativos](/curso-a2/unit-5)

Guías relacionadas:

- [Gramática inglesa: guía por niveles](/blog/gramatica/gramatica-inglesa-guia)
- [Gramática inglesa B1](/blog/gramatica/gramatica-ingles-b1-guia)
