title: Present Simple Negativa y Preguntas (A1): don’t y Do you…?
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 14 del curso A1: Present Simple con I/you/we/they en negativa (don't) y preguntas (Do you…?), respuestas cortas Yes, I do / No, I don't, y vocabulario de ocio y casa. Con audios, esquemas y ejercicios.
description: Aprende la negativa don't y las preguntas Do you…? del Present Simple con I, you, we, they. Guía Unidad 14 A1 con ocio, tareas domésticas, audios y ejercicios.
alt: Esquema de don't en Present Simple inglés nivel A1
keywords: yes i do no i don't

faqs.question: ¿Cómo se forma la negativa del Present Simple con I/you/we/they?
faqs.answer: Sujeto + don't + verbo (sin -s): I don't like coffee. We don't watch TV. They don't play football. Don't = do not.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo hago preguntas con Do you…?
faqs.answer: Do + sujeto (you/we/they) + verbo…? Do you cook? Do they do the housework? Respuestas cortas: Yes, I do. / No, I don't.

faqs.question: ¿Por qué no digo I don't likes?
faqs.answer: Tras don't el verbo va en forma base, sin -s: I don't like (no *likes*). La -s es solo para he/she/it en afirmativa (Unidad 15).

faqs.question: ¿Qué vocabulario practico en la Unidad 14?
faqs.answer: Ocio y casa: watch TV, cook, play football, do the housework, like music, read books, meet friends, listen to music.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 14 del curso A1?
faqs.answer: En la Unidad 14 del curso A1 de Linguafly practicarás don't y Do you…? con ejercicios de gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y speaking.

content:
Ya sabes contar tu día con *First, Then, After that*. En la **Unidad 14 del curso A1** (*Present Simple: I, You, We, They*) aprendes a decir **qué no haces** y a **preguntar hábitos** con *don't* y *Do you…?*.

Esta guía cubre la **negativa**, las **preguntas**, las **respuestas cortas** (*Yes, I do / No, I don't*) y vocabulario de **ocio y tareas domésticas**. Incluye **audios**, **esquemas** y **ejercicios**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 14 — Present Simple: I, you, we, they](/curso-a1/unit-14)  
> **Cuaderno de ejercicios (con soluciones):** [Ejercicios Unidad 14 A1](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-14-present-simple-dont-do-you-ejercicios-soluciones)  
> **Repaso previo:** [Unidad 13 — Rutina diaria](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-13-rutina-diaria) · [Unidad 5 — Present Simple](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-5-present-simple-rutinas)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 14 (A1)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Formar la **negativa** con *don't* (*I don't like…*).
- Hacer **preguntas** con *Do you / we / they…?*.
- Responder con ***Yes, I do*** / ***No, I don't***.
- Hablar de **ocio** y **tareas de casa** en Present Simple.

---

## 1. Vocabulario: ocio y tareas domésticas

| Inglés | Español | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **watch TV** | ver la tele | I watch TV in the evening. |
| **cook** | cocinar | Do you cook? |
| **play football** | jugar al fútbol | We don't play football. |
| **play tennis** | jugar al tenis | Do you play tennis? |
| **do the housework** | hacer las tareas de casa | They do the housework. |
| **like** | gustar | Do you like music? |
| **read (books)** | leer | I read books. |
| **listen to music** | escuchar música | I like listening to music. |
| **meet friends** | quedar con amigos | On the weekend I meet my friends. |
| **stay at home** | quedarse en casa | I stay at home on Sunday. |
| **prefer** | preferir | I prefer tea. |
| **eat** | comer | They don't eat meat. |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-14/watch-tv.mp3" title="🔊 Watch TV"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-14/cook.mp3" title="🔊 Cook"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-14/play-football.mp3" title="🔊 Play football"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-14/do-the-housework.mp3" title="🔊 Do the housework"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-14/like-music.mp3" title="🔊 Like music"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-14/read-books.mp3" title="🔊 Read books"></audio>

![Vocabulario de ocio y tareas domésticas en inglés A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-14/a1-unit14-vocab.png)

### Tips de uso

- **do the housework** = las tareas en general (limpiar, fregar…).  
- **watch TV** (sin *the* en muchos contextos A1).  
- **listen to** music (hace falta *to*).  
- **play** + deporte: *play football / tennis*.

---

## 2. Negativa: *don't*

Con **I / you / we / they** la negativa se forma así:

```
Sujeto + don't + verbo (forma base)
```

| Afirmativa | Negativa |
| :--- | :--- |
| I like coffee. | I **don't** like coffee. |
| We watch TV. | We **don't** watch TV. |
| They play football. | They **don't** play football. |
| You cook. | You **don't** cook. |

![Esquema de don't en Present Simple A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-14/a1-unit14-dont.png)

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-14/i-dont-like-coffee.mp3" title="🔊 I don't like coffee"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-14/we-dont-watch-tv.mp3" title="🔊 We don't watch TV in the morning"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-14/we-dont-play-football.mp3" title="🔊 We don't play football"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-14/i-dont-like-getting-up.mp3" title="🔊 I don't like getting up early"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-14/they-dont-eat-meat.mp3" title="🔊 They don't eat meat"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-14/i-dont-watch-tv.mp3" title="🔊 No, I don't watch TV in the morning"></audio>

### Reglas de oro

1. ***don't* = *do not*** (forma contraída, la más habitual).  
2. Tras *don't* el verbo **no lleva -s**: *I don't like* (no *likes*).  
3. *don't* es para **I / you / we / they**. (*doesn't* es para he/she/it → Unidad 15.)

### Más ejemplos

| Español | Inglés |
| :--- | :--- |
| No me gusta levantarme temprano. | I **don't** like getting up early. |
| No vemos la tele por la mañana. | We **don't** watch TV in the morning. |
| No comen carne. | They **don't** eat meat. |
| No hago deporte. | I **don't** play sport. |

---

## 3. Preguntas: *Do you…?*

```
Do + sujeto + verbo (forma base) + …?
```

| Pregunta | Traducción |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Do you** like coffee? | ¿Te gusta el café? |
| **Do you** cook? | ¿Cocinas? |
| **Do they** do the housework? | ¿Hacen las tareas de casa? |
| **Do we** need milk? | ¿Necesitamos leche? |

![Esquema de Do you en Present Simple A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-14/a1-unit14-do-you.png)

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-14/do-you-like-coffee.mp3" title="🔊 Do you like coffee? Yes, I do"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-14/do-you-cook.mp3" title="🔊 Do you cook? No, I don't"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-14/do-they-do-housework.mp3" title="🔊 Do they do the housework? Yes, they do"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-14/do-you-read-books.mp3" title="🔊 Do you read books? Yes, I do"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-14/do-you-play-tennis.mp3" title="🔊 Do you play tennis? No, I don't"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-14/do-you-like-music.mp3" title="🔊 Do you like music?"></audio>

### Respuestas cortas

| Afirmativa | Negativa |
| :--- | :--- |
| Yes, I **do**. | No, I **don't**. |
| Yes, we **do**. | No, we **don't**. |
| Yes, they **do**. | No, they **don't**. |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-14/yes-i-do.mp3" title="🔊 Yes, I do"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-14/no-i-dont.mp3" title="🔊 No, I don't"></audio>

**Importante:** en la respuesta corta **no repitas el verbo principal**:  
✅ Yes, I do. · ❌ Yes, I like. (posible en contexto largo, pero la forma corta es *do/don't*)

---

## 4. Cuadro completo (I / you / we / they)

| Tipo | Estructura | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Afirmativa | sujeto + verbo | I **like** music. |
| Negativa | sujeto + **don't** + verbo | I **don't like** coffee. |
| Pregunta | **Do** + sujeto + verbo…? | **Do you** like music? |
| Respuesta | Yes, … **do**. / No, … **don't**. | Yes, I **do**. |

### Combina con Unidades 10–13

| Tema | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| Hora | Do you get up at seven? No, I don't. |
| Días | Do you work on Saturdays? Yes, I do. |
| Rutina | I don't have a shower in the evening. |
| Secuencia | First I wake up. Then I don't watch TV — I have breakfast. |

---

## 5. Texto modelo (del curso)

### Sara's habits

> My name is Sara. I **don't** like getting up early. I get up at eight. I **don't** watch TV in the morning. I have breakfast and go to work. In the evening I cook dinner. I **don't** eat in restaurants often. I like reading and listening to music. I **don't** play sport. On the weekend I meet my friends or stay at home.

### Tu plantilla en 8 frases

1. I like \_\_\_\_.  
2. I don't like \_\_\_\_.  
3. I don't \_\_\_\_ in the morning.  
4. Do you \_\_\_\_? — Yes, I do. / No, I don't.  
5. We don't \_\_\_\_.  
6. On the weekend I \_\_\_\_.  
7. I don't \_\_\_\_ often.  
8. They do / don't \_\_\_\_.

---

## 6. Preguntas útiles

| Pregunta | Respuestas |
| :--- | :--- |
| Do you like coffee? | Yes, I do. / No, I don't. |
| Do you cook? | Yes, I do. / No, I don't. |
| Do you watch TV in the morning? | No, I don't. |
| Do you do the housework? | Yes, I do. |
| Do you play football? | No, I don't. I prefer tennis. |
| Do they like music? | Yes, they do. |

---

## 7. Errores típicos de hispanohablantes

| ❌ Incorrecto | ✅ Correcto | Explicación |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *I no like coffee* | *I **don't** like coffee* | Negativa con *don't* |
| *I don't likes coffee* | *I don't **like** coffee* | Sin -s tras *don't* |
| *Do you likes music?* | *Do you **like** music?* | Forma base tras *Do* |
| *Yes, I like* (respuesta corta) | *Yes, I **do*** | Respuesta corta con *do* |
| *Does you cook?* | ***Do** you cook?* | you → *Do*, no *Does* |
| *I don't watching TV* | *I don't **watch** TV* | No -ing tras *don't* |
| *Do you do housework?* | *Do you do **the** housework?* | Suele llevar *the* |

---

## 8. Pronunciación de *don't* y *Do you*

| Forma | Tip A1 |
| :--- | :--- |
| **don't** | Suena como *dont* (una sílaba). |
| **Do you** | En habla rápida: *d'you* /də ju/. Practica claro primero: *Do you…?* |
| **Yes, I do** | Acentúa *do*. |
| **No, I don't** | Acentúa *don't*. |

Escucha los audios del artículo y repite en voz alta. Empieza despacio: *Do you like coffee?* → *No, I don't.* Luego acelera un poco, pero sin saltarte *don't* o *do*.

---

## 8b. Mini-diálogos para memorizar

Usa estos pares como plantilla. Cambia el verbo y el objeto:

> **A:** Do you like tea?  
> **B:** Yes, I do. And you?  
> **A:** No, I don't. I prefer coffee.

> **A:** Do you cook in the evening?  
> **B:** Yes, I do. I cook dinner.  
> **A:** Do you do the housework too?  
> **B:** Yes, I do. On Saturdays.

> **A:** Do they play football?  
> **B:** No, they don't. They play tennis.  
> **A:** Nice! Do they watch TV after that?  
> **B:** No, they don't. They read books.

Idea de práctica: grábate haciendo las preguntas y responde tú mismo. Así entrenas *Do you…?* y *Yes, I do / No, I don't* sin depender de otra persona.

---

## 8c. Afirmativa, negativa y pregunta juntas

Para fijar la estructura, escribe siempre el mismo verbo en tres formas:

| Afirmativa | Negativa | Pregunta |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| I like music. | I don't like music. | Do you like music? |
| We watch TV. | We don't watch TV. | Do you watch TV? |
| They cook dinner. | They don't cook dinner. | Do they cook dinner? |
| I play tennis. | I don't play tennis. | Do you play tennis? |
| We read books. | We don't read books. | Do you read books? |

Cuando veas una frase afirmativa en un texto o en una app, intenta convertirla a negativa y a pregunta. Ese “triple salto” es el mejor ejercicio de esta unidad.

---

## 9. Ejercicios prácticos (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — Completa con *don't* o el verbo en forma base

1. I \_\_\_\_ like coffee. (don't / doesn't)  
2. We don't \_\_\_\_ TV in the morning. (watch / watches)  
3. They \_\_\_\_ play football. (don't)  
4. I don't \_\_\_\_ getting up early. (like)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **don't**  
2. **watch**  
3. **don't**  
4. **like**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Completa con *Do* y respuestas cortas

1. \_\_\_\_ you like music? — Yes, I \_\_\_\_.  
2. \_\_\_\_ you cook? — No, I \_\_\_\_.  
3. \_\_\_\_ they do the housework? — Yes, they \_\_\_\_.  
4. \_\_\_\_ you play tennis? — No, I \_\_\_\_.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Do** / **do**  
2. **Do** / **don't**  
3. **Do** / **do**  
4. **Do** / **don't**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Traduce al inglés

1. No me gusta el café.  
2. ¿Cocinas? — No.  
3. No vemos la tele por la mañana.  
4. ¿Hacen las tareas de casa? — Sí.  
5. No juego al fútbol.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I don't like coffee.  
2. Do you cook? — No, I don't.  
3. We don't watch TV in the morning.  
4. Do they do the housework? — Yes, they do.  
5. I don't play football.
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Corrige el error

1. *I no like coffee.*  
2. *I don't likes music.*  
3. *Does you cook?*  
4. *Do you watches TV?*  
5. *Yes, I like.* (respuesta corta a *Do you like tea?*)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I **don't** like coffee.  
2. I don't **like** music.  
3. **Do** you cook?  
4. Do you **watch** TV?  
5. Yes, I **do**.
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Elige la opción correcta

1. I \_\_\_\_ like getting up early. (don't / doesn't)  
2. \_\_\_\_ you play sport? (Do / Does)  
3. We don't \_\_\_\_ TV after dinner. (watch / watches)  
4. Do they like music? — Yes, they \_\_\_\_. (do / don't)  
5. She \_\_\_\_ cook. *(pista: esto es Unidad 15; aquí solo recuerda que NO usamos doesn't con you)*  

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **don't**  
2. **Do**  
3. **watch**  
4. **do**  
5. En U14 no trabajamos *she*; la forma correcta será *doesn't* en la [Unidad 15](/curso-a1/unit-15). Con *you* siempre: *don't / Do*.
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Ordena las palabras

1. don't / I / coffee / like  
2. you / Do / cook  
3. don't / We / football / play  
4. do / Yes / I

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I don't like coffee.  
2. Do you cook?  
3. We don't play football.  
4. Yes, I do.
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Elige la opción correcta

1. I (don't / doesn't) watch TV in the morning.  
2. (Do / Does) you like music?  
3. They (don't play / don't plays) tennis.  
4. Do you cook? — Yes, I (do / cook).

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **don't**  
2. **Do**  
3. **don't play**  
4. **do**
</details>

### Ejercicio 7 — Escribe 4 frases sobre ti

2 afirmativas + 2 con *don't* (ocio o casa).

**Modelo:**

> I like music. I read books. I don't play football. I don't watch TV in the morning.

### Ejercicio 8 — Mini diálogo

Escribe 4 líneas: pregunta *Do you…?*, respuesta corta y una frase extra.

**Modelo:**

> A: Do you play tennis?  
> B: No, I don't. I prefer football.  
> A: Do you like music?  
> B: Yes, I do.

### Ejercicio 9 — Transforma a negativa

1. I like coffee. → \_\_\_\_  
2. We watch TV. → \_\_\_\_  
3. They play football. → \_\_\_\_  
4. You cook every day. → \_\_\_\_

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I **don't** like coffee.  
2. We **don't** watch TV.  
3. They **don't** play football.  
4. You **don't** cook every day.
</details>

### Ejercicio 10 — Mini redacción (80–100 palabras)

Escribe sobre tus hábitos: qué te gusta, qué no haces, y 2 preguntas que harías a un amigo con *Do you…?*.

**Modelo:**

> I like reading and listening to music. I don't like getting up early. I don't watch TV in the morning. In the evening I cook dinner. I don't eat in restaurants often. On the weekend I meet my friends or stay at home. Do you cook? Do you play sport?

---

## 10. Diálogo modelo

> **Tom:** Do you like coffee?  
> **Sara:** No, I don't. I prefer tea.  
> **Tom:** Do you cook?  
> **Sara:** Yes, I do. In the evening I cook dinner.  
> **Tom:** Do you watch TV in the morning?  
> **Sara:** No, I don't. I have breakfast and go to work.  
> **Tom:** Do you play football?  
> **Sara:** No, I don't. I don't play sport. I like reading.  
> **Tom:** Nice! Do you do the housework on Saturdays?  
> **Sara:** Yes, I do.

---

## 11. Plan de práctica (15 minutos)

1. **3 min** — Repite: *I don't… / We don't… / They don't…*  
2. **4 min** — Haz 6 preguntas *Do you…?* en voz alta y respóndelas.  
3. **4 min** — Escucha los audios y repite.  
4. **4 min** — Escribe 6 frases: 3 con *don't* y 3 preguntas.

### Checklist

- [ ] Sé formar *don't* + verbo base.  
- [ ] Sé preguntar con *Do you…?*.  
- [ ] Uso *Yes, I do / No, I don't*.  
- [ ] No mezclo *does* con *you*.

---

## 12. Consejos para practicar

1. **Haz una lista** de 5 cosas que no haces: *I don't…*  
2. **Entrevista** a alguien: *Do you like…? Do you cook…?*  
3. **Contrasta** afirmativa vs negativa: *I like tea. I don't like coffee.*  
4. Prepárate para la [Unidad 15](/curso-a1/unit-15): *doesn't / Does he…?*  
5. Practica en la [Unidad 14 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-14) o el [cuaderno con soluciones](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-14-present-simple-dont-do-you-ejercicios-soluciones).

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Lo esencial |
| :--- | :--- |
| Negativa | I/you/we/they + **don't** + verbo |
| Pregunta | **Do** + you/we/they + verbo…? |
| Respuestas | Yes, I **do**. / No, I **don't**. |
| Vocabulario | watch TV, cook, play, do the housework, like, read |
| Atención | Tras *don't/Do* → verbo **sin -s** |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

En la **Unidad 15** aprenderás la 3.ª persona: ***doesn't*** y ***Does he/she…?***.

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 14 A1 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-14-present-simple-dont-do-you-ejercicios-soluciones)

Guía dedicada:

- [Unidad 15 — Present Simple: doesn't y Does he/she…?](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-15-present-simple-doesnt-does)

Guías relacionadas:

- [Gramática inglesa: guía por niveles](/blog/gramatica/gramatica-inglesa-guia)

---

faqs.question: ¿Cómo se forma la negativa del Present Simple con he/she/it?
faqs.answer: Sujeto + doesn't + verbo (sin -s): He doesn't like coffee. She doesn't study. It doesn't eat meat. Doesn't = does not.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo hago preguntas con Does he/she/it…?

content:
En la [Unidad 14](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-14-present-simple-dont-do-you) aprendiste *don't* y *Do you…?* con **I, you, we, they**. En la **Unidad 15 del curso A1** (*Present Simple: He, She, It*) pasas a la **3.ª persona**: *doesn't* y *Does he/she/it…?*. Es el complemento natural de la unidad anterior.

Esta guía cubre la **negativa**, las **preguntas**, las **respuestas cortas**, la **ortografía** (*goes, watches, studies, has*) y vocabulario de **animales** y **rutinas profesionales**. Incluye **audios**, **esquemas** y **ejercicios**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 15 — Present Simple: He, She, It](/curso-a1/unit-15)  
> **Cuaderno de ejercicios (con soluciones):** [Ejercicios Unidad 15 A1](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-15-present-simple-doesnt-does-ejercicios-soluciones)  
> **Repaso previo:** [Unidad 14 — don't y Do you](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-14-present-simple-dont-do-you) · [Unidad 5 — Present Simple](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-5-present-simple-rutinas)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 15 (A1)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Formar la **negativa** con *doesn't* (*He doesn't like…*).
- Hacer **preguntas** con *Does he / she / it…?*.
- Responder con ***Yes, he does*** / ***No, she doesn't***.
- Aplicar la **-s / -es / -ies** en afirmativa (y quitarla tras *does/doesn't*).
- Hablar de **hábitos de animales** y **rutinas de trabajo**.

---

## 1. Vocabulario: animales y rutinas (he/she/it)

| Inglés | Español | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **wake up / wakes up** | despertarse | She wakes up at seven. |
| **go / goes** | ir | She goes to work at nine. |
| **write / writes** | escribir | He writes reports every week. |
| **teach / teaches** | enseñar | The teacher teaches English. |
| **help patients** | ayudar a pacientes | The doctor helps patients. |
| **bark / barks** | ladrar | The dog barks. |
| **meow / meows** | maullar | The cat meows. |
| **fly / flies** | volar | The bird flies in the sky. |
| **swim / swims** | nadar | The fish swims. |
| **hunt** | cazar | The owl hunts at night. |
| **eat grass** | comer hierba | The cow eats grass. |
| **have / has breakfast** | desayunar | She has breakfast at eight. |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-15/wakes-up.mp3" title="🔊 Wakes up"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-15/writes-reports.mp3" title="🔊 Writes reports"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-15/barks.mp3" title="🔊 Barks"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-15/meows.mp3" title="🔊 Meows"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-15/flies.mp3" title="🔊 Flies"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-15/swims.mp3" title="🔊 Swims"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-15/teaches.mp3" title="🔊 Teaches"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-15/helps-patients.mp3" title="🔊 Helps patients"></audio>

![Vocabulario de hábitos he/she/it y animales en inglés A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-15/a1-unit15-vocab.png)

### Tips de uso

- Con **he/she/it** el verbo de la afirmativa lleva **-s** (o **-es / -ies**).  
- **have** → **has** (irregular en 3.ª persona).  
- Animales = *it*: *The dog barks. It doesn't like cats.*  
- Nombres propios = he/she: *Maria works. Does Maria cook?*

---

## 2. Negativa: *doesn't*

Con **he / she / it** la negativa se forma así:

```
Sujeto + doesn't + verbo (forma base)
```

| Afirmativa | Negativa |
| :--- | :--- |
| He likes coffee. | He **doesn't** like coffee. |
| She studies English. | She **doesn't** study English. |
| It eats meat. | It **doesn't** eat meat. |
| She goes to work at nine. | She **doesn't** go to work at nine. |
| He plays football. | He **doesn't** play football. |

**Regla clave:** tras *doesn't* el verbo **pierde la -s**. No digas *He doesn't likes*.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-15/he-doesnt-like.mp3" title="🔊 He doesn't like getting up early"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-15/she-doesnt-study.mp3" title="🔊 She doesn't study English"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-15/it-doesnt-eat-meat.mp3" title="🔊 It doesn't eat meat"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-15/the-cow-doesnt-eat.mp3" title="🔊 The cow doesn't eat meat"></audio>

![Esquema de doesn't con he she it en Present Simple A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-15/a1-unit15-doesnt.png)

### *don't* vs *doesn't* (mapa rápido)

| Sujeto | Negativa |
| :--- | :--- |
| I / you / we / they | **don't** + verbo |
| he / she / it | **doesn't** + verbo |

> I don't like coffee.  
> He **doesn't** like coffee.  
> We don't watch TV.  
> She **doesn't** watch TV.

---

## 3. Preguntas: *Does he / she / it…?*

```
Does + he/she/it + verbo (forma base)…?
```

| Pregunta | Significado |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Does** he play football? | ¿Juega al fútbol? |
| **Does** she cook? | ¿Cocina? |
| **Does** the cat like milk? | ¿Al gato le gusta la leche? |
| **Does** Maria work on Sunday? | ¿María trabaja el domingo? |
| **Does** your brother study? | ¿Tu hermano estudia? |

Tras *Does* el verbo va **sin -s**: *Does she like…?* (no *likes*).

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-15/does-he-play.mp3" title="🔊 Does he play football?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-15/does-she-cook.mp3" title="🔊 Does she cook?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-15/does-the-cat-like.mp3" title="🔊 Does the cat like milk?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-15/does-maria-work.mp3" title="🔊 Does Maria work on Sunday?"></audio>

![Esquema de Does he she it en Present Simple A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-15/a1-unit15-does-he.png)

### *Do* vs *Does*

| Sujeto | Pregunta |
| :--- | :--- |
| I / you / we / they | **Do** + sujeto + verbo…? |
| he / she / it | **Does** + sujeto + verbo…? |

> Do you cook?  
> **Does** she cook?  
> Do they like music?  
> **Does** he like music?

---

## 4. Respuestas cortas

| Pregunta | Sí | No |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Does he play football? | Yes, he **does**. | No, he **doesn't**. |
| Does she cook? | Yes, she **does**. | No, she **doesn't**. |
| Does it like milk? | Yes, it **does**. | No, it **doesn't**. |

No respondas solo *Yes* o *Yes, she likes*. En A1 la respuesta corta estándar es *Yes, she does* / *No, she doesn't*.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-15/yes-he-does.mp3" title="🔊 Yes, he does"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-15/no-she-doesnt.mp3" title="🔊 No, she doesn't"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-15/yes-it-does.mp3" title="🔊 Yes, it does"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-15/she-goes-to-work.mp3" title="🔊 She goes to work at nine"></audio>

---

## 5. Ortografía de la 3.ª persona (afirmativa)

En afirmativa, he/she/it añaden terminación. En negativa y pregunta **esa -s desaparece** porque ya está en *does/doesn't*.

| Regla | Infinitivo → 3.ª pers. | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| + **-s** (la mayoría) | work → works, like → likes | He works. |
| + **-es** (-ch, -sh, -ss, -x, -o) | watch → watches, go → goes | She watches TV. She goes. |
| **-y** tras consonante → **-ies** | study → studies, fly → flies | He studies. The bird flies. |
| Irregular | have → **has** | She has breakfast. |

### Triple salto (muy útil)

| Afirmativa | Negativa | Pregunta |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| She likes tea. | She doesn't like tea. | Does she like tea? |
| He goes to work. | He doesn't go to work. | Does he go to work? |
| It eats meat. | It doesn't eat meat. | Does it eat meat? |
| She watches TV. | She doesn't watch TV. | Does she watch TV? |
| He studies English. | He doesn't study English. | Does he study English? |

---

## 6. Más ejemplos en contexto

### Personas y trabajo

> My sister is a nurse. She **wakes up** at six. She **goes** to the hospital. She **helps** patients. She **doesn't** work on Sunday.  
> **Does** she work on Saturday? — Yes, she **does**.

> Tom is an engineer. He **writes** reports every week. He **doesn't** teach.  
> **Does** he design buildings? — Yes, he **does**.

### Animales

> The dog **barks** when it sees a stranger. It **doesn't** meow.  
> The cat **meows**. **Does** the cat like milk? — Yes, it **does**.  
> The cow **doesn't** eat meat. It **eats** grass.  
> The bird **flies**. The fish **swims**. The owl **hunts** at night.

### Comparación U14 vs U15

> I don't like coffee. / He **doesn't** like coffee.  
> Do you cook? / **Does** she cook?  
> Yes, I do. / Yes, she **does**.  
> No, I don't. / No, he **doesn't**.

---

## 7. Errores típicos de hispanohablantes

| ❌ Incorrecto | ✅ Correcto | Explicación |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *He don't like coffee* | *He **doesn't** like coffee* | he → *doesn't* |
| *She doesn't likes tea* | *She doesn't **like** tea* | Sin -s tras *doesn't* |
| *Does she likes music?* | *Does she **like** music?* | Forma base tras *Does* |
| *Do he play football?* | ***Does** he play football?* | he → *Does* |
| *Yes, she like* | *Yes, she **does*** | Respuesta corta con *does* |
| *He go to work* | *He **goes** to work* | Afirmativa: -s/-es |
| *She study English* | *She **studies** English* | study → studies |

---

## 8. Pronunciación de *doesn't* y *Does he*

| Forma | Tip A1 |
| :--- | :--- |
| **doesn't** | Dos sílabas: *DUZ-nt*. |
| **Does he** | *Does* suena como *duz*. |
| **Yes, he does** | Acentúa *does*. |
| **No, she doesn't** | Acentúa *doesn't*. |

Practica en voz alta: *Does she cook?* → *No, she doesn't.* Empieza despacio y luego un poco más rápido, sin saltarte el auxiliar. Escucha los audios del artículo y repite dos veces cada frase.

### Ortografía vs sonido (nota rápida)

En afirmativa, la *-s* de *likes / goes / watches* a veces suena /s/, /z/ o /ɪz/. No hace falta memorizar todas las reglas aún: imita el audio. Lo importante en esta unidad es **cuándo** usas *-s* (afirmativa he/she/it) y **cuándo no** (tras *does/doesn't*).

---

## 8b. Mini-diálogos para memorizar

> **A:** Does he like coffee?  
> **B:** No, he doesn't. He prefers tea.  
> **A:** Does he cook?  
> **B:** Yes, he does. In the evening he cooks dinner.

> **A:** Does your sister work in a hospital?  
> **B:** Yes, she does. She is a nurse.  
> **A:** Does she work on Sunday?  
> **B:** No, she doesn't.

> **A:** Does the cat like milk?  
> **B:** Yes, it does.  
> **A:** Does the dog like cats?  
> **B:** No, it doesn't. It barks a lot!

Cambia el verbo y el sujeto: *Does Maria…? Does your brother…? Does the bird…?*

---

## 8c. Tabla resumen U14 + U15

| | I / you / we / they | he / she / it |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Afirmativa | I like tea. | He like**s** tea. |
| Negativa | I **don't** like tea. | He **doesn't** like tea. |
| Pregunta | **Do** you like tea? | **Does** he like tea? |
| Sí | Yes, I **do**. | Yes, he **does**. |
| No | No, I **don't**. | No, he **doesn't**. |

Cuando dudes, pregunta: ¿el sujeto es *he/she/it*? → *does / doesn't* + verbo base. Si no → *do / don't*.

### Frases para copiar y personalizar

1. He doesn't like \_\_\_\_.  
2. She doesn't \_\_\_\_ on Sunday.  
3. Does he \_\_\_\_? — Yes, he does.  
4. Does she \_\_\_\_? — No, she doesn't.  
5. The dog barks. It doesn't \_\_\_\_.  
6. My sister wakes up at \_\_\_\_. She goes to \_\_\_\_.

Rellena con tu vida real: así el Present Simple deja de ser “teoría” y se convierte en frases que sí dirías.

---

## 9. Ejercicios prácticos (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — Completa con *doesn't* o el verbo base

1. He \_\_\_\_ like getting up early.  
2. She doesn't \_\_\_\_ English. (study)  
3. It \_\_\_\_ eat meat.  
4. Maria doesn't \_\_\_\_ on Sunday. (work)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **doesn't**  
2. **study**  
3. **doesn't**  
4. **work**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Completa con *Does* y respuestas cortas

1. \_\_\_\_ he play football? — Yes, he \_\_\_\_.  
2. \_\_\_\_ she cook? — No, she \_\_\_\_.  
3. \_\_\_\_ the cat like milk? — Yes, it \_\_\_\_.  
4. \_\_\_\_ Maria work on Sunday? — No, she \_\_\_\_.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Does** / **does**  
2. **Does** / **doesn't**  
3. **Does** / **does**  
4. **Does** / **doesn't**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Traduce al inglés

1. Él no se levanta temprano.  
2. ¿Cocina ella? — Sí.  
3. El gato no come carne.  
4. ¿Ladra el perro? — Sí.  
5. Ella va al trabajo a las nueve.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. He doesn't get up early. / He doesn't like getting up early.  
2. Does she cook? — Yes, she does.  
3. The cat doesn't eat meat.  
4. Does the dog bark? — Yes, it does.  
5. She goes to work at nine.
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Corrige el error

1. *He don't like coffee.*  
2. *She doesn't likes music.*  
3. *Do he play football?*  
4. *Does she watches TV?*  
5. *Yes, she like.* (respuesta a *Does she like tea?*)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. He **doesn't** like coffee.  
2. She doesn't **like** music.  
3. **Does** he play football?  
4. Does she **watch** TV?  
5. Yes, she **does**.
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Afirmativa: elige la forma correcta

1. She \_\_\_\_ to work at nine. (go / goes)  
2. He \_\_\_\_ reports every week. (write / writes)  
3. The bird \_\_\_\_ in the sky. (fly / flies)  
4. She \_\_\_\_ breakfast at eight. (have / has)  
5. He \_\_\_\_ TV every night. (watch / watches)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **goes**  
2. **writes**  
3. **flies**  
4. **has**  
5. **watches**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Escribe sobre alguien

Escribe 5–7 frases sobre un amigo, familiar o mascota: qué hace, qué no hace, y 2 preguntas con *Does…?*.

**Modelo:**

> My brother wakes up at seven. He goes to work at eight. He writes emails every day. He doesn't cook. He doesn't like getting up early. Does he play football? Yes, he does. Does he study English? No, he doesn't.

---

## 10. Diálogo modelo

> **Ana:** Does Tom like coffee?  
> **Luis:** No, he doesn't. He prefers tea.  
> **Ana:** Does he cook?  
> **Luis:** Yes, he does. In the evening he cooks dinner.  
> **Ana:** Does he watch TV in the morning?  
> **Luis:** No, he doesn't. He goes to work early.  
> **Ana:** And your cat? Does it like milk?  
> **Luis:** Yes, it does. It doesn't eat meat, though — wait, it does!  
> **Ana:** Nice! Does Maria work on Sunday?  
> **Luis:** No, she doesn't. She rests at home.

---

## 11. Plan de práctica (15 minutos)

1. **3 min** — Repite: *He doesn't… / She doesn't… / It doesn't…*  
2. **4 min** — Haz 6 preguntas *Does he/she/it…?* y respóndelas.  
3. **4 min** — Escucha los audios y repite.  
4. **4 min** — Escribe el “triple salto” con 4 verbos (*like, go, watch, study*).

### Checklist

- [ ] Sé formar *doesn't* + verbo base.  
- [ ] Sé preguntar con *Does he/she/it…?*.  
- [ ] Uso *Yes, he does / No, she doesn't*.  
- [ ] No mezclo *don't* con *he/she/it*.  
- [ ] Tras *does/doesn't* no añado -s al verbo.

---

## 12. Consejos para practicar

1. **Elige una persona** (hermano, compañero) y escribe 5 hábitos con *-s* y 3 con *doesn't*.  
2. **Pregunta sobre mascotas:** *Does your dog bark? Does your cat sleep a lot?*  
3. **Contrasta U14 y U15:** *I don't…* vs *He doesn't…*; *Do you…?* vs *Does she…?*.  
4. Repasa la [Unidad 14](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-14-present-simple-dont-do-you) si dudas con *don't/Do*.  
5. Practica en la [Unidad 15 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-15) o el [cuaderno con soluciones](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-15-present-simple-doesnt-does-ejercicios-soluciones).

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Lo esencial |
| :--- | :--- |
| Negativa | he/she/it + **doesn't** + verbo |
| Pregunta | **Does** + he/she/it + verbo…? |
| Respuestas | Yes, he **does**. / No, she **doesn't**. |
| Ortografía | goes, watches, studies, has |
| Atención | Tras *doesn't/Does* → verbo **sin -s** |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

En la **Unidad 16** practicarás el inglés de **cafetería**: *Can I have…?*, *I'd like…*.

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 15 A1 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-15-present-simple-doesnt-does-ejercicios-soluciones)

Guía dedicada:

- [Unidad 16 — Pedir en la cafetería: Can I have e I'd like](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-16-cafeteria-can-i-have-id-like)

Guías relacionadas:

- [Gramática inglesa: guía por niveles](/blog/gramatica/gramatica-inglesa-guia)
- [Pronunciación de -ed y -s](/blog/gramatica/pronunciacion-ed-s-ingles)
- [Inglés A1: guía para empezar](/blog/metodos/ingles-a1)

---

title: Pedir en la cafetería (A1): Can I have…? e I’d like…
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 16 del curso A1: pedir en la cafetería con Can I have…? e I'd like…, Would you like…?, bebidas, snacks, precios y la cuenta. Con audios, esquemas y ejercicios.
description: Aprende a pedir en un café en inglés A1 con Can I have…? e I'd like…. Guía Unidad 16: bebidas, snacks, la cuenta, precios, audios y ejercicios.
alt: Esquema de Can I have en inglés nivel A1 cafetería

faqs.question: ¿Cómo pido un café en inglés de forma educada?
faqs.answer: Usa Can I have a coffee, please? o I'd like a coffee, please. Ambas son más educadas que Give me… o I want….

faqs.question: ¿Qué diferencia hay entre Can I have e I'd like?
faqs.answer: Ambas sirven para pedir. Can I have…? es una petición directa educada. I'd like… (= I would like) suena un poco más suave o formal. En un café A1 puedes usar las dos.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo pregunto el precio y pido la cuenta?
faqs.answer: How much is it? / How much is the coffee? Para la cuenta: Can I have the bill, please?

faqs.question: ¿Qué vocabulario practico en la Unidad 16?
faqs.answer: Bebidas (coffee, tea, juice, water, milk), snacks (croissant, sandwich, cake, cookie, toast) y frases de servicio (counter, bill, Anything else?).

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 16 del curso A1?

content:
Tras dominar *doesn't* y *Does he/she…?* en la [Unidad 15](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-15-present-simple-doesnt-does), en la **Unidad 16 del curso A1** (*At the Cafe*) aprendes a **pedir en una cafetería**: *Can I have…?*, *I'd like…* y *Would you like…?*.

Esta guía cubre las **fórmulas de pedido**, el **vocabulario de bebidas y snacks**, **precios**, **la cuenta** y diálogos típicos. Incluye **audios**, **esquemas** y **ejercicios**.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 16 — At the Cafe](/curso-a1/unit-16)  
> **Cuaderno de ejercicios (con soluciones):** [Ejercicios Unidad 16 A1](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-16-cafeteria-can-i-have-id-like-ejercicios-soluciones)  
> **Repaso útil:** [Unidad 8 — Números, edad y precios](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-8-numeros-edad-precios) · [Unidad 15 — doesn't](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-15-present-simple-doesnt-does)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 16 (A1)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Pedir con ***Can I have…, please?***
- Pedir con ***I'd like…*** (*I would like*).
- Responder a ***Would you like something to drink/eat?***
- Usar vocabulario de **café**, **snacks** y **servicio**.
- Preguntar el **precio** y pedir **la cuenta**.

---

## 1. Vocabulario: bebidas, snacks y servicio

### Bebidas

| Inglés | Español | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **coffee** | café | Can I have a coffee, please? |
| **tea** | té | I'd like a tea, please. |
| **(orange) juice** | zumo (de naranja) | I'd like an orange juice. |
| **water** | agua | Can I have a water, please? |
| **milk** | leche | Would you like milk? |

### Snacks / comida

| Inglés | Español | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **croissant** | croissant | I'd like a croissant. |
| **sandwich** | bocadillo | Can I have a sandwich? |
| **cake** | tarta / pastel | Would you like some cake? |
| **cookie** | galleta | I'd like a cookie. |
| **toast** | tostada | Can I have toast, please? |

### Servicio y precios

| Inglés | Español | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **counter** | mostrador | I'm at the counter. |
| **table / chair** | mesa / silla | A table for two. |
| **bill** | cuenta | Can I have the bill, please? |
| **How much is it?** | ¿Cuánto es / cuesta? | How much is the coffee? |
| **Anything else?** | ¿Algo más? | No, that's all, thanks. |
| **please / thanks** | por favor / gracias | A tea, please. Thanks! |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-16/coffee.mp3" title="🔊 Coffee"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-16/tea.mp3" title="🔊 Tea"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-16/orange-juice.mp3" title="🔊 Orange juice"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-16/water.mp3" title="🔊 Water"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-16/croissant.mp3" title="🔊 Croissant"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-16/sandwich.mp3" title="🔊 Sandwich"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-16/cake.mp3" title="🔊 Cake"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-16/cookie.mp3" title="🔊 Cookie"></audio>

![Vocabulario de cafetería en inglés A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-16/a1-unit16-vocab.png)

### Tips de uso

- En A1 suele decirse *a coffee / a tea* (una taza), aunque en casa digas *coffee* sin artículo.  
- *orange juice* → **an** orange juice (empieza por vocal).  
- *the bill* = la cuenta (con *the*).  
- Añade **please** al pedir: suena educado y natural.

---

## 2. *Can I have…?*

Fórmula de pedido educado:

```
Can I have + a/an + cosa, please?
```

| Pedido | Significado |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Can I have** a coffee, please? | ¿Me pone un café, por favor? |
| **Can I have** a tea, please? | ¿Me pone un té, por favor? |
| **Can I have** a sandwich, please? | ¿Me pone un bocadillo, por favor? |
| **Can I have** the bill, please? | ¿La cuenta, por favor? |

Es más educado que *Give me a coffee* o *I want a coffee*.

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-16/can-i-have-coffee.mp3" title="🔊 Can I have a coffee, please?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-16/can-i-have-tea.mp3" title="🔊 Can I have a tea, please?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-16/can-i-have-bill.mp3" title="🔊 Can I have the bill, please?"></audio>

![Esquema Can I have en cafetería inglés A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-16/a1-unit16-can-i-have.png)

### Variantes útiles

> Can I have a coffee **and** a croissant, please?  
> Can I have **two** teas, please?  
> Can I have a water, please?

---

## 3. *I'd like…* / *I would like…*

```
I'd like + a/an + cosa, please.
```

*I'd* = *I would*. Misma idea: “Me gustaría…”.

| Pedido | Significado |
| :--- | :--- |
| **I'd like** a tea, please. | Me gustaría un té. |
| **I'd like** a croissant, please. | Me gustaría un croissant. |
| **I'd like** an orange juice. | Me gustaría un zumo de naranja. |
| **I would like** a sandwich, please. | Forma completa (más formal). |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-16/id-like-croissant.mp3" title="🔊 I'd like a croissant, please"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-16/id-like-tea.mp3" title="🔊 I'd like a tea, please"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-16/id-like-juice.mp3" title="🔊 I'd like an orange juice"></audio>

![Esquema I'd like y Would you like en inglés A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-16/a1-unit16-id-like.png)

### *Can I have* vs *I'd like*

| | Uso típico |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Can I have…?** | Pedido directo y educado en el mostrador |
| **I'd like…** | Pedido suave; también responde a *Would you like…?* |

Ambas son correctas en un café. Practica las dos.

---

## 4. *Would you like…?* (ofertas del camarero)

El personal pregunta:

```
Would you like + something to drink / eat?
Would you like + a/an + cosa?
```

| Oferta | Respuesta típica |
| :--- | :--- |
| Would you like something to drink? | Yes, I'd like a coffee. / No, thanks. |
| Would you like something to eat? | Yes, a croissant please. |
| Would you like milk? | Yes, please. / No, thank you. |
| Anything else? | No, that's all, thanks. |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-16/would-you-like-drink.mp3" title="🔊 Would you like something to drink?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-16/would-you-like-eat.mp3" title="🔊 Would you like something to eat?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-16/anything-else.mp3" title="🔊 Anything else?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-16/thats-all-thanks.mp3" title="🔊 No, that's all, thanks"></audio>

*Would you like…?* es más educado que *Do you want…?* en este contexto.

---

## 5. Precios y la cuenta

Recuerda *How much* de la [Unidad 8](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-8-numeros-edad-precios):

| Frase | Uso |
| :--- | :--- |
| **How much is it?** | ¿Cuánto es? |
| **How much is the coffee?** | ¿Cuánto cuesta el café? |
| It's **two euros fifty**. | Son dos euros con cincuenta. |
| **Can I have the bill, please?** | La cuenta, por favor. |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-16/how-much-is-it.mp3" title="🔊 How much is it?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-16/two-euros-fifty.mp3" title="🔊 Two euros fifty"></audio>

### Mini-secuencia en el mostrador

1. Hello!  
2. Can I have a coffee and a croissant, please?  
3. Would you like something else? — No, that's all, thanks.  
4. How much is it? — Two euros fifty.  
5. Can I have the bill, please? — Sure.

---

## 6. Diálogo modelo completo

> **Waiter:** Hi! What can I get you?  
> **Sara:** Can I have a coffee, please?  
> **Waiter:** Would you like something to eat?  
> **Sara:** Yes, I'd like a croissant, please.  
> **Waiter:** Anything else?  
> **Sara:** No, that's all, thanks. How much is it?  
> **Waiter:** Three euros twenty.  
> **Sara:** Can I have the bill, please?  
> **Waiter:** Sure. Here you are.  
> **Sara:** Thank you!

Otro diálogo breve:

> **Tom:** I'd like a tea and a sandwich, please.  
> **Server:** Would you like milk in your tea?  
> **Tom:** Yes, please.  
> **Server:** OK. That's four euros.  
> **Tom:** Thanks!

---

## 7. Errores típicos de hispanohablantes

| ❌ Incorrecto | ✅ Correcto | Explicación |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *Give me a coffee* | *Can I have a coffee, please?* | Más educado |
| *I want a tea* (seco) | *I'd like a tea, please* | Suave y natural |
| *Can I have coffee?* (sin *a*) | *Can I have **a** coffee?* | En café: *a coffee* = una taza |
| *I'd like a orange juice* | *I'd like **an** orange juice* | Vocal → *an* |
| *Can I have bill?* | *Can I have **the** bill?* | *the bill* |
| *How many is the coffee?* | *How **much** is the coffee?* | Precio → *much* |
| *I like a coffee* (pedido) | *I'd like a coffee* | Pedido = *would like*, no *like* |

---

## 8. Pronunciación útil

| Forma | Tip A1 |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Can I have** | *Can* a menudo se debilita; practica claro: *Can I have…?* |
| **I'd like** | *I'd* = *aid* corto + *like*. |
| **Would you like** | En habla rápida: *wood-ya like*. Primero di las tres palabras. |
| **please** | Al final del pedido: *…, please?* |
| **bill** | Suena *bil*. |

Escucha los audios y repite dos veces cada pedido. Grábate pidiendo café + croissant.

### Mapa de cortesía (de menos a más educado)

| Menos educado | Mejor en A1 |
| :--- | :--- |
| Give me a coffee. | Can I have a coffee, please? |
| I want a tea. | I'd like a tea, please. |
| Do you want juice? | Would you like some juice? |

No hace falta sonar “demasiado formal” en un café: con *please*, *Can I have* e *I'd like* ya entras bien en casi cualquier sitio en inglés.

---

## 8b. Mini-diálogos para memorizar

> **A:** Can I have a coffee, please?  
> **B:** Sure. Would you like milk?  
> **A:** Yes, please.  
> **B:** Anything else?  
> **A:** No, that's all. How much is it?  
> **B:** Two euros fifty.

> **A:** Would you like something to drink?  
> **B:** Yes, I'd like an orange juice.  
> **A:** Would you like something to eat?  
> **B:** I'd like a sandwich, please.

> **A:** Can I have the bill, please?  
> **B:** Of course. One moment.

Cambia solo la bebida o el snack: así fijas la estructura sin aprender diálogos de memoria largos.

---

## 8c. Plantillas para copiar

1. Can I have a \_\_\_\_, please?  
2. I'd like a \_\_\_\_ and a \_\_\_\_, please.  
3. Would you like something to drink? — Yes, I'd like \_\_\_\_.  
4. How much is the \_\_\_\_?  
5. Can I have the bill, please?

Rellena con tu pedido habitual (café con leche, té, zumo…). Si lo dices en voz alta cada mañana, se queda.

### Más ejemplos en contexto

> At the counter: *Hi! Can I have a coffee and a cookie, please?*  
> With a friend: *I'd like a tea. And you?* — *I'd like an orange juice.*  
> The waiter asks: *Would you like something to eat?* — *Yes, a sandwich please.*  
> Paying: *How much is it?* — *Four euros.* — *Can I have the bill, please?*

Practica también **pedidos dobles**: bebida + snack. Es lo más realista en una cafetería (*a coffee and a croissant*).

---

## 9. Ejercicios prácticos (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — Completa con *Can I have* o *I'd like*

1. \_\_\_\_ a coffee, please? (*pregunta/pedido con Can*)  
2. \_\_\_\_ a croissant, please. (*I'd…*)  
3. \_\_\_\_ the bill, please?  
4. \_\_\_\_ an orange juice.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **Can I have** a coffee, please?  
2. **I'd like** a croissant, please.  
3. **Can I have** the bill, please?  
4. **I'd like** an orange juice.
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — Elige la opción correcta

1. Can I have \_\_\_ coffee, please? (a / an / the)  
2. I'd like \_\_\_ orange juice. (a / an)  
3. Can I have \_\_\_ bill, please? (a / the)  
4. How \_\_\_ is it? (much / many)  
5. Would you like something \_\_\_ drink? (to / for)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **a**  
2. **an**  
3. **the**  
4. **much**  
5. **to**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Traduce al inglés

1. ¿Me pone un café, por favor?  
2. Me gustaría un té.  
3. ¿Te gustaría algo para comer?  
4. ¿Cuánto es? — Dos euros cincuenta.  
5. La cuenta, por favor.  
6. No, eso es todo, gracias.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. Can I have a coffee, please?  
2. I'd like a tea (, please).  
3. Would you like something to eat?  
4. How much is it? — Two euros fifty.  
5. Can I have the bill, please?  
6. No, that's all, thanks.
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Corrige el error

1. *Give me a coffee.*  
2. *I want tea.* (hazlo educado)  
3. *I'd like a orange juice.*  
4. *Can I have bill?*  
5. *How many is the coffee?*

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. Can I have a coffee, please? / I'd like a coffee, please.  
2. I'd like a tea, please. / Can I have a tea, please?  
3. I'd like **an** orange juice.  
4. Can I have **the** bill?  
5. How **much** is the coffee?
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Empareja pregunta y respuesta

1. Would you like something to drink?  
2. How much is it?  
3. Anything else?  
4. Can I have a sandwich, please?

a) Two euros fifty.  
b) Yes, I'd like a tea.  
c) Yes, of course.  
d) No, that's all, thanks.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1 → **b**  
2 → **a**  
3 → **d**  
4 → **c**
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Escribe tu pedido

Escribe un mini-diálogo (6–8 líneas) en una cafetería: saludo, pedido con *Can I have* o *I'd like*, oferta *Would you like…?*, precio y cuenta.

**Modelo:**

> Hello! Can I have a coffee and a cookie, please?  
> Would you like milk? — Yes, please.  
> Anything else? — No, that's all, thanks.  
> How much is it? — Three euros.  
> Can I have the bill, please? — Sure. Thank you!

### Ejercicio 7 — Elige la frase correcta para la situación

1. Estás en el mostrador y quieres un té.  
2. El camarero pregunta si quieres comer algo.  
3. Quieres saber el precio.  
4. Quieres pagar.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. Can I have a tea, please? / I'd like a tea, please.  
2. Yes, I'd like a croissant / sandwich, please. (o *No, thanks.*)  
3. How much is it? / How much is the tea?  
4. Can I have the bill, please?
</details>

---

## 10. Plan de práctica (15 minutos)

1. **3 min** — Repite: *Can I have a coffee / tea / water, please?*  
2. **3 min** — Repite: *I'd like a croissant / sandwich / juice.*  
3. **4 min** — Escucha los audios y actúa el diálogo modelo.  
4. **5 min** — Escribe tu pedido habitual + *How much* + *the bill*.

### Checklist

- [ ] Sé pedir con *Can I have…, please?*  
- [ ] Sé pedir con *I'd like…*  
- [ ] Respondo a *Would you like…?*  
- [ ] Uso *a/an* y *the bill* correctamente  
- [ ] Pregunto *How much is it?*

---

## 11. Consejos para practicar

1. **Haz la carta** de tu café favorito en inglés (5 bebidas + 5 snacks).  
2. **Representa** el diálogo delante del espejo o con un amigo.  
3. **Combina** con números de la Unidad 8: precios reales (*three euros forty*).  
4. Prepárate para la [Unidad 17](/curso-a1/unit-17): desayuno, comida y cena.  
5. Practica en la [Unidad 16 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-16) o el [cuaderno con soluciones](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-16-cafeteria-can-i-have-id-like-ejercicios-soluciones).

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Lo esencial |
| :--- | :--- |
| Pedir | **Can I have** a coffee, please? |
| Pedir (suave) | **I'd like** a tea, please. |
| Oferta | **Would you like** something to drink? |
| Precio | **How much** is it? |
| Cuenta | Can I have **the bill**, please? |
| Cierre | No, **that's all**, thanks. |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

En la **Unidad 17** hablarás de **Breakfast, Lunch & Dinner** e introducirás ideas de contables/incontables.

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 16 A1 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-16-cafeteria-can-i-have-id-like-ejercicios-soluciones)

Guía dedicada:

- [Unidad 17 — Comidas: Breakfast, Lunch & Dinner](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-17-comidas-breakfast-lunch-dinner)

Guías relacionadas:

- [Can / Could en inglés](/blog/gramatica/can-could-ingles)
- [Inglés en restaurantes y bares](/blog/viajes/ingles-restaurantes-bares-viaje)
- [Inglés para camareros y hostelería](/blog/trabajo/ingles-para-camareros-y-hosteleria)

---

title: Comidas y gustos (A1): Breakfast, Lunch & Dinner
author: linguafly-team
excerpt: Guía de la Unidad 17 del curso A1: breakfast, lunch y dinner; have breakfast; like/love/hate + comida; introducción a contables e incontables. Con audios, esquemas y ejercicios.
description: Aprende a hablar de desayuno, comida y cena en inglés A1: have breakfast, like/love/hate + comida, contables e incontables. Guía Unidad 17 con audios y ejercicios.
alt: Vocabulario de desayuno comida y cena en inglés A1

faqs.question: ¿Se dice have breakfast o eat breakfast?
faqs.answer: En inglés lo más natural es have breakfast / lunch / dinner. También se oye eat breakfast, pero en A1 prioriza have.

faqs.question: ¿Cómo digo que me gusta o no me gusta una comida?
faqs.answer: I like / I love / I hate + nombre: I like cheese. She loves pasta. He hates fish. Negativa: I don't like broccoli. She doesn't like meat.

faqs.question: ¿Qué son nombres contables e incontables en A1?
faqs.answer: Contables se cuentan (an apple, two eggs). Incontables no llevan plural ni a/an (milk, cheese, bread, rice, meat). Es una introducción; más adelante verás some/any.

faqs.question: ¿Qué vocabulario practico en la Unidad 17?
faqs.answer: Comidas del día (breakfast, lunch, dinner), fruta, verdura, carne, lácteos y granos: apple, milk, cheese, eggs, bread, vegetables, chicken, fish, pasta, rice.

faqs.question: ¿Dónde practico la Unidad 17 del curso A1?
faqs.answer: En la Unidad 17 del curso A1 de Linguafly y en el cuaderno de ejercicios con soluciones del blog: gramática, vocabulario, reading, listening y writing.

content:
Tras pedir en la cafetería en la [Unidad 16](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-16-cafeteria-can-i-have-id-like), en la **Unidad 17 del curso A1** (*Breakfast, Lunch & Dinner*) hablas de **las comidas del día**, de **qué te gusta** (*like / love / hate*) y de una intro a **contables e incontables**.

Esta guía cubre *have breakfast/lunch/dinner*, gustos con comida, vocabulario de **fruta, verdura, carne y lácteos**, y ejemplos claros. Incluye **audios**, **esquemas** y **ejercicios**. Es el complemento natural de lo que ya sabes pedir en un café.

> **Practica en el curso:** [Unidad 17 — Breakfast, Lunch & Dinner](/curso-a1/unit-17)  
> **Repaso útil:** [Unidad 16 — Cafetería](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-16-cafeteria-can-i-have-id-like) · [Unidad 14 — don't / Do you](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-14-present-simple-dont-do-you)

---

## Qué aprenderás en la Unidad 17 (A1)

Al terminar esta unidad serás capaz de:

- Nombrar **breakfast, lunch y dinner** y decir a qué hora las tomas.
- Usar ***have breakfast / lunch / dinner***.
- Expresar gustos: ***like / love / hate*** + comida.
- Distinguir (intro) **contables** (*apple, egg*) e **incontables** (*milk, bread*).
- Hablar de **fruta, verdura, carne, pescado y lácteos**.

---

## 1. Vocabulario: comidas del día y alimentos

### Las tres comidas

| Inglés | Español | Cuándo | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **breakfast** | desayuno | morning | I have breakfast at eight. |
| **lunch** | comida (almuerzo) | midday | She has lunch at one. |
| **dinner** | cena | evening | We have dinner at eight. |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-17/breakfast.mp3" title="🔊 Breakfast"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-17/lunch.mp3" title="🔊 Lunch"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-17/dinner.mp3" title="🔊 Dinner"></audio>

### Alimentos frecuentes

| Inglés | Español | Tipo |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **apple / banana / orange** | manzana / plátano / naranja | fruit (countable) |
| **fruit** | fruta (en general) | often uncountable |
| **vegetables / carrots / broccoli** | verduras / zanahorias / brócoli | vegetables |
| **eggs** | huevos | countable |
| **toast / bread** | tostada / pan | toast/bread often uncountable |
| **cereal** | cereales | often uncountable |
| **milk / cheese / yogurt** | leche / queso / yogur | dairy (uncountable) |
| **meat / chicken / fish** | carne / pollo / pescado | meat |
| **rice / pasta** | arroz / pasta | uncountable |
| **salad / soup** | ensalada / sopa | lunch items |
| **sandwich** | bocadillo | countable |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-17/apple.mp3" title="🔊 Apple"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-17/milk.mp3" title="🔊 Milk"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-17/cheese.mp3" title="🔊 Cheese"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-17/bread.mp3" title="🔊 Bread"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-17/eggs.mp3" title="🔊 Eggs"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-17/vegetables.mp3" title="🔊 Vegetables"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-17/meat.mp3" title="🔊 Meat"></audio>

![Vocabulario breakfast lunch dinner en inglés A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-17/a1-unit17-vocab.png)

### Tips

- *fruit* (general) suele ir sin plural: *I like fruit.*  
- *vegetables* es plural: *I like vegetables.*  
- *chicken* puede ser la carne (incontable en muchos contextos A1) o el animal.

---

## 2. *Have breakfast / lunch / dinner*

```
have + breakfast / lunch / dinner
```

| Persona | Ejemplo |
| :--- | :--- |
| I / you / we / they | I **have** breakfast at eight. |
| he / she / it | She **has** lunch at one. |
| Negativa | I **don't** have breakfast. / She **doesn't** have lunch. |
| Pregunta | **Do** you have dinner at home? / **Does** he have breakfast? |

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-17/i-have-breakfast.mp3" title="🔊 I have breakfast at eight"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-17/she-has-lunch.mp3" title="🔊 She has lunch at one"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-17/we-have-dinner.mp3" title="🔊 We have dinner at eight"></audio>

### *for* + comida

> I have eggs **for** breakfast.  
> She likes salad **for** lunch.  
> We have pasta **for** dinner.

---

## 3. *Like / love / hate* + comida

```
sujeto + like / love / hate + nombre (comida)
```

| Intensidad | Ejemplo | Significado |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **like** | I like cheese. | Me gusta |
| **love** | She loves pasta. | Me encanta / adora |
| **hate** | He hates fish. | Odia / no soporta |
| **don't like** | They don't like broccoli. | No les gusta |
| **doesn't like** | She doesn't like meat. | No le gusta |

Recuerda la 3.ª persona: *She **loves** / He **hates** / She **doesn't** like…*  
Y las preguntas de U14/U15: *Do you like milk? Does she like eggs?*

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-17/i-like-cheese.mp3" title="🔊 I like cheese"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-17/she-loves-pasta.mp3" title="🔊 She loves pasta"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-17/he-hates-fish.mp3" title="🔊 He hates fish"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-17/they-dont-like-broccoli.mp3" title="🔊 They don't like broccoli"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-17/do-you-like-milk.mp3" title="🔊 Do you like milk?"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-17/i-like-fruit.mp3" title="🔊 I like fruit for breakfast"></audio>

<audio controls preload="none" src="/audio/blog/curso-a1/unit-17/she-doesnt-like-meat.mp3" title="🔊 She doesn't like meat"></audio>

![Esquema like love hate con comida en inglés A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-17/a1-unit17-like-love-hate.png)

### Escala rápida

> I hate broccoli. → I don't like broccoli. → I like broccoli. → I love broccoli.

En A1, *like* + nombre es suficiente. Más adelante (U18) profundizarás en *like + -ing*.

---

## 4. Contables e incontables (introducción A1)

| Contable (countable) | Incontable (uncountable) |
| :--- | :--- |
| Se puede contar: 1, 2, 3… | No se cuenta con números simples |
| *a/an* + singular; plural *-s* | Sin *a/an*; normalmente sin plural |
| an **apple**, two **eggs**, three **carrots** | **milk**, **cheese**, **bread**, **rice**, **meat**, **water** |

![Esquema contables e incontables comida inglés A1](/blog/curso-a1/unit-17/a1-unit17-countable.png)

### Ejemplos en frases

> I like **apples**. / I like **fruit**.  
> She has **an egg** for breakfast. / She drinks **milk**.  
> We eat **bread** with cheese. (*not* *a bread* en A1 básico)  
> Do you like **vegetables**? — Yes, I love **carrots**.

No necesitas dominar *some/any* aún (vendrá más adelante). Por ahora: reconoce si puedes decir *an apple* o solo *milk*.

### Tabla práctica

| Palabra | ¿Contable? | Ejemplo seguro A1 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| apple | Sí | an apple, two apples |
| egg | Sí | an egg, eggs |
| sandwich | Sí | a sandwich |
| milk | No | milk (I like milk.) |
| cheese | No | cheese |
| bread | No (A1) | bread |
| rice / pasta | No | rice, pasta |
| meat | No | meat |
| water | No | water |

---

## 5. Más ejemplos en contexto

### Un día de comidas

> I **have breakfast** at eight. I have toast, eggs and milk. I **like** fruit for breakfast.  
> I **have lunch** at one. I often have a sandwich and water. I **don't like** soup.  
> I **have dinner** at eight. We have chicken and vegetables. My brother **loves** pasta. He **hates** fish.

### Preguntas útiles

> What do you have for breakfast?  
> Do you like cheese?  
> Does she like vegetables?  
> What time do you have dinner?

### Conectar con la cafetería (U16)

> In a cafe: *I'd like a coffee and a sandwich, please.*  
> At home: *I have a sandwich for lunch. I like cheese sandwiches.*

---

## 6. Errores típicos de hispanohablantes

| ❌ Incorrecto | ✅ Correcto | Explicación |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| *I eat breakfast* (único foco) | *I **have** breakfast* | Lo más natural en A1 |
| *I like the cheese* (siempre) | *I like cheese* | Gustos generales sin *the* |
| *She like pasta* | *She **likes** pasta* | 3.ª persona *-s* |
| *I like milks* | *I like **milk*** | Incontable: sin plural |
| *A bread* / *a milk* | *bread* / *milk* (o *a glass of milk*) | Sin *a/an* en intro A1 |
| *I love the pizzas* (gusto general) | *I love **pizza*** | Comida en general |
| *Do you like?* (sin objeto) | *Do you like **milk**?* | Hace falta el nombre |

---

## 7. Pronunciación útil

| Forma | Tip A1 |
| :--- | :--- |
| **breakfast** | *BREK-fəst* (dos sílabas fuertes al inicio). |
| **lunch / dinner** | Claras y cortas. |
| **vegetables** | *VEJ-tə-bəlz* (a menudo 3 sílabas). |
| **cheese / meat** | Vocal larga en *cheese*. |
| **loves / hates** | Con *-s* sonora: *luvz / heits*. |

Escucha los audios y repite: *I have breakfast… I like cheese… She doesn't like meat.*

### Ortografía y artículos (recordatorio breve)

- Contable singular: **a/an** (*an apple*, *an egg*).  
- Contable plural: *-s* (*apples*, *eggs*, *carrots*).  
- Incontable: sin *a/an* y sin plural (*milk*, *cheese*, *bread*).  
- Gustos generales: suele ir **sin the** (*I like cheese*, no *the cheese*).

Si dudas entre *a milk* y *milk*, en esta unidad elige **milk**. Más adelante aprenderás *a glass of milk* / *some milk*.

---

## 7b. Mini-diálogos para memorizar

> **A:** What do you have for breakfast?  
> **B:** I have toast and eggs. And you?  
> **A:** I have cereal and milk. I love fruit too.

> **A:** Do you like fish?  
> **B:** No, I don't. I hate fish. I like chicken.  
> **A:** Does your sister like pasta?  
> **B:** Yes, she does. She loves pasta!

> **A:** What time do you have dinner?  
> **B:** At eight. We have vegetables and rice.  
> **A:** Nice! I have dinner at nine.

Cambia solo la comida: fijas *have* + *like/love/hate* sin memorizar diálogos largos.

---

## 7c. Plantillas para copiar

1. I have breakfast at \_\_\_\_. I have \_\_\_\_ and \_\_\_\_.  
2. I like \_\_\_\_. I love \_\_\_\_. I don't like \_\_\_\_.  
3. She has lunch at \_\_\_\_. She likes \_\_\_\_ for lunch.  
4. Do you like \_\_\_\_? — Yes, I do. / No, I don't.  
5. We have dinner at \_\_\_\_. We have \_\_\_\_ and \_\_\_\_.

Rellena con tu rutina real. Si lo escribes y lo dices en voz alta, se queda mucho mejor.

### Mapa U14–U17 (gustos y comida)

| Unidad | Aporte |
| :--- | :--- |
| U14 | *Do you like…? / I don't like…* |
| U15 | *Does she like…? / She doesn't like…* |
| U16 | Pedir comida/bebida en el café |
| U17 | Comidas del día + *love/hate* + contable/incontable |

### Más frases para memorizar

> I have breakfast at seven. I have toast and milk.  
> I like apples. I don't like broccoli.  
> She loves pasta. She doesn't like meat.  
> He hates fish. He likes chicken.  
> What do you have for lunch? — A sandwich and water.  
> Do you like cheese? — Yes, I do. I love cheese!

Lee la lista dos veces en voz alta. Luego tapa el inglés y traduce desde el español. Si puedes, grábate y comprueba que usas *have* (no solo *eat*) y que en 3.ª persona aparece la *-s* (*likes / loves / hates*).

Otra idea rápida: escribe tu desayuno de hoy en tres frases (*I have… / I like… / I don't like…*) y compártelas con alguien o déjalas en una nota del móvil.

---

## 8. Ejercicios prácticos (con soluciones)

### Ejercicio 1 — Completa con *have / has*

1. I \_\_\_\_ breakfast at eight.  
2. She \_\_\_\_ lunch at one.  
3. We \_\_\_\_ dinner at home.  
4. He \_\_\_\_ eggs for breakfast.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **have**  
2. **has**  
3. **have**  
4. **has**
</details>

### Ejercicio 2 — *like / love / hate* (y 3.ª persona)

1. I \_\_\_\_ cheese. (like)  
2. She \_\_\_\_ pasta. (love)  
3. He \_\_\_\_ fish. (hate)  
4. They \_\_\_\_ broccoli. (don't like)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **like**  
2. **loves**  
3. **hates**  
4. **don't like**
</details>

### Ejercicio 3 — Contable o incontable

Marca C (contable) o U (incontable): apple, milk, egg, bread, cheese, sandwich, rice, carrot.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

- **C:** apple, egg, sandwich, carrot  
- **U:** milk, bread, cheese, rice
</details>

### Ejercicio 4 — Traduce al inglés

1. Desayuno a las ocho.  
2. Me gusta el queso.  
3. A ella le encanta la pasta.  
4. Él odia el pescado.  
5. ¿Te gusta la leche?  
6. Ella no come carne. / No le gusta la carne.

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I have breakfast at eight.  
2. I like cheese.  
3. She loves pasta.  
4. He hates fish.  
5. Do you like milk?  
6. She doesn't like meat. (o *She doesn't eat meat.*)
</details>

### Ejercicio 5 — Corrige el error

1. *I eat breakfast at seven.* (hazlo más natural A1)  
2. *She like eggs.*  
3. *I like milks.*  
4. *A bread for breakfast.*  
5. *Do you like?*  

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. I **have** breakfast at seven.  
2. She **likes** eggs.  
3. I like **milk**.  
4. **Bread** for breakfast. / I have **toast** for breakfast.  
5. Do you like **milk / cheese / …**?
</details>

### Ejercicio 6 — Escribe tu día alimentario

Escribe 6–8 frases: qué tomas en breakfast/lunch/dinner y qué te gusta o no.

**Modelo:**

> I have breakfast at eight. I have toast, an egg and milk. I like fruit. I have lunch at one: a sandwich and water. I don't like soup. I have dinner at eight. We have chicken and vegetables. I love pasta. I hate broccoli!

### Ejercicio 7 — Elige la opción correcta

1. I \_\_\_\_ breakfast at nine. (have / has)  
2. Milk is \_\_\_\_. (countable / uncountable)  
3. An apple is \_\_\_\_. (countable / uncountable)  
4. She \_\_\_\_ meat. (don't like / doesn't like)  
5. What do you have \_\_\_\_ lunch? (for / to)

<details>
<summary>Ver solución</summary>

1. **have**  
2. **uncountable**  
3. **countable**  
4. **doesn't like**  
5. **for**
</details>

---

## 9. Diálogo modelo

> **Ana:** What do you have for breakfast?  
> **Luis:** I have cereal and milk. Sometimes I have an apple. And you?  
> **Ana:** I have toast and eggs. I love cheese too.  
> **Luis:** Do you like fish?  
> **Ana:** No, I don't. I hate fish. I like chicken.  
> **Luis:** What time do you have dinner?  
> **Ana:** At eight. We have pasta or rice and vegetables.  
> **Luis:** Nice! I have dinner at nine. I don't like broccoli, but I love carrots.

---

## 10. Plan de práctica (15 minutos)

1. **3 min** — Di en voz alta: *I have breakfast / lunch / dinner at…*  
2. **4 min** — Lista 5 comidas que te gustan y 3 que no (*like / don't like / hate*).  
3. **4 min** — Escucha los audios y repite.  
4. **4 min** — Clasifica 10 palabras en contable / incontable.

### Checklist

- [ ] Sé usar *have breakfast/lunch/dinner*  
- [ ] Sé decir *I like / love / hate* + comida  
- [ ] Formo *She likes / She doesn't like*  
- [ ] Distingo *an apple* vs *milk*  
- [ ] Pregunto *Do you like…?* / *What do you have for…?*

---

## 11. Consejos para practicar

1. **Etiqueta** tu nevera: *milk, cheese, eggs, apples* en post-its.  
2. **Cuenta tu día** alimentario en voz alta cada noche (1 minuto).  
3. **Combina** con U16: en el café pide lo que *likes*; en casa descríbelo.  
4. Prepárate para la [Unidad 18](/curso-a1/unit-18): *like + -ing* y *because*.  
5. Practica en la [Unidad 17 del curso A1](/curso-a1/unit-17) o el [cuaderno con soluciones](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-17-comidas-breakfast-lunch-dinner-ejercicios-soluciones).

---

## Resumen rápido

| Tema | Lo esencial |
| :--- | :--- |
| Comidas | breakfast / lunch / dinner |
| Verbo | **have** breakfast (she **has**) |
| Gustos | like / love / hate + comida |
| Contable | an apple, two eggs |
| Incontable | milk, bread, cheese, rice, meat |
| Pregunta | Do you like…? What do you have for…? |

---

## Siguiente paso en el curso A1

En la **Unidad 18** profundizarás en **Likes & Dislikes**: *like + -ing* y *because*.

Practica ahora:

- [Ejercicios Unidad 17 A1 (con soluciones)](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-17-comidas-breakfast-lunch-dinner-ejercicios-soluciones)

Guía dedicada:

- [Unidad 18 — Gustos: like + -ing y Why? Because…](/blog/curso-a1/unidad-18-gustos-like-ing-because)

Guías relacionadas:

- [Inglés en la cocina](/blog/viajes/ingles-en-la-cocina)
- [Inglés en restaurantes y bares](/blog/viajes/ingles-restaurantes-bares-viaje)
- [Inglés A1: guía para empezar](/blog/metodos/ingles-a1)

---

title: Gustos y hobbies (A1): like + -ing y Why? Because…

description: Aprende likes and dislikes en inglés A1: like/don't like + -ing, Why? Because…, hobbies, música y películas. Guía Unidad 18 con audios y ejercicios.
